# Phase26 normative volume B — D14–D26

This volume is implementation authority for the fully ratified decisions, not an adversarial report. REQ identifiers bind exact obligations; AC identifiers state independently testable outcomes. Implementation is not complete until the confirmed acceptance, database, browser, provider, operations and intended-user lanes pass where applicable. This volume contains no new founder selection.

## Authority and later refinements

Final accepted roots and ratification clarifications control antecedent review language. D17 uses the policy's frozen IANA zone for calendar Months/Years and requires a finite exceptional pause capability; earlier independent UTC/optional-pause suggestions are not alternatives. D24 controls the only initial compound reply-and-work patch. D26 permits work-only inbox readiness. D35 permits own-note edits with history, without renewing D17 age or repeating mentions. D37 and D38 define separate private Reply and new-Note drafts; note autosave/post never enters external P17 preparation. D39 personal reading is separate from Follow/P17 engagement. D40 excludes currently unwanted originals from ordinary work views while keeping authorized labelled search; it never invents target credit or a new status. D40 future holds are persistent exact-pair future-intake policy for the qualified receiving inbox and observed source mailbox, evaluated for each newly accepted matching occurrence. D19 Release/Dismiss remains one-input review; a future hold is neither its replacement nor a CRM/outbound block.

Historical words such as “proposed” in an underlying research record do not defer a ratified requirement. Release-specific qualified values remain explicit owner evidence requirements where the accepted decision deliberately did not invent a universal number.

## D14 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D14-R01 — Scope, necessity and terminology

Deliver optional internal reply guidance plus truthful operational reporting. A reply target is a measured expectation for a particular response; a D3 reminder is a chosen review/follow-up time; a D11 task due date belongs to the task owner; resolution describes Support's actual ending. None substitutes for another. No resolution timer, public commitment, automatic update cadence, customer-tier entitlement, donation-value priority, personal target, custom policy hierarchy, AI quality grader or generic rule builder is needed for this decision. Ordinary staff promises remain governed by D3/D5. The current schema's mandatory resolution duration is a compatibility gap to repair, not a product requirement.

### REQ26-D14-R02 — Complete simple configuration

One current configuration family per inbox has optional First reply and Next reply durations; at least one must be configured before enabling. Defaults are Off/unconfigured and blank durations, including migrated legacy seeds. An administrator chooses positive whole-minute durations using hours/minutes controls; no ambiguous days unit. Conversion is exact, rejects NaN/infinity/zero/negative/fractional minutes/overflow, and fits the existing positive PostgreSQL integer-minute range; do not arbitrarily round a requested duration. A duration is not a claim of staff coverage. Explicit Service hours requires the qualified calendar; Elapsed time counts continuously, including nights/weekends. Missing/loading/inaccessible calendar never silently selects elapsed time. Use one staged Save/Cancel and expected revision, with a calculation preview and no real test email. The full UI is in the blueprint.

### REQ26-D14-R03 — Versioned activation, edits and Off

Publish immutable policy revisions with trusted effective intervals, and a separate enable-episode boundary. Bind the source-time applicable revision and time basis to each new collecting reply period using the qualified original receipt and inbox-scope provenance; use its already captured bundle when present. An ordinary duration/calendar revision must not make delayed eligible input untargeted merely because the latest revision is newer. Truly pre-enable or Off-period input remains untargeted. If the historical source/policy binding cannot be proved, retain visible applicability-unknown review rather than guessing. Persist each original input's applicable policy bundle for a later proven successor split. Existing periods keep their rules across ordinary duration/calendar edits. Untargeted or withdrawn current periods do not become targeted through re-enable, another message in the same unresolved burst, a move or a retry; a genuinely new period can qualify.

**Turn off [Inbox] reply targets** is an explicit stop of new target applicability and withdrawal of unfinished targets created by that configuration family, across its revisions and current work homes. It does not close the underlying response period, cancel reminders, resolve work, restore a prior wait or clear a known miss. Review that scope before admission; show only authorized impact rows/counts and never a false zero when cross-inbox detail is restricted. A destination inbox with its own configuration Off may still contain pending targets created under another inbox's policy; explain that accurately. Already known pre-stop misses remain misses; before-due withdrawals are visible exclusions. Same-family Off, input, due evaluation and fulfillment use a current control fence so races have one auditable result. Re-enable never resurrects withdrawn target applicability. Record the exact target-applicability cutoff and cause for Off/withdrawal/No reply needed/valid ending. Late acceptance proved before that cutoff can establish the historical response result; acceptance after it remains real mail but does not revive the target. An interval crossing the cutoff is applicability/timing unknown. Resolve equality with a qualified common logical-order fence where available; otherwise retain uncertainty. Callback arrival order cannot decide this result.

### REQ26-D14-R04 — Qualified calendar ownership and revision

Qualify the existing Support service-hours capability at the shared API owner, with reusable immutable schedule revisions and typed consumers; do not invent an app-local timezone calculator or whole-product calendar platform. A service calendar identifies an IANA zone, local weekly intervals, dated closures/overrides and its qualified timezone-data/calculation version. Split overnight intervals into their actual local dates; holidays/overrides apply to each affected local date. Normalize overlaps and reject malformed, contradictory or wholly unavailable schedules. Calendar names and previews obey current permissions.

D14 binds the calendar revision and materialized due instant for an existing period. Ordinary edits and timezone-data upgrades affect future calculations; they do not silently improve past performance or move pending deadlines. A proven source/calculation defect is corrected through an audited revision and reviewed repair, preserving the prior interpretation. D13's optional hours wording still uses its own current-fact checks; frozen internal target history does not authorize stale public hours content. A calendar's existence or elapsed-time mode never proves someone is staffed.

### REQ26-D14-R05 — Precise clock arithmetic and display

For Service hours, count actual elapsed duration over the union of real instants whose local calendar representation belongs to the selected half-open working intervals. Nonexistent DST clock time contributes nothing; both real occurrences of an included repeated local interval count; gaps between repeated short intervals do not. Overlapping intervals never double-count. The due instant is the earliest instant at which the configured duration has accumulated from the original start. Elapsed mode adds that duration directly. Store UTC instants plus policy/calendar/zone/calculator provenance; timestamptz alone does not retain the originating zone.

Use bounded interval arithmetic and calendar-indexed computation, not minute-by-minute production loops. Reject unrepresentable combinations or retain visible timing-unavailable recovery when source-time/calendar evidence cannot produce a finite due instant; never invent now, zero, infinity or a distant sentinel. An unresolved target is due at equality; a qualified reply at the exact due instant is on time. Compare full source precision before display rounding. Viewer timezone changes display, not the instant. Show exact dates/zones when useful and distinguish service duration from elapsed duration. Zero service minutes outside hours is a real possible result, distinct from no data. The eight research examples specify DST/overlap/holiday behavior without pretending that oracle is production code.

### REQ26-D14-R06 — Qualified input, original age and admission

Only first-time admitted relevant human Support email creates or contributes to a reply period. Detected automated, malicious, quarantined/unqualified, unrelated and replayed input does not. Preserve its immutable original receipt identity/time, trusted admission order and actual original conversation; email Date, updated_at, current CRM data and new tracking rows cannot reset age. On qualified hold release, requester wait starts at the original trusted receipt, with intake delay separately visible; applicability still requires the original policy-generation cutoff. Unknown time produces unscored visible review rather than an apparently fresh deadline. This does not alter D13's much shorter automatic-confirmation eligibility.

Source intake/work creation, reply contribution and durable target-evaluation outbox commit atomically at the owner boundary. A calendar or target failure cannot prevent D1 recoverable intake. An explicit staff-origin conversation or first outgoing email alone does not create an incoming-response target. D12 citations/referrals are not new received messages.

### REQ26-D14-R07 — Reply correspondent and First/Next meaning

Maintain a stable source-scoped reply-correspondent identity for each original conversation, based on qualified correspondence/response-route authority, never an inferred CRM person, household or organization. Passive CC membership does not create a target; a participant's own qualified input can. A different sender gets their own start instead of inheriting another person's nearly expired deadline. Shared mailboxes remain mailbox correspondence scopes, not proof of a single person. No global address matching, plus-alias collapsing, Party merge or preferred-email change silently combines scopes.

First/Next follows the logical source admission sequence, not provider-webhook arrival order or proof of receipt/read. A qualified D4 human public send establishes a boundary at its immutable Core send-intent admission position, once P6 proves acceptance for the relevant correspondent. Input admitted after that boundary uses Next; input admitted before it uses First unless an earlier qualified boundary already exists. An input is satisfied only by explicit coverage, regardless of boundary position. Keep original provider receipt time for waiting duration while using trusted Core admission order for this sequence. Queued intent alone establishes no confirmed boundary; unresolved acceptance retains candidate interpretations and definite rejection establishes none. A genuinely accepted human Start email thread in a staff-origin original can establish Next for later incoming work, without satisfying that future period in advance. No reply needed, automated mail and internal notes do not establish human correspondence. A transferred original's target kind and source history are preserved. Ambiguous prior acceptance retains both permitted interpretations under R10 rather than choosing according to webhook arrival order. Reports count First/Next target instances explicitly; several periods ended without a human reply can be First-kind instances without inventing several actual first replies.

### REQ26-D14-R08 — Collecting periods, bursts and explicit reply coverage

Allow at most one collecting segment per original/correspondent, with explicitly sealed transferred segments and unresolved response-coverage candidates where necessary. Do not impose one unfinished target per current merged root or even per original/correspondent: D12-transferred input and later native input can remain owed in different homes. Contributions in an ordinary same-correspondent unanswered burst retain the oldest outstanding start; a new message cannot extend that due time.

The existing human send review/admission captures an immutable reply-coverage receipt: exact permitted original/correspondent contributions or qualified sequence cutoffs, current home/topology/source revisions and the actual intended recipient mapping. It proposes coverage only for input the actor has reviewed in the current authorized work; a mere related link, unseen message or shared Party is insufficient. One human reply can cover multiple eligible scopes only with that explicit reviewed mapping and the actual accepted P6 recipients. Coverage never expands the email audience. A reply only to B cannot clear A. Recipient-route correction is an explicit source-authorized change preserving original waiting time and evidence, not a CRM preference lookup or target reset.

Do not add a new routine send modal: use D2/D4's existing reviewed source/audience and collision boundary, with target details showing what the approved reply can cover when needed. A stale source/recipient/topology change requires the existing review; the target module cannot override the send decision.

### REQ26-D14-R09 — What satisfies a reply and what it proves

Fulfillment requires a genuine human-approved public Support response with qualified P6 **accepted for delivery** evidence for the exact actual recipient/member and reviewed source coverage. A useful answer, clarification question or substantive progress update can count; it does not have to resolve the underlying issue. Empty/draft/queued mail, automated confirmations/answers, internal notes, unrelated outgoing mail, a status click or completion of an owner task cannot count. Software proves the authorized human-reply classification and coverage, not semantic helpfulness through an AI scorer or body-length heuristic; quality remains a staff/review responsibility.

Use the P6-owned acceptance occurrence time when qualified. If an API success proves acceptance without its exact time, retain a conservative possible-acceptance interval bounded by the relevant server-call/evidence times. Earlier ambiguous calls may widen it; a definite earlier rejection does not. On time requires the entire possible acceptance interval to be on/before due; late requires the entire interval to be after due. A straddling interval is timing unknown until stronger evidence narrows it. Once all contributions have qualified accepted-response coverage, the reply obligation is fulfilled even if acceptance timing, historical First/Next attribution or report-cohort membership remains uncertain. That uncertainty is reporting/evidence work; it cannot keep the fulfilled period in Replies needing attention or reopen Support solely to score it. Candidate deadlines create live reply attention only for still-unanswered contributions. A separate genuinely actionable delivery problem still follows D3. Never backdate a later successful retry to the first attempted POST. Mailbox Delivered/read is separate and cannot be inferred from this metric.

A later genuine bounce does not erase a real timely submission; it creates prominent D3 delivery recovery and remains visible beside the metric. Evidence correcting supposed acceptance to pre-send suppression/rejection/wrong-member mapping does correct the derived fulfillment. No P6 event is fabricated to improve the score.

### REQ26-D14-R10 — Pending sends, later input and late proof

Ordinary send preparation freezes coverage but does not erase the collecting obligation. Later input remains unconsumed. When qualified acceptance covers a complete oldest contribution prefix, atomically close that covered period and form the successor from the oldest uncovered input, preserving that input's receipt time and pinned policy bundle. Partial coverage cannot erase an uncovered older contribution or reset its deadline. Definite send rejection leaves the original owed period/start in force. Multiple sends reconcile exact coverage; a late callback for already covered input cannot consume newer input or create another completion.

While acceptance or First/Next interpretation is unresolved, preserve candidate successor boundaries and the earliest applicable possible deadline, labelled **Reply timing needs confirmation**, never a scored success or certain breach. Example: First is 24 hours, Next is one hour; input at 09:51 after a 09:50 send with unknown acceptance may need a 10:51 response. Keeping only tomorrow's First deadline would hide it. Retain the candidate even when First is disabled and Next enabled. On qualified acceptance finalize the applicable successor; on definite rejection discard only the invalid candidate split, keeping older work and delivery recovery. Source evidence revisions can correct derived interpretation, not rewrite message history, send again or restore an old D3 state.

### REQ26-D14-R11 — No reply needed and honest endings

Provide an explicit, current-revision **No reply needed** disposition for the exact reviewed outstanding contributions, for cases such as an acknowledgment while internal work continues. It marks only those exact contributions as needing no reply; it preserves any uncovered older/newer inputs, D3 work/reminders/owner actions and creates no sent event or response credit. Removing a complete oldest prefix starts the remaining collecting period from its own oldest input and stored policy bundle without inventing human First fulfillment; removing a non-prefix cannot reset the older owed deadline. Preserve already-confirmed misses for the disposed portion. It cannot settle a known outstanding promised reply or unreviewed actionable recovery merely to clear a target. Use current source/obligation review, not text classification. New input after the reviewed cutoff remains owed.

An eligible D3 Resolve can end remaining no-longer-owed reply periods in the same approved command rather than force a redundant second action. No response, continued elsewhere and created in error retain their distinct D5/D12 meanings. D12 transferred work follows R15 rather than being ended for reporting. Before-due no-reply/withdrawal is an explicit exclusion, never met; after a known miss that miss remains alongside the eventual disposition. A source-owned correction proving mistaken eligibility/time can revise results with audit; ordinary late cleanup cannot improve the denominator. Persistent Undo no reply needed reverses only the still-current mistaken disposition for the exact still-unfulfilled contribution set, through a new authorized correction and contribution/source fences. Preserve original age/policy, reconcile with the current collecting period and create current review with a new generation, without duplicate active periods or restoring old status/reminder snapshots. Already accepted-covered contributions are a no-op; newer input is untouched. Independent Off/withdrawal remains effective, so restoring reply work does not re-enable its stopped target. A valid restored target uses its original due/history interpretation, with any resulting miss/correction explicit. Undo never cancels admitted mail.

### REQ26-D14-R12 — Due review: narrow D3 extension

A still-applicable owed reply reaching its qualified due instant creates one current **Reply target reached — review needed** effect and Open review. This is a narrow D3 amendment: preserve a still-valid explicit later follow-up reminder as a separate fact, while the due review overrides deferral for work visibility. Ordinary staff-selected Open still clears the reminder under D3. The due effect is not a new status, an arrived owner result, an automatic reply or resolution.

The effect binds exact period/generation/current work home and is rechecked atomically. A duplicate/late timer, already fulfilled/withdrawn period or stale topology cannot reopen work. After staff explicitly review and choose a valid plan, do not repeatedly force Open for the same overdue period; the overdue fact remains visible until the reply/disposition is settled. Independent new source or due events can create new review normally. No reply needed may settle this exact reply-review obligation without ending unrelated work. Off/late proof/correction does not automatically restore a previous wait.

D7 coverage and D8 handoff restrictions respond to the resulting qualified Open work under their existing rules; D6 workload truth also remains accurate. This is not a new target-specific escalation. If a delayed worker has not yet committed the Open transition, authorized due queries still reveal the actionable target, with the actual current status and pending review truth; they do not wait for a tag to make work discoverable or pretend a transition already happened.

### REQ26-D14-R13 — Assignment, moves and current responsibility

Assignment, Receive Off, coverage, handoff, inbox move and changing a CRM owner cannot restart or replace a reply period's original time, kind, bound target or calendar. The current responsible work home and current assignment determine where staff act; historical origin policy and responder evidence determine their named report dimensions. A normal move carries existing goals and their originating policy; destination settings govern genuinely new eligible periods, not the moved backlog. A missing handler does not pause a target or invent staff coverage. Timing information grants no extra assignment/CRM authority, and source-policy Off has the explicit cross-home scope in R03.

### REQ26-D14-R14 — Merge and Undo

D10 retains original periods/inputs, existing due instants, candidate/coverage receipts and policy history. Project the earliest applicable authorized target through each original's current work home and D10 root; deduplicate the displayed work row, not the original obligations or actual replies. A reviewed reply in merged work can satisfy several original scopes only through R08/R09 coverage. Merge/Undo never count as a reply, reset First/Next or change the recipient list. Undo partitions present work by original evidence and current work-home/control lineage, not old snapshots. A pending outcome or due callback resolves the current topology under one fence. No double overdue event, copied target or shared-Party shortcut is permitted.

### REQ26-D14-R15 — D12 continuation, later old-route input and correction

An exact reviewed D12 whole-obligation continuation receipt can change a reply period's **current work-home original** from A to B while preserving original identity, input set, oldest start, kind, policy and deadline. This seals that transferred contribution set against automatic growth. Later native A input starts/joins local collecting work at A under its actual route; it cannot silently become B's duty. Mere related creation/link/referral does not transfer a target. A later explicit referral/continuation needs its own exact coverage/current-plan authority; partial topic context cannot transfer all remaining A obligations.

A B-source human reply can cover the transferred A inputs only through the live continuation/coverage receipt and exact qualified recipient evidence. Its P6 email remains genuinely B-source; do not copy it into A or fabricate another CRM communication. The target may reference that real reply as fulfillment. Canceling unused B or correcting the handoff rehomes still-owed targets under the qualified D12 current plan before retirement, with their existing deadlines; it does not reconstruct old snapshots or drop obligations. Combining D10 topology with D12 work-home changes must be atomic and cycle-safe.

### REQ26-D14-R16 — Authoritative data and narrow source extensions

Support owns original reply-correspondent scopes, collecting/sealed periods, contribution/coverage receipts, policy application and current reply-work home. Its current snapshots derive from durable causal evidence and remain rebuildable. P6 owns actual message/member acceptance, uncertainty, delivery and corrections; P17 owns prepared message/publication and any separately qualified system attention. CRM/Finance/care/task owners retain their records/actions. Reuse current shared commands, outbox and workflow mechanisms; do not introduce a generic workflow engine, shadow CRM or wholesale event sourcing.

Separate work disposition, target applicability, provider-proof precision, evaluated timeliness and current D3 review. At most one collecting segment exists per original/correspondent; sealed transferred segments and pending coverage candidates can coexist. One input has one authoritative coverage/history interpretation per source revision and cannot be fulfilled twice. Candidate splits are not duplicate scored periods. Stable original IDs, period generations and source receipts survive retries and correction. No client-supplied result, first_responded_at or mutable current root is authoritative history.

### REQ26-D14-R17 — Database, RLS and mutation safety

Require non-null tenant/environment, original/source/policy identities where applicable, stable period/contribution/control IDs, monotonic revisions and trusted actor/cause. Use tenant-aware foreign keys among originals, correspondents, period contributions, actual P6 member references, policy/calendar revisions, coverage and work-home receipts. Enforce unique source ingestion, one collecting segment per lane, unique reply-coverage consumption/current due-review generation and valid nullability combinations for untargeted/uncomputable/targeted states. Positive integer minutes and finite UTC instants use appropriate types; no `due_at > now()` constraint on rows that must naturally become overdue. This decision changes no money fields.

Deny raw authenticated/anonymous SELECT and DML on protected policy/control/coverage/period/audit records; expose only current-PDP owner-filtered projections or equally authorized views. Enable tenant RLS as defense in depth; both USING and WITH CHECK and all grants/functions/views must preserve the same resource boundaries. Privileged workers independently enforce them. Human identity comes from authenticated profile context; a system due cause is not the current assignee or a nil UUID inserted into a human FK. Callers cannot retarget tenant, actor, original, recipient, proof, policy or history through an allowed update. No cascading delete may erase required evidence; index actual tenant/home/state/due and source/member queries.

### REQ26-D14-R18 — Durable evaluation, races and idempotency

Commit input/period changes, fulfillment/disposition, work-home changes, due-review and required outbox/history effects atomically at their owning boundary. Where owners communicate asynchronously, use durable unique receipts and monotonic source revisions. Timer claims and wakeups are hints; current owner predicates are authority. Process early callbacks as early, stale generations as obsolete and duplicates as prior results. Reconciliation reads the same operation identity after a lost response. One current input/reply/Off/move/merge/No reply needed winner cannot be overwritten by a late old response or job.

Use indexed due queries and bounded fair batches through existing workflow orchestration. Current due/unknown views derive from durable state plus server As of time even during worker backlog. Do not schedule a browser timer as authority, scan every conversation each minute, hydrate all message bodies or create a task/email for each clock tick. Rebuilding a projection cannot append duplicate misses or trigger customer mail. The target module never calls Resend to repair a metric; P6 alone reconciles the original delivery.

### REQ26-D14-R19 — Daily list and conversation UX

Use one **Reply due** column/control showing the earliest applicable target in the visible current work item, neutral before due and restrained text/icon **Reply overdue** afterward. Exact local date/time is primary; a contextual relative label may supplement it. No green shield, On track claim or Due soon color threshold. Add **Reply due** sorting and **Overdue replies** filtering within existing inbox views; preserve All unfinished, unassigned, recovery and D8 visibility. Uncertain timing uses **Reply timing needs confirmation** with its conservative candidate due detail, not false met/missed status. A confirmed overdue obligation takes primary attention precedence over an earlier uncertain candidate; its filter membership must not disappear. Detail preserves the additional uncertainty. Conversely, a known future deadline cannot conceal an earlier possible deadline needing confirmation. This is one compact primary cue plus contextual detail, not a stack of routine badges.

For multiple scopes, **View reply targets** shows only authorized sources, correspondents, kind, target/calendar, original start, due and proof. Explain one deadline through **Why this time?** without requiring hover or technical IDs. Keep **Follow-up reminder** visibly distinct. Reaching a target creates a quiet durable review entry, not a toast/email avalanche. Preserve draft, scroll, selected row and focus across projection changes; ticks do not move an item under the pointer or auto-navigate. Narrow screens use the existing responsive detail pattern and keep source/target actions usable without a wide table. Use exact shared base-maia/Base UI components and semantic tokens.

### REQ26-D14-R20 — Configuration, disable and correction UX

Reuse the selected inbox's settings and existing calendar owner, with a compact summary, independent First/Next controls, explicit time basis and one sample due preview using the same server calculator. Publish no seeded hours, resolution rows, priority matrix or new policy builder. State that ordinary saves apply to new reply periods and pending targets keep their saved rules. Off has the separate explicit R03 scope review. A stale or unavailable impact count is not zero; restricted targets are not listed or inferred through counts. Show pending/saved/conflict states at the changed control and reconcile ambiguous results by operation identity.

Use **No reply needed** only from target detail/current work with its exact affected scope visible. Default the simple one-correspondent case without an unnecessary selection table; disclose additional scopes only when present. Explain **Marks the selected messages as needing no reply. The conversation and follow-up reminder stay in place** and preserve known promises/recovery guards. Current-state Undo/correction remains available where safely reversible; do not make an ephemeral toast the only recovery path. Settings, deadlines and outcomes must be accessible by keyboard/screen reader, at 200% zoom and on a 320-CSS-pixel screen, with visible focus, text not color alone and restrained announcements rather than minute-by-minute live-region updates.

### REQ26-D14-R21 — Live waiting view

The **Replies needing attention** section is a current, all-age authorized snapshot with an explicit server **As of** time, independent of a historical report date filter. Show waiting within target, overdue, timing unavailable/unconfirmed, and untargeted work as distinct facts. Ordinary inbox display can collapse them to the earliest owed cue, but drilldown cannot hide the other original scopes. Deferred/waiting/unassigned/transferred work remains discoverable; a recent-period filter must not remove an old overdue obligation. Counts and page results share the full authorized predicate before pagination. Offline/stale data is labelled and refreshed on reconnection; it cannot prove current on-time status or authorize offline consequential edits.

### REQ26-D14-R22 — Target results cohort and denominators

The primary historical target report is **Targets due in [period]**, using the period's frozen due instant in a half-open reporting interval and an explicit report timezone. Count finalized original reply-target instances, not current conversations or candidate splits. Separate First and Next, then show on time, replied late, still unanswered overdue, outcome/timing unknown, and ended/withdrawn exclusions. Pending targets not yet due belong in the live view; withdrawn/no-reply-needed targets retain their originally scheduled cohort for explanation. Mixed calendar policies cannot be relabelled using today's default calendar.

Attainment is **on-time assessed targets / all assessed targets due**, where assessed includes on-time, replied-late and confirmed unanswered-overdue misses. Unknowns and before-due exclusions are shown next to the denominator as counts; never silently display 100% coverage. Label **On time among assessed**, with **X of Y finalized targets assessed**. Additionally show **Potential targets — timing/applicability unconfirmed**: one deduplicated unresolved source/period unit when any valid candidate due instant can fall in the selected half-open interval. Keep this outside the finalized scored denominator and disclose uncertain cohort membership; never show complete coverage from finalized rows alone. Uncertain membership counts are non-additive across ranges it might occupy; combined totals deduplicate source/period identity rather than sum daily candidate counts. No reply needed or Off after a confirmed miss preserves the miss and records the later disposition; source-owned audited correction can revise mistaken eligibility/time. A late valid event can correct an earlier provisional interpretation with history. No data is —/Not enough measured data, not zero minutes or 100%. Do not average per-inbox percentages to produce a tenant total.

### REQ26-D14-R23 — Completed reply durations and workload context

The separate **Reply times** section is labelled **Waiting periods ended by a staff reply in [period]**. It is anchored to qualified actual completion/acceptance time and counts completed response periods, not emails or every request received in the period. Persistently explain **One reply can end several waits** and label the sample **N completed waits**. Show median and p90 with the measured sample count, separate First/Next and explicit time basis. Use exact timed, source-valid completions for numeric duration aggregates; accepted-but-only-bounded/uncertain timestamps are disclosed as excluded timing evidence, not invented exact values. Assign a non-exact acceptance to this completion cohort only if its entire qualified interval lies within the selected period; if an interval straddles a boundary, show one separate uncertain-cohort count/list wherever intersection is possible. Do not force it into a chosen day or double-count it as an exact sample. Preserve original start and bound calendar per period; do not compute service durations by filtering event dates or substituting the current default calendar. Do not pool elapsed-mode and service-hour durations in one unlabeled percentile. Genuine elapsed duration can be compared across completed waits; service-hour comparisons require each wait's qualified bound calendar, with missing-calendar cases disclosed separately.

Calculate the median conventionally (middle value; mean of middle two for even n) and p90 by nearest rank `ceil(0.9*n)` over ordered qualifying durations; round only display. Show a genuine zero service-time result correctly. Display missing/unanswered/unknown work alongside the duration section or through the always-visible live summary so favorable completed-response statistics do not hide abandoned work. Offer precise drilldowns and qualified exports of the same cohort/formula/snapshot, not a client-side body dump. Outcome/ending volumes, current backlog and reply-time statistics remain separate from donor satisfaction, resolution success or actual staff effort.

### REQ26-D14-R24 — Attribution and historical integrity

Current assignee/inbox filters are legitimate for current workload when labelled **Currently assigned/handled by**. They cannot rewrite the responding actor, original source, policy-at-start or custody-at-due dimensions. Record historical responsibility references and reply actor evidence under their own owners, including Shared and unavailable hydration without inventing a person. A response spanning several scoped obligations does not become several emails or hours of labor. Multi-tenant/CRM merges, source relinking, staff departure and calendar changes never rewrite past events or create duplicate authoritative state.

Historical source corrections append revision/cause/evidence; reports disclose the applied interpretation and As of/generated-at version. A previously generated export remains its captured snapshot, not silently edited history. Report access is evaluated currently; preserving attribution never preserves revoked access to private content. Do not introduce individual leaderboards, donation-weighted response performance or claims about staff productivity from queue assignment alone.

### REQ26-D14-R25 — CRM, owner work and messaging boundaries

Expose the same authorized target summary when staff open Support from a CRM record, with return location/filter/draft context preserved. Require the intersection of Support/source and CRM permissions for names, counts, dates, report rows and links. Related Party context, actual recipient, authenticated user, represented organization, reply correspondent, Support handler and CRM owner remain distinct. No target setting or overdue status grants access or mutates donor/Finance/care records. Actual business actions are initiated and audited by their owner; a target or a replied status cannot finish a refund, change a gift or close D11's task.

Target changes/reviews produce Support work/audit evidence, not a CRM communication event. P6 actual replies remain one event with actual recipient attribution under D9/D13. No automatic deadline email, in-product notification family or Resend template is introduced solely for D14. If an existing qualified recovery event applies, use its exact P17/P6 meaning; do not reopen the whole deferred SLA-notice family. D13's approved confirmation stays receipt-only and never includes these internal target values. AI may not classify a no-reply disposition, grade a reply or take a target-changing action in this scope.

### REQ26-D14-R26 — Failure, visibility and recovery

Distinguish policy/source/calendar unavailable, provider outcome unknown, delayed due evaluation, stale projection, denied access and current uncovered reply work. Fail closed on unauthorized mutation and fail visibly on missing clock evidence; ordinary intake and staff correspondence continue through their existing qualified paths. A worker outage must not hide due work in authorized queries. Reconcile input/reply/outbox gaps by original IDs and revisions, not by retrying a send or creating a new response period from now.

Grouped repair belongs to the exact source/calendar/delivery/projection owner. Known acceptance/delivery correction affects only the covered period and current relevant D3 recovery. Expired/purged provider artifacts remain under ADR0032 and cannot be revived for scoring. Off, current source correction or projection rebuild never roll back completed external work, cancel promised follow-up, restore stale assignment/status or remove an independently required review. Keep safe operational reasons available beyond a toast without logging bodies, raw recipient lists, sensitive CRM context or secrets.

### REQ26-D14-R27 — Scale, privacy and retention

Use server-side authorized summaries/joins and indexes for tenant/current home/period state/due, source contribution, policy lineage and actual member proof. Do not use the current full-conversation/all-message report fetch or a truncated 2,000-row client array as complete history/counts. Page stable IDs with deterministic tie-breaks and a consistent As of snapshot; bulk/export freezes the intended predicate and applies current read authorization. Derived caches are scoped by tenant/resource permission context and source/policy generations; clock-dependent results cannot remain falsely current after deadline or revocation.

No speculative new warehouse, global cache, search engine or sharding is required. Require query-plan/load proof with skewed tenants, mixed calendars, large backlog and records beyond 2,000; declare measured hardware/dataset/latency before making capacity claims. Bound jobs, exports and date-range calculations using qualified shared mechanisms rather than unbounded loops/body hydration. Retain body-free source/target/audit references under existing owner retention and restriction rules; no new indefinite donor-content archive, money fields or extra provider copy. Erasure/backup restore reapply current restrictions while preserving permitted aggregate/tombstone history without identity recreation.

### REQ26-D14-R28 — Migration, rollout and stop controls

Deploy qualified source/coverage/calendar/policy readers and additive data contracts before enabling writers. Inventory and fence the old SLA forms/collections, browser selectors, generic first_responded_at writers, parallel Support module and direct DML. Existing guessed policy numbers and due timestamps are legacy evidence, not reconstructed precise periods or automatically enabled settings. Unknown historical clocks remain labelled legacy/unscored; no historical success/miss or new target is fabricated. New targets start from eligible future periods after explicit configuration; intact known source facts remain available for accurately labelled reporting.

Canary by tenant/inbox after real authorization, clock, race, source/P6, topology, reporting and UX proof. Stop new target creation/effects independently of intake, human sending, current due visibility and delivery reconciliation. A damaged calculator/projection shows timing unavailable and qualified recovery; it does not silently declare goals met or freeze public promises. Rollback must keep compatible readers/repair for already-written periods, source coverage and due-review history; never restore a bypassing old writer or delete new evidence. Normal policy Off remains the R03 product operation, not a deployment rollback.

### REQ26-D14-R29 — Exact proof and traceability

Trace the selected A, every clause below, glossary and accepted ADR through implementation OpenSpec/owner contracts, design, tasks/tickets, implementation, outcome tests and release evidence. Explicitly admit the D3 due-review-with-preserved-reminder amendment, original/correspondent First/Next meaning, D10 projection and D12 exact work-home continuation. No current UI seed, source-only test, research oracle or passing document validator proves those runtime contracts. The proof matrix defines positive, negative, boundary, authorization, concurrency, migration, accessibility and Support-to-CRM outcomes.

### REQ26-D14-R30 — Completed scope and non-goals

This is the permanent scoped solution to the selected internal-target capability: configuration, current guidance, exact timing/coverage, repair, history/reporting and cross-surface continuity. It does not postpone a needed clock/ownership decision to an implementation agent. Physical names, index tuning and shared-component details can follow repository conventions without changing these invariants. Target hours are deliberately chosen by each tenant, not invented from a competitor or old fixture; absence of a universal default is a product decision, not unfinished research. No public SLA, business-action completion deadline, automated reminder campaign or unrelated product redesign is authorized.

### REQ26-D14-C001 — A small feature with clear meanings

The ordinary experience is one time beside the work: **Reply due today, 14:30**. Once needed, it becomes **Reply overdue · due 14:30**. There is no green On track shield, countdown animation or repeated warning. Time remaining proves neither progress nor coverage.

The donor continues normal email and sees no internal target. Staff's **Follow-up reminder** remains separate: it means when they intend to review/follow up, while **Reply due** comes from the inbox's timing policy. Resolving a conversation or completing Finance work is a different fact. The D13 automatic confirmation has no human reply credit and does not publish these targets.

Reuse Core's exact base-maia/Base UI components, spacing, typography, semantic tokens, existing list/detail layout and light/dark behavior. Do not introduce a new palette, animation language, card-heavy dashboard or another Support application. Beauty is a stable hierarchy with the right detail available on demand.

### REQ26-D14-C002 — Set up an inbox

In the selected inbox's existing settings, use **Reply targets** with this helper:

> Internal timing goals for your team. These do not send messages or promise a response time to requesters.

Start **Not configured**. Queues and follow-up reminders remain useful. Do not fill in the old 480/720-minute/five-day values or invent another industry-wide promise. Tenant administrators choose durations based on their actual coverage; no extra founder question is needed to prescribe a universal number.

This is a layout sketch, not executable input or selected durations. First and Next are independently optional; enabling the feature requires at least one valid duration. Each is a positive whole-minute value, with exact hours/minutes conversion and inline errors for invalid or unrepresentable values. Do not offer a days unit whose meaning changes with service hours. Provide accessible definitions:

- **First reply:** the reply expectation before human correspondence with that person/address has begun in the original conversation.
- **Next reply:** the expectation once that human exchange is underway, measured from the next input requiring a reply—not between two staff messages.

An already-accepted human outgoing initiation can establish Next for a later incoming message. A system confirmation or No reply needed does not. First/Next follows the logical human-send/input sequence recorded by Core, validated by actual acceptance; it does not mean a person already received or read the earlier email. When evidence is uncertain, the server supplies the qualified uncertainty state; the browser does not choose a different duration.

**Service hours** counts only the selected calendar's working intervals. **Elapsed time** counts continuously, including nights and weekends; do not call it 24/7 coverage. Show calendar name, actual zone and a concise schedule summary. Missing/loading/inaccessible/unqualified calendar are distinct and block Service hours, without silently changing the basis. View/Edit opens the authorized existing calendar surface and preserves the settings return context.

The **Example** preview uses the same qualified server calculator as real targets and synthetic input. Allow a sample receipt instant and show the exact resulting due time/zone. Include an outside-hours example when applicable. The preview is not a response promise, real work item or test email. Saving does not silently enroll older waiting work or change pending times.

Ordinary edits publish prospective revisions. Delayed input uses its applicable source-time revision or captured bundle, not whichever revision happens to be current when a worker runs. Truly pre-enable/Off input stays untargeted. This detail belongs in **How targets apply**, not a technical explanation on every form row.

### REQ26-D14-C003 — Turning targets off

Use a separately named action **Turn off [Inbox] reply targets**, with a concise consequence preview:

> Stops new targets and withdraws unfinished targets created by these settings, including conversations now handled in another inbox. Missed targets remain in reports. Conversations, assignments and follow-up reminders stay in place.

Show only permitted impact rows/counts. If cross-inbox detail cannot be disclosed, state the scope without a count or false zero. The operation is conditional and reconciled by its durable identity; a stale preview refreshes instead of silently applying a changed scope.

Because moved work can retain another inbox's target, an Off summary must be accurate:

> No new targets from this inbox. Existing targets from other inboxes may still apply.

Off withdraws target applicability, not the underlying need to reply. Re-enable does not resurrect old targets. Before-due withdrawal is a visible reporting exclusion; a confirmed miss already incurred remains. Mail already submitted remains real, and late acceptance is evaluated against the exact withdrawal cutoff rather than webhook arrival order.

### REQ26-D14-C004 — Daily inbox and detail

The sketch shows actual work state and target independently. A due-review transition may be pending during worker delay; do not display Open before its authoritative transition. The due query still surfaces the work and explains review is needed. Once committed, the ordinary status is Open.

The inbox list remains one row per current continuing work item. Its primary cue uses the earliest applicable authorized target, with attention precedence for a confirmed overdue obligation. An earlier uncertain candidate must not hide a different confirmed overdue target; details retain both facts. Conversely, a known future target cannot hide an earlier possible deadline. Use one primary cue and exceptional detail, not a badge for each participant.

Add **Reply due** sorting and **Overdue replies** filtering to existing views. Count inbox rows as conversations, not individual reply periods; a tooltip/helper can say **Conversations with overdue replies**. Filter membership checks all permitted underlying periods, not only whichever cue won display precedence. A **Timing needs confirmation** filter may overlap Overdue when different underlying obligations coexist; do not add the counts as disjoint totals. No historical date filter may remove old current overdue work.

**Why this time? / View reply targets** opens an accessible detail panel with:

- Who needs the reply, using permitted observed/source identity and qualified response route.
- The original message/source link and oldest uncovered receipt time.
- First/Next classification, configured duration, time basis and bound calendar/zone.
- Due time, actual current coverage and any acceptance uncertainty.
- An explanation of original policy/work-home lineage when work moved or continued elsewhere.

Do not expose raw IDs, profile rules or sensitive hidden-source counts in ordinary display. One person's reply deadline does not imply they are a unique CRM person; a church shared mailbox can represent several legitimate users. A reply to another participant does not clear their input. The server-owned source/audience review supplies coverage; the user is not forced through another modal on every Send.

### REQ26-D14-C005 — When the target is reached

Explain this once in setup help:

> When a reply target is reached, the conversation returns to Open for review. Its existing follow-up reminder is kept.

The durable detail/history wording is **Reply target reached — review needed**. This overrides deferral for visibility but preserves a valid later follow-up reminder. Ordinary explicitly selected Open still follows D3's clear-reminder behavior. Existing D7 coverage and D8 restrictions apply to the new Open work; no separate target escalation or new assignment rule is introduced.

Once staff review and choose a valid plan, the same overdue period does not repeatedly reopen work. Its overdue result remains until response/disposition; new independent input or another due period can create review normally. There are no per-target email alerts, reminder campaigns, repeated toasts or minute-by-minute screen-reader announcements. Current recovery remains discoverable through existing qualified surfaces.

### REQ26-D14-C006 — Replies, uncertainty and No reply needed

After **Send reply**, show the real P6 state. A queued draft or a request awaiting provider evidence cannot become a successful reply-time result. A properly accepted human reply can satisfy its exact reviewed recipients/input scopes; it does not prove mailbox delivery, reading, resolution or helpfulness. A later bounce remains prominent as current delivery recovery without erasing a genuine earlier submission time.

If a new input arrives after the reply's coverage was frozen, it stays owed. If prior acceptance changes whether its target is First or Next, show **Reply timing needs confirmation** and the earliest applicable possible deadline. Do not hide a possibly imminent Next target behind a longer First target. The existing source/delivery repair flow owns the uncertainty; no timer retry sends another email. When accepted-response coverage is confirmed, the reply obligation is fulfilled even if its exact historical timing cannot yet be scored. Show that uncertainty in outcome/report detail; do not keep telling staff to reply or reopen work merely to calculate a score.

For messages that genuinely need no reply, use **No reply needed** on the exact current reviewed response scope. This action remains meaningful even when targets are Off. Copy:

> Marks these messages as needing no reply. The conversation and follow-up reminder stay in place.

Use “this message” for a single contribution and show additional scopes only when necessary. It does not settle a known promised reply or unreviewed recovery. Partial selection preserves uncovered older/newer input. When a valid Resolve already ends all remaining response work, do not force a separate No reply needed click.

Persistent **Undo no reply needed** corrects only the still-current mistaken disposition for still-unfulfilled input, with current authorization and source fences. Preserve original age/policy; reconcile current work instead of restoring an old status/reminder snapshot. Already-fulfilled input is unchanged, newer input remains separate, and a separately disabled target remains disabled. Any resulting historical correction/miss is explicit. A toast may offer convenience, but is not the only correction path.

### REQ26-D14-C007 — Reporting without misleading scores

Reuse existing Support Reports and its Inbox/Overview structure, with **Reply timeliness** as a focused section. Dates, filters and definitions belong beside the data; do not add a separate reporting application. Each section has a different, explicit unit:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Section                                                  | Date anchor and unit                                                                                                                  | What it shows                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Replies needing attention**                            | Current, all ages; server **As of** time. Work-list rows/counts are current conversations, with underlying waits in detail.           | Waiting, confirmed overdue, evidence/timing problems and untargeted response work. Historical date selection does not hide this backlog.                 |
| **Targets due in [period]**                              | Frozen target due instant in a half-open interval, displayed in the selected report zone. Unit: finalized reply-target instances.     | First/Next on-time, replied-late, confirmed unanswered-overdue misses, outcome-unknown and ended/withdrawn exclusions.                                   |
| **Potential targets — timing/applicability unconfirmed** | A valid candidate due can intersect the selected period. Unit: deduplicated unresolved source/period, outside the scored denominator. | Prevents uncertainty or candidate splits disappearing from coverage; does not claim a finalized target or a miss.                                        |
| **Reply times**                                          | **Waiting periods ended by a staff reply in [period]**. Unit: completed waits, not emails.                                            | Median/p90, exact measured sample count, First/Next and chosen time basis, plus excluded/unconfirmed timing counts. **One reply can end several waits.** |

For target attainment use **On time among assessed** and **X of Y finalized targets assessed**. Show unknowns/exclusions/potential targets beside that coverage. On-time numerator and assessed denominator are explicit; a confirmed still-unanswered miss belongs in the denominator. Before-due No reply needed/Off is excluded rather than “met”; a known post-due miss remains despite later cleanup. Source-owner correction is visible history. No data displays **—**, never 0 minutes or 100%.

For duration charts, show **N completed waits** and the exact-timed sample count. A bounded acceptance interval that straddles the selected period is listed under **Completion period uncertain**, outside exact samples; do not force it into a day. Uncertain cohort counts are not additive across periods that the same interval might occupy; totals deduplicate source/period IDs. Median/p90 uses the specified formula and bound clock evidence, never a current default-calendar recomputation. Do not pool elapsed and service-hour durations into a misleading unlabeled percentile. Elapsed comparisons can use genuine elapsed start/end; service-hour results require each wait's qualified bound calendar and disclose missing-calendar exclusions.

Keep completed-duration charts next to a link/summary of outstanding work. A low median does not mean an old unanswered request disappeared. Avoid rankings or a score implying staff effort, donor satisfaction or successful resolution. Label **Currently assigned/handled by** separately from historical responding actor and policy-at-start/custody-at-due dimensions. A transferred conversation does not rewrite who sent the earlier reply.

Every chart/number drills into the same authorized source-backed cohort. Export uses that same snapshot/definitions and current download authorization, with no hidden message-body export. Counts, bars, tables and filtered results must agree; no browser aggregation of a capped conversation list or message payload download.

### REQ26-D14-C008 — CRM and other owner surfaces

When staff open a conversation from a permitted CRM record, show the same Reply due/overdue/uncertain projection and preserve their record/filter/draft location on return. Only actually permitted source and CRM details appear. A Related Party does not automatically receive email or become the reply correspondent; target changes do not create CRM interactions. P6 retains the actual reply once.

A Finance task can remain open after a timely Support update. A receipt/refund/account change can finish without a human Support reply. Each owner validates, authorizes and records its own action; staff deliberately communicate or mark no reply needed based on the actual current obligation. Internal targets never become donor-facing business completion promises.

### REQ26-D14-C009 — Accessibility, mobile and stability proof

Use named semantic controls, visible focus, sufficient contrast and text/icon meaning. All target detail and definitions must work without hover. At 320 CSS pixels and 200% zoom, preserve the selected conversation, useful due information and accessible action labels without horizontal mandatory tables. RTL, long international names, locale-specific dates and timezone abbreviations must not truncate the essential date or hide the source identity.

Ticking time may refresh display but must not reorder a row beneath a pointer, move keyboard focus or announce every minute. Explicit refresh/filter/sort follows established stable-selection behavior. Low-bandwidth/offline data shows its As of/stale status; reconnect revalidates current permissions and state. A pending action remains pending until its durable outcome is known; a later old response cannot replace a newer result.

The required scenarios are D14-P01–P55. The source probe and calendar oracle inform them but are not browser, accessibility, provider or ministry usability proof.

## D14 — Independently verifiable acceptance criteria

### AC26-D14-P01

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Off/unconfigured starts with no active targets or seeded hours; existing queues/reminders work. Enable First only, Next only or both with deliberate durations and explicit basis.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P02

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Zero, negative, nonfinite, fractional-minute, ambiguous days and overflow inputs reject with preserved fields; hours/minutes conversion is exact.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P03

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Service hours requires a qualified permitted calendar; absent/unavailable calendar never becomes elapsed mode or 24/7 staffing.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P04

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

New policy generation cannot adopt earlier received/unbound work; repeat processing and re-enable cannot target the same untargeted current burst. Ordinary edits preserve pending targets.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P05

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Off withdraws only exact configuration-family pending targets, including transferred homes; scope/count disclosure respects PDP. Known misses persist and other policies' targets remain.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P06

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Calendar preview and production computation agree for local zones, weekends, holidays, overnight split, overlaps, DST gap and repeated short intervals; compare all eight research fixtures independently.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P07

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Due equality and reply equality use full precision correctly; display rounding/zone changes never change the instant or score. Actual zero service duration differs from no data.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P08

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Calendar/tzdb edits leave pending/historical instants unchanged; a proved calculation defect uses audited correction with before/after evidence, no send or stale-state restoration.

Stories: US26-D14-01. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R01, REQ26-D14-R02, REQ26-D14-R03, REQ26-D14-R04, REQ26-D14-R05, REQ26-D14-R20.

### AC26-D14-P09

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Duplicate/automated/quarantined/unrelated input creates no new human reply period; qualified late release preserves original source age and separately exposes intake delay.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P10

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Same-correspondent burst keeps oldest unanswered start; a second active correspondent gets their own full target. Passive CC and same-Party association do not create or merge targets.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P11

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

First/Next is exact original/correspondent history: no-reply ending does not fabricate first response; accepted staff-origin initiation establishes prior correspondence for later work without satisfying it.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P12

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Actual human reply to B cannot clear A; a group reply covers only reviewed actual accepted members. Reply-to/route correction preserves age and does not use CRM matching as authority.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P13

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Unseen source/recipient/topology change blocks stale coverage under existing send review; target logic never adds recipients, bypasses collision or requires a redundant normal send modal.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P14

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Input after frozen send coverage stays owed. Acceptance closes only covered oldest work and creates the proper original-time successor; definite rejection preserves older debt/deadline.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P15

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

First=24h/Next=1h, pending send at 09:50/new input 09:51 exposes possible10:51 deadline as unscored uncertainty; no tomorrow-only hidden target. Also test First disabled/Next enabled.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P16

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Multiple pending sends, partial/non-prefix coverage and late duplicate proof cannot double-count completion, consume newer input or overwrite a newer period generation.

Stories: US26-D14-02. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R06, REQ26-D14-R07, REQ26-D14-R08, REQ26-D14-R10.

### AC26-D14-P17

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Draft/queued/automatic/internal-note/status/task events earn no human reply credit. Genuine human progress or clarification may count without resolution. No AI/body-length classifier decides semantic quality.

Stories: US26-D14-03. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R09, REQ26-D14-R11.

### AC26-D14-P18

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Exact P6 acceptance time scores correctly. Bounded intervals wholly before/after/straddling due yield on-time/late/unknown; earlier ambiguity and definite rejection alter bounds correctly.

Stories: US26-D14-03. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R09, REQ26-D14-R11.

### AC26-D14-P19

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

An accepted retry is never backdated to its first HTTP attempt; delayed webhook receipt uses qualified source occurrence time, not current worker time.

Stories: US26-D14-03. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R09, REQ26-D14-R11.

### AC26-D14-P20

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Later true bounce preserves submission-time fact and opens relevant D3 recovery; correction to pre-send suppression/wrong member revises false fulfillment with evidence. No automatic Resend replay.

Stories: US26-D14-03. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R09, REQ26-D14-R11.

### AC26-D14-P21

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

No reply needed applies only to exact reviewed contributions and respects known reply promises/recovery. It preserves work/reminder/owner action and is never a human reply or met target.

Stories: US26-D14-03. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R09, REQ26-D14-R11.

### AC26-D14-P22

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

No reply needed/Off before due are explicit exclusions; after a confirmed miss the miss remains. Unknown outcome is not mislabelled a known miss; source-owned correction remains auditable.

Stories: US26-D14-03. Requirements: REQ26-D14-R09, REQ26-D14-R11.

### AC26-D14-P23

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Eligible Resolve ends only no-longer-owed periods in the same command; No response/continued/admin reasons retain distinct meanings. Transferred obligations are not canceled by A ending.
