Stories: US26-D16-05. Requirements: REQ26-D16-R19, REQ26-D16-R20, REQ26-D16-R21, REQ26-D16-R22, REQ26-D16-R23, REQ26-D16-R24.

### AC26-D16-P38

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Mixed-version rollout/backfill and legacy representation inventory prove every enabled path conforms before tenant activation.

Stories: US26-D16-05. Requirements: REQ26-D16-R19, REQ26-D16-R20, REQ26-D16-R21, REQ26-D16-R22, REQ26-D16-R23, REQ26-D16-R24.

### AC26-D16-P39

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

No unrelated CRM/task mutation, automatic scanner, PDF editor, reveal archive, bulk eraser or replacement notification platform is introduced.

Stories: US26-D16-05. Requirements: REQ26-D16-R19, REQ26-D16-R20, REQ26-D16-R21, REQ26-D16-R22, REQ26-D16-R23, REQ26-D16-R24.

### AC26-D16-P40

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Applicable rights/hold/records/provider/backup evidence and deadlines are signed off by actual owners; routine redaction cannot close broader duties.

Stories: US26-D16-05. Requirements: REQ26-D16-R19, REQ26-D16-R20, REQ26-D16-R21, REQ26-D16-R22, REQ26-D16-R23, REQ26-D16-R24.

## D16 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D16-O01

**Signal and threshold:** Any verified post-restriction unauthorized content read/egress or resurrected payload: threshold 1

**Owner:** Security incident owner + affected platform owner

**Response:** Contain the affected path immediately, preserve body-free evidence, disable unsafe release and investigate/repair before re-enable.

### OP26-D16-O02

**Signal and threshold:** Active-copy cleanup unresolved for 15 elapsed minutes or 3 consecutive failed attempts, whichever comes first

**Owner:** Support engineering on-call

**Response:** Keep restriction; inspect scoped owner result, retry/reconcile safely, escalate to the failing representation owner. No customer/follower blast.

### OP26-D16-O03

**Signal and threshold:** Deferred provider/backup obligation reaches its recorded disposal deadline without evidence: threshold 1

**Owner:** Provider/records owner

**Response:** Escalate the contractual/legal exception immediately, retain restriction, obtain evidence or approved corrective response; never silently extend deadline.

### OP26-D16-O04

**Signal and threshold:** Restricted preservation/unknown-policy item lacks an accountable owner: threshold 1; assigned item misses its recorded review date: threshold 1

**Owner:** Tenant records/privacy administrator

**Response:** Assign qualified custody promptly or resolve the check; review scope/release through owner authority. Do not auto-reveal or auto-erase.

### OP26-D16-O05

**Signal and threshold:** Missing source-revision barrier in restore/rollout qualification: threshold 1 failed check

**Owner:** Database/platform release owner

**Response:** Block restore activation or rollout; correct barrier/compatibility and rerun the failed proof.

### OP26-D16-O06

**Signal and threshold:** Cleanup backlog exceeds measured supported capacity, or p95 command latency exceeds the published release budget for 15 minutes

**Owner:** Support/platform operations owner

**Response:** Apply per-tenant backpressure, investigate capacity regression, preserve intake and restriction; adjust capacity only after measured proof.

## D17 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D17-R01 — Necessity, alternatives and product boundary

A is the chosen ordinary model: preserve context while staff handle the request, then perform predictable disposal without a recurring approval queue for every ordinary item. B, qualified review before routine disposal, is the strongest conservative alternative where continuing value is routinely uncertain, but creates recurrent workload. C, individual message-age expiry during active work, bounds old content more directly but can fragment a legitimate conversation. Neither vendor availability nor an illustrative ministry scenario establishes measured demand, frequency or satisfaction gains.

Support remains a surface within Asym. D17 does not create a second CRM, organization-wide records manager, scanner, public message archive, knowledge base, automatic summary-before-delete feature or enterprise rule builder. It settles ordinary Support retention and its required integration, not a universal time period for all Asym data.

### REQ26-D17-R02 — One finite tenant default

Provide one tenant-level **Support content retention** policy for ordinary Support bodies, published note content and Support-owned attachment occurrences. No ordinary per-inbox, per-person, per-conversation Never switch, separate attachment clock or arbitrary conditions builder at launch. A different legally governed source class or official artifact keeps its own actual owner policy; it is not an implicit inbox override. Routing, team membership, related Parties and merge topology cannot select a more lenient policy.

The duration field is blank until configured: positive whole-number quantity plus an explicit Days, Months or Years unit. No guessed recommended period, forever, zero, negative, fractional, NaN or infinity. Reject quantities that cannot be represented exactly in the bounded integer contract or whose calculated deadlines overflow the authoritative timestamp type; UI and API share these bounds. The approved owner policy must substantiate the duration and comply with applicable maximums/requirements. This is a maximum ordinary post-purpose content lifetime, not a guaranteed minimum or an extension of shorter P6/P17/source limits.

Live activation of this retention capability requires a qualified finite policy and actual owner inventory. Missing legacy configuration is an owned migration/custody exception, not proof of compliance or permission to lose new intake. Preserve D1 recoverable intake while the responsible owner resolves it; do not silently disconnect a working inbox or auto-delete unclassified history.

### REQ26-D17-R03 — Policy authority without transcript access

Use Core's current tenant administration capabilities for retention policy management and a separately qualified complete, body-free policy-impact view. The actor, tenant, authorization and activation time derive from trusted server context. Ordinary Support assignees/followers, CRM owners and people with redaction permission do not automatically receive policy publication authority.

A policy administrator may be authorized to govern the whole declared tenant Support scope without reading every transcript. Such authority must be explicit, and aggregate impact access must be qualified as its own administrative purpose. Samples and drill-downs still require current source permission. Never disclose hidden names, subjects, Parties, legal matters or filenames to make an impact preview convenient. A partial personal inbox view cannot be represented as a complete tenant preview. Privileged automation acts as the source owner under the approved policy, not by impersonating the publishing administrator or treating their past body access as permanent authorization.

### REQ26-D17-R04 — Stable original content and active-purpose eligibility

Retirement binds a bounded content generation/frontier of one original Support source. It never deletes a changing merged-root query result or the entire conversation row. A generation covers all Support-owned content admitted through that frontier, including automatic confirmations and generated/system-note content and their files/representations, with original identities and monotonic admission ordering. Human content is the limited renewal class, not the only content subject to expiry. Typed content-free control facts retain their separate policy. Pre-qualified intake/quarantine material remains with its actual owner and shorter limits. A generation is not a new CRM person or necessarily a new conversation each time content expires.

Normal eligibility requires ended Support work plus absence of a qualified continuing Support need for that original content. D3 Open and both Waiting categories remain unfinished. D10 merged-away status does not prove finished purpose while the duplicate-work component still handles the issue. D12 Continued endings and D11 delegated work require their exact source-interest/obligation checks. A Finance task merely existing, a peer-related conversation, Party link, follower or citation is neither an indefinite hold nor disposal authority. Retain only the explicit source scope genuinely needed by ongoing work; no recursive whole-CRM retention graph.

### REQ26-D17-R05 — Precise inactivity anchor

For an unexpired content generation, the ordinary anchor is the later of its latest genuine relevant Support-purpose ending and its latest first durable admission of native human content. Count only qualified human incoming content becoming Support-ready, a human reply admitted for sending through the qualified Core command, and a newly published human internal note. Count the event once. Draft typing, unsent preparation alone, automatic confirmations, generated/system notes, note edits, redaction, expiry, delivery callbacks, imports of duplicates, reads, assignments, labels, links, merge/Undo and repeat identical Resolve do not move the anchor.

Do not wait for or use P6 provider acceptance as the retention activity clock: deliberately admitted reply content can exist while delivery is unknown. P6 actual send/delivery evidence stays separate and truthful. Provider/email Date, backdated user text and worker execution time cannot replace first qualified source admission. A genuinely new human note on ended work is new content and updates inactivity; no AI semantic test tries to decide whether it was meaningful. Oldest-content purpose review and mandatory owner ceilings address repeated chatter retaining older context.

If continuing purpose ends later, record that real ending once and use its time; repeated status commands are no-ops for this clock. A status-only correction or reopen–resolve cycle without a new qualified purpose preserves the prior anchor; mechanically cycling status is not new work evidence. If note editing is supported, saving edits keeps that content's existing deadline and must not imply a renewed lifetime. Legacy dates that cannot prove the anchor remain explicitly unknown and require bounded reconciliation, not created_at guessing, a fresh retention lifetime on migration or immediate destruction.

### REQ26-D17-R06 — Duration arithmetic and displayed dates

Compute from immutable UTC instants with explicit duration semantics. Days mean elapsed 24-hour days added on the instant timeline, including across daylight-saving changes. Months and Years use the policy's frozen IANA timezone, initially taken from the tenant setting and visibly reviewed at activation. Convert the original anchor to that zone, add the whole calendar quantity directly, preserve local time-of-day and clamp an unavailable destination day to that month's last day. Years equals twelve calendar months, not 365 elapsed days. Always calculate directly from the anchor, not by repeatedly adding one month. Thus 31 January in the policy timezone plus two months ends on 31 March in that timezone; 29 February plus one year ends on 28 February in a non-leap year.

Resolve a nonexistent destination local time by shifting forward by the gap; choose the earlier instant if the destination local time occurs twice. Requalify the shared D14 timezone/calculation primitives for these exact calendar operations; business-hours arithmetic alone is not proof. Test the behavior explicitly rather than assuming a library name or its default offset preference. No Temporal dependency or new calendar platform is mandated.

Store quantity/unit, frozen zone, timezone-data/calculator evidence, policy revision, authoritative anchor and materialized UTC deadline. Display exact localized examples and the policy calendar zone. Existing materialized deadlines remain authoritative across timezone-data upgrades; replay/restore must retain sufficient pins/evidence or use the recorded results, not silently recalculate under a new runtime. Adopting another tenant zone or calculator interpretation is an explicit reviewed policy revision with the same E/d rules; viewer or unrelated tenant setting changes do not move deadlines. Use the same qualified arithmetic for purpose-review intervals. Business hours, holidays and staffing calendars do not pause retention. Earlier actual owner obligations may end availability sooner; this policy cannot override them.

### REQ26-D17-R07 — Purpose review for long-lived content

Use the same configured interval to require an accountable review when the oldest ordinarily available, unexpired content in the current generation has reached that age while ongoing purpose prevents ordinary expiry or repeated new content keeps renewing the inactivity anchor. Exclude already-expired bytes held under D16 restricted custody. This oldest-content review clock is independent of labels, new chatter, reopening loops and last_updated. No new arbitrary secondary period is required.

Maintain one source-scoped review obligation, grouped through existing staff work/records capabilities. The qualified owner records a current continuing need and next review no later than the interval added directly to that review's trusted admission instant, ends actual work when appropriate, or places required evidence with its proper records owner. Policy shortening reevaluates pending reviews without resetting oldest-content age; newly due reviews become due at E. Lengthening cannot erase a prior missed-review fact. A shorter actual owner deadline/review rule wins. Overdue review produces owned attention; it does not auto-Resolve, fabricate lack of need, silently erase active evidence or grant indefinite retention. A mere self-assigned Never/Keep switch is unavailable. Purpose decisions must be attributable and source-specific without pasting the content into the review task.

### REQ26-D17-R08 — Draft, review and publish policy

Editing produces an inert draft. **Review changes** obtains a server-calculated impact snapshot for the exact tenant scope, candidate duration/calendar basis, current active policy revision and declared immediate effective-time semantics. Display old/new values and any zone/calculator-basis change, existing-plus-future applicability, the fact that some existing content can expire immediately, counts with exact units, exclusions/unknown classes and calculation time. Use original histories, native messages (including source-owned system content) and attachment occurrences as distinct units; current merged rows and unique physical blobs are different units.

The final **Activate policy** or **Apply changes** is approval of that explicit ongoing rule and complete authorized scope, not a per-message selection manifest. Counts are a dated snapshot and may change as work changes; a changing count alone is not a new scope. Revalidate actual eligibility at execution. Policy, scope, authority, calculation semantics or omitted legacy-class changes require fresh review; a failed/incomplete calculation is not zero. No all-target-ID manifest or body download is required just to publish a policy. For unsafe/unclassified scope, block that scope's destructive activation and assign the exception rather than silently omit it.

### REQ26-D17-R09 — Immediate effective time and existing history

One confirmed publication atomically records an immutable policy version, trusted actor, complete scope, prior-version comparison and authoritative effective instant E. It applies to existing and future **unexpired** ordinary content in that scope; this is stated before confirmation. There is no hidden trash period, automatic seven-day extension, undocumented grandfathering or silent prospective-only exclusion. Content newly overdue under activation/shortening expires at E, never retroactively before the policy existed.

A stale concurrent settings edit conflicts rather than overwrites another published revision. Exact retry returns the original activation receipt and current status. A timeout is reconciled, not resubmitted as a new policy. Old revisions remain immutable evidence. Metadata display may update, but changing a period means publishing a new version. Setting the same effective policy again is a no-op, not a retention reset.

### REQ26-D17-R10 — Policy changes cannot reverse elapsed authority

Let d be the source's already-authoritative expiry deadline. An authorized policy change or qualifying new work admitted at E strictly before d may affect future eligibility/deadline. At E equal to or after d, the old content has expired even if no worker has yet nulled a body or deleted an object. Process that expired frontier before admitting new content or applying an extension; it cannot be rescued by worker lag, policy lengthening, reopening, an inbox move or Undo.

Conversely, an extension validly effective before d must be honored even when a due-date projection still contains the old deadline. A stale worker must not destroy content using the old version. Evaluate policy-version history, source events and purpose state at the relevant authority boundary; a current-value-only setting plus best-effort mass row updates is insufficient. Current source authority may be computed lazily or projected, but every read/mutation/disposal must qualify it against the actual effective revisions. No giant cross-tenant transaction is required.

### REQ26-D17-R11 — Bounded pause and operational controls

Provide an exceptional **Pause future expiry until…** to a qualified policy owner, with a finite end instant, content-free reason and impact review. It is an explicit bounded policy revision and cannot override an earlier mandatory disposal or owner safety ceiling. It affects only content not already expired. Normal source access restrictions, accepted cleanup obligations, required physical disposal and incident response continue. There is no permanent Off/Never mode for an active retention policy.

At the approved pause end, recompute against original anchors and current work: still-eligible overdue content expires then, not one new full interval later. The pause review explains this automatic resumption and the expected backlog. An earlier deliberate Resume is a reviewed policy change. Extending a pause requires current authority and another finite reviewed decision; it is not a silent scheduler retry. An infrastructure kill switch that stops work execution is different: it does not extend logical content authority, conceal deadline failures or disable source/restore barriers.

### REQ26-D17-R12 — Logical expiry before physical cleanup

At the effective deadline, ordinary read, search-membership, download, preparation, export and new dispatch authority for that expired frontier ends. Due workers materialize one content-free expiry receipt, current source restriction and identifier-only owner cleanup obligations through a guarded source transaction. Reads and competing writes also enforce elapsed authority when workers lag. Missing owner/revision proof fails closed for affected content without declaring physical deletion complete.

Use a unique durable effect identity tied to tenant, original source and expired content generation/frontier, not policy revision alone or a cron run. Duplicate/replayed jobs reconcile the same effect and cannot sweep in messages admitted after the frontier. Later automatic/system content cannot create a fresh retention interval on an already-ended expired source: apply its existing source cutoff or independently qualified owner class, retaining only permitted typed facts when payload authority is absent. Atomically preserve expiry/policy evidence and D16 restriction/outbox obligations; perform external cleanup outside the transaction. A transaction failure, lost response or partial downstream failure has a truthful recoverable result. Never restore ordinary content because cleanup failed.

### REQ26-D17-R13 — Exact retained-data allowlist

The data inventory is normative contract. Expire Support-owned body text/HTML/editor data, private-note bodies, obsolete source titles/subjects/snippets/summaries, selected-generation file appearances and derived text, unsafe filename/URL/header/address snapshots, parsed intake/MIME copies and affected managed previews/exports. Unknown or free-form fields are content until their owner explicitly classifies and permits a narrower retained fact. No automatic summary or export-before-delete recreates the archive.

Preserve only separately permitted typed facts/control: original/message identities, source lineage/frontiers, actual communication channel/direction/time/outcome and authority references, genuine work transitions, D14 coverage/timing/uncertainty, qualified Party relevance and necessary routing/dedupe/restore barriers. Each has an owner, purpose, access rule and actual retention/anonymization horizon. A skeleton or body-free fact is still potentially identifying; neither is forever by default. Retained structural fields must not secretly contain arbitrary user-authored strings.

Never implement expiry as DELETE conversation or inbox. Current cascades can destroy messages, assignment history and audit. Keep the minimal factual skeleton only while justified; later owner-authorized retirement handles its dependencies and obligations safely. No new money column, amount precision change, CRM synchronization or financial mutation is introduced.

### REQ26-D17-R14 — CRM continuity and independent records

D9 remains the discovery model. Where a qualified relevance/correspondence basis and current joint authorization survive, CRM Communications/All can show one source-backed conversation with a neutral reference/title, permitted event/outcome facts and **Content expired under your retention policy**. Unfinished Overview remains about current work; a later reopened source can appear there with its new content and a truthful older-expiry marker. No duplicated transcript, new CRM Activity communication, last-contact update or extra ownership link is generated by expiry.

If the owner removes the last lawful discovery basis, withdraw the normal CRM row/count rather than promote a service-only tombstone into access authority. Current Party identity and relationships remain with CRM; no expired email rematching creates historical correspondence. Giving records, official receipt/statement facts, independent notes/tasks and member-care records keep their owners and permissions. Source content expiry neither deletes those records nor implies their work succeeded. A shared physical file remains under a valid independent owner, but its expired Support link cannot become a backdoor to that copy. Navigate to the owner and reauthorize there.

### REQ26-D17-R15 — Safe late mail and expired reply context

Retain the narrow tenant/source routing and deduplication control justified by its approved horizon separately from raw readable headers and addresses. A Message-ID can itself contain personal text; qualify an opaque or appropriately protected exact-equality representation and key lifecycle. Never lower-case arbitrary identifiers, use sender-plus-subject matching, choose the first ambiguous result, or rematch old content against today's CRM email. D1's qualified routing and quarantine rules govern.

A verified duplicate of expired input remains duplicate without body rehydration. Genuine new admitted input uses its own current authorization and a new content frontier; it may continue the same still-qualified original/root while old content stays unavailable. Missing lawful correlation follows the ordinary new-input path; ambiguity follows established review/quarantine. No junk Party is created.

An old-message **Reply/Reply all** action cannot reconstruct an expired audience from current CRM details, participant unions or cached drafts. Explain that the old reply context is unavailable. A genuinely new incoming message supplies its own D2-qualified audience; deliberate new outbound conversation uses D12/current recipient review. This preserves serviceability without turning a retained shell into an address book.

### REQ26-D17-R16 — Merge, continuation and content generations

D10 merge/Undo operates on current structural/work state while each original retains its own content frontier and expiry. Merging never restarts a period or makes a discarded source automatically eligible. A current shared issue can provide an actual purpose dependency; ending/releasing it updates the appropriate original's purpose evidence once. Undo after expiry cannot return old payload, titles, files, tokens or previews.

D11/D12 explicit source interests and transferred reply obligations may preserve a real current need before expiry. Their closure changes eligibility only where that actual dependency governed the source. A reference removal does not complete independent work; an unrelated task's Done state does not prove Support is finished. Native content newly written on continuing B does not become new native content on A merely because A is linked. If B actually needed A's original evidence, its qualified source-purpose interest—not copied text or topology alone—governs that dependency. Owner-record preservation stays distinct.

### REQ26-D17-R17 — Holds, required records and actual legal limits

A legal/records hold can block physical destruction of necessary still-existing bytes, but does not by itself extend ordinary Support visibility. At ordinary expiry, retained required material moves/remains under qualified restricted custody with safe status; it is not labelled erased and has no ordinary Reveal. A genuine ongoing Support purpose is evaluated separately. Unknown preservation checks block destruction and create an owned exception; they do not authorize unlimited ordinary access or a made-up legal conclusion.

Hold/admission/disposal transitions share current owner guards. A valid hold arriving after logical expiry but before physical disposal can preserve remaining bytes without restoring ordinary use. It cannot recover bytes already destroyed. Before deleting a file that is the sole required record, qualify its proper owner custody; do not assume every receipt-related attachment must be kept or that every attachment is disposable.

Follow D16's US applicability assessment and current primary evidence. No claim that all nonprofits are CCPA-covered/exempt, every private health sentence is HIPAA, every email must be kept seven years, or ordinary expiry completes a formal rights request/incident response. Actual notice, contract, preservation and deletion duties remain owner-qualified. Policy lengthening cannot silently authorize an incompatible new use or override a promised/legal limit. The finite tenant field is configured from those facts; no missing numeric global default remains to be guessed.

### REQ26-D17-R18 — P6, P17, reports and following

D17 supplies a narrow **automatic original-frontier expiry intent** with system source-owner authority and policy/purpose/hold evidence. It invokes D16's restriction and owner cleanup contracts. It does not broaden D16's one-message human selection command, impersonate staff or introduce generic Phase6 pruning/DSAR jobs. This explicit shared-owner conformance extension must be captured before implementation activation; the reserved generic platform stays reserved.

Preserve P6's actual body-free occurrences and D14's permitted timing/coverage outcomes. Expiry is not a reply, successful resolution, cancelled obligation or reason to remove an overdue result. Where an owner legitimately retires factual evidence, reporting must show reduced availability/coverage honestly, not silently improve success rates. New durable P17-governed P6 events cannot restore the superseded raw recipient_email field. Historical attribution means permitted owner evidence, not raw endpoint snapshots forever.

Routine expiry sends no requester/follower email and creates no ordinary unread or last-contact event. D15 following intent may continue for future allowed activity on the retained original; only expired contributions/previews/unsent authority become unavailable. Source/identity retirement remains D15's separate ending condition. Current duty/failure/purpose-review attention uses the existing owner and P17 capabilities. Any separately authorized external response uses Email Studio/P6 Resend; no expiry email template or new sender is added because no routine expiry email is selected.

### REQ26-D17-R19 — Prepared material and the send race

Existing source-derived quotes, files, destinations and prepared material lose applicable read/decrypt/send authority when their source frontier expires. Preserve unrelated authored work where it can be separated safely; otherwise require clean current review. Never silently replace frozen bytes or submit a cleaned message on the user's behalf. A later expired-source autosave cannot repopulate the old quote.

P6 `dispatching` remains the I/O boundary. Source expiry before new dispatch admission blocks the attempt; a send authorized earlier may already be in flight/accepted/unknown. Preserve that evidence without a recall claim; deny later payload-bearing retries after the source stop. ADR0032 sealed envelopes cannot be split/rerendered/rekeyed, including when only one member's source expired. Fresh review alone cannot justify replacing an accepted or indeterminate send. Preserve the existing 24-hour prepared execution-material purge rule after authority removal and any earlier owner deadline; the tenant retention period never extends it.

### REQ26-D17-R20 — Database, RLS and immutable evidence

Use tenant-aware foreign keys/cardinality for policy revisions, current activation, original source, content generation, native messages/files, source-purpose interests, expiry receipts and owner cleanup effects. At most one effective default policy revision per tenant at any instant; publication uses expected revision and a non-overlapping effective history. Activated version, source identity/frontier and attributed outcome evidence are immutable except for separately recorded owner corrections. Use timezone-aware instants, exact integer durations and validated closed unit/state values.

Ordinary database roles cannot publish policy, change tenant/source/generation, fabricate actor or expiry/hold state, restore expired content or delete protected evidence through generic UPDATE/DELETE. Verify both USING and WITH CHECK, effective permissive policy combinations, grants, views/RPC/function execution and search_path, storage policies and service-role parity. A permitted row cannot be transformed into a forbidden source/tenant/private-public state. Background jobs carry narrow tenant/source effect authority; caller IDs and old policy-admin permissions are not trust roots.

Preserve D16 expiry/restore barriers against incidental conversation/inbox/Party deletion. Qualified tenant offboarding may retire the complete scope only through its own obligations, not an unrestricted cascade shortcut. Avoid unvalidated polymorphic identifiers, permanent JSON before-images and a second retention database. Index tenant/source/generation, effective policy time and pending due/cleanup queries.

### REQ26-D17-R21 — Read models, search, files and restoration

The current source gate applies before response membership/counting as well as body rendering. Expired terms cannot produce stale search hits, facets, counts or match reasons. Rebuild indexes behind the gate. Current client source revisions reject late stale responses and revalidate on reconnect; no persistent offline transcript archive is created. Old already-received browser/clipboard/download copies remain outside recall.

Reuse D16's private source-gated attachment path, no reusable URL bypass, legacy URL qualification and owner physical-object disposal. A stale replica, cache TTL, signed URL expiry or metadata-row deletion is not permission/deletion proof. Hosted exports, CRM snippets, Recent copy, permitted AI material and logs have registered owners and source correction behavior; no new AI feature is introduced.

Restore current policy history, expired source frontiers and restriction evidence before any restored read, materialization, index/export, decryption or send. Keep that evidence outside the rollback horizon of the data it constrains. Missing reconciliation fails closed for affected content. Policy extension, restore, old deployments and retry cannot revive expired content or renew disposal deadlines. Subsequent owner corrections may reopen cleanup for missed copies without undoing expiry.

### REQ26-D17-R22 — Audit and accountable data remaining

Retain content-free activation/expiry receipts: policy ID/version/duration/unit/effective time, trusted actor/system cause, tenant/source/frontier references, scope/units, event/anchor/deadline/observed processing times and owner disposition evidence. No expired body/subject/filename/address/header, arbitrary before-image or guessable secret hash. Settings history shows old/new configured values and actor; source business history distinguishes policy change, logical expiry, hold custody and physical cleanup. Logs/traces diagnose jobs without becoming a content store.

Every retained class has a qualified horizon and final disposition. Do not use ordinary Support duration to erase required P6/financial facts, or use those facts' horizon to keep bodies. Routing/dedupe and restore barriers may need different service-only lifetimes from staff-visible skeletons. Before Live activation, the owning policy inventory must name actual horizons and restore/replay bounds, not placeholders such as forever or later. This is a release qualification requirement for real environments, not an invented global numeric law.

### REQ26-D17-R23 — Bounded processing and actual proof of scale

Use server-owned tenant/source eligibility and aggregate queries, keyset iteration, bounded transactions, indexed due work and fair worker concurrency. Current UI lists capped at 2,000 before some filtering cannot supply complete policy previews or cleanup enumeration. No full transcript hydration or whole-CRM graph traversal is needed to calculate due work. Treat preview timeout/incomplete scope distinctly from zero; an approximate labelled planning count is not a passed activation qualification.

Release evidence must state concrete supported source/file sizes, tenants/records, policy-version density, preview latency, due-backlog processing rate, worker concurrency and physical cleanup budgets, then exercise those boundaries and above-limit backpressure. Do not copy vendor throughput/limits or claim performance measured here. Deadline-based read denial must hold even when cleanup backlog grows. Intake remains recoverable independently of preview, expiry-job or provider failure.

### REQ26-D17-R24 — Migration and activation order

First qualify D16 source restriction/cleanup and retained-data inventory. Add immutable work/content admission and policy history, exact correlation separate from raw headers, then current expiry evaluation on every reader/writer. Reconcile legacy source identity, timestamps, content copies and policies with bounded proof; unknowns remain restricted/owned exceptions rather than guessed dates or email matches. Do not reset all legacy anchors to migration day.

Qualify old-code/new-schema and new-code/old-schema behavior, dispatch/preparation/export/index writers, actual grants/RLS/storage, provider/backup custody and restore barriers before enabling a tenant policy. Show legacy exclusions and resolve them; an exclusion is not compliance completion. A kill switch preserves current restrictions and accepted cleanup. After expiry data exists, rollback uses compatible safe reads/roll-forward; restoring a database or deploying old unguarded code is not Undo. No hook bypass, production activation or schema work is performed by this specification.

### REQ26-D17-R25 — Quiet, accessible policy and CRM experience

The UX blueprint is the complete interface contract. Use one existing tenant settings section, a finite duration control, inert draft, review with old/new effects, one meaningful confirmation, clear current status and on-demand details. Do not make staff subtract hidden disposal grace, type magic words routinely, navigate a new compliance app, inspect storage internals, or receive expiry emails/countdowns on every conversation.

Use Core's exact base-maia/Base UI/shared semantic design system. Keyboard, screen-reader and touch users must configure, review, correct and confirm the same scope; async errors/progress must be programmatic and not mistaken for success. Preserve CRM/Support route, filter and scroll context; distinguish expired, restricted, missing authority and temporary failure without revealing hidden sources. Unit/timezone explanations are accessible; zoom/mobile keyboard never obscures critical controls. Beautiful/easy is an intended result requiring actual usability/a11y proof, not a claim earned by this document.

### REQ26-D17-R26 — Traceability and stage boundary

Carry R01–R26, the inventory, UX, category fixes, proof matrix and operational controls into implementation OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets/tests/release evidence. Resolve the narrow P6/D16 automatic-expiry owner extension, P6 endpoint supersession and known current-source gaps explicitly, rather than silently preserving weak code or rewriting prior ADRs.

The policy model is complete: actual tenant quantities, lawful inventory horizons and measured deployment capacities are required configuration/release evidence, not unfinished founder questions or assertions that the feature already works.

### REQ26-D17-C001 — The policy surface

Use the existing tenant settings area, **Support → Content retention**, through Core's shared navigation and permission patterns. It is one section for ordinary Support content, not a new compliance application. Use exact base-maia, Base UI primitives, semantic tokens and shared components.

The first configuration has no preselected numeric value. The form reads:

Days/Months/Years are explicit choices; the illustration's unit is not a recommended duration. No Never value, automatic two-year default, hidden attachment period, custom conditions or inherited inbox policy. The authorized administrator selects a finite period from the tenant's actual approved purpose/records policy. Validate the complete value with a localized message, without accepting zero, fractions, negatives, overflow or an unrepresentable deadline.

Brief expandable help explains that days are elapsed 24-hour days; months/years use the policy's frozen tenant IANA timezone and calendar anniversary with the specified month-end rules. Show **Calendar timezone: [tenant zone]** in the review with exact localized examples. Ordinary staff do not have to understand timestamp storage or choose daylight-saving rules. Changing a viewer or unrelated tenant timezone setting does not move existing policy deadlines. Adopting a different policy calendar zone requires a reviewed version showing old/new zone and all immediate/future effects. Avoid converting one year into 365 days silently.

The active section shows its duration, effective date/time, status, last changed actor/time, a short scope statement and **Change policy**. Qualified details/history show versions, activation and actual processing/exceptions. The numeric field can be edited in a draft without changing any live policy.

### REQ26-D17-C002 — Review and activation

**Review policy** or **Review changes** opens a focused review in the same settings context. Keep entered data if a request fails. The review must show:

- Current and proposed duration, with units and any calendar-zone/basis change.
- **Applies to existing and future unexpired Support content in this tenant.**
- **Takes effect when you confirm.** Clearly state when existing content will expire immediately.
- A dated policy-scope calculation with separate original histories, native messages and attachment occurrences. Identify excluded/unknown classes and their owners. Do not label unique stored blobs as files or merged rows as original histories.
- What remains: permitted communication/work facts and independently owned CRM/giving/official records, each under its own policy.
- **Expired content cannot be recovered by lengthening this policy.**

The final action is **Activate policy** for first publication or **Apply changes** for a replacement. If the reviewed rule makes existing content expire now, include that consequence beside the button: **Applying this policy will expire eligible existing content immediately.** Use one meaningful final confirmation, not an extra generic dialog, typed phrase, automatic dual approval or hidden grace period.

The administrator approves an ongoing rule and its complete authorized scope. A preview is a timestamped calculation, not a frozen promise about every item. Counts may change with actual work; scope/policy/authority changes require a new review. No enormous per-record selection list or full transcript download is required. Server eligibility and source guards govern each actual effect.

All numbers above are synthetic examples, not defaults, performance claims or actual tenant data. Unknown/excluded legacy classes cannot be quietly omitted to make an activation look complete. A policy administrator's aggregate authority does not reveal restricted source details; samples/drill-downs retain their own authorization. Unqualified aggregate scope blocks that publication and routes to the qualified policy owner.

### REQ26-D17-C003 — Clear policy-adjustment outcomes

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Situation                                | Outcome and product copy                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Shortening the period                    | Preview new effects on existing unexpired content. On confirmation, newly overdue eligible content expires at that instant. No retroactive deletion timestamp.                     |
| Lengthening before current expiry        | Still-valid content can receive the new future deadline. Stale old-policy projections cannot delete it early.                                                                      |
| Lengthening after current expiry         | Old content stays expired even if byte cleanup is unfinished. Explain the boundary before confirmation; new content remains independently usable.                                  |
| Editing the same effective value         | No new lifetime or unnecessary versioned effect. Show the existing policy accurately.                                                                                              |
| Another administrator published a change | **The policy changed while you were editing. Review the current policy before applying yours.** Preserve the draft as uncommitted.                                                 |
| Preview fails or is incomplete           | **We couldn't calculate the policy's full impact. Try again.** Identify safe known scope limitations; never show zero or enable destructive activation on a false complete result. |
| Apply response lost                      | **Checking whether the policy was applied…** Reconcile its durable operation; do not invite blind repeated activation.                                                             |
| New policy active, cleanup pending       | **Policy active. Content cleanup is processing.** Current ordinary availability already follows the effective policy. Show owned failures only where actionable.                   |

No automatic email is sent for healthy policy operation. A separate required administrative/security duty can use existing P17 attention, with content-free scope and the proper owner. The tenant period never extends P17 prepared-material or Recent-copy limits.

### REQ26-D17-C004 — Exceptional pause

Place **Pause future expiry…** in a secondary policy action menu for qualified policy owners. It opens a small reviewed form with **Pause until**, explicit timezone, a bounded content-free reason and impact. It cannot be indefinite, revive expired content, stop accepted cleanup, or override a stricter owner/legal deadline.

Copy: **This pauses future ordinary expiries until the selected time. Already expired content stays unavailable. Eligible overdue content will expire when the pause ends.** Show the pause-end instant and qualified backlog estimate. Confirmation records a bounded policy change, not a worker toggle. **Resume now** also reviews its effects before applying. The active section shows **Future expiry paused until [date/time]**; no persistent warning appears on every conversation.

A technical cleanup pause is an operational control, not this tenant policy action. It does not extend content access or prove compliance. Missed processing/deadlines reach the responsible operator through existing grouped attention.

### REQ26-D17-C005 — Daily Support and CRM behavior

Ordinary staff see no retention form on each reply. When the current source is authorized, they can open **Content retention** details to understand the applicable period, genuine activity/work anchor, exact expiry date and relevant current availability. Do not show a continuously changing countdown in every list row. If an existing note can be edited, its details preserve the original deadline and explain that saving an edit does not extend retention; expiry during composition still requires clean review while preserving separable authored draft text.

At expiry, use **Content expired under your retention policy** in the original position. Preserve permitted facts and navigation; do not display the original sensitive subject, file name or excerpt. When newer content exists, use a compact **Earlier content expired** separator plus the new readable messages. Do not mark the entire current conversation unreadable merely because an older generation expired.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Source condition                                   | Safe display                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ordinary generation expired                        | **Content expired under your retention policy**; permitted history/details remain.                                      |
| Older expired generation with new current messages | **Earlier content expired**; show new messages and current work normally.                                               |
| Required bytes retained under hold                 | Ordinary expired/unavailable display. Qualified records detail says **Preservation required**; no ordinary Reveal.      |
| Authority/eligibility check unavailable            | Safe temporary-unavailability state. Do not falsely claim expiration, successful destruction or a confirmed legal hold. |
| Cleanup failed after expiry                        | Content remains expired. Qualified details show **Cleanup needs attention**, owner and retry/reconcile outcome.         |
| Actual source/CRM access absent                    | Existing non-disclosing access behavior; no hidden title/count/hold details.                                            |
| All lawful CRM discovery basis removed             | Withdraw normal CRM row/count. Service-only control evidence does not create visible history.                           |

CRM Communications uses D9's same source row and current availability. Expiry does not add Activity, last contact, an artificial donor interaction or a new CRM note. The actual giving receipt is unchanged; access to it is reauthorized in its owner surface. The existing financial-support summary retains its distinct meaning.

If old Reply/Reply all context has expired, state **Reply details for this older message are no longer available.** Do not substitute today's CRM email. Genuine new email provides a new qualified reply audience. Deliberate new outbound conversation uses the existing authorized flow. A normal late reply must not be lost just because its predecessor text expired, nor may it recover the old text.

### REQ26-D17-C006 — Long-running work and required records

When the oldest ordinarily available unexpired content reaches the chosen interval and ongoing work/chatter still prevents expiry, create one accountable purpose-review obligation through existing staff/records work. Already-expired held bytes do not repeatedly trigger review of new content. It is grouped and does not send a per-message warning storm. The qualified reviewer confirms current need and next review within one interval of that actual review; policy shortening updates pending reviews, while lengthening cannot erase a missed-review fact. The owner may finish actual work or place a required record in its owning domain. No auto-close action or Keep forever switch.

Staff must understand that an open Finance task or CRM link alone does not hold all conversation content. Conversely, a merged-away source can still support an active shared issue. The exact source interest drives eligibility. If a required record only exists in the Support upload, qualified records custody precedes its destruction; do not ask staff to casually export everything to a local folder.

### REQ26-D17-C007 — Accessibility and verification

Use shared accessible form/dialog primitives with programmatic labels, units, errors, current/effective values and quiet status announcements. Maintain focus on an understandable heading/least destructive action, offer Back/Cancel before commitment and return to the stable settings/source location. Avoid destructive Enter submission from a duration or date input. A closed review surface does not undo an accepted publication.

Require keyboard/AT/touch parity, visible focus, adequate target size, no color-only warnings, localized time/number presentation, mobile-keyboard clearance and 200%/400% zoom/reflow. Low-bandwidth retries preserve drafts and distinguish checking from saved. The preview and activation experience needs actual usability proof that staff can explain what disappears, what remains, when the change applies and why expired content cannot return. W3C error prevention, status messages, dialog guidance.

No rendered interface, accessibility certification, tenant user study or performance benchmark is claimed. D17 P01, P06–P15, P25–P30 and P37–P39 require those actual outcomes before release. The blueprint defines the complete intended experience without selecting a new component system, provider or compliance product.

### REQ26-D17-C009 — What a CRM user sees

When D9's qualified relevance/correspondence and joint authorization still permit a row, CRM Communications can show:

This is an illustrative semantic layout, not a rendered component. Only permitted facts are shown. Do not retain a sensitive subject as its title, add a new Activity event, use expiry as a fresh last-contact date, or expose a source whose discovery authority was withdrawn. An existing Finance receipt is reached through Finance's authorized navigation; the expired Support attachment does not automatically redirect to it.

If new qualified mail later continues this source, the current conversation can contain readable new messages and an older content-expired marker. A source-level generic expired badge must not hide the fact that new content is available. The old message's Reply/Reply all control cannot rebuild lost audience evidence from CRM. New incoming mail supplies a new qualified response audience; deliberate new outbound remains a separate reviewed action.

### REQ26-D17-C010 — Database invariants

The current conversation table combines work state and unsafe display snapshots; current parent deletion cascades into messages, assignments and audit. The permanent design must use content availability and a protected minimal skeleton, not generic parent DELETE. Support schema.

Require one tenant-aware authoritative source identity; validated message/file/frontier relationships; unique policy activation and expiry-effect identities; immutable published policy/effect evidence; trusted actors/times; and controlled delete behavior that preserves unresolved cleanup/custody/barriers. Expired payload fields and serving authority cannot be restored through generic row updates or new policy versions. Logical payload-availability constraints should make an expired generation with a readable current payload impossible through the ordinary mutation/read boundary.

Current source threading queries raw message-header JSON and then sender/subject. Those are observed legacy paths, not endorsed D1 identity behavior. Separate justified correlation from raw payload before enabling expiry; never preserve the entire header blob or unsafe fallback merely to keep current code working. Current lookup.

Keep minimum retained-class policy records: owner, permitted purpose, visibility, applicable horizon, final disposal/anonymization outcome and replay/restore dependencies. Actual values must be qualified before the affected deployment. Source barriers outlive the maximum permitted recovery path they constrain; a shorter ordinary staff-visible history horizon cannot remove the service-only protection prematurely. These obligations are not a universal indefinite archive.

The endpoint policy must obey the current P6 supersession of its older durable-recipient-email wording. P6 endpoint amendment. Broader authority remains Asym-owned CRM truth and body-free communication history. CRM ADR0001, ADR0031.

### REQ26-D17-C011 — Privacy and records rationale

FTC guidance supports minimizing unnecessary data and documenting justified retention. IRS guidance requires appropriate supporting records; it does not establish a single lifetime for every Support email. Preserve the owning facts and actual required record rather than all support-side copies. FTC guide, IRS exempt-organization recordkeeping.

D16's US legal/provider assessment remains qualified and ratified. Applicable law, actual holds and processor contracts govern real deployments; no universal nonprofit exemption, numerical retention period or legal certification is inferred. Every class above must have real owner evidence before Live activation. The inventory is complete as a design contract; no database, storage or provider deletion was executed here.

### AC26-D17-P01

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Configure a blank finite policy, review old/new scope/effects and activate once; no default number or pre-confirmation expiry.
