## D17 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D17-O01

**Signal and threshold:** Any verified post-expiry forbidden read/egress, stale resurrection or premature destruction: 1

**Owner:** Security/platform incident owner

**Response:** Contain affected path immediately, preserve content-free evidence, disable unsafe release and repair/reprove before re-enable.

### OP26-D17-O02

**Signal and threshold:** Accepted active-copy cleanup unresolved for 15 elapsed minutes or 3 consecutive failed attempts, whichever first

**Owner:** Support engineering on-call

**Response:** Keep expiry effective; inspect owner result, retry/reconcile safely and escalate the failing owner.

### OP26-D17-O03

**Signal and threshold:** Source-purpose review passes its recorded deadline or lacks an owner: 1

**Owner:** Tenant Support/records owner

**Response:** Assign/perform qualified review; retain safe existing authority only under actual purpose/custody, never auto-close or treat review backlog as a legal exception.

### OP26-D17-O04

**Signal and threshold:** Pause has no finite end, exceeds its approved end, or a mandatory owner disposal deadline lacks completion evidence: 1

**Owner:** Tenant policy/records owner

**Response:** Reject invalid pause or honor automatic resumption; escalate missed disposal immediately without renewing the deadline.

### OP26-D17-O05

**Signal and threshold:** Missing policy/class/horizon in activation qualification, incomplete legacy scope or unresolved preservation status: 1 affected scope

**Owner:** Platform rollout owner + tenant records owner

**Response:** Block that destructive activation, assign bounded remediation/custody and expose its real status; preserve intake.

### OP26-D17-O06

**Signal and threshold:** Backlog exceeds measured supported capacity or p95 command/preview latency exceeds its published budget for 15 minutes

**Owner:** Support/platform operations

**Response:** Apply fair backpressure, diagnose capacity/regression, maintain expiry read denial and recoverable intake; remeasure before raising limits.

### OP26-D17-O07

**Signal and threshold:** Restore/old-writer barrier failure or expired content in audit/log output: 1

**Owner:** Database/platform owner + security

**Response:** Block release/restore, restrict unsafe output, apply owner correction and rerun the failed boundary proof.

### REQ26-D17-C013 — Operating and qualification sequence

**Capture in implementation design/spec:** first map actual retained classes and source-purpose dependencies; qualify immutable work/admission/policy history and minimal safe correlation; define the automatic-frontier intent and current read/decrypt/dispatch guard; then carry the policy preview/activation/pause and CRM availability contract. The source boundary determines what the UI can promise.

**Require in implementation:** close current generic-DML/cascade/list/clock gaps, qualify D16 owner cleanup and source-safe files, implement policy evaluation and idempotent expiry, then prove migration/restore/races and real UX/capacity. Enable only qualified tenant scopes after actual policy and owner evidence. These are release gates, not monitor-only exceptions.

**Monitor only after those gates pass.** The following thresholds are accepted operating controls, not legal grace periods or measured performance. Earlier applicable owner deadlines always govern.

## D18 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D18-R01 — Scope and strongest alternative

Adopt B as the ordinary launch model. A—curated Shared only—is the strongest simpler alternative: less duplication and fewer custody states, at the cost of personal reuse and maintainer dependence. C—broader collaborative Shared publishing—reduces contribution handoffs but increases the group affected by ordinary edits and additions. No measured ministry study proves B universally superior; B is a deliberate product judgment balancing personal writing and maintained guidance.

Complete this bounded library, not an enterprise help-desk suite. Reuse the already accepted Saved reply wording concept. No new CRM, knowledge base, AI suggestion/translation system, marketing designer, business-action macro builder, general form engine or three-mode tenant configuration is selected.

### REQ26-D18-R02 — One authoring owner and two scopes

Qualify a narrow Saved Section specialization within Email Studio's canonical structured authoring capability. A logical item has one tenant, one immutable identity and exactly one scope: personal with one tenant-membership custodian, or shared with tenant stewardship and no individual ownership dependency. Creator/editor attribution is separate. No global-account personal library, implicit cross-tenant portability, second raw-HTML store, provider template authority, new Layout Role or system-message catalog key.

Scope is not a generic editable null owner field. Promotion creates a distinct destination-owned shared candidate with provenance; it does not mutate the personal item into a different audience. Item identity, content revision, language variant, usage purpose and presentation dependencies remain distinct. The same shared item is managed from Email Studio and consumed in Support, not synchronized between duplicate stores.

### REQ26-D18-R03 — Rights and the meaning of personal

Separate ordinary use, own-item maintenance, shared-content maintenance/publication, and exceptional personal-custody administration using Core capabilities. Shared maintainers do not automatically read others' My replies or their source conversations. My replies is personal ordinary use inside this tenant, not a secrecy promise against specifically authorized tenant records/security custody. Exceptional custody requires its explicit tenant-scoped capability, purpose, current authorization and audit; no hidden supervisor inheritance or routine export-all-personal button from shared-edit rights.

Save to My replies commits a validated immutable authoring revision usable only by its current authorized custodian. It is not publication and grants no template dispatch authority; the tenant's another-reviewer-for-every-publication setting does not add a reviewer to this save or normal human composition. This narrow distinction cannot lower an actual protected publication floor: personal items admit only qualified reusable human wording, not protected system/artifact/layout sources or recipient-specific protected material stripped of provenance. Current insertion, content-safety, preparation and Send/Add note checks still apply. Membership/permission loss stops new unauthorized reads and use, including cached clients.

### REQ26-D18-R04 — Reply versus Internal note, not dozens of template types

Each item declares one insertion purpose: **Reply** or **Internal note**. Both may live in My or Shared. The picker filters by the active composer purpose and labels it clearly. It never switches composer mode; an internal-note item cannot be fetched through an external-reply insertion path. A deliberate separately reviewed conversion creates another appropriate candidate; an unsafe body is not made public by toggling a label.

Changing mode after insertion also does not authorize disclosure of internal-only wording. Preserve separate Reply and Internal note drafts. External preparation rejects retained internal-only item provenance, including content recovered through Replace/Undo; do not silently carry the note body into Reply, relabel it or strip its source. Any deliberate conversion requires owner-qualified content/audience review. Internal notes reuse the shared authoring validator but never enter external email preparation, P6 dispatch, Resend or the external prepared-material lifetime. Their Add note command owns admission.

Full answers, short phrases, greetings, closings, information requests, updates, instructions and handoff/checklist wording use the same bounded content model. Their length/tone are content choices, not workflow types. No stored mention activates notifications during save/preview; a note template uses safe text or fill-ins, and any later real mention must be explicitly selected through the existing current-user authorization path. Saving/inserting adds neither a note nor a D11 delegated action by itself.

### REQ26-D18-R05 — Useful styles with one visual system

Use P17's qualified semantic paragraphs, emphasis, headings, lists, safe links and approved images, plus reusable files under R12. Quoted wording may be plain text within that vocabulary; no new blockquote or general-table authoring is selected. Protected domain-owned tables remain only in their already qualified owner context. Keep actual HTML and plain-text output consistent. Full responses remain body content: no embedded From/To/subject, outer email document, duplicated brand wrapper, executable script/CSS, remote font, tracking pixel or live nested snippet reference.

Use concise plain-language copy as the starter style, with optional warm, formal, concise, detailed or translated authored alternatives. These are titles/wording, not a tone-generation engine or mandatory matrix of every variant. Shared presentation, sender identity and signature/framing remain with D4/P17; do not invent a separate Support signature policy or duplicate a signature on every inserted fragment. Email Studio tools retain base-maia and accessible outline parity. Formatting must remain usable with images blocked, narrow screens, long names, RTL text and real plain text.

### REQ26-D18-R06 — Creation and editing without harvesting a case

Offer New saved reply from the picker and the same library management surface. Start clean with title, purpose, language and content; default an ordinary author's new item to My replies. Scope and recipient visibility are visible before saving. Allow an optional search alias and category; do not require administrative metadata before a useful personal save. Preserve drafts, errors and confirmed save state.

Do not automatically save a sent message, a whole reply draft, conversation history, live donor values, attachments or hidden links as reusable material. Provide no one-click Save conversation as template. Deliberate reusable authoring can preserve approved unresolved typed fields; known source-derived material keeps its dependency restrictions and must pass generalized-content review before the owner admits it as reusable. Unsupported opaque source mappings fail closed for that copy, not for all ordinary composition. A warning or AI guess is not proof of anonymization. Freely typed misleading prose cannot be perfectly detected; guidance and actual domain-action boundaries remain necessary.

### REQ26-D18-R07 — Typed context values and CRM are separate authorities

Expose only fields qualified by the actual Reply or Internal note content contract. Resolve values server-side from the current tenant, exact conversation/audience and permitted source. Label the authenticated replying author separately from the Support assignee; an unassigned queue is not a person. Do not split international display names at the first space, choose the first To recipient or first related Party, treat matching email as identity, or guess represented-organization authority.

Missing/ambiguous/unauthorized required values block preparation with a precise repair path. Optional neutral wording must be explicit; use a safe greeting rather than fabricated names. A no-Party reply remains possible through D1. Shared authoring previews use synthetic data; actual context appears only in the authorized current draft. D2 visible groups use one audience-safe body. Display permission is not permission to disclose every CRM value. No blank CRM property is filled as a side effect, and a snippet cannot assert receipt/refund completion as a protected fact without its owner's actual evidence.

### REQ26-D18-R08 — Explicit one-use fill-in fields

Qualify a narrow **Fill-in field** authoring node through the shared compiler: plain-language label/instruction, required or optional, and safe bounded text input. Values belong only to the current insertion/draft. They are not CRM properties, query expressions, executable braces or live cross-draft values. A required field has no silent example/default; an optional default is explicit reusable wording. After insertion, fields display clearly in the draft and keyboard order; the author can complete them or remove the associated field/wording deliberately.

Unresolved required fields block Send or Add note at the authoritative command, not only in the client. Whitespace is not completion. Human literal brace text remains ordinary text. A resolved value is escaped once as text, never recursively interpreted as variables, mentions or markup; links/assets use their separate qualified tools. Repeated appearances of one field in an item share that insertion's value, while another insertion receives fresh identity and no old answers. Deleting/changing an input invalidates its prior review. Values cannot update the library, another draft, an authoritative CRM fact or imply a business action. This requires a narrow P17 authoring/input qualification, not a generic forms platform.

### REQ26-D18-R09 — Explicit language and honest translation freshness

An item may contain independently authored language variants under the same logical identity and purpose. Each variant has an exact canonical locale, explicit content revision and availability. Reuse the owning locale validation and structured RTL/bidi support; do not introduce a second locale registry or infer a person's language from nationality, name or email. A current explicitly selected draft language can filter the picker. Otherwise show the tenant's configured authoring default clearly, with the language control available.

Missing target-language content is visible: offer other available languages for deliberate selection or a normal authored reply; never silently send a different language or machine translation. Changing UI locale does not replace inserted wording. Record a translation's declared reviewed source revision when supplied; a source change can mark linked translations Needs review in management without silently rewriting or automatically withdrawing still-safe approved wording. Actual safety revocation remains a separate enforceable fence. Display freshness only where relevant. A language variant is not a new publication of every other language or a mandatory all-locale campaign rollout.

### REQ26-D18-R10 — Find the right item without a noisy library

One searchable picker supports Shared, My and Favorites filters, a small current-purpose recent-selection area, and optional single-level categories. Categories organize content and are not permission boundaries or live nested snippets. Shared category maintenance follows shared rights; personal categories/preferences belong to the current tenant/custodian. Deleting a category leaves items uncategorized rather than deleting them. Reuse a shared item directly as a favorite instead of forcing personal copies of official wording.

Search authorized titles, descriptions, aliases and reusable body text with Unicode-aware literal matching through the shared search capability. Resolve tenant, purpose, source eligibility, locale and ACL before membership, results, counts, autocomplete or ranking. Do not scan only the first page or capped current conversation list. Exact alias/title matches precede ordinary matches; scope and locale disambiguate duplicates. Aliases are search hints, never record identity or executable expansion. They do not silently shadow a Shared item with a personal match. A slash/keyboard command opens the same picker; it never auto-sends, opens on ordinary slash-containing text indiscriminately, or bypasses explicit choice. Search ranking stays stable during keyboard navigation; late results cannot move focus to another item.

Favorites and recent IDs grant no access and keep no body/hidden title after revocation. Management can include authorized Archived items; ordinary use excludes them. Empty, no matches, wrong-language, unavailable and denied states are distinct without exposing hidden assets. No automatic folder hierarchy, AI ranking, shortcut collision oracle or cross-tenant popularity index.

### REQ26-D18-R11 — Safe insertion, combination and replacement

Preview the exact currently eligible item revision and assets before or alongside selection, then insert at a stable current caret/selection. A complete answer still uses Insert by default; replacing existing content is a distinct Replace reply/Replace note action with local Undo. Do not require a modal preview for every simple insertion. Switching purpose, target, tenant or draft while a result is loading cannot apply it to the wrong editor; stale bookmarks/versions require reapply without losing typed text.

Copy the selected structured content with immutable provenance, fresh fill-in occurrence IDs and asset appearances in one coherent draft edit. Multiple insertions can combine a greeting, instructions and closing. Repeated exact file references do not duplicate already present attachments; Undo removes only text/fields/appearances introduced by that insertion, never a preexisting file or later independent work. Undo cannot restore restricted content or convert internal-only provenance to Reply; restore only currently permitted material and preserve unrelated authored work. No live saved-item reference remains in the body. New library edits do not alter restored drafts. Actual source restrictions still govern retained dependency material, preparation and dispatch. Review any changed source facts/audience under D4; do not replace text behind the author's back.

### REQ26-D18-R12 — Governed reusable files and images

Support static reusable attachments such as approved general guidance through Email Studio's governed asset owner, with immutable version references, filename/type/size, scan/readiness, author permission, reuse purpose and current source availability. Insertion and actual sending both validate compatibility and audience disclosure. Images require suitable alternative text unless genuinely decorative; plain-text output preserves the useful linked meaning. No external image fetch, iframe, remote executable content or hotlinked private-case asset is admitted as trusted library material.

Actual receipts, statements, identity proofs, care records, expiring action links and donor-uploaded documents do not become general attachments by saving a pointer. Use the owning action/document flow in the current authorized conversation. Updating a library file produces a new revision; old pins follow their valid owner lifecycle, while a safety-revoked version stops new unsafe use. Respect the stricter of source, library, prepared-message and provider limits. Publish numeric size/count/total-byte limits from the qualified shared contract before activation, and prove exact boundaries; do not copy a vendor's arbitrary file budget or claim unlimited capacity.

### REQ26-D18-R13 — Shared publication and audience

Shared items have explicit authorized-use scope: all eligible Support staff in the tenant or selected existing qualified Support teams. This scope is an actual asset authorization rule, not merely a From-channel filter. Shared maintenance applies to the actor's explicit asset-management scope and does not grant any CRM/conversation access. A title or aggregate count cannot leak out of that scope. No arbitrary sharing with email addresses or cross-tenant users.

Shared editors create an unpublished candidate, review exact wording/purpose/locale/fields/assets/scope, and Publish through the owning immutable publication boundary. Ordinary qualified self-publication stays simple. Existing protected and tenant-stricter review apply; a Support-local permission or personal copy cannot bypass them. Widening scope requires a reviewed publication. Failed validation or stale concurrent publication leaves the previous complete valid shared version active. Saving a draft does not update colleagues' picker. Publishing sends no mail, changes no work and creates no CRM interaction.

The effective item audience governs all old revisions, deep links, favorites, previews and new insertion/preparation. A historical audience snapshot is provenance, not enduring access. Audience narrowing takes effect through a current authorization revision; it differs from routine Archive and preserves D4's treatment of admitted or possibly-sent envelopes. Widening an item audience reviews every currently exposed locale/asset in that scope; a valid single-language candidate cannot authorize unseen incompatible variants.

### REQ26-D18-R14 — Deliberate contribution, not implicit promotion

Offer to Shared creates an immutable contribution snapshot of an exact eligible personal revision and declared proposed audience. The author sees what will become visible to qualified maintainers. Those maintainers gain only the offered candidate, not the source conversation or all personal items. A later personal edit neither changes the offer nor updates Shared. An authorized maintainer may edit a separate candidate and publish through R13 with truthful provenance; accepting an existing candidate against another shared item requires an explicit target and current-head comparison.

Before exposing an offered file/image to maintainers or publishing it to a broader audience, re-prove exact reuse/disclosure authority and establish a destination-owned governed occurrence/reference. Never hotlink Shared to the author's personal file area. Valid Shared assets survive ordinary source-item deletion/departure under their own custody while true safety/source restrictions still propagate. No physical byte copy is mandated. An invalid asset prevents exposure of the affected candidate; do not create a partly shared body/file result.

Use existing Email Studio review/task attention, with an accountable maintainer or qualified shared work home. No new notification campaign, approval engine or content-bearing task copy. Pending contributions may be withdrawn before publication; concurrent publish/withdraw is conditional and resolves one ordered result. Once published, withdrawing the offer does not unpublish the independent Shared item; use its owner action. Declined/withdrawn offers stop pending work and obey asset retention. Identical retry creates one contribution; deliberately offering revised wording is a new reviewed snapshot, with duplicate hints rather than silent merging. Known source safety restrictions propagate to affected copies even though ordinary edits do not.

### REQ26-D18-R15 — Archive, restore and ordinary edits

Draft, saved/published usable revision, Archived, and safety-restricted are distinct facts. **Archive** stops new picker selection/insertion without making routine maintenance an emergency block on otherwise safe already-inserted drafts or prepared messages. Shared editors can archive within scope; authors can archive My items. The action needs clear effect wording and safe correction, not typed confirmation for every item. Archiving must not require the broken body still to compile.

Restore returns an archived item to use only after current ownership, scope, schema/assets and publication rules are satisfied; it never simply resurrects a safety-restricted source. Restoring an older content version creates a reviewed new candidate with attribution, not in-place history editing. Editing content always creates a new revision. Published/usable versions are immutable; cosmetic metadata changes cannot secretly modify an existing prepared body. Ordinary library retirement, item disposal and dangerous-source revocation are not interchangeable APIs.

### REQ26-D18-R16 — Safety restriction, deletion and source correction

Unsafe or unauthorized content uses existing owner quarantine/restriction and D16-style active-use/cleanup obligations for affected material. Safety changes can stop new reads/insertion/preparation and qualifying definitely-unsubmitted work; in-flight/unknown provider effects remain D4/P6 reconciliation, not recall or a replacement send. Apply the owner's correctly declared quarantine effect rather than treating every archive as an all-envelope incident.

Do not offer generic hard Delete as a shortcut around source history, contributions or prepared references. Permanent disposal follows the actual asset owner's policy, restrictions and retention, preserves minimum necessary provenance/control evidence, and never cascades through sent messages, independent CRM records or official files. Wrong cleanup evidence is corrected append-only; content already disposed is not restored. Exports, previews, search, logs and backups/restore obey current source boundaries. No implicit forever archive or Reveal bypass for personal items.

### REQ26-D18-R17 — Departure and tenant custody

Shared replies stay tenant-managed when a creator changes role or leaves. Attribution can retain a minimized former-author reference under the identity owner's policy; it does not retain login/access rights. Personal use stops on membership/capability loss. Personal items are neither published to Shared nor deleted automatically by an agent-parent cascade. Their actual tenant authoring retention/custody determines later disposition; no universal permanent retention or guessed grace period.

An explicit qualified custody action may inspect, restrict, export or prepare a new permitted shared candidate only within the existing records/security administrative purpose and audit. Ordinary shared-edit permission cannot silently claim a departed person's entire library. Reactivation/recovery rechecks actual current identity/membership and source lifetime; a newly invited person with the same email does not inherit another person's My replies. Open contributions already deliberately offered remain governed by their own scope and maintainer, not dependent on the author staying logged in.

### REQ26-D18-R18 — Retention of library content and its copies

Generic reusable library wording has an authoring purpose and owner policy distinct from an individual conversation's D17 clock. That does not create an exemption for known case-derived content. Establish each actual library, draft, offer, asset, preference, audit and recovery class's owner, permitted use, visibility, horizon and disposal outcome before activation. An unsent insertion remains draft material under its qualified draft lifetime and inherited source restrictions; it is not a new admitted Support original or a retention-renewal event. Once the reply or note is actually admitted, its Support content follows D17. P17 prepared material and P6/owner-qualified Recent copies retain their separate tighter ceilings. Ordinary library edits are not retention events for old conversations.

Known source-derived content or files cannot lose their restriction by copying, editing, offering, importing, exporting or renaming an item. Keep the minimum source dependency evidence required for correction and expiry; do not retain the original secret in audit. Human generalization must produce valid reusable content under the owner review; opaque lineage does not justify automatic extraction. Pasted literals can require human correction, so do not claim perfect semantic DLP or build an AI archive scanner to justify B.

### REQ26-D18-R19 — CRM integration and cross-surface continuity

Requester, participant, authenticated author, assignee, related Party, represented organization and CRM owner remain distinct. D9 allows several related records without a main designation; insertion cannot select a first record as the authoritative personalization source. Resolving ambiguity belongs in the current authorized reply context, with neutral wording available. Requesting a receipt, initiating a refund or updating contact data uses the real owner action, with context-preserving navigation and its audit/approval; words saying done never perform or prove it.

The same authorized Support composer opened from CRM sees the same eligible library and exact draft. Returning preserves context without exposing hidden CRM data to the library editor. Shared editing, personal custody and item use grant no additional giving/care/missionary access. Save, favorite, insert, offer and publish produce no communication event or fresh donor interaction. Actual send adds only P6's proper deduplicated communication evidence; the final message retains permitted source revision attribution without a second canonical body. Ordinary contact merges/changes cannot rewrite old attribution or covertly choose a new recipient.

### REQ26-D18-R20 — Database, grants and source-safe mutation

Require tenant-aware keys and foreign keys for items, revisions, variants, scopes, assets, offers, insertion provenance and preferences. Personal scope requires exactly one valid tenant-membership custodian; Shared scope has no personal custodian. Tenant/source/purpose identity, accepted actor and audit fields derive from trusted context. Scope changes use the explicit owner command, never an allowed update that turns a private row into Shared by nulling owner. No sentinel string stands in for a nullable owner namespace.

Uniqueness protects immutable revision identities, one current usable head per item/locale, contribution/effect identities and per-user preferences. Titles and optional aliases may collide without granting access or selecting a hidden target; they are not authoritative keys. Validate locale/schema/state combinations, positive revision ordering, bounded data sizes and typed timestamps. Published source and durable business history are append-only except authorized source-content disposal with protected minimal evidence. Explicit delete behavior preserves surviving consumers and required recovery; no cascading staff deletion of shared truth.

RLS and grants must enforce current read and allowed mutation boundaries with both USING and WITH CHECK, plus relevant column/command restrictions. Replace or reconcile broad existing grants/policies; adding a restrictive-looking permissive policy alongside an allowing policy does not narrow their OR-combined result. Views/functions/RPCs, source files, storage, exports and privileged service-role paths require equivalent authority; current broad staff DML is insufficient. All business writes live at the qualified shared business API boundary. Recheck revocation at use, publication, preparation and dispatch, not just picker load. Cached projections, client-supplied actor/scope and generic JSON metadata never become write authority.

### REQ26-D18-R21 — Concurrency and durable effect identity

Save/edit, shared publication, offer, withdraw, archive, restore and scope changes compare their expected head/owner/governance state at the authoritative command. Concurrent stale edits return compare/reload or a deliberate personal draft copy, never last-write-wins or automatic three-way publication. Revalidate the exact candidate after changed rights/assets/review floor; historical approval does not authorize a new body.

Bind idempotency to the durable business effect and immutable semantic input. Same identity/input returns its original receipt plus current authorized state; changed input conflicts. A timeout triggers reconciliation, not blind new promotion/publication. Source revision/effect/audit and required shared attention are committed atomically or through the qualified durable owner outbox; delivery of attention is independently retryable. UI insertion likewise has one local edit identity so retries cannot duplicate text/files/fill-ins or metrics. No network call or email dispatch occurs as part of authoring transaction.

### REQ26-D18-R22 — Minimal maintenance evidence and quiet reporting

Show authorized creator/last editor, content language, last changed time, scope, active/archive state and translation review state where useful. Management may show **Insertions** and last insertion based on deduplicated completed editor insertions, labelled as authoring use—not sends, delivery, requester satisfaction or D14 response performance. A later Undo does not erase the fact that an insertion occurred; the metric definition says so. Failed previews/clicks, retries and imports do not count. Unknown legacy coverage is Unknown, not zero. Do not rank staff or build a separate analytics product.

Keep audit evidence for scope/publish/custody/retirement/safety outcomes with trusted actor and revision references, not before/after donor bodies or filled-in answers. Ordinary favorites, searches and healthy insertions do not notify the team. Existing owned attention handles contribution requests, safety restrictions and failed durable obligations. Preferences and usage facts retain actual owner horizons; anonymous-looking counters are not a blanket retention exemption.

### REQ26-D18-R23 — Portability and existing content

Reuse the qualified Email Studio native portability package for explicitly selected eligible library content where that owner contract is activated. No Support-specific CSV dialect, automatic foreign HTML execution or bulk publish. Import creates destination-owned drafts with schema/asset/locale/purpose checks, source provenance, actual disclosure rights and collision review. Source IDs, owner IDs, permissions, review decisions, real filled values, secrets and temporary URLs do not become destination authority. Personal import defaults to the current authorized custodian only when personal creation is permitted; Shared import still requires reviewed publication. Export filters scope before counts/materialization, omits live conversation context and respects current restrictions and expiry.

Inventory legacy canned-response and macro routes before activation. Convert only proved generic eligible wording; preserve unknowns read-only for qualified remediation. Do not infer Shared from missing ownership or fabricate an author. Existing unsafe raw HTML, private data and mixed macro effects do not become usable because a migration succeeded. Preserve immutable source/provenance and existing message history; migration sends, publishes and changes no Support work. No automatic cross-tenant synchronization.

### REQ26-D18-R24 — Failure and repair without losing the reply

Library load/search/save/offer errors preserve the author's draft and exact unsaved status. A library outage does not block an otherwise qualified plain D4 reply or internal note; it does not excuse bypassing the shared compiler, current permissions or Resend connection fences. Missing assets/values or changed source authority stop only the affected unsafe operation with a useful repair path. Do not replace the chosen item with another locale/version/personal match silently.

Source write success with lost response reconciles one receipt; secondary projection/task failure remains visible and replayable. Revocation clears stale local display and prevents new unauthorized fetch/use; loss of rights during editing preserves only authored material the user may still retain, not hidden source bodies. Existing shared work handles failed owner obligations; no routine SQL repair, local-file export workaround or blind provider resend is a normal journey.

### REQ26-D18-R25 — Complete search and bounded scale

Use indexed tenant/scope/purpose/locale/current-state queries with complete authorized pagination, stable ordering and safe search projections. Do not load all tenant content into a browser to filter personal rights or reuse the current 2,000-conversation cap. Bound source document/node/alias/variant/asset counts, payload bytes, result pages, exports and worker concurrency through the shared capability's published numerical contract and production-shaped qualification. No arbitrary vendor cap or claim of infinite scale.

Isolate expensive imports, search and publication work with tenant fairness. Keep ordinary typing and insertion responsive without uncontrolled body caches or polling every conversation. Test at, below and above supported sizes and concurrent large-tenant activity; actual numerical budgets and query plans are release evidence, not guessed benchmark claims. Search/usage projections can lag only with honest UI and current authorization, never stale disclosure or wrong mutation targets.

### REQ26-D18-R26 — Complete accessible journey

The UX blueprint defines new staff discovery, daily insertion, variable repair, multiple fragments, personal authoring, shared contribution, maintainer review, languages, assets, archive and departure. Preserve the CRM/source location and draft. Use shared base-maia primitives, labels, focus and semantic states; no hover-only preview, color-only warning or hidden Enter-to-send while a picker/fill-in owns input. Keyboard and touch expose the same choices; search result changes do not move active selection. RTL/IME, long labels, 200%/400% reflow, mobile keyboard and low-bandwidth recovery require actual proof.

Keep authoring instructions outside the customer-visible document, but do not treat an internal-only description as permission to store secrets. Distinguish Save to My replies, Offer to Shared, Save draft, Publish, Insert, Replace and Send/Add note. No single ambiguous Save & apply command performs hidden publication and message mutation. Routine successful use stays quiet; brief inline state is enough.

### REQ26-D18-R27 — Activation and migration order

First qualify the owner asset scope, purpose, manual-input and source-dependency contracts; then tenant-aware constraints/commands and source guards; then compatible picker/editor/admin surfaces and migration readers. Fence old raw CRUD/macro/template/test routes before real library use can bypass these rules. Prove personal read isolation, current revocation, publication races, D16/D17, actual asset delivery, source-safe CRM journeys and P6 send behavior before enabling the affected scope.

Old-code/new-schema and new-code/old-schema paths must fail safely or remain explicitly disabled; feature flags do not manufacture missing RLS or source checks. Rollback cannot restore expired/restricted bytes, rewrite immutable sends or grant old private access. Use a compatible roll-forward after new evidence is written; keep accepted-intent reconciliation and recoverable inbound work operating.

### REQ26-D18-R28 — Traceability and exclusions

Record this selected answer, all clauses, category findings, UX/examples, data contract, source evidence, independent amendments and operational controls together. OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets must map these IDs to real tests and release evidence; source inspection and document verification are not runtime proof.

No blanket US-compliance certification, vendor-parity obligation, perfect PII detector, automatic translation, public knowledge publishing, Support action engine or compulsory numerical retention/usage score is inferred. Existing D1–D17 and broader domain boundaries stay intact. Do not advance to Q19 before that stage is handled.

### REQ26-D18-C001 — The everyday experience

Alex opens a request from CRM and stays in the same authorized Support conversation. Alex needs the maintained receipt-help instructions and a short personal closing. **Use template** opens one **Saved replies** picker in context. The current Reply/Internal note purpose is clear; an optional language selector reflects the declared draft language. A visible control works on touch; the optional slash command is a faster path to the same picker, not a separate feature.

The layout illustrates hierarchy, not required pixel dimensions or prepublished tenant wording. Empty search can show favorites and a small recent list; typed search ranks matching wording first. Scope is always distinguishable; language and usage guidance appear when relevant. No row needs simultaneous scores, badges, avatars and analytics. A longer preview or included files is inspectable without requiring an extra modal before every short phrase.

Alex inserts the shared instructions at the caret, then adds a personal closing. The draft remains editable. Any required one-use fields become clear inline controls, with a compact unresolved-fields summary only while needed. Completing them changes this draft only. The existing named **Send reply** action and **After sending** choice remain exactly D4's. Library use sends nothing, changes no status and adds no CRM interaction.

### REQ26-D18-C002 — Content forms and safe styles

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Form                                        | Appropriate use                                              | UX and safety rule                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Greeting, thanks, empathy or closing phrase | Add a short human passage around the actual answer.          | Neutral names/pronouns by default; do not duplicate the shared signature.                                                                 |
| Complete answer                             | A maintained explanation of a known process.                 | Complete still means editable body content; Insert does not become automatic Replace or Send.                                             |
| Clarifying request                          | Ask for the minimum information needed.                      | Use a clear one-use field; never request passwords or complete payment credentials as a generic template.                                 |
| Step-by-step instructions                   | Help someone complete a real supported task.                 | One action per numbered step, descriptive links, meaningful plain text; images supplement instructions.                                   |
| Progress update                             | Explain actual current work and the next step.               | Use only when the described work is real. No guessed response-time promise, automatic Waiting change or reminder.                         |
| Outcome explanation                         | Describe an actually verified owner-domain result.           | Wording does not perform or prove a refund, receipt correction or contact change. Actual protected facts/artifacts come from their owner. |
| Internal handoff/investigation outline      | Structure a staff-only note.                                 | Internal note purpose only; no implicit mention, delegation, task, assignment or requester-visible content.                               |
| Language or phrasing variant                | A translated, concise, detailed, warm or formal alternative. | Independently authored wording, clearly labelled. No automatic tone engine or required matrix of every style.                             |

Use the shared editor's qualified paragraphs, headings, lists, emphasis, links and images. Generate HTML and plain text from one source. Do not add snippet-specific fonts, CSS, promotional layouts, a general table/blockquote builder, tracking pixels, video embeds or live nested snippets. Quoted wording can remain plain text. Tenant voice and existing shared presentation are respected; a new Support signature policy is not smuggled into the library.

### REQ26-D18-C003 — Starter examples

These are synthetic opt-in authoring examples, not automatic Shared publications or assertions about a tenant's policies. Selecting an example creates a draft. The author reviews wording and purpose before saving or publishing. Field notation below describes real structured fill-in controls, not literal bracket syntax to send.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Title / purpose                         | Example wording                                                                                                           | Use guidance                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Thanks for checking / Reply             | Thank you for checking with us.                                                                                           | A short fragment that needs no CRM lookup.                                                                               |
| Receipt help / Reply                    | Thanks for letting us know. Please describe the correction you need. We’ll review your request and explain the next step. | Use when accepting review of a receipt question; it does not issue or correct a receipt.                                 |
| One detail needed / Reply               | To help with this, please provide **Needed information**.                                                                 | Needed information is a required one-use text field. Ask only for the information the current authorized workflow needs. |
| Current update / Reply                  | Here is the latest update: **Current update**. The next step is **Next step**.                                            | Both fields required. The staff author must describe actual work, not a predicted provider/financial success.            |
| Practical steps / Reply                 | Please follow these steps: **Instructions**. If anything is unclear, let us know which step needs help.                   | Instructions is a required one-use text field; an author may instead write a maintained numbered list using the editor.  |
| Internal review outline / Internal note | Request: **Request summary**. Checked: **Checks performed**. Next step: **Next step**.                                    | All are required draft fields. Save no real case details in the reusable source; fill them only in the authorized note.  |

No ready-made “refund completed,” “receipt attached,” financial amount, protected link or guaranteed response-time example is published without its actual owner qualification. The starters are useful writing scaffolds, not domain automations.

### REQ26-D18-C004 — Find, preview, insert and correct

**Find:** search titles, descriptions, optional aliases and authorized reusable text across the complete library. Filters narrow scope, purpose, language and a simple category when needed. Titles can use ordinary spaces and international text. Aliases are optional search hints, not a requirement to remember magic words. Similar Shared/My titles display both permitted candidates; no invisible personal priority. Current authorization precedes result membership/counts. Favorites point to the shared identity and therefore offer the current eligible revision at the next insertion without cloning it.

**Preview:** focus or deliberate selection exposes the same full preview for keyboard, touch and pointer users. It shows the exact language, wording, required fields and files, plus concise author-only usage guidance clearly outside the outgoing body. A permitted but context-incompatible item can explain why it is unavailable. Unauthorized items expose no title, body, count or cause. Opening a preview does not count as insertion or change a draft.

**Insert:** preserve the saved caret/selection and current editor identity. If the user typed, navigated or changed mode while content loaded, safely revalidate the bookmark or ask to insert again; never overwrite new typing. One completed insertion is one Undo unit. **Replace reply** or **Replace note** remains an explicit secondary action. A blank draft needs no extra confirmation. Combining several passages preserves field identities and avoids duplicate file appearances.

**Correct:** Undo affects only that insertion and cannot recover newly restricted content or transform internal-only wording into Reply. A file already attached before the insertion survives its Undo. Library updates leave existing drafts unchanged. If a source becomes unsafe, explain the affected field/file and preserve unrelated authorized writing; do not silently swap a different template or remove an attachment without showing the problem.

**Mode:** switching between Reply and Internal note preserves separate drafts. An internal-note template remains internal even after a later switch or Undo. External preparation rejects internal-only provenance. Add note uses Support's note admission and shared authoring validation; it never creates email preparation or Resend work.

### REQ26-D18-C005 — Personalization without accidental CRM edits

The authoring tools distinguish **Insert information** from **Add fill-in field**. The former is an approved typed owner value. The latter is information the staff author supplies for this one use. There is no “fill missing CRM property” behavior.

Fields show their meaning: replying author is not the assignee; a conversation with several related Parties has no implicit first/primary Party. Unknown names use neutral wording. A visible group receives one body safe for every admitted recipient, not personalized fan-out. Shared library preview uses synthetic fixtures; real recipient information stays in the current authorized draft.

Required fill-ins have a label, instruction and no silent sample default. Unresolved or whitespace-only values block Send/Add note with a focusable repair link. Optional defaults or phrase removal are deliberate. Repeated occurrences within one insertion share a value; another insertion starts fresh. Literal brace text is not executed. Filled values cannot become URLs, mentions, markup or a shared-library edit merely because they resemble syntax.

### REQ26-D18-C006 — Save to My replies

**New saved reply** opens the same qualified Email Studio authoring surface without losing the conversation. Required fields are title, Reply/Internal note, language and reusable content. Optional description, alias and category live under details. The primary action says **Save to My replies**. It validates and commits an immutable authoring revision, not a system-message publication. It sends nothing and requires no additional reviewer merely because the tenant reviews publications.

The personal authoring class admits only qualified reusable human wording and assets. It cannot impersonate a protected notice/layout or erase a protected source's provenance. Source safety, shared authoring validation and actual Send/Add note admission checks still apply; only external replies require email preparation. This distinction is an explicit owner extension, not an assumption that current canned-response CRUD is safe.

Create generic wording from a clean editor. Do not harvest the selected conversation, old outgoing message or filled draft automatically. A later source-derived shortcut must earn its complete provenance and generalized-content safeguards; it is not needed to make New saved reply useful. Saving a link to a private receipt does not make it reusable.

### REQ26-D18-C007 — Offer wording to Shared

An author chooses **Offer to Shared**, sees the exact candidate, language, purpose, assets and proposed audience, then submits. This exposes that candidate to qualified maintainers, not all My replies or the inspiring CRM record. The personal item remains unchanged. Editing it afterward does not alter the submitted snapshot.

Files/images receive checked destination custody before they become visible in the offer. Sharing never depends on a personal file URL that disappears when the creator leaves. Invalid assets block the affected offer without partial exposure. True safety/source restrictions still follow known copies.

Status is visible in the author's existing library details: awaiting review, changes requested, declined/withdrawn or published outcome. Reuse Email Studio's existing review and staff attention. No extra approval application or mass email. The author may withdraw a pending offer; after publication, the independent Shared item is managed through its own action. If the author already has Shared publishing rights, they can create and publish the destination candidate directly under the normal review rules.

### REQ26-D18-C008 — Maintain Shared replies

Shared maintainers can create, edit, review, publish, organize and archive within their authorized scope. Usual copy edits can self-publish after the owner checks. Protected content and the tenant's stricter publication rule still require their actual review; no Support exception lowers that floor.

The management list provides name, purpose/language, scope, state and useful edited/usage context. Optional flat categories and favorites keep everyday selection simple. Selecting an item exposes its versions, assets, languages, contributions and safe audit details. A colleague need not read implementation hashes to understand the action. Concurrent edits show a clear comparison/reload path and preserve the uncommitted draft.

Publishing applies the reviewed future usable revision. It never updates existing drafts or messages. A reviewed audience change applies current authorization to all old revisions and links; earlier broad visibility is not a permanent access grant. Widening visibility evaluates every exposed language/asset. Shared content remains tenant-managed after creator departure.

**Insertions** is a small maintenance measure, not staff performance or number of emails sent. It counts completed editor insertion identities, including those later undone, once; previews, retries and imports do not count. Unknown old coverage is labelled. No leaderboard or automatic retirement based solely on low use.

### REQ26-D18-C009 — Languages and files

Each logical item can have separately authored language variants. The current selected language is visible. Missing translations offer an explicit alternative-language choice or ordinary writing; no hidden fallback or automatic translation. A source-language change can mark a linked translation for review without silently replacing it. Real safety revocation can stop an affected variant. Long translated names and RTL remain supported, not squeezed into English-only controls.

Reusable files are approved general guidance assets with version, filename, type, size and readiness shown. Images carry useful alternative text. The shared owner checks safe reuse and actual audience at insertion and sending. Protected artifacts and expiring donor-specific links use their actual owner flow in the current conversation. Updating a library asset does not rerender an existing prepared message.

### REQ26-D18-C010 — Archive, restriction, departure and recovery

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Situation                                            | Clear behavior                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Routine wording is no longer useful                  | **Archive** stops new selection. Explain that safe existing drafts/history stay unchanged.                                              |
| Archived item is useful again                        | **Restore** rechecks current rights, content/assets and publication rules.                                                              |
| Content is unsafe or no longer authorized            | Existing source-safety restriction blocks the affected use; it is not merely hidden from the picker.                                    |
| Shared creator leaves                                | Shared content and its independently valid assets remain under tenant stewardship.                                                      |
| Personal author loses membership/use rights          | Ordinary My access stops; no automatic sharing or hard-delete cascade. Qualified tenant custody and retention govern.                   |
| Save or publish response is lost                     | **Checking whether your change was saved…** Reconcile the operation; retain the draft.                                                  |
| Library search fails                                 | **We couldn’t load saved replies. Try again.** Keep ordinary qualified composition available.                                           |
| An item changes audience or is restricted while open | Remove newly forbidden source display/use and preserve only material the user may still retain. No stale body behind a disabled button. |

My replies means ordinary personal use in the current tenant. Explain exceptional authorized records/security custody honestly without exposing private content to routine shared editors. A different account invited with the same email cannot inherit the former person's personal library.

### REQ26-D18-C011 — Accessibility and proof

Use the existing shared Base UI/base-maia controls, semantic tokens, visible focus and proper labels. Desktop can use a compact list/preview arrangement; mobile can use a full-height sheet with reachable search, preview and Insert. Keep the virtual keyboard from covering required controls. Escape preserves the draft; Tab navigates normally; Enter in a picker or fill-in cannot also send. Scope any character shortcut so ordinary typing, URLs, paste and IME remain intact.

Require keyboard/screen-reader/touch parity, 200%/400% zoom/reflow, long names, mixed scripts, RTL, images-blocked/plain text and low-bandwidth tests. Automated a11y checks supplement actual focus and comprehension testing. Staff must demonstrate that they can find the intended item, identify its audience/language, distinguish personal save from Shared publication, resolve a required field and explain archive versus safety restriction. W3C combobox, character shortcuts, target size.

The D18 proof groups require those actual outcomes. No mockup, rendered UI, browser/AT test, ministry usability study or performance gain is claimed here.

### REQ26-D18-C012 — One capability, distinct effects

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Staff action or fact               | Authoritative owner                                                              | Exact boundary                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Save to My replies                 | Email Studio reusable authoring                                                  | Commit one validated immutable authoring revision for the current tenant-membership custodian. This is not Shared publication, sending or a system-message template.                                       |
| Save Shared draft / Publish        | Same Email Studio owner                                                          | Unpublished edits remain a candidate. Publish changes the reviewed usable revision under standard/protected/tenant-stricter policy. It sends nothing and does not rewrite existing drafts or preparations. |
| Offer to Shared                    | Same owner with existing review/attention capability                             | Freeze the deliberately offered candidate and establish permitted destination asset occurrences. Maintainers gain no access to other My content or the inspiring CRM/conversation.                         |
| Find and preview                   | Email Studio authorized asset projection, consumed in Support                    | Current tenant, person, purpose, language and audience govern search, counts, old revisions, favorites and assets. Support has no synchronized second library.                                             |
| Insert / Replace / Undo            | Support's current draft, consuming an eligible source revision                   | Copy structured wording and provenance with fresh fill-in occurrences. Preserve caret/draft and current purpose. No publication, message admission, CRM write or business action.                          |
| Insert information                 | Actual qualified source-domain context; shared validator/compiler                | Server resolves exact authorized values. Display access is not automatically external disclosure. No first related Party, recipient or assignee inference.                                                 |
| Fill-in answer                     | Current Support draft, using a qualified Email Studio authoring node             | One-use bounded text. Required missing fields block the applicable admission command. No library/CRM write or recursive syntax.                                                                            |
| Language and style                 | Email Studio structured item/variant and existing presentation owners            | Exact authored language revisions and supported semantic content. No live snippet/translation graph, raw HTML authority or new Layout Role.                                                                |
| Reusable file/image                | Actual governed asset owner plus library/destination occurrence                  | Exact revision, purpose, access, readiness and retention. No Shared hotlink to personal custody; actual case/receipt/action artifacts stay with their source owner.                                        |
| Add note                           | Support's authorized note command                                                | Shared structured validation, separate Internal note draft and retained internal-only provenance. No external preparation, P6 envelope, Resend or email-material lifetime.                                 |
| Send reply                         | Support D4 admission plus P17 qualified preparation                              | Exact approved reply/audience/work choice is validated, compiled and durably prepared before atomic local admission. Preparation itself has no dispatch authority.                                         |
| External delivery and its outcome  | P6 communication/dispatch owner; Resend executes transport                       | Seal exact connection, sender/reply identity, bytes, assets, member relationships and idempotency before I/O. Reconcile truthful accepted/delivered/rejected/unknown evidence.                             |
| Automatic new-request confirmation | D13 source producer + separate P17 catalog/publication/preparation contract + P6 | Uses the qualified **Support request received** Email Studio template, source eligibility, one recipient and original utility window. It is not a human saved reply.                                       |
| CRM and actual business action     | The actual CRM/giving/document/care domain                                       | Library activity creates no Party, interaction, last-contact date, refund, receipt or task completion. Actual governed communication contributes only proper P6 evidence.                                  |
| Restriction, expiry and disposal   | Actual source, asset and records owners under D16/D17/P17/P6                     | Known source copies keep restrictions. Draft, admitted content, prepared execution material, Recent copy and authoring assets have distinct lifetimes.                                                     |

### REQ26-D18-C013 — Logical flow for human work

This diagram shows responsibility, not new API names or a claim that these services already ship.

The same source revision appears in the permitted library from Support or CRM. Real recipient context is confined to the authorized draft and preparation; shared Email Studio authoring previews remain synthetic. A maintainer can improve generic wording without seeing the donor data used when someone later inserts it.

### REQ26-D18-C014 — Personal Save is not Shared publication

D18 qualifies a bounded personal authoring revision. An ordinary author can save eligible generic wording for their own use without invoking the tenant's another-reviewer-for-every-publication rule. That rule applies to actual publication, not every human composition or personal saved phrase.

This is not a protected-source bypass. My items cannot admit protected system/artifact/layout sources or recipient-specific protected material stripped of provenance. Shared publishing still uses the owner's current floor and exact candidate review. A general `layout.manage` capability or nullable owner field does not grant personal read, Shared publication or exceptional custody rights.

Human Support replies remain outside the finite system-message catalog. Saved wording is not a whole system-message template; a full answer is still bounded body content. No Personal correspondence or Support reply Layout Role, new Brand Kit, arbitrary template key, provider-hosted rendering authority or second compiler is created.

### REQ26-D18-C015 — Notes reuse authoring without becoming email

Reply and Internal note are independently qualified purposes. They can reuse structured validation and fill-in controls without sharing external send authority. Notes retain their own Support admission, current source access and later D17 content lifecycle. They do not use the external human-reply preparation-material class.

Mode changes preserve separate drafts. External preparation rejects internal-only provenance, including content restored through Replace/Undo. Selecting note wording does not add a note, notify mentioned staff, delegate work or alter status. Those effects require their actual authorized commands.

### REQ26-D18-C016 — Preparation, admission and Resend

Before human Send-and-work admission, P17 supplies the exact ready validated/compiled preparation under the D4-qualified human body and presentation contract. Support atomically admits that exact preparation, reply intent, any explicitly selected work transition, safe history and durable dispatch obligation. There is no database transaction around Resend I/O.

P6 then owns the exact sealed transport request, tenant connection and current send fences. No production path launches the Resend CLI, calls an app-local sender, invokes a mutable provider template alias, changes account on failure or rerenders on retry. Already possible external effects reconcile under D4/P6/ADR0032; a lost response does not authorize a new send. Local Queued is not Delivered.

Native To/Cc group handling requires D2/D4's separately qualified shared-submission/member contract; a Resend batch of independent messages does not prove it. Never send the whole group once per member. Record one canonical communication effect per admitted recipient copy, linked to the shared submission, and keep provider evidence at its actual specificity.

D4's distinct maximum seven-day human-reply preparation-material class is an implementation qualification, not a library-retention period or permission to extend an earlier source/safety/utility/provider deadline. P17 execution material and P6/owner-qualified Recent copy remain separate; neither is a permanent transcript archive.

### REQ26-D18-C017 — D13 automatic confirmation stays separate

The automatic **New request confirmation** has its own qualified source occurrence, closed P17 message meaning, compatible published **Support request received** template, material profile and current sender/return-route proof. The inbox setting preserves Preview/Edit in Email Studio and a return path to the inbox configuration.

Saving a personal phrase, publishing Shared wording or opening Email Studio cannot activate automatic confirmations or replay old requests. D13's single qualified recipient, suppression rules and original fifteen-minute utility window remain unchanged. Ordinary held-mail release cannot renew that window. The template confirms receipt only, not human review, financial completion or a response-time promise.

### REQ26-D18-C018 — Source and data continuity

- The reusable item, revision, variant, audience, asset occurrence and contribution are Email Studio-owned authoring facts. Support stores only its own draft/admitted content and the justified source/provenance references it consumes; it does not synchronize a second editable library.
- An unsent insertion stays draft material with inherited restrictions. After actual reply/note admission, its Support original follows D17. Generic active reusable wording has its own authoring purpose and retention; known case-derived material cannot escape source disposal by being renamed a saved reply.
- Ordinary library edits and Archive do not rewrite safe old drafts. Current audience narrowing and safety restrictions apply to retained revisions, links and new use through the appropriate owner fences. In-flight sends retain truthful evidence.
- Deliberately offered files establish destination-governed custody before broader exposure. Creator departure cannot break valid Shared artifacts, but actual source/asset restrictions continue to propagate.
- Saving, favoriting, offering, publishing and inserting create no communication occurrence or CRM interaction. Actual Send contributes one canonical communication effect per admitted recipient copy, with the shared submission relationship and evidence at its actual specificity; it never creates duplicate CRM history. CRM projections never become library write authority.

### REQ26-D18-C021 — Required constraints and mutation boundaries

Use tenant-aware keys/FKs across item, revision, locale, asset occurrence, contribution, preference and provenance relationships. Personal scope requires one tenant-membership custodian; Shared has tenant stewardship rather than a personal owner. Actor, tenant, custody and accepted time derive from trusted authenticated context. Enforce consistent scope/state/purpose/locale combinations and immutable accepted revisions. One current usable head exists per item/locale under its owner lifecycle. Titles and aliases are not primary keys; collision never exposes a hidden item or changes which item was selected.

No generic update may turn a personal row Shared by nulling owner, assign another custodian, rewrite published evidence or replace tenant/source identity. Shared promotion creates a destination candidate with exact disclosure checks, including files. Scope widening validates all exposed variants/assets; narrowing governs all retained revisions and deep links immediately according to the current authorization revision. Personal Save, Shared Publish, Offer, Withdraw, Archive, Restore and custody are distinct authorized effects even if they reuse infrastructure.

Use expected revisions and immutable operation input for concurrent edits and lost responses. Same operation/input reconciles its receipt; different input conflicts. Contribution withdrawal cannot retroactively delete a published Shared item. Source effect, safe audit and required owned-attention obligation commit together or use the existing transactional outbox. Ordinary library edits do not modify inserted drafts; ordinary Archive stops new insertion, while current safety restrictions and permissions govern future preparation/dispatch according to D4/P17/P6.

RLS USING and WITH CHECK, table/column grants, views/functions/RPCs, storage and privileged service paths must enforce the same boundary. Multiple permissive policies combine with OR; adding a nominally restrictive policy alongside broad staff access is insufficient. Current authorization precedes query membership, counts, search, exports and caches. A user with all-tenant administrative execution cannot use that service privilege as a substitute for personal/shared application policy. Opaque source IDs and cached data are not capabilities.

Control deletes explicitly. No staff/agent-parent cascade deletes shared content, message history, unresolved contributions, source restrictions or required provenance. Archived and restricted content cannot be restored by old writers, migration or backup replay. The source owner can dispose governed payload while retaining only justified safe evidence; immutability does not mean permanent readable content.

### REQ26-D18-C022 — Data classes and retention

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Class                                                          | Retention/correction rule                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active generic reusable wording                                | Continues only under its actual authoring purpose and owner policy; no arbitrary universal numeric expiry. |
| Abandoned drafts, superseded source, declined/withdrawn offers | Actual authoring retention and disposal; no indefinite readable versions by default.                       |
| Known case-derived text, files, URLs or rendered values        | Inherited source authority/correction applies; they cannot be laundered into generic library content.      |
| Unsent insertion and fill-in answers                           | Qualified draft lifetime, current author/source rights; no new admitted-message retention clock.           |
| Admitted messages and notes                                    | D17's actual original-content policy; note mode never becomes an email artifact.                           |
| P17 prepared material and P6/qualified Recent copy             | Independent tighter limits, immutable preparation and actual safety/reconciliation fences.                 |
| Compiled previews/search indexes/exports                       | Derived, permission-aware, revocable and disposed through the owner's current-source contract.             |
| Audit/operation/provenance/usage/preference facts              | Minimum allowed fields, named owner/purpose/horizon; no filled answers or before/after case HTML in logs.  |
| Backups/restore/replay controls                                | Actual owner lifecycle and barriers preventing resurrection before any ordinary serving resumes.           |

Every deployed class must have actual owner-approved horizons, scope and final disposition before activation. This is not a global indefinite metadata exception or a numerical retention policy for every Asym domain. D16/D17 remain ratified and unchanged.

### REQ26-D18-C023 — CRM journeys to prove

1. **Unknown requester:** staff inserts neutral shared wording, fills a one-use clarification field and sends through D1/D4 without creating a Party or storing the answer in CRM.
2. **Several related records:** a conversation concerns a person and an organization. The library cannot choose the first record. Any actual field resolution identifies the authorized source and common audience; ordinary neutral copy remains possible.
3. **Receipt request:** Support uses general instructions. The actual receipt correction/delivery follows its owner validation, approval and current artifact rules. The Support message does not manufacture a successful correction or duplicate official records.
4. **CRM-to-Support navigation:** the same permitted composer and draft uses the same library. Opening the asset editor reveals synthetic/generalized content, not the real recipient data used in that draft.
5. **Staff-only note:** note wording is inserted, filled and added through the note boundary. Switching to Reply cannot carry internal provenance into external mail. No P6 email preparation or Resend action occurs.
6. **Departure:** Shared remains usable under tenant stewardship, including independently valid assets. Personal ordinary use ends; same-email reinvitation does not confer old custody. Authorized records administration is separate and audited.

Saving, publishing or inserting produces no CRM communication, last-contact date, gift/refund state or task completion. The actual admitted send produces only its qualified P6 evidence. This is coherent context reuse, not data synchronization between a new help desk and another CRM.

## D18 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D18-O01

**Signal and threshold:** Any unauthorized personal/shared/CRM body, count, asset or export disclosure: 1 verified event

**Owner:** Security/platform incident owner

**Response:** Restrict the affected path, preserve safe evidence, repair and re-prove before reopening.

### OP26-D18-O02

**Signal and threshold:** Any known restricted/expired case copy admitted or revived in a library/offer/export: 1

**Owner:** Email Studio/source-custody owner

**Response:** Restrict affected copies and actual dependencies, run governed cleanup, repair the admission path.

### OP26-D18-O03

**Signal and threshold:** Accepted save/publish/offer has no reconciled result or required attention after 15 minutes, or 3 consecutive owner failures, whichever first

**Owner:** Email Studio engineering on-call

**Response:** Reconcile original identity, recover the owner outbox, preserve drafts and prohibit blind replacement.

### OP26-D18-O04

**Signal and threshold:** Pending shared contribution has no eligible responsible work home, or passes its explicitly recorded review due date: 1

**Owner:** Tenant shared-library maintainer

**Response:** Assign/review or close the specific offer through existing work; do not send routine team-wide reminder storms.

### OP26-D18-O05

**Signal and threshold:** Any new unauthorized use after membership/capability loss or safety revocation: 1

**Owner:** Identity/library security owner

**Response:** Stop stale read/use path, invalidate projections safely, audit custody and re-prove revocation.

### OP26-D18-O06

**Signal and threshold:** p95 library command/search latency exceeds its published qualified budget for 15 minutes, or queue exceeds measured supported capacity

**Owner:** Support/platform operations

**Response:** Apply fair backpressure, diagnose queries/owner failures and remeasure; preserve authorized plain composition.

### OP26-D18-O07

**Signal and threshold:** Wrong published head, duplicate durable publication, lost required provenance, restore barrier failure or sensitive audit payload: 1

**Owner:** Email Studio/database owner

**Response:** Stop unsafe mutations/restore, reconcile immutable evidence, repair and rerun the failed boundary tests.

### REQ26-D18-C024 — Operating and qualification sequence

**Capture in implementation spec/design:** first the narrow P17 authoring-scope and manual-field extensions plus source dependencies; then tenant-aware identity/revisions/ACLs/asset lifecycle; then publication/contribution/custody and idempotency; then the complete picker/editor/CRM journey. The owner contract determines what the UI may safely promise.

**Require during implementation:** repair/fence current raw CRUD/canned/macro paths, qualify current source reads and artifacts, implement guarded mutations and projection/attention recovery, migrate inertly, and prove P01–P50 across real owners and UX.
