These are release gates, not monitor-only exceptions.

**Monitor after those gates pass.** The thresholds below are accepted operating controls, not measured availability or new permission/retention grace periods.

## D19 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D19-R01 — Scope and one accountable operating model

Support Hub owns the ordinary business-review decision for accepted input that is already bound to a trustworthy tenant and a qualified review scope. Designate reviewers per responsible inbox, backed by tenant oversight; one eligible team may cover multiple or all inboxes. Reuse Core membership, teams, authorization, attention and durable work capabilities after qualifying them for this purpose. Do not create a new omnipotent reviewer role, a second help desk, CRM, classification engine or tenant workflow builder.

### REQ26-D19-R02 — Reasons and authority determine available actions

Retain independent evidence for every current gate. Present one plain-language primary reason plus expandable additional reasons; compute allowed actions from the intersection of all gates, not the first or least restrictive reason. Routine reviewable uncertainty can be decided by eligible intake reviewers. Missing content/provider retrieval uses technical recovery; unsafe files, non-overridable security restrictions and care classification use the actual safety/classification/care owner. Conflicting or unknown tenant binding remains separately authorized platform recovery. A generic release command cannot clear those gates. Closing one reason leaves the item held if another still blocks admission.

### REQ26-D19-R03 — Configuration that shows effective coverage

In the existing inbox settings, use one **Intake review** section: **Reviewers**, **Backup**, and the tenant **Oversight owner** reference. Support named existing people or teams, not copied users or email addresses. Select only qualified candidates within the configuring actor's authority; show effective eligible coverage, not raw team size. Assignment of review responsibility alone grants no body, conversation, CRM or restricted-data access. One eligible reviewer is sufficient; multiple eligible people or a qualified backup are recommended, not a mandatory two-person approval rule. The same person can cover a small tenant's roles with a clear single-person coverage indication.

Before new real inbox activation, require a viable review route, finite owner-qualified content schedule and an accountable oversight route. Configuration edits use versioned guarded commands and show resulting coverage before save. Removing the last qualified coverage route through settings requires a replacement; security revocation or offboarding always proceeds immediately and creates a coverage exception rather than being blocked to protect staffing.

### REQ26-D19-R04 — Absence, team changes and oversight

Evaluate current tenant membership, relevant inbox/review scope, source classification and action permission on every list, preview and command. Team membership changes cannot silently confer a missing base permission. Planned absence uses existing availability/coverage information where sound; do not build an on-call scheduler. A backup may act whenever independently eligible and remains visible as coverage. Stale or unavailable primary coverage raises one source-owned attention condition for the named oversight owner. That owner can repair staffing under actual administration permissions or use a separately authorized review capability; oversight does not imply message-body access. Coverage loss does not discard retained mail, fabricate a completed review, or grant replacement staff access automatically.

### REQ26-D19-R05 — Quiet, source-authorized queue

Show **Needs review** within Support Hub and as an inbox-scoped view for eligible staff. Default to items requiring a business decision; keep technical recovery visibly separate as **Processing issues** for qualified operators. List authorized sender/address, subject or safe fallback, responsible inbox, plain reason, received age and content expiry. No body snippets by default. An informational header says: “Incoming email held before it enters Support work.” It does not call every item spam or a ticket. Include **To review**, **Processing**, and **History** views; history filters distinguish Released, Dismissed and Expired. Counts, search matches, pagination and empty states are authorized at source, including metadata. “No messages need a decision” requires successful loading of the stated scope and must not conceal authorized pending releases. Unknown or partial scope is explicit without leaking concealed records. Processing here means pending release only; Processing issues remains the qualified technical-recovery view. They reference the same source rather than duplicate it.

### REQ26-D19-R06 — Inspect without executing incoming content

Use a read-only text-first preview; provide qualified sanitized formatting only when useful. Block scripts, forms, active embeds, remote images/tracking, automatic link fetching, mailto actions and browser navigation from the message. Link text and actual destination can be inspected as inert text. Normal review does not expose raw provider download URLs, raw MIME downloads or open unscanned files. Attachments show safe names or neutral labels, actual availability and scan status; preview/download requires the separately qualified asset path and current source permission. A failed or pending scan is not a clean file. Provider file fetching uses the qualified connection, bounded size/type checks and permitted URL/redirect policy; it is not an arbitrary URL-fetch proxy. Displaying body content is itself authorized sensitive access. Store original permitted evidence separately from its display representation; do not recover by copying plain text and dropping original HTML/files.

### REQ26-D19-R07 — Authentication is evidence, not identity

Derive tenant/provider binding and machine verification evidence from trusted receiver context, not user-editable email fields. A signed Resend webhook proves the provider event's provenance, not the human sender's identity, business authority or harmlessness. Authentication-Results headers require a qualified receiver trust boundary; text supplied by the sender cannot certify itself. Present useful distinctions such as “Sender checks could not be confirmed,” with technical details on demand. A familiar name, matching CRM email, shared address, valid domain signature, quoted forward or reviewer recognition alone grants no identity/CRM access. Routine false-positive review can admit an eligible input without promoting uncertain evidence to verified identity. It cannot override a separately non-overridable rule.

### REQ26-D19-R08 — One deliberate release

In the preview, show **Release to [inbox]** with the qualified destination and whether intake will create a new conversation or continue an identified authorized conversation. If that outcome is not yet provable, say it will be checked during processing; never promise “new ticket” or silently attach to an arbitrary record. Show concise scope copy: “Only this message. Future mail rules stay the same.” An explicit review of this summary is the ordinary confirmation; do not add a second generic “Are you sure?” dialog when scope is unchanged. Admit a source-version-bound decision, recheck every gate and record one durable processing obligation. Show **Release requested** until canonical admission is proven, then **Released** with the authorized destination link. Release is not Send, Resolve, registration, email verification, allowlisting, a refund or any other business action. When D13 confirmation may still apply, show “The usual new-request confirmation may follow if this message is eligible”; never promise no email can follow admission.

### REQ26-D19-R09 — Destination and continuation corrections

A reviewer may choose a one-item destination only when separately authorized for the source, destination and review action. Missing or ambiguous routing goes to the qualified tenant routing owner; it never chooses the first candidate, searches message text for a tenant or exposes unauthorized inbox names. Qualified continuation uses D1/D2 correlation and current restrictions; subject/sender similarity does not prove a thread. Do not offer free-form forced attachment to an arbitrary conversation. Unresolved correlation remains reviewable by its proper owner; choosing a genuinely new conversation, where permitted, is an explicit decision preserving original references and not guessing identity. Persistent **Change future routing** is a separate owner action with its own scope/impact review, never a checked default beside one-item release. It must not automatically grant held-content admission or supersede another reviewer's dismissal.

### REQ26-D19-R10 — Dismissal and correction

**Dismiss** means “Keep this message out of Support work.” It records one typed reason and removes the item from To review; it neither blocks future mail nor deletes a CRM contact or immediately destroys content. Show “Recoverable until [exact original deadline]” and a persistent **Return to review** action in History while current authority and content lifetime permit. A transient Undo can invoke that same command, but is never the only recovery route. Returning to review does not release, renew content retention or clear safety gates. At expiry the action becomes unavailable with an honest explanation; no background lag extends the recovery promise. Preserve Dismissed as the historical decision and Content expired as current availability; expiry does not rewrite who decided or imply a missed business review.

### REQ26-D19-R11 — Bounded bulk work

Allow bulk Dismiss for explicitly selected, currently authorized reviewable items, with one reviewed reason and an exact selection summary. Limit selection to the loaded page of at most 50 items; no “all matching,” bulk release, future-sender policy or permanent deletion. Fifty is the accepted bounded UI/command safety limit, not a vendor performance claim. Revalidate each selected source and return per-item outcomes; never claim whole-batch success after a partial conflict. No body-prefetch requirement or cross-tenant batch. Individual release and one-item recovery remain the deliberate normal path. Reassess adding other bulk effects only for demonstrated work and independent authorization.

### REQ26-D19-R12 — Qualified handoffs and technical recovery

**Ask the responsible team** uses existing restricted staff work/attention with a source reference and typed reason, not emailed copies of the body. It transfers or establishes accountable review scope only after destination authority is proven; the source cannot lose its sole accountable owner before destination custody/obligation is durable. Do not create a second Support conversation merely to investigate intake. Technical **Retry retrieval** repairs body/file availability and runs current source/expiry guards; it does not approve safety, future policy or identity. Safe attachment-only inputs are not rejected merely because text is empty. A genuinely unavailable essential body stays visibly unavailable; an optional unavailable file may follow D1's qualified partial-content path without implying the file passed checks. No blanket “ignore all errors.”

### REQ26-D19-R13 — One durable input and admission effect

Use the canonical accepted-input identity and its source generation, with a separately recorded review-decision sequence. Provider retries, duplicate webhook IDs, repeat commands and worker retries must reconcile that input's single current admission result. One source may legitimately map to permitted recipient occurrences under D1; never duplicate a conversation/message merely because a transport request ID changed. Atomically commit the review decision, source version and durable dispatch/outbox obligation. Canonical Support admission atomically commits its own source linkage/custody and receipt once. If a shared database permits one transaction, use it; otherwise keep the durable intermediate state and reconcile by authoritative effect identity. No provider I/O occurs inside the transaction. The stable admission-effect identity belongs to the canonical input and each D1-qualified recipient occurrence; source/gate revisions, review decisions and attempt IDs are fences and lineage, not reasons for another admission effect. Cancel release invalidates its pending decision/continuation generation. A later eligible release records a new decision and attempt against the same stable admission-effect identity: old canceled workers cannot act, and an earlier canceled attempt cannot permanently suppress valid re-release.

### REQ26-D19-R14 — Trusted attribution and tenant-aware data

Derive tenant, actor authentication ID, actual profile/membership ID, owner capability and decision time from trusted server context. Do not substitute auth user ID for profile ID merely because development rows happen to match. Stored tenant-owned review/source/inbox/conversation/team/route endpoints enforce equal tenant identity structurally. Global auth/profile identities, where applicable, bind through authoritative tenant membership and the actual acting-profile relationship rather than a copied tenant identity. Foreign keys establish relational integrity; current authorization/classification remains required at each command and admission fence. Use composite tenant-aware foreign keys or an equivalent constrained authoritative boundary, non-null tenant for tenant-review rows, no self-contradictory state combinations, positive monotonic versions, exact typed reason/status values and unique durable business-effect keys. Unbound input remains outside tenant review, not tenant-null rows exposed through a broad fallback. No cascading parent delete may erase required evidence or detach policy authority silently.

### REQ26-D19-R15 — RLS, grants and privileged execution

Keep raw intake, review commands and sensitive mutation server-owned through the shared business API. RLS-enabled tables with no anon/authenticated grants are a valid server-only design; they do not need permissive browser policies. Privileged services must still prove exact tenant, current source and action scope. Revoke direct review-state, tenant, attribution, admission and audit mutations from general staff paths. Any approved direct-read projection uses current tenant and source predicates. If an UPDATE policy exists, USING must qualify the old row and WITH CHECK the new allowed state; immutable scope/actor fields cannot be transformed through an allowed update. Qualify every RPC/view/storage/cache/export path and SECURITY DEFINER search path/execution grant. Never treat UI filtering or a generic admin/staff label as the boundary.

### REQ26-D19-R16 — Durable history without a content archive

Keep source occurrence, original receipt evidence, review reason/policy revision, actor/membership attribution, chosen scope, decision sequence, actual admission/outcome and correction lineage as typed owner-qualified history. Append corrections rather than rewrite historical decisions. Durable business history is distinct from technical logs and notification engagement. Audit carries no copied subject/body/raw headers, credentials, provider URLs or arbitrary pasted sensitive reason. If explanatory text is truly required, it is bounded classified content with its own permitted lifetime; default reasons remain typed. Body-free facts are potentially identifying and need an owner horizon, access and anonymization/disposal contract. Existing mutable support_audit_log grants are not append-only proof.

### REQ26-D19-R17 — Concurrency and expired authority

Release, Dismiss, Return to review, gate changes, destination changes, permission revocation and admission/expiry share current source-version guards and a defined serialization point. Stale decisions conflict with a readable current outcome instead of overwriting. At an exact content deadline, admission is forbidden; admission must commit strictly before the deadline. A later fetch, retry, browser tab, route repair or policy lengthening cannot rehydrate expired content. Outbox replay rechecks current gates, content frontier and approved scope before positive effects. At admission the decision must remain qualified for its deciding actor/designation and current source/destination; the worker's service privileges do not substitute. Revocation before admission blocks the pending effect and records an owned current outcome. Admission that already committed retains truthful historical attribution, with current restrictions governing subsequent access/effects. Use the qualified owner fences, not a new global platform version counter. A worker cannot dismiss/expire a source using an obsolete policy version. Missing proof fails closed for that effect, with an accountable recovery state; uncertainty is not fabricated success.

### REQ26-D19-R18 — Correct a mistaken release truthfully

Before canonical admission commits, a qualified **Cancel release** may stop a pending release through the same current source guard. If admission has committed or cannot yet be reconciled, the UI must not promise Undo or deletion: reconcile first, then offer the authorized conversation/source correction path. Existing D9/D10/D16 owner commands handle wrong links, actual duplicates or unsafe admitted content; stop unsafe pending effects through their actual owner. Never unsend mail, erase valid staff work, delete CRM facts or make a delivered message disappear to simulate reversal. Preserve original review and correction evidence. A later security restriction always applies even if the earlier decision was legitimate.

### REQ26-D19-R19 — Finite ordinary held-content schedule

Use **14 elapsed days from the first qualified provider receipt** as the ordinary business-review content schedule, published through the actual intake/records owner. This is a product judgment providing two calendar weeks for routine review and short absences; it is not a universal legal period or a claim of measured optimality. The earlier applicable mandatory owner ceiling wins. Missing trustworthy original receipt uses a bounded owner-reconciliation exception, not now, migration time or email Date as a fresh timestamp. Reads, touches, review reopening, retries, rule changes, dismissal and repeated receipts never renew the anchor.

Use one tenant-level owner-qualified held-content policy, displayed from inbox settings; no per-reviewer or per-inbox timer hierarchy and no Never. Tenant changes select only published owner-qualified finite schedule variants/limits; the default is 14 days, and no additional arbitrary duration is authorized by this decision. Publishing or changing a qualified variant requires the actual intake semantic owner and records/private-byte contract, not a generic tenant timer. An authorized schedule change requires the existing policy-owner review/publication contract, showing old/new periods, affected existing unexpired scope and exact effective-time semantics; reviewers cannot extend an item. Shortening cannot silently dispose hidden or unclassified scope. Lengthening strictly before expiry can affect remaining permitted life; at/after expiry it cannot revive bytes. Technical, security/care and unbound input are separately owned classes with explicit finite access/review/disposal or restricted-preservation schedules. Do not force them into ordinary dismissal or the D17 Resolved-work clock. For unknown original receipt, use a separate restricted timing-recovery class: anchor it once to trusted first durable platform acceptance where known, otherwise to the explicitly recorded first restricted-recovery registration for legacy evidence. Normal recovery access ends no later than 14 elapsed days from that recovery anchor, earlier known source ceilings still win, and source-owned review attention is due at 24 elapsed hours. Registration never fabricates provider receipt, resets prior restrictions or grants routine body access. Qualify original evidence before ordinary release; if its true cutoff has passed, ordinary admission remains forbidden. At recovery cutoff, ordinary recovery access ends, while actual required preservation or unknown-preservation handling stays restricted with a finite owner review date; no repeated registration renews it.

### REQ26-D19-R20 — Expiry, holds and copy custody

At the ordinary cutoff, end routine content visibility and release/recovery authority even if cleanup workers lag; record **Expired before admission** or the actual dismissed-expired outcome. Admission approval alone cannot establish a new D17 lifetime: only actual qualified Support admission/custody strictly before cutoff can do so, with its truthful readiness event. Dispose redundant intake copies under their actual transient-copy schedule; do not retain duplicate MIME forever after admission. Cleanup retires only the redundant occurrence/copy, never a shared authoritative blob still needed by the admitted source or another qualified owner.

Phase 26 owns the meaning of its intake schedule; the Phase 21 catalog does not classify intake or become its semantic owner. Reuse D16 source restriction and the existing qualified records/private-byte execution mechanisms for disposal and restore barriers to bodies, headers, safe previews, attachments, derived text, review exports, caches and retained provider copies. A legal/records/security preservation obligation can retain remaining required bytes in restricted custody without ordinary review access; unknown preservation blocks destruction and raises an owned exception, not an unlimited Reveal. Do not claim physical deletion, provider recall or backups erased until independently proved. Provider-retained bytes cannot become a rehydration route. Before live activation, every retained class/copy must have an owner, finite normal horizon, hold behavior, recovery boundary and disposal evidence contract; an unqualified class blocks its activation rather than being silently omitted.

### REQ26-D19-R21 — Honest clocks and downstream eligibility

Keep first qualified provider receipt, first durable platform acceptance, gate/readiness transitions, review decision, canonical Support-ready admission and processing outcome separately. D14 reply-target time starts at its qualified source-ready event; queue age remains visible so a review delay cannot be concealed. Do not backdate readiness to provider receipt or reset original age to release time. D13 automatic request confirmation remains eligible only under its original rules and strictly before qualified first provider receipt plus 15 minutes; review never starts a new utility window, clears automation/loop suppression or creates a second confirmation. Reviewing, dismissing or admitting input is not a human reply, resolution, satisfied business action or achieved target.

### REQ26-D19-R22 — CRM continuity and minimum necessary context

Held input is not an ordinary CRM conversation/communication row and must not update last-contact, create or merge a Party, establish a related-record association, assert verified identity, or perform a CRM mutation automatically, register a user, change consent or verify an address. Authorized read-only identity lookup follows the existing owner semantics; a candidate never establishes person identity, representation or a related-record association. D9-R02 correspondence eligibility still requires genuinely admitted source-message evidence and is not created by a held-item lookup. An eligible reviewer may open already-authorized CRM context when necessary through the normal owner surface; recognizing a correspondent is not permission to expose their giving, location or care data. On actual admission, D1/D2 identity distinctions and D9 qualified source-backed CRM discovery apply exactly once. Requester, message participant, authenticated user, CRM Party/relationship, assigned worker, reviewer and CRM owner remain distinct. CRM merge/deletion/link changes never rewrite original evidence or trigger re-ingestion. No synchronization between two Asym-owned CRM copies is introduced. Actual financial, receipt, recurring-gift, contact or care actions retain their domain permissions, approvals and truthful histories.

### REQ26-D19-R23 — Email Studio, Resend and attention

Review UI is not an email composer. Keep D18's ratified Email Studio ownership of reusable content and prepared human replies, and D13's separate qualified **Support request received** template. Intake Release/Dismiss/Retry use neither a canned reply nor an ad hoc email template. Resend remains the qualified receiving provider; tenant/provider authority must be proven before fetch/replay, and Phase 6 remains the only external dispatch/evidence owner. Raw provider URLs and connection secrets stay server-side.

Use the shared in-product attention capability for coverage failure, aged unresolved review and expiring unresolved content; qualify a bounded source meaning and the existing source-actionable presentation policy before enabling it. Group by tenant/inbox/condition and reauthorize at display. Read/archive is not source completion. Default reviewer attention is in-product with no per-message email, external sender notification, push/body digest or dedicated notification engine. Any implementation email channel must use an exact Email Studio meaning/template plus P6/tenant Resend; it cannot be assembled by a queue worker or extend source lifetime.

### REQ26-D19-R24 — Coverage, aging and reporting

Show live authorized backlog by reason and oldest received age, plus distinct Processing issues, coverage gaps and approaching expiry. Default ordinary reviewer attention is due after **24 elapsed hours**, including weekends, from the once-set first routine-reviewable admission; also surface inputs already older than 24 hours at that point. This is an internal operational threshold, not a donor promise, business-hours SLA or D14 reply target. Before expiry, surface unresolved ordinary content with **48 elapsed hours or less remaining**; already-shorter schedules surface immediately. Changing responsible inbox, reviewer, reason or returning from dismissal does not reset that first-reviewable time. Do not send repeated alerts per item. One grouped active condition stays actionable until resolved; no per-user leaderboard.

Report received occurrences, business-reviewable occurrences, released admissions, dismissed decisions, expired-before-admission, corrections, unresolved age and technical delay as distinct units. A release request is not released. Show cohort, timestamps, scope, unknowns and excluded classes. “Released after review” is an operational outcome, not a measured false-positive rate; actual correctness needs qualified sampling evidence. Do not count hidden records in unauthorized totals or erase previous delays/misses when responsibility or policy changes. Use current actionable owner for recovery and immutable original attribution for historical evidence.

### REQ26-D19-R25 — Reuse qualified capabilities and retire conflicting paths

Extend the canonical intake/source workflow, guarded API boundary, existing team/permission system, source-backed CRM read model, Email Studio/P6 and records/asset owners. Requalify rather than blindly reuse current retry, route-resume, first-match threading, audit or broad staff endpoints. Preserve actual provider evidence and legacy input identity while consolidating the older parallel Support path. The existing future-route command cannot be relabeled single-message release. Leave Phase 34 as the sole configurable rule-engine owner. No queue-specific CRM, new sender registry, local template/compiler, custom security scanner or generic review/approval platform is introduced.

### REQ26-D19-R26 — Bounded performance and abuse resilience

Use tenant/review-scope/state/deadline indexes and stable cursor pagination; page size defaults to 25 with a hard maximum of 50. Fetch body/asset details only on authorized inspection. Counts are bounded projections with stated freshness and current authorization; never label an incomplete count zero. Separate attachment retrieval and cleanup into bounded owner work with tenant fairness, durable retry and rate-limit-aware backoff. Review responsibility does not bypass intake abuse controls or trigger one notification per hostile email. The inherited workflow's current retry/concurrency numbers are code facts, not demonstrated D19 capacity. Before release, record the tested tenant/queue/attachment/burst/skew profile, concurrency and measurable latency/error/backlog limits, then require capacity to complete work within active content/review windows; no unsupported scale promise is ratified.

### REQ26-D19-R27 — Safe migration and activation

Ship additive source identities/constraints/decision history before activating new readers or writers. Reconcile legacy tenant/reference/actor/timestamp gaps; do not guess values, backfill reviewer approval, generate duplicate messages, restart old clocks or retroactively purge unknown mail. Invalid legacy items remain in an owned bounded reconciliation class with restricted access. Stop conflicting old writers before new authority is enabled. Activate per tenant/inbox only after qualified coverage, copy schedules, source/asset safety, provider contract, authorization and proof gates pass. Use a write kill switch and separate read/cleanup controls; disabling dispatch never removes restriction/expiry enforcement. Rollback preserves new decisions, tombstones and negative controls; old binaries unable to honor them cannot resume writes. Prefer forward repair after irreversible effects.

### REQ26-D19-R28 — Operational ownership and recovery

The controls O01–O08 below are required operational contracts after release gates pass. Source owners handle business correction; platform owners handle transport/storage/durable-work failures; security/records owners handle restricted preservation and disposal. Provide scoped retry/reconciliation and receipts in normal tools, not recurring direct SQL repair. An alert is resolved by correcting its source condition, not marking a notification read. For irreversibly missed intake, the source-owned operational review records a typed cause and remedial action or explicit no-further-action conclusion under oversight authority; that completes the review obligation without changing the original expiry/miss or rehydrating content. A deliberately dismissed item later expiring has no missed-business-review obligation. Incidents preserve permitted evidence and publish an accurate status to affected qualified staff without copying sensitive content.

### REQ26-D19-R29 — Proof and traceability

Preserve the founder selection, all required amendments, considered alternatives, evidence classifications and limits in the grill record, accepted feature ADR and glossary. P01–P42 are required user-visible/domain proof groups, not tests executed by this review. Documentation consistency and read-only source observations are separately reported. No “complete” claim may convert source inspection, a mocked screen, current broad grants or a vendor screenshot into actual tenant/runtime safety proof.

### REQ26-D19-R30 — Deliberately limited scope

The complete launch journey is configure coverage, inspect, decide, correct, recover and oversee. It does not add a requester quarantine portal, automatic trust learning, AI release decisions, reply-from-quarantine, mass allowlists, mandatory two-person review, routine legal approval, mailbox synchronization, enterprise security console or another workflow platform. A person may receive review authority and remain unable to read a restricted conversation or CRM record. International names/addresses remain intact; translated labels and exact local dates support comprehension without transforming identifier equality or pausing server clocks.

### REQ26-D19-C001 — 1. Configure responsibility once

Open **Settings → Shared inboxes → Donor care → Intake review**. The tenant's actual naming/navigation conventions govern the final location; do not create a second Settings hierarchy if the existing one provides this scope.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Field            | Behavior and wording                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reviewers        | Existing eligible people or teams. “Reviews incoming email held before it enters this inbox.” Show effective eligible coverage, not all team members.                                                                         |
| Backup           | Existing qualified person/team. “Can cover review when needed.” Optional when adequate coverage exists; no forced second approver.                                                                                            |
| Tenant oversight | Named accountable owner/reference from tenant settings. “Keeps review coverage and unresolved work on track.” This does not grant message access.                                                                             |
| Held content     | Read-only summary of the current owner-qualified tenant schedule, with **Manage policy** only for the actual policy owner. Proposed ordinary default: 14 elapsed days from qualified receipt; earlier restrictions can apply. |

Use an ordinary searchable people/team picker, selected chips and inline effective-coverage status. Show **Coverage ready**, **Single-person coverage** or **No eligible reviewers** with text and a restrained icon. A coverage change reviews only affected responsibility/access facts; it is not a legal checklist or a second role system. The system must never silently grant broader access to make a selected person eligible.

New inbox activation needs viable coverage and qualified lifecycle/provider safeguards. Routine removal of the last reviewer asks for a replacement as part of that settings transaction. Emergency access revocation always succeeds; it leaves an owned coverage exception. One person or one central team can cover a small tenant. A reviewer who leaves does not retain access through an old assignment or notification.

Policy editing remains a link to the existing owner capability. It shows the old/new finite schedule, exact effective time, affected existing unexpired content, unresolved/unknown exclusions, and shortening/irreversibility consequences. The ordinary reviewer cannot click Keep forever or extend one item. The 14-day proposal is a product default, not legal advice or a promise overriding actual provider/owner ceilings. Only published owner-qualified finite variants/bounds are selectable; this decision does not authorize arbitrary tenant-entered periods.

### REQ26-D19-C002 — 2. Notice only meaningful work

The Support sidebar includes **Needs review** for eligible staff. Its count covers only the stated current authorized scope. A reviewer opening Donor care lands in that inbox scope; a reviewer covering several inboxes can choose **My review inboxes** without loading unauthorized names or counts.

Within Needs review:

- **To review**: an ordinary business decision is currently available.
- **Processing**: a release decision is accepted but canonical admission is not yet proved.
- **History**: authorized released, dismissed and expired outcomes, with filters.

**Processing issues** is the qualified operator's separate technical-recovery view. “Processing” in Needs review means pending release, not every provider fault. When a release develops a technical issue, its row says **Processing needs attention**, references the same source and qualified recovery route, and does not create duplicate work. Restricted/platform cases are shown only in their actual authorized surfaces; the ordinary list does not reveal hidden case existence through counters or placeholders.

The first-use/empty helper is one sentence: “Incoming email held before it enters Support work.” The normal row shows sender, subject or safe fallback, inbox, reason, received age and a quiet expiry date. No message-body snippets, avatars implying verified identity, decorative warning cards or flashing timers. Use optional filters for inbox, reason and disposition, and authorized text search. Default page size is 25; maximum 50. Search remains bounded to permitted retained fields, and a search term must not expose an expired or restricted match.

The queue preserves sort, filters, scroll and selected item while inspecting, returning from CRM, or recovering a request. Do not reorder the row under a pointer during an action. After a completed action, keep its receipt visible and let staff choose Next; never send a release click to a newly shifted row.

### REQ26-D19-C003 — 3. Inspect one input

Illustrative scenario, not a claimed observed ministry workflow: a church's legitimate donor-care question is held as possible spam. Alex, an eligible reviewer, opens it. The detail pane uses this reading order:

This is information hierarchy, not a pixel-perfect mockup. Use a desktop split pane and a full-width detail route on narrow screens; avoid a tall modal for reading email. Dates use the viewer's locale with an accessible exact date/time/timezone detail. IDs and addresses retain exact meaningful characters. Names do not require first/last splitting; long names, international scripts and right-to-left display must not obscure the actual sender address or link destination.

**Details** expands typed source evidence such as authentication uncertainty, original destination and processing status. The server determines the current reason and action set. An email claiming “verified by Asym” remains quoted sender content, visually separate from system evidence. Several gates can coexist; show the most relevant next step with **2 more checks** only when those details/counts are authorized.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Reason shown                | Meaning                                                            | Permitted next step                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Possible spam               | Reviewable uncertainty, not established abuse.                     | Inspect; Release or Dismiss if all other gates permit.                               |
| Sender check needs review   | Qualified receiving evidence is incomplete or discrepant.          | Decide only if this class permits human review; otherwise refer to its actual owner. |
| Destination needs review    | Tenant is known, but routing/correlation needs a qualified choice. | Select an authorized one-item destination or ask the routing owner.                  |
| Waiting for message content | Essential provider content is not yet available.                   | Qualified technical retry; no false security approval.                               |
| File check pending          | Required asset assessment is incomplete.                           | Wait/owner recovery; no “Open anyway.”                                               |
| Restricted review required  | Actual classification/security owner must act.                     | Qualified referral only; conceal body and even reason/existence where not permitted. |

Preview blocks external loads, scripts/forms/active embeds and clickable message links. Actual link destinations remain inspectable as inert text. Formatting is sanitized by the qualified shared renderer; text view remains available. Do not use the provider dashboard's public-sharing feature or hand reviewers raw temporary download URLs. Only an eligible scanned asset occurrence can use Core's governed preview/download action. File unavailability remains visible if the qualified input can otherwise proceed; it is not silently discarded.

### REQ26-D19-C004 — 4. Release deliberately

The primary button names the authorized target: **Release to Donor care**. The consequence summary is the confirmation. Another generic modal would add a step without clarifying scope. If the target or relevant gates changed since inspection, stop with **This message changed. Review the latest details** and show the actual current state.

If a valid conversation continuation is already known and visible, show its reference. If only the permitted inbox scope is settled, explain that normal intake will check continuation during processing; do not pretend that every release creates a new conversation. Do not offer free-form forced linking to arbitrary conversations.

When D13's original confirmation may still apply, show one conditional line: **The usual new-request confirmation may follow if this message is eligible.** Never promise that release can send no email whatsoever. No composer, recipient picker, canned reply or template editor appears here. Human replies occur later in the normal conversation; automated confirmation retains the original 15-minute eligibility ceiling and all suppression rules.

After clicking, disable the same action until the server outcome is reconciled and show **Release requested**. On a lost response, **Checking result…** uses the original operation identity; Retry must not create another request identity. Once admission is proved, show **Released to Donor care · Open conversation** if that link is authorized. If admission fails, preserve **Processing needs attention** and its proper recovery path. A reviewer who lacks destination conversation access may receive only the authorized processing result, not a backdoor link or title.

### REQ26-D19-C005 — 5. Dismiss and recover a mistake

Dismiss asks for a small typed reason selection, for example **Unwanted message** or **Not Support work**. The latter is not a substitute for a known required care/routing handoff. Show **Keep out of Support work** and **Recoverable until [date/time]** beside confirmation. No preselected “Block sender” checkbox. No contact deletion, future policy change, automated reply or immediate destructive delete.

After the decision, show **Dismissed · Return to review**. The same action is available in History until the original cutoff; a toast is supplementary. Recovery returns the input to current review under its remaining gates, not directly into Support. If expired, preserve the **Dismissed** decision and show **Content expired** with permitted typed evidence and no unusable recovery button. For inputs with no decision, show **Content expired before admission**; never fabricate a human dismissal.

For a burst of obvious unwanted inputs, staff can select specific loaded rows and **Dismiss selected**. Review exact count and reason; maximum 50, never all filtered results. Partial conflicts produce per-item outcomes and leave unresolved items visible. Do not offer bulk Release or permanent deletion. These bounds are accepted product choices for manageable review, not research-derived optimal batch sizes.

### REQ26-D19-C006 — 6. Ask for qualified help

When Alex cannot determine a destination or needs a restricted owner, **Ask responsible team** refers the same source through the existing qualified internal-work capability. It carries a typed reason and source reference. No forwarding of raw mail, copying a transcript, opening another conversation or expanding reviewer permissions. The UI states who now owns the next action only to the extent that scope is visible. Sending a request cannot drop the last accountable owner before the receiving obligation/custody is durable.

A technical operator can retry a failed fetch without approving a suspicious message. A security owner can resolve a false detection through its proper procedure without certifying the human sender. Ordinary staff do not receive an override switch that treats every held reason alike.

### REQ26-D19-C007 — 7. Correct a mistaken release

If release is pending, **Cancel release** attempts a guarded cancellation only while canonical admission has not committed. A race returns the actual result: **Already released** or **Returned to review**. Unknown results remain under reconciliation.

After actual admission, use **Open conversation** and the existing authorized source/link/restriction correction actions. Do not display universal Undo. Valid later replies, target history and CRM facts cannot be erased merely to restore a prettier queue. A safety incident uses the actual source restriction owner immediately; no claim can recall mail already delivered to another mailbox.

### REQ26-D19-C008 — 8. Oversight without a wall of alerts

The tenant oversight view summarizes permitted inbox coverage, unresolved age, pending release issues and approaching expiry. It does not require access to every message body. Restricted scopes may be omitted or represented only through a separately authorized aggregate, never guessed totals labeled tenant-wide.

One grouped in-product condition becomes actionable when coverage is missing, ordinary review reaches 24 elapsed hours (or enters already older), or unresolved content has 48 elapsed hours or less left. Show **Review due**, **Expires tomorrow** or exact due date with restrained semantic emphasis, not live second-by-second counters. These elapsed-hour thresholds include weekends and are not a response promise to the sender. First-reviewable age does not restart on reassignment or recovery. A calendar pause, read notification or hidden browser tab cannot pause content expiry or satisfy the source condition. Routine new held input does not send an email to every reviewer.

Report units clearly: received inputs, held inputs, actual admitted releases, dismissals, expiries and corrections. “Released after review” is not called “false-positive rate” without a measured correctness audit. Review speed is not used as a staff leaderboard that rewards unsafe release. An input that expires without a decision produces an operational review obligation; the oversight owner records a typed cause and response to complete that obligation without changing the expiry. Deliberately dismissed inputs do not generate this missed-review obligation. The full controls/owners are in D19 O01–O08.

### REQ26-D19-C009 — 9. CRM and Email Studio remain coherent

Authorized **Open CRM record** preserves return context. It never grants access, establishes identity, writes a Party, or places held content on ordinary CRM history. Upon actual admission, the single source-backed conversation appears wherever D9's existing qualified related-record rules permit; no second interaction is generated by the reviewer action. Finance, receipts, contact edits and care remain separately authorized owner work.

Email Studio keeps the ratified D18 role: authoring, saved wording, approved presentation and qualified preparation. D13 has its distinct Support request received template. Review attention uses the existing in-product presentation contract, not an ad hoc mailer. Resend receives under qualified tenant/provider authority, and P6 sends any real communication. No authoring/template control can override intake.

### REQ26-D19-C010 — Accessibility and interrupted-work acceptance

- Complete setup, inspection, release, dismissal and recovery using keyboard and screen reader. Use semantic tables/lists, persistent text labels, visible focus and announced status changes; no color-only meaning or hover-only explanations.
- Follow Core's 44px touch-target convention, narrow-screen reflow and zoom support. Full message detail is a route/pane; a short dismissal/impact dialog has a clear title, logical initial focus, Escape behavior where cancelable and return focus. A committed action cannot be canceled by merely closing the dialog.
- While a selected row is being acted on, preserve its identity. After completion, focus the result or predictable next navigation, never a destructive control. Announce changed counts politely without repeating the entire message body.
- Remote image/file loading is explicit and authorized; no speculative body/asset prefetch on mobile or low bandwidth. Interrupted requests retain operation identity and reconcile; expiry/revocation removes content on subsequent qualified reads without presenting a cached copy as valid.
- Test long localized labels, international names, bidirectional text, missing subjects, dates across DST, short policy deadlines and all keyboard/AT paths. Observe representative staff/admin comprehension of the four central distinctions before release; no usability result is claimed here.

The comparison basis and dates are retained in the evidence register and independent UX research. These patterns reduce known ambiguity; their real Asym effectiveness still requires the specified browser and user proof.

### REQ26-D19-C012 — One platform, distinct operations

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Operation                                          | Authority and output                                                                                       | Email Studio / transport boundary                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Receive, fetch or retry incoming mail              | Receiving/source/asset owners bind exact tenant/provider/input and current availability.                   | Incoming mail is untrusted source evidence, not authored template content. No outgoing preparation or send.                                                                             |
| Preview held mail                                  | Current source-authorized inert representation and qualified file access.                                  | A shared safe renderer may be reused; preview does not import, edit, publish or store a second Email Studio source.                                                                     |
| Designate reviewer/backup/oversight                | Support responsibility using actual membership/team/authorization.                                         | Intake reviewer is not automatically an Email Studio reviewer, publisher, reply author or CRM operator.                                                                                 |
| Release, Dismiss, Return to review, Cancel release | Guarded one-input decision and durable admission/correction outcome.                                       | No subject/body, recipient picker, template ID, From/Reply-To or provider send command. Future sender/routing policy remains separate.                                                  |
| Coverage, aging, expiry or missed-review condition | D19 producer owns applicability, source episode, qualified responsibility and completion/correction.       | Producer supplies bounded safe facts and typed destination; it cannot choose arbitrary email/template/recipient addresses.                                                              |
| Staff in-product attention                         | P17 resolves the exact role-safe presentation; P6 records the local `in_product` available occurrence.     | Uses `prepared.none@1`; no prepared artifact, provider message/state or Resend call. This is not an email rendered into a bell.                                                         |
| Eligible new-request confirmation                  | D13 owns exact original-source eligibility and its original 15-minute ceiling.                             | The distinct **Support request received** Email Studio template/meaning, publication and exact preparation feed P6/tenant Resend.                                                       |
| My replies / Shared library                        | Same D18 Email Studio source owns reusable wording and publication; Support owns its copied current draft. | Human replies remain outside the system-message catalog while using the qualified shared validator/compiler/preparation contract. No second library sync.                               |
| Human Send or Add note after admission             | Support admits exact work intent.                                                                          | External Send requires ready P17 preparation, then P6/tenant Resend. Internal note uses shared validation and Support admission without external preparation or send.                   |
| Actual CRM communication/business history          | Admitted source/actual P6 effect under current joint owner authority.                                      | Review decisions and staff attention are not donor contact, last-contact updates, Party creation, refunds or business completion.                                                       |
| Restriction, retention, custody and disposal       | Exact source, asset, records, P17 material/presentation and P6 evidence owners.                            | Held payload, admitted content, attention preview, prepared material and body-free history have separate permitted lifetimes. No template or notification prolongs source availability. |

### REQ26-D19-C013 — In-product attention is a qualified local contract

D19-R23/P32 already require an exact bounded source meaning before activation. For each enabled meaning, qualify its real producer, source episode and applicability, recipient-role authority, safe fact/destination schema, occurrence identity, correction/end rule and P17/P6 binding. Do not borrow an unrelated delivery-repair key or mint a generic support-notification template as a shortcut. Exact registry/API names remain implementation design details, not new founder decisions.

The inherited `presentation.source_actionable_then_recent_90d@1` policy keeps required work actionable after a notification is read; reading changes engagement, not source completion. Source resolution ends actionable treatment. Authorized recent presentation follows the existing 90-day ceiling, shortened by source/privacy/access restrictions. It retains only the permitted minimized projection, never the held body/snippet or a stale working release link. Access and elapsed restrictions are enforced on reads even if cleanup is delayed. Notification ADR0027.

Grouping respects tenant, inbox and condition **plus** the inherited recipient-role, privacy, meaning and genuine episode boundaries. Oversight may receive qualified coverage health without message content. New meaningful source transitions receive proper new occurrences; retries, read state or reassignment cannot keep renewing an old item.

At content expiry, release/recovery authority ends. If expiry occurred without a business disposition, the separate source-owned operational review remains actionable until its typed cause/response or qualified no-further-action conclusion is recorded. That completion preserves the miss and does not restore bytes. Deliberately dismissed content later expiring does not create a missed-review obligation. This distinction prevents an expired-mail card from becoming permanently unresolvable.

P6 local materialization uses the no-artifact contract. It must not invent external preparation, a provider ID, send/delivery state or Resend traffic just to record an in-product notification. Prepared-message ADR0032, P6 common seam.

### REQ26-D19-C014 — Actual email after admission

Release is not an email operation, but actual admission may satisfy D13's already accepted confirmation rules. Keep the conditional UI copy: **“The usual new-request confirmation may follow if this message is eligible.”** Original receipt plus 15 minutes remains the strict utility end; no release, retry, template edit, corrected destination or return from dismissal restarts it. All recipient, suppression, courtesy, source and connection controls remain intact. A late release may admit valid Support work while producing no stale confirmation.

The automatic confirmation has a distinct qualified **Support request received** Email Studio template. Inbox settings retain contextual Preview/Edit in Email Studio. Publishing wording sends nothing, admits no held input, activates no inbox, changes no eligibility and replays no historical occurrence. The message confirms receipt; it cannot claim human review, achieved reply targets, completed refunds or any other unproved business result. Ratified D13.

Human replies use D18's My/Shared source and current Support draft. P17's exact ready preparation precedes the atomic Support reply/work admission; P6 owns dispatch and evidence at actual recipient-copy/submission specificity. A whole To/Cc group is never sent once per member. Notes remain structurally separate. Library save/publication, current draft insertion and sending retain their different permissions and outcomes. Ratified D18 integration.

The provider name does not collapse receiving and sending authority. Receiving needs its qualified source/connection and retrieval capability. Outbound consumes the exact proved owner connection and frozen delivery identity; a send-only credential does not establish retrieval powers, and receiving credentials do not confer outbound authority. No global/platform fallback account or request-level sender override is permitted. No production workflow shells out to the Resend CLI. Tenant-owned Resend ADR0029.

### REQ26-D19-C015 — Authoritative ownership

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact or action                                                               | Owner                                                           | Required invariant                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Provider receipt, provider account/connection and retrievable provider bytes | Qualified receiving integration and provider                    | Bind tenant from trusted integration/routing evidence; a webhook signature does not identify the human sender.         |
| Accepted logical input and recovery disposition                              | Canonical intake owner                                          | Stable source/connection identity; retained or explicitly recoverable outcome; no surrogate re-ingestion after expiry. |
| Content retrieval/scan availability                                          | Receiving/asset/security owner                                  | Technical completeness and safety are distinct; optional missing files cannot masquerade as clean files.               |
| Safety/classification gates                                                  | Actual security/classification/care domain                      | Routine business review can resolve only its allowed reason class; multiple gate conjunction is preserved.             |
| Reviewer designation and coverage                                            | Support responsibility using existing membership/team authority | Designation does not grant data access; effective qualified coverage is evaluated now.                                 |
| Tenant oversight                                                             | Qualified tenant operations responsibility                      | Health/coverage scope does not imply body access or authority to clear restricted gates.                               |
| One-input review decision                                                    | Intake review owner                                             | Versioned immutable decision receipt, current authorized actor, no persistent routing/trust side effect.               |
| Future routing/sender policy                                                 | Actual routing/security policy owner                            | Separate mutation, scope review and evidence; a rule edit cannot overrule dismissal or security.                       |
| Canonical Support admission                                                  | Support intake/source owner                                     | One authorized admission effect per qualified input occurrence; actual source/custody commit establishes readiness.    |
| CRM Party/relationships/business records                                     | Asym Postgres CRM and actual domain owners                      | No copied CRM, automatic Party creation, consent change or business completion from review.                            |
| Conversation discovery on CRM                                                | D9 source-backed authorized projection                          | Held mail absent from ordinary timeline; actual admitted source appears once under joint authority.                    |
| Human/automatic message preparation and sending                              | Email Studio/Phase17; Phase6/tenant Resend                      | D18 human authoring and D13 automatic confirmation remain distinct; review owns neither delivery nor templates.        |
| Ordinary held payload lifetime                                               | Intake semantic owner with actual records/asset custodians      | Proposed 14-day class; finite published policy, original receipt, earlier owner ceilings and independent preservation. |
| Review/technical/control audit retention                                     | Each evidence owner                                             | Typed minimized facts with actual horizons; not forever merely because no body is present.                             |

### REQ26-D19-C016 — Orthogonal state, not an overloaded ticket status

Keep these axes distinct even if the implementation stores projections together:

1. **Binding:** trustworthy tenant/review scope, or platform-owned unbound/conflict.
2. **Availability:** payload/files available, pending, unavailable, restricted or expired.
3. **Gates:** current source-owned reasons, evidence/policy revision and permitted resolutions.
4. **Review:** pending, release requested, dismissed, or corrected through a later decision.
5. **Admission:** absent, in progress, admitted with exact source receipt, or blocked/failed with recoverable evidence.
6. **Custody/disposal:** live ordinary purpose, restricted required custody, disposal obligations, actual disposed/residual result.

No new Open/Waiting/Resolved conversation state is introduced to model these pre-admission facts. A title, status, team name or existing claim flag does not prove any other axis. An item may be dismissed and still contain protected required bytes; that does not make it ordinary-reviewable forever.

This is a logical ownership flow. Technical/protected/unbound classes have their own qualified finite schedules; the ordinary cutoff arrows do not grant deletion authority over them. An admission result and its downstream communication evidence remain distinct.

### REQ26-D19-C017 — Required stored/control facts

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Record concept                   | Minimum qualified facts                                                                                                                               | Constraints and lifetime                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Accepted input                   | Tenant binding when proved; provider connection/source identity; original receipt evidence; platform acceptance; payload generation/frontier          | Provider replay identity and durable admission uniqueness; raw content follows its actual class; platform-null binding never leaks into tenant review.       |
| Review coverage                  | Tenant/inbox, existing member/team references, backup/oversight references, version and trusted actor                                                 | Equal-tenant relations; no email-address identity; dynamic effective eligibility; changes audited.                                                           |
| Gate evidence                    | Source ID/version, closed reason, actual owner, evidence/policy revision, current permitted resolution                                                | Multiple gates conjunctive; sender-provided text is not system evidence; classification details protected.                                                   |
| Review decision                  | Tenant/input, decision sequence, action, reviewed source/version/scope, actual actor profile/membership, trusted decision instant and command receipt | Immutable when durably accepted; subsequent corrections append; corrections append; exact retry returns existing outcome; no generic editable approved flag. |
| Current disposition              | Exact input + current decision sequence, finite processing/error/terminal outcome reference                                                           | One current state through compare-and-set/locking; invalid combinations rejected.                                                                            |
| Admission obligation and receipt | Durable effect identity, exact input occurrence, eligible destination/correlation scope, source cutoff/gates, actual admission linkage/time           | Decision/outbox atomic; admission consumed once; duplicate worker resumes secondary effects without duplicate message.                                       |
| Payload schedule                 | Owner class/version, original qualified receipt, materialized cutoff, current effective policy/earlier restrictions                                   | At equality no positive admission; no touch renewal; unknown receipt uses the separately bounded restricted recovery class, not guessed now.                 |
| Restriction/disposal evidence    | Exact original source/copy frontier, source restriction, actual custody/holds, owner obligations/results                                              | No new surrogate input can evade tombstones; physical deletion separate from ordinary authority end.                                                         |
| Attention/report projections     | Source event/condition, authorized tenant/inbox scope, units, freshness, source-end evidence                                                          | No copied bodies; not authoritative work; current permissions and source eligibility rechecked.                                                              |

Use existing canonical records where they satisfy these invariants. Do not freeze an unnecessary forest of new tables. A decision event stream here is a bounded business history, not a new platform event-sourcing migration. Index current review work by tenant/scope/state/deadline with stable ordering. Constraints should prevent contradictory tenant references, duplicate admission and editable attribution, while owner commands enforce action semantics that cannot be expressed in a simple check.

### REQ26-D19-C018 — Mutation and authorization contract

List and detail commands return safe projections through the shared business API. Review commands accept only the caller's selected action/target where permitted, expected source/decision version and logical request identity. Tenant/actor/profile/author/time/approval are resolved by the server. A caller must not replace the source ID, tenant, target, reason revision or profile through a generic update.

For every command, qualify: current authenticated tenant membership; explicit effective review designation; action capability; source/reason/classification; current available payload; source and destination scope; prior state/version; finite policy authority. Deferred positive work rechecks current deciding-actor designation/capability as well as source/destination gates; the service worker's privilege is not the actor's continuing authority. Current eligibility does not mean rewriting historical attribution after someone leaves.

Keep raw intake/review data server-only. Existing RLS-enabled/no-browser-grants posture is valid. Service-role/BYPASSRLS access is not self-authorizing. If an exposed ordinary update is allowed, specify and prove old-row eligibility and new-row validity. PostgreSQL can use USING as the applicable default check when WITH CHECK is omitted; omission alone is not the finding. A same-tenant predicate still does not constrain changing inbox, actor or forbidden state. Protected views, definer functions, search paths, RPC execution grants, storage URLs and owner jobs require the same boundary.

Tenant-aware relationships are structural: review→input, review→route, route→inbox, review→decision/admission, member/team→tenant and any conversation reference must agree. Source identity and original event evidence are not mutable caller fields. Required history must not cascade away with an inbox or staff record. A held input cannot be force-linked to a guessed tenant or current CRM contact to satisfy a database constraint.

### REQ26-D19-C019 — Durable effect and correction sequence

Example: decision sequence 7 requests release; its durable obligation references sequence 7 and source version 12. A repeated network request returns the same command receipt. A worker replay cannot invent another admission. If an authorized cancellation commits sequence 8 before admission, the sequence-7 obligation is no longer positive authority. A new valid release at sequence 9 gets its own decision receipt but still targets the same input's single admission effect. It cannot consume a stale rejected/expired sequence as permission or create a second conversation.

If admission wins first, cancellation reports **Already released**. Review correction history may be appended, but actual admitted work is corrected by its owning commands. If the outcome is unknown, reconcile the admission effect before promising a result. Never free a transient work claim and assume that prevents a duplicate hours later; durable uniqueness and source guards provide that guarantee.

Decision, audit receipt and dispatch obligation commit atomically. When admission requires a separate transaction, its source-to-Support linkage and custody receipt commit atomically once. A transaction failure creates no partial business success. A committed receipt followed by lost response remains reconcilable. Provider fetches, scans and network delivery run outside database transactions and cannot refresh expired authority.

### REQ26-D19-C020 — Temporal and custody examples

All examples assume the ordinary class is qualified and no earlier restriction applies. They illustrate exact boundaries, not existing runtime results.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Scenario                                                                 | Required result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Qualified provider receipt 12 Sep 2026 02:10 UTC, ordinary 14 days       | Cutoff 26 Sep 2026 02:10 UTC: exactly 1,209,600 seconds. Viewer timezone changes display only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Reviewer opens every day; dismisses day 3; returns day 10                | Same original cutoff; no touch/dismiss/reopen renewal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Release requested one second before cutoff, admission commits at cutoff  | No admission of expired payload; truthful expired/blocked outcome and no D17 lifetime.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Admission/custody commits before cutoff; provider callback arrives later | Existing admitted source retained under D17/actual owners; duplicate callback does not create new content.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Eligible automatic confirmation considered after an hour held            | D13 utility has ended; release creates no new 15-minute window.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Missing original receipt                                                 | Restricted timing recovery: once-set first trusted platform acceptance, otherwise first explicit legacy recovery registration; 24-hour review, at most14-day normal recovery access, earlier source limits honored. No fabricated receipt, renewed restriction or ordinary admission until original evidence is qualified. |
| Valid policy lengthening before expiry; stale worker has old deadline    | Owner-effective policy governs; stale worker cannot destroy on old projection.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Policy lengthening at/after expiry before physical cleanup               | Old bytes remain expired; worker lag is not recoverability.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Hold arrives after logical expiry but before physical disposal           | Preserve only still-existing required bytes in restricted custody under the real owner; ordinary review stays unavailable.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Provider fetch finishes after expiry/redaction                           | Current source/copy fence prevents persistence/rehydration; no new surrogate input or reset timestamp.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Unknown tenant later bound correctly                                     | Original evidence/lifetime remains; no new receipt or synthetic lifetime on tenant binding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Optional attachment unavailable but D1 permits admission                 | Show exact unavailable file fact; no claim that bytes or scan exist; essential requirements still block.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Ordinary expiry removes body/subject/snippet/parsed/raw/header/address/filename/URL and derived content from normal review according to the owner inventory. Minimal typed source/decision/admission/restore facts survive only under their actual qualified horizons. Required independent financial/care/records evidence stays with its real domain. There is no cleanup by deleting a conversation parent or exporting the body into a permanent “audit note.”

The 14-day period does not replace D17's separately ratified ended-work retention policy. Phase26 owns intake schedule meaning; Phase21 supplies no blanket semantic authority. Tenant edits use only published qualified finite variants/bounds. Technical, security/care and unbound recovery need actual owner schedules before activation; those schedules may impose stricter availability and preservation than routine review. Generic missing policy cannot be quietly treated as unlimited storage, permission to destroy, or a fresh ordinary period.

## D19 — Independently verifiable acceptance criteria

### AC26-D19-P01

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

One small tenant person or one shared team can cover all inboxes; no mandatory hierarchy or second engine.

Stories: US26-D19-01. Requirements: REQ26-D19-R01, REQ26-D19-R03, REQ26-D19-R30.

### AC26-D19-P02

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

A reviewer for inbox A cannot list, count, search, inspect or mutate unauthorized B or another tenant through any surface.

Stories: US26-D19-01. Requirements: REQ26-D19-R02, REQ26-D19-R05, REQ26-D19-R14, REQ26-D19-R15.

## D19 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D19-O01

**Signal and threshold:** Any active inbox has zero currently eligible primary/backup coverage, or required oversight route is invalid.
