## D21 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D21-O01

**Signal and threshold:** Any confirmed cross-tenant/unauthorized label disclosure or mutation, privacy resurrection, or forbidden raw writer success: **one occurrence**.

**Owner:** Platform security/on-call plus Support API owner.

**Response:** Immediately contain the affected path, revoke/disable unsafe access, preserve minimal incident evidence, reconcile impacted scope and require authorization/restore regression proof before reactivation.

### OP26-D21-O02

**Signal and threshold:** Any observed committed-effect/receipt/history mismatch, old-intent resurrection, dangling authoritative membership or silent saved-predicate broadening: **one confirmed mismatch**.

**Owner:** Support API/data owner.

**Response:** Stop the affected mutation class, recover from authoritative receipt/source evidence, correct projections and run targeted integrity/concurrency proof; never replay toggles or blindly restore snapshots.

### OP26-D21-O03

**Signal and threshold:** Any completed label report/export whose declared cohort, authorization, N/L/U or distinct-count contract fails reconciliation: **one confirmed mismatch**.

**Owner:** Support reporting owner.

**Response:** Withdraw the misleading completed result, expose unavailable/partial status, repair the query/projection and verify population/count/drilldown parity before returning it to use.

### OP26-D21-O04

**Signal and threshold:** An active-scope authoritative read/query or post-commit projection remains failed beyond its registered recovery deadline, or exceeds its registered latency/error budget in **two consecutive five-minute windows**. Exact budgets and recovery deadline are deployment-profile gates.

**Owner:** Core operations/on-call and owning query/index service.

**Response:** Apply existing retry/backpressure, show accurate unavailable/freshness state, bound offending work per tenant, repair/rebuild from source and verify recovery; no success-to-zero fallback.

### OP26-D21-O05

**Signal and threshold:** At rollout, **any unresolved identity/normalizer/tenant/provenance conflict**; afterward, **any reproducible save/apply/restore defect reported by staff**. Sparse optional classification alone is excluded.

**Owner:** Tenant Support administrator with Support configuration owner.

**Response:** Block only unsafe activation/operation, preserve the rest of Support work, assign bounded repair through existing operations and verify exact IDs/history. For ordinary vocabulary requests use normal maintenance; no automatic merge, mandatory tagging or inferred urgency.

### REQ26-D21-C027 — Operating and qualification sequence

These controls are accepted release/operational requirements, not scheduled automations created during this session. Owners are accountable product/service roles using existing incident/operations tooling. They do not require labels to send email. Numeric sampling thresholds below are explicit operational choices, not measured vendor optima.

## D22 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D22-R01 — Closed current coverage and explicit future intent

Provide keyword search over eligible Support conversation details, admitted message and internal-note text, and attachment filenames. Details include permitted Support references/IDs, subjects and Support-owned requester/participant display details; a qualified D12 staff brief is Staff context. Include admitted human and automated messages only with their truthful provenance. Search no attachment contents, OCR, image/audio interpretation, semantic/AI answers, embeddings, external AI provider or global CRM corpus now. The founder's future broader/AI intent is recorded, not activated. Do not add disabled AI chrome, speculative vector columns or a parallel future-search framework.

### REQ26-D22-R02 — Index eligibility is separate from read permission

A source must be durably admitted, currently available, allowed to be indexed for this Support purpose, and currently readable by the actor under the exact source/field scope. Phase10 restricted-tier exclusions and P9 member-care/finance-provenance indexing exclusions are governing floors. A clearance-holder's direct read is not permission to index that material or scan it through a fallback. Apply policy classifications, not a guessed sensitive-keyword blacklist that rejects ordinary donor-care discussion. Private drafts, unadmitted prepared candidates, raw headers/MIME/provider evidence, D19-held intake, Email Studio reusable-library sources and P6/P17 Recent copies are excluded. ADR0031 expressly forbids turning Recent copies into a search corpus. No source means no fallback to an older readable copy.

### REQ26-D22-R03 — Truthful typed source items

Search one original source item at a time: one subject/reference/detail field, one allowed participant-name or address field, one admitted message, one internal note, one Staff context brief, or one attachment-name item. Keep stable tenant/original-conversation/source-kind/source-ID/revision and current owner availability. An admitted queued, failed or uncertain outgoing reply can be eligible but is never called Sent/Delivered without P6 evidence. Internal note and Automated message remain distinct from human correspondence. Staff context may exist with zero messages; its citations do not recursively index the cited conversation. Label names are already covered by D21's explicit label filter, not a reason to copy catalog/CRM fields into every source item.

### REQ26-D22-R04 — Plain literal matching with phrases

The new Support text predicate requires every entered unquoted fragment and quoted phrase within the same eligible source item; ordinary unquoted fragments may appear in any order. A fragment matches literally within normalized visible text, including partial words: receipt can match receipts. Preserve punctuation and stopwords; no stemming, accent stripping, spelling correction, synonym expansion, implicit OR/NOT, regex or wildcard language. Names/addresses in another field cannot supply a missing query fragment. Use a separate qualified Person or email filter with content search when staff want that explicit cross-field condition.

Normalize source/query text through the same versioned Unicode NFC, full casefold and whitespace rules; preserve a map back to displayed source text. Straight double quotes and paired typographic double quotes delimit an exact phrase after whitespace normalization. Apostrophes are literal. The companion contract defines escaping, incomplete quotes and literal operators. Invalid syntax is an actionable input error, not No matches or a silently broadened query. Query bounds are 256 Unicode scalar values after outer trim, at most 16 nonempty fragments/phrases and at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes; these are explicit product bounds, not a vendor optimum. A nonblank single-character query is valid but may need narrower scope under the server query budget. Never drop short/stopword-only queries silently.

### REQ26-D22-R05 — Match only source-visible text, without invented adjacency

Use the owning domain's qualified visible-text projection, not JSON-stringified message bodies, raw HTML attributes, scripts/styles, hidden transport fields or a merged transcript. Current permitted quoted content within a message may match under that source's own custody; repetition does not increase relevance. Redacted/hidden/expired spans create hard boundaries: a literal fragment or phrase cannot cross them. Unquoted fragments may occur in separate eligible visible runs of the same source item, but no excluded text contributes. Rendered placeholders such as Content removed are UI state, not searchable source text. Chunking may accelerate candidate retrieval but cannot change item/phrase boundaries or lose a match across a storage chunk boundary.

### REQ26-D22-R06 — Preserve visible context and simple filters

Retain the existing inbox/view/CRM/report scope when searching. Keep Status, Assignee and Labels as compact familiar controls; other already-qualified D20 Following/reply-attention criteria remain under Filters. Add a compact Search in refinement for All searchable content, Details, Messages, Internal notes, Staff context or Attachment names; All is the ordinary new-search coverage. Person or email narrows permitted Support participant/detail facts, not an arbitrary CRM property builder. Show active scope/refinement chips; use D20 AND-across-facets and D21 Any/All/No labels semantics. No second filter builder, date wizard or raw operator syntax is required. Do not import D21 report dates into ordinary root createdAt filtering.

In a Support list, **Search all my accessible Support conversations** is an explicit action: keep entered query and Search in; remove ordinary inbox/view/status/assignee/label/person/following/attention filters, clearly describing that consequence. Permission/source exclusions remain. In a CRM record or report, broader search first uses explicit Open in Support Hub with preserved return context; never silently remove the anchor or exact report predicate. An exact reference obeys the same visible scope—do not jump to an out-of-scope result automatically.

### REQ26-D22-R07 — Predictable updates, sorting and clearing

Retain a deliberate existing saved/user sort. A new unconfigured text search uses Best match: exact full Support reference/ID matches first, then eligible matches by original source admission/creation time descending, unknown time last, with deterministic source/root-ID ties. The best eligible source item represents each continuing conversation; no popularity/frequency or unavailable-source ranking contribution. Explain the simple ordering; it is not semantic AI relevance. A query-local automatic search order does not overwrite the underlying queue/view sort. Clearing text restores that underlying order unless the user deliberately changed it, while retaining current filters. Clear search, Clear filters and D20 Reset view remain distinct.

Use the existing 200ms input debounce as an initial interaction setting, with cancellation/generation checks, IME-composition handling and Enter/Search to run the current valid query immediately. This is a tuning choice, not a latency promise. Distinguish input being edited, the executed query and displayed results. New results cannot move focus, substitute the selected conversation or retarget an action under a pointer. Show quiet Updating/Results changed treatment; preserve the opened conversation and draft. Blank query returns the qualified filtered list; malformed/over-budget input does not silently run blank All.

With blank text, Search in retains its preference but is dormant: it is not a has-message/note/file filter. Clear filters resets Search in to All searchable content and removes ordinary status/assignee/label/person/following/attention refinements while retaining text, current inbox boundary, the active view's identity as Modified where applicable, and mandatory CRM/report context. Reset view remains the distinct D20 command. The exact-reference ranking tier applies only when the entire parsed query is one atom equal to a complete permitted reference/ID; one fragment inside a larger query does not receive that tier.

### REQ26-D22-R08 — Explain the result and open the right source

Show one authorized continuing-conversation row under D10, with current subject/handler/work context and a concise matching excerpt or filename, source kind and truthful source time/state. Never show inaccessible-match counts or synthetic text assembled across sources. A best-match preview is a navigation aid, not a new Support message. Opening a result targets the exact original source/revision within the current allowed topology, preserves list position/query/return context and rechecks current access. Filename matches locate attachment metadata; they never download/open bytes automatically. If a match changed, was removed or became forbidden, show current source-safe unavailability and refresh options, not the old excerpt or a nearby unrelated match presented as the same evidence.

### REQ26-D22-R09 — Find within a conversation

Provide a visible Find in conversation entry and qualified keyboard shortcut without hijacking typing or ordinary browser shortcuts. It uses the same literal/phrase and owner-eligibility contract, limited to current permitted original sources in that conversation/context. Match navigation reaches eligible retained messages beyond the mounted page; DOM-only find is not the product's whole-conversation feature. Show current match position/next/previous only when that count is complete; preserve access and source revision at navigation. A CRM-anchored Find stays limited to its qualified source basis; opening full Support handling is explicit. Index-forbidden sources remain excluded even if directly readable elsewhere.

Empty Find clears highlights and disables match navigation; it does not treat every item as a match.

### REQ26-D22-R10 — Source authorization before matching and aggregation

Trusted server context resolves tenant, actual actor/profile, current membership and purpose. Apply the D9 CRM/source basis or report constraint, indexing eligibility, current source revision and field/attachment-metadata authority before any source can contribute a hit, snippet, rank, facet, aggregate or count. Seeing a conversation shell, assignment, follow or related Party grants none of these. Establish valid contributing source hits first, then D10 continuing-root projection/deduplication, ordering and pagination. Return no raw body/index rows to the browser for filtering. Searchability never proves identity, representation, receipt issuance, consent or completion of a giving/care action.

### REQ26-D22-R11 — One source-owned derived projection

Asym Support owns original conversation/source truth; its search projection is rebuildable and has no independent write, retention or authorization power. Extend the qualified shared API/list/named-query machinery with a closed Support search subject and versioned source/query contract. Use Asym Postgres candidate retrieval and exact verification behind that boundary; qualify the P9 pg_trgm approach for this subject where suitable. P9's CRM body-search deferral and Cmd-K budgets remain CRM-specific; no global CRM body search is enabled. Current intended pg_trgm architecture is not proof that an extension/index is already deployed. No new external engine, full taxonomy/search platform or provider dependency is required for D22.

### REQ26-D22-R12 — Database, RLS and privileged paths

Projection identity and references are tenant-aware and source-kind constrained, with immutable original endpoints, source/projection/schema revisions, purpose/eligibility state and minimal source ordering/freshness facts. Derive actor, tenant, source admission and eligibility from trusted owners, not a caller body. Enforce same-tenant relationships and valid non-null states/revisions through constraints and one qualified projection writer. If heterogeneous sources need a tagged reference, each allowed source kind must have a verified endpoint-integrity boundary; no unconstrained arbitrary record_type/id reference or polymorphic data leak.

Projection text is private server-side derived content; revoke unneeded raw anonymous/authenticated reads and writes. Prove query RPC/view/function execution grants, invoker/definer choice, fixed search_path, USING and WITH CHECK, table owner/BYPASSRLS, service-role/worker and raw Data API paths. Existing broad staff message reads are not a safe substitute. Parameterize queries and escape LIKE metacharacters when LIKE is used; no caller SQL, regex or raw tsquery execution. Tenant/source permission predicates must hold for both existing rows and proposed projection updates, and old permissive policies must not OR unsafe access back open.

### REQ26-D22-R13 — Durable indexing without source-write coupling

Source admission/update/restriction commits the necessary durable projection intent or equivalent discoverable revision gap atomically with its owner event. Index workers reread current owner data, act idempotently on original source identity/revision, and never let older or out-of-order work replace a newer projection or revive a withdrawn source. Jobs carry identifiers, not long-lived body copies. Index failure does not undo admitted mail/notes, stop valid replying or pretend the source never arrived. Creation of a source is not proof search is complete: expose truthful indexing readiness. Use existing durable-work and reconciliation capabilities, not a new job service or one polling timer per conversation.

### REQ26-D22-R14 — Current restriction wins before asynchronous purge

D16 redaction, D17 expiry, source correction, privacy reclassification and access changes fence serving immediately at their authoritative admission boundary. A stale index can contribute no hit, rank, count, snippet, filename or match reason while physical purge catches up. Projection updates cannot extend source availability. Revoke queued/cached results and revalidate at navigation; no rendered app can recall content already observed or independently copied, but Asym must stop serving it. Remove forbidden source text/derived index material through its actual owner purge process, including backups/restore barriers; search history/logs are not an alternate archive. No direct-scan fallback over index-forbidden or expired sources.

### REQ26-D22-R15 — Complete queries and honest limits

Apply complete eligible predicates before result limits/counts/page, eliminating the current 2,000-before-filter and unpaged hydration assumptions. Indexed candidates are not authoritative matches until the exact contract verifies them; candidate truncation cannot become a complete zero. Use bounded keyset pages and stable ties, with query/normalizer/coverage version, scope and ordering bound into opaque current-authorized continuation. Root topology or source changes may alter live results; detect invalid continuation/visible changes, deduplicate known rows and offer deliberate refresh rather than claim a historical snapshot. Do not hold indefinite DB snapshots or preserve result bodies for stable pagination.

Only display an exact total when the complete authorized query and coverage justify it; otherwise show page/progress and an explicit incomplete/unavailable result state. No per-filter/per-source counts by default. Timeout, index backlog, unreadied source generation and failed projection are different from No matches. Supported source units that exceed a processing budget remain a visible coverage/recovery condition, not an undocumented unsearchable tail. Excluded source types and inaccessible data are outside declared coverage, without revealing hidden-match counts.

### REQ26-D22-R16 — Bounded performance and exact matching

Index qualified normalized source text and tenant/source keys as justified by measured plans. Literal substring semantics can use escaped LIKE/position verification with pg_trgm candidates; do not substitute fuzzy similarity or English tsvector stopword/stemming semantics. Trigram-poor short/punctuation queries can require scans: apply authorized structured scope first, enforce registered execution/resource limits and return a clear Refine search outcome if the budget is exhausted, never fake zero. Segmentation/chunking must preserve source and redaction boundaries; retrieve candidate parent items then verify all terms/phrases against the same qualified item. No all-terms-in-one-chunk shortcut or cross-chunk phrase loss.

Before activation publish and test a finite Support search profile: normalized-input expansion, eligible source/segment size, snippets, pages, row/query time, concurrency, per-tenant fairness, cancellation, index/recovery/freshness deadlines and cache/query-state retention. The 256-scalar/16-atom/1,024-byte input bounds do not imply those source/index limits. Do not import P9 Cmd-K's p95 target or a vendor's result/comment caps as an unmeasured Support SLA. Existing source records above a profile boundary require honest qualification, not silent clipping. No payload embeddings or attachment parsing to improve performance.

### REQ26-D22-R17 — Safe excerpts and accessible emphasis

Generate bounded excerpts from the current qualified display projection, escape text and add only trusted highlight markup. Never render raw source HTML or trust PostgreSQL ts_headline as an XSS sanitizer. Highlight only actual verified matches, mapping normalization/casefold expansion back to original visible grapheme boundaries; preserve punctuation and meaningful whitespace. Do not highlight private removed spans or fabricate adjacency across them. Long matches may need multiple clearly separated excerpts from the same source, not a false continuous quote. Untrusted links/attachments remain inert until their separately qualified actions. Announce meaningful state changes without reading entire private excerpts into global live regions.

### REQ26-D22-R18 — Sensitive query state and client isolation

Reuse D20's bounded authenticated query-state reference for sensitive text/criteria in navigation and saved contexts; no plaintext query in share URLs, telemetry, referrers or cross-user recent-search lists by default. A handle is not a bearer access grant. Current authorization and owner lifetime govern handle resolution, not knowledge of its value. Bind caches and responses to tenant/principal/acting scope/source purpose, query/coverage/version and current authority. A late response after logout, tenant switch, scope change or revocation cannot populate the new UI. Invalid/expired handles show unavailable/re-enter-search rather than blank All. Do not add a new recent-search product, session-replay capture or analytics corpus of raw queries.

### REQ26-D22-R19 — D20 saved meaning and D21 report boundaries

Save search through the existing shared named-view contract, explicitly recording query, Search in source coverage and matching/normalization version. New coverage defaults never silently broaden existing details-only saved queries. Migrate supported legacy meaning faithfully under an explicit legacy version or require reviewed upgrade; no approximate reinterpretation of old substring/concatenation semantics as the new predicate. Known ambiguous old source meaning becomes bounded owned reconciliation. My privacy, Shared audience/field-use checks and versioned defaults remain D20's rules. D21 report drilldown retains its exact cohort and source query; it is not translated to ordinary root createdAt or silently made a saved search. Future AI mode cannot reinterpret a stored keyword query automatically.

### REQ26-D22-R20 — CRM and source continuity

D9 anchors the CRM record and qualified original-source basis. A Party linked through original B does not gain A's historical message matches through merge. Intersect permitted relevant sources before D10 grouping/ranking; projected results remain attributable. D12 related conversations stay independent. Open in Support Hub explicitly enters separately qualified broader handling, preserving return context. Requester, participant, authenticated actor, represented organization, CRM Party, support handler and CRM owner remain distinct; searching an address creates none of those links. No support-side copy of CRM identity, giving facts, care notes or CRM search index is introduced. Source association changes, Party merge/delete/archive and permission changes require current requalification, not silent search-result reassignment.

### REQ26-D22-R21 — Filename discovery is not byte access

Index only attachment names whose Support/file owner allows that metadata in the declared source context. An allowed name may be discoverable even when a file is unsupported for preview; a blocked/held name is not eligible merely because bytes exist. Store no signed URL as searchable text and make no byte download/provider fetch during search. Opening/downloading uses the current original attachment, immutable byte version and separate source/storage/malware/access checks. Filename edits/removal and parent-message restrictions invalidate old name matches. Finding a filename never proves that its contents were searched, are safe, or may be opened. Phase29 retains storage/access/hygiene mechanics; D22 does not implement text extraction.

### REQ26-D22-R22 — Email Studio, Resend and business actions

Search is a read capability over qualified admitted Support sources. It neither publishes Email Studio wording, creates a template variable, prepares mail, changes recipients, follows, labels, creates CRM interaction/last-contact history nor calls Resend/provider search. P6/P17 Recent and private prepared material are never used to fill missing source text. Searching an admitted queued reply does not imply it was sent. An actual later Reply or Note rechecks its current source/draft/recipient purpose: P17 ready preparation→Support atomic admission→P6 tenant Resend for external replies; Notes remain non-deliverable. Search outage cannot block otherwise qualified handling, and a hit never authorizes a CRM/giving/care mutation or business completion.

### REQ26-D22-R23 — Future broader/AI search reuses the boundary

Preserve typed original source identities, eligible projection/schema revisions, query-mode/coverage semantics, match provenance and a current-authorized source retrieval contract as the extension seam. Future attachment content and AI search are separately designed and reviewed with Phase29/40 and existing shared AI connection/capability/egress/invocation/suggestion owners. They must inherit indexing exclusions, current retrieval checks, source disposal and citation/provenance requirements. No generic plugin framework, embeddings, extraction jobs, external prompts, autonomous actions, provider keys or AI placeholders are added to D22. This records the founder's direction without charging current users for an unused feature or claiming future compliance/readiness.

### REQ26-D22-R24 — Observability without a second content store

Technical metrics/traces record safe query class/version, scope identifiers where permitted, latency/cancellation, eligible projection freshness and repair codes; avoid raw query/source/filename text and sensitive snippet payloads. Durable source/index lifecycle receipts establish which revision was projected or withdrawn; they are distinct from customer-visible conversation history and security read audit. Reuse existing required sensitive-read/export audit when a permitted operation qualifies; index-forbidden content stays excluded rather than becoming an audited indexing exception. No search itself fabricates a communication or last-contact event. O01–O05 below name concrete signals and accountable responses.

### REQ26-D22-R25 — Migration, rollout and recovery

Inventory actual searchable-source stores, old list/message endpoints, raw browser/fixture paths and saved definitions before activation. Add projection/source revision/coverage contracts and indexes compatibly; seed only currently admitted index-eligible sources. Backfill carries original source identity and current policy, not current-time admission or invented historical sent state. Gate source kinds/tenants until coverage and privacy proofs pass. Fence old body-leaking reads, raw-query URL serializers and incomplete pre-filter paths. Do not keep permanent parallel search engines or competing write authority; all supported query versions run through the single qualified owner, and unsafe or unsupported legacy meanings require reviewed upgrade under R19. Stop controls disable unsafe search while preserving source work, current privacy and owner navigation. After new restrictions/versioned queries exist, rollback cannot re-enable old unsafe projections or reinterpret saved meaning; roll forward and rebuild only from current authorized sources. Restored backups must apply withdrawal/revision barriers before serving.

### REQ26-D22-R26 — Proof and stage discipline

Trace D22-R01–R26 and P01–P40 through selected answer, glossary, feature ADR, eventual OpenSpec/design/tasks/issues, implementation and release evidence. Broadening beyond A requires an explicit future scope decision, not a dependency convenience. The current review includes source inspection and limited synthetic matcher experiments only; real SQL/RLS/indexing/privacy/concurrency/browser/accessibility/capacity proof is required before activation. D1–D21 are preserved; the complete D22 amendments await ratification.

### REQ26-D22-C001 — Start in the existing workspace

Keep one **Search conversations** field in the existing list toolbar. Replace donor-only copy with **Search conversations…**. Short help explains **“Search details, messages, internal notes and attachment names. File contents aren’t searched.”** Do not add an AI button, new global search destination or a separate query builder.

Keep the active inbox/view and any CRM/report context visible. Place the familiar Status, Assignee and Labels controls beside search; other qualified D20 filters remain under **Filters**. Search in is a compact refinement, default **All searchable content**, with Details, Messages, Internal notes, Staff context and Attachment names. Its nondefault choice becomes a visible chip. Do not display six permanent source buttons or count every source/facet before the person searches.

**Person or email**, inside Filters, matches permitted Support participant/detail facts. It is useful for an explicit request such as “messages containing receipt in conversations involving Alex.” It does not search the whole CRM, verify identity or create a contact. Keep labels as D21's existing filter with Any/All/No labels; do not invent a competing label matcher or a date filter with ambiguous Updated semantics.

Searching retains current work filters. A resolved conversation outside an Open view stays outside it even for an exact ID. For wider retrieval in a Support list, the explicit action is **Search all my accessible Support conversations**. Describe its effect beside the action: **“Keeps your text and Search in choice; removes the current work filters.”** The current permissions and source exclusions remain. From CRM/report context, use **Open in Support Hub** before broader search, preserving return context; no automatic anchor removal.

### REQ26-D22-C002 — Search text that behaves predictably

Ordinary terms are literal fragments, all required in one eligible source item. A source item is one message, note, filename, Staff context item or individual detail field. **receipt address** may find one message containing both, but not a name in one field plus receipt in an unrelated message. Fragments can match inside a word, so receipt can find receipts. Case is ignored under the shared Unicode contract; spelling, accents, punctuation and short words are not silently removed or interpreted as AI meaning.

Concise help says **“Use quotes for an exact phrase. To combine a person with message wording, use Person or email.”** Support normal straight quotes and paired typographic double quotes from mobile keyboards. No Boolean/wildcard/regex syntax or second Match-mode control. The data contract fixes the exact parser and escape behavior, including repairable unfinished quotes. Operators such as OR, NOT, `%` and `_` remain literal text.

Retain 200ms debounced typing as the initial setting, with IME-aware behavior, Enter and an accessible Search action to run immediately. Do not submit mid-composition. Show the executed query's results separately from unfinished input; while updating, preserve last-known authorized rows with a quiet **Updating…** state rather than announcing them as matches for the new text. Cancel/fence stale requests. Keyboard focus and an opened conversation remain stable when new results arrive.

The accepted query ceiling is 256 Unicode scalar values, 1,024 UTF-8 bytes and 16 parsed fragments/phrases. The input explains exceeded bounds without discarding text. Single-character input is allowed; a genuinely too-broad query can ask for more text or narrower scope without pretending no matches exist. These are product/technical bounds, not an assertion about optimal human query length.

### REQ26-D22-C003 — Sorting, clearing and returning

Preserve an explicit saved/user sort. For an otherwise unconfigured text search, **Best match** means exact full references first, then the newest qualifying source match—not an AI score or term-frequency contest. Source timestamps are original admitted/created facts; index rebuild and label edits do not make old content new. Unknown source time sorts last and is not replaced with now.

The automatically selected search order does not change the underlying queue/view order. **Clear search** removes only the entered query and the transient automatic search order; other filters stay. A deliberately changed work sort remains. **Clear filters** removes ordinary work/source refinements while leaving text and mandatory context. **Reset view** uses D20's saved definition. Label actions and old query replies cannot erase typed text or reset unrelated filters. Clearing invalid input is a deliberate action, not a parser fallback to All.

With blank text, Search in retains its preference but contributes no predicate; clearing a filename search must not become a hidden has-attachment filter. Clear filters explicitly returns Search in to All searchable content, clears ordinary work/person/label refinements, and retains the current inbox boundary, view identity as Modified where applicable, text and mandatory CRM/report context. Exact-reference priority applies only to a complete one-atom reference query, not a reference fragment among other terms.

Back from a result restores the qualified query, visible scope, scroll position and focus. D20 query-state handles keep sensitive literals out of URLs/referrers. An expired private handle yields **This search is no longer available. Enter your search again.** It does not open All conversations or expose another user's query. No recent-search history or raw-query analytics feature is added.

### REQ26-D22-C004 — Results show the reason for the match

Use the shared conversation list with one row per current continuing conversation. Show current subject, work/handler context and a short qualified matching excerpt or filename. Identify the reason as **Subject**, **Detail**, **Message**, **Internal note**, **Staff context** or **Attachment name**. An automated message and a queued/failed/uncertain reply retain truthful provenance/state. Never describe a note as a requester-visible reply or a queued message as delivered.

Emphasize exact matched text using escaped display text and trusted markup, not raw email HTML. Multiple separated excerpts from the same item are clearly separated, not fused into a quotation. No redaction placeholder is a search hit; hidden gaps cannot create new phrase adjacency. Internal-note excerpts stay within current authorized staff scope and are not announced wholesale through a global live region.

Opening a text result lands at the exact original source within the current eligible conversation. It never silently picks a nearby replacement if the original changed. A filename result reveals its authorized attachment row, without opening/downloading the file. The ordinary file action separately checks current byte access and hygiene. A matching filename does not mean the file's contents were searched.

Offer **Find in conversation** in the open conversation, with next/previous matches across its declared eligible retained sources—not only mounted DOM elements. Preserve the narrower CRM/report source basis. The Find field uses the same parser and current eligibility; it is distinct from the broad list search. Do not take over browser Ctrl/Cmd-F by default; use Core's available qualified shortcut convention and a visible action. Actual shortcut mapping is tested against existing bindings before release.

Empty Find clears highlights and disables next/previous; it does not enumerate every source as a match.

### REQ26-D22-C005 — Honest states without noisy warnings

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| State                        | Treatment                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Successful no matches        | **No matches in this scope.** Keep active filters visible and offer explicit clear/narrow/widen actions. Do not promise nothing exists outside permitted/indexable coverage.         |
| Incomplete projection        | **Search is still updating. Available matches are shown.** Show no exact total/rank-completeness claim; retry/refresh is available. Do not disclose how many hidden items may match. |
| Temporary search failure     | **Search couldn’t finish. Try again.** Keep query/filters and ordinary conversation handling available.                                                                              |
| Budget exhausted             | **This search is too broad. Add more text or narrow the filters.** Distinct from zero and from a permissions refusal.                                                                |
| Unfinished/malformed phrase  | **Close the quote to search a phrase.** Preserve input and previous executed-query context; do not run a broader query.                                                              |
| Result changed/removed       | **This match is no longer available.** Use current source-safe detail, refresh and retain allowed return context. Never render the old snippet.                                      |
| Privacy/source scope changed | Remove forbidden results/actions immediately and use the existing unavailable-context treatment. No inaccessible result count or reason exposing hidden source data.                 |
| Valid blank search           | Return the current qualified filtered list with underlying sort; do not clear view/CRM/report anchors.                                                                               |

Exact totals appear only when the full query and coverage justify them. Otherwise show truthful displayed-page/progress states. Do not make a row jump under the pointer when index work completes; show **Results changed — Refresh** when a deliberate refresh is needed. Existing explicit selected IDs remain the action targets. Search never automatically selects all matches, saves a view or sends/labels/follows anything.

### REQ26-D22-C006 — Accessibility, mobile and product consistency

Preserve exact Core base-maia/Base UI and semantic CSS-variable tokens; reuse existing responsive list, popover/filter, status and empty-state components. Avoid tiny source toggles, color-only distinctions and hover-only context. Text input has a visible/accessible name, Clear has an explicit name, active chips have named removal, and result links have meaningful source labels. Focus, selection and loading announcements remain separate.

Test keyboard-only search/refine/clear/open/Find/back, screen-reader announcements, IME composition, non-Latin/RTL/combining text, mobile keyboard overlap, touch targets, 200%/400% zoom/reflow, high contrast, reduced motion and slow/reconnecting networks. Respect WCAG2.2 target-size requirements and exceptions. A screenshot or automated score alone does not establish a good staff journey. W3C status messages, target size.

Representative staff must distinguish a note match from a sent reply, find an old source beyond the mounted page, recognize current search scope, understand filename-only coverage, recover from malformed/incomplete results and return to CRM without losing context. Future AI gets no visible placeholder or hidden operation. The independent UX evidence documents the relevant vendor patterns and the recall tradeoff of matching one item instead of scattered conversation text.

### REQ26-D22-C008 — One source of truth at each step

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact or operation                                                                           | Authoritative owner                          | Consequence for Support search                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Personal/shared reusable wording and published revisions                                    | D18 / Phase17 Email Studio                   | The library is not conversation history. Search does not copy it or query it as a fallback.                   |
| Compatible presentation, typed variable contract and exact preparation                      | Phase17 shared compiler/preparation boundary | No compiler/provider call merely to search. Prepared but unadmitted content remains outside the corpus.       |
| Current human draft, Reply/Note mode, intended recipients, actor and source admission       | Support, with qualified owner/IAM checks     | Drafts remain private and unsearchable. Admitted content becomes eligible only through current source policy. |
| Original source kind, revision, index eligibility, available text and conversation relation | Support plus the actual source/records owner | A rebuildable index has no independent read, retention or write authority.                                    |
| Actual sending connection, Sender/Reply Identity, frozen envelope and provider evidence     | Phase6, using tenant-owned Resend            | Search cannot infer send/delivery success from a body, template or prepared state.                            |
| CRM identity, relationships, giving/care facts and business outcomes                        | Their existing Core domains                  | Search reads only permitted Support context; a result grants no CRM access or business mutation.              |

P17 is an authoring/preparation owner within Asym, not an external CRM to synchronize. Support does not add a second template library, compiler, Brand Kit, credential store or CRM identity. Current scaffolding remains subject to these intended contracts; this document does not claim those seams are fully implemented.

### REQ26-D22-C009 — The user journey

A staff member searches an authorized inbox/view or CRM-context Support list. Query matching uses eligible current original Support sources. A reusable reply used in a past message contributes only through the admitted source's currently permitted text, not through a live join to today's library version. Updating or archiving the reusable source does not rewrite historical correspondence. Redaction/expiry/source restrictions still remove forbidden historical content from serving and governed derivatives.

Opening a result rechecks access and navigates to the actual source. It neither starts a draft nor selects recipients. If the person deliberately replies, D18 can insert eligible wording into their current draft through the same qualified authoring seam. Support validates actual audience and disclosure, P17 prepares the exact approved content/presentation, Support admits the intent, and Phase6 delivers through the tenant's qualified Resend connection. Already admitted queued/failed/uncertain content may be searchable under D22, but its delivery status remains truthful.

The internal-note path remains local and non-deliverable. Notes do not call external preparation or Resend merely because their wording originated in an eligible shared library. Search results, saved views, labels, follows or CRM associations never supply automatic audience authority.

### REQ26-D22-C010 — Templates and messages

**No new Email Studio template is required for search.** A successful search, zero matches, Refine search, result click, Find, index catch-up or ordinary query failure sends no email. D13's existing **Support request received** template retains its own producer and eligibility window; searching or recovering an index cannot renew it or release D19-held intake.

Human replies remain outside the finite system-message template catalog under D4. They consume P17's bounded content/presentation preparation; they do not acquire a made-up system template key or provider-hosted template mirror. Phase6 sends the sealed prepared HTML and real plain text using Resend, without mutable template rendering at dispatch. Source/preparation/connection revision and frozen audience remain part of the exact admitted effect.

### REQ26-D22-C011 — Failure, privacy and recovery

Email Studio or Resend unavailability does not prevent an otherwise authorized search. An indexing outage cannot block otherwise valid source admission: commit durable projection intent or a discoverable gap and show truthful coverage. Searching a failed outgoing reply does not retry delivery. Selecting its existing recovery action requires that action's current ownership and exact-effect checks.

P6/P17 Recent is explicitly excluded by ADR0031. Neither a unavailable source nor a broken index can justify reading a retained Recent/provider copy. Rebuilding rereads current eligible source revisions; no template expansion, provider archive fetch or new recipient lookup is part of repair. Source deletion/redaction/expiry and restore fencing apply to index text, snippets and cache contributions. Published reusable content, drafts, admitted messages, prepared artifacts and delivery evidence have separate owner lifetimes; no signature/template/library reference extends D17's body clock.

D22 O01–O05 concern real source/search failures. Where an existing owner contract already qualifies staff attention, its source-owned local presentation remains separate from an email entitlement. A qualified no-artifact local occurrence uses `prepared.none@1`/local `available`, without a Resend call or invented provider state. Reading attention is not fixing the source/index problem.

### REQ26-D22-C012 — Source ownership and eligibility

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Source kind                      | Current searchable projection                                                                              | Required exclusion / truthful interpretation                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Support reference/ID             | Qualified original/current Support reference field                                                         | Not a CRM Party identifier lookup or bypass of visible scope. Aliases route through current owner identity.                                             |
| Subject and Support detail field | Current indexable owner-visible plain text from one field                                                  | No concatenation of subject, names, addresses and arbitrary JSON. Source restrictions/expiry can remove text while structural identity remains.         |
| Participant/name/address detail  | One currently allowed Support-owned name or address field with source provenance                           | No unrelated current CRM profile fields, hidden BCC/headers, identity inference or automatic relationship.                                              |
| Admitted message                 | Owner-qualified visible text, current revision, original admission time and human/automated/outgoing state | Exclude unadmitted drafts/preparations. Queued/failed/uncertain is not Sent or Delivered. Search actual Support source, never provider/Recent fallback. |
| Internal note                    | Published/admitted ordinary Support note, current indexable visible revision                               | Not personal drafts, care notes or an authority to index restricted tiers. Keep internal provenance.                                                    |
| Staff context                    | Qualified D12 brief with its own source/retention and current disclosure                                   | Can exist with no native messages. No recursive indexing of citation targets or invented correspondence.                                                |
| Attachment name                  | Current indexable owner-visible filename metadata linked to original attachment/message                    | No file bytes, extracted text, raw/signed URL or automatic download. Metadata and byte access are independently qualified.                              |

Eligibility is an intersection: source admission/purpose, allowed indexing classification, owner availability/revision, context source basis and current actor field/resource authority. Phase10 restricted-tier data and P9 excluded care/finance-provenance remain outside ordinary indexing even for cleared actors. A general donor-care message is not excluded merely because it mentions a receipt: use the actual owner classification, not a keyword classifier. P6/P17 Recent, reusable Email Studio sources, drafts/preparations, raw MIME/header/evidence and held intake are not fallback source kinds.

Each projection item retains tenant, source kind, immutable original conversation/source/attachment ID as applicable, current source revision, projection/query-normalization version, purpose/classification eligibility and original owner time. A current-root ID is a derived routing/grouping value; it cannot replace original provenance. Preserve the minimum safe withdrawal/revision fence required for replay and restore without retaining forbidden text.

### REQ26-D22-C013 — Exact literal query contract

The new normal form is **literal all-fragments within one source item**, plus quoted phrases. This is not PostgreSQL's English full-text meaning and not a general query language.

1. Preserve the typed string for current authorized editing. After trimming outer Unicode whitespace, reject more than 256 Unicode scalar values or 1,024 UTF-8 bytes before parsing. Reject invalid scalar sequences/NUL and unsupported non-whitespace control characters with a clear input error. Blank means no text predicate, not a failed search. A nonblank one-character query is valid subject to resource limits.
2. Separate atoms on whitespace outside quotation. Normalize qualifying whitespace sequences to one space for matching. Straight double quotes pair with straight double quotes; typographic opening/closing double quotes pair together. Text enclosed in either pair is a contiguous phrase. Apostrophes are literal. Do not treat OR/AND/NOT, colon, `%`, `_`, `*`, `?` or parentheses as operators.
3. Backslash escapes a supported double-quote delimiter or another backslash. Before another character it remains literal, preserving ordinary path-like text. Quoted and unquoted adjacent runs within one whitespace-delimited atom concatenate into the same literal atom, so a phrase can include a literal prefix/suffix without a second operator model. An unclosed/mismatched delimiter, empty quoted atom, or more than 16 nonempty atoms is invalid; return the specific repairable error and do not run an older/broader/empty query as its result.
4. Apply the same versioned NFC and Unicode full casefold to eligible source runs and parsed atoms, with a bounded normalized expansion profile. Do not assume JS lowercasing or PostgreSQL17 lower() equals full casefold. Preserve accents, punctuation and stopwords. A source fragment may match inside a word; no language stemming, fuzzy match or spelling correction. All atoms must be verified within one eligible item; repeating an atom does not require extra occurrences.
5. A literal fragment or quoted phrase must lie wholly in an eligible contiguous display run. Never bridge a redaction, hidden node, expired span, field boundary or different message. Separate unquoted atoms may be found in different currently eligible runs of the same item. No excluded characters influence matching or ranking. Owner-rendered removal placeholders are not source text.
6. Maintain offsets from normalized runs back to current visible source grapheme ranges. Casefold expansion, combining marks and whitespace folding cannot make highlights reveal adjacent hidden text or split a grapheme. Return escaped text with trusted marks, not HTML supplied by the sender or an unsafe headline function.

Examples: `receipt address` requires both fragments in one item; a participant named Alex plus a message saying receipt does not satisfy `Alex receipt`. Use Person or email=Alex plus q=receipt for an explicit conversation-level conjunction. `"not received"` preserves not and requires contiguous normalized wording. `100%` means literal percent; `a_b` is not an SQL wildcard. A phrase split between subject and requester name is not a hit. Two phrases in one query must both appear within the same item. Text separated by a redaction marker cannot manufacture a phrase, although visible unquoted terms on either side can satisfy a same-item conjunction.

Query and normalization versions are stored with saved definitions/handles. Old q substring/concatenated semantics are not silently reinterpreted as this language; supported old meanings run under an explicitly declared legacy compatibility contract or receive reviewed upgrade/reconciliation. New-source coverage and a parser version are separate facts.

### REQ26-D22-C014 — Structured scope and result order

The effective query contains trusted tenant/actor purpose, mandatory CRM/report/source basis, current inbox/view/work filters, Search in, optional Person or email, text/normalizer/coverage version and current ordering. Text matches source items; work/label/person filters operate over the qualified conversation scope with their explicit owner meaning. A Person or email criterion matches only a permitted Support detail item with literal normalized name/address fragments (or an explicitly selected stable eligible participant reference), not all linked CRM records. Email text remains a lookup clue, not identity or provider mailbox canonicalization.

D20/D21 filters retain their accepted AND/Any/All/No labels/current-target meanings. No new free-form date criterion is smuggled in; a D21 report drilldown keeps its exact component-first cohort as mandatory context. Ordinary broader search removes work filters only through the explicit UI action. In CRM/report context, source-basis escape requires Open in Support Hub with fresh authority. Empty text retains remaining filters; syntax failure never removes them.

For an unconfigured text search, Best match has a small deterministic order: exact full Support reference/ID result first; otherwise select each root's newest qualifying source match by original owner admission/creation instant, unknown last, then stable kind-prefixed source identity. Order root results by the selected match and stable continuing-root identity. No hidden source, repeated phrase, length or occurrence-count boost. An explicit supported saved/user sort takes precedence without changing the text predicate; preview selects the best qualified matching item by the rule above. The transient automatic search sort never overwrites underlying queue/view preferences. Clear text removes that transient order while retaining deliberate filters/sort.

When text is blank, Search in is a retained dormant preference, not an existence condition. Clear filters resets it to All, removes ordinary work/person/label refinements and retains text, current inbox boundary, view identity as Modified where applicable and mandatory CRM/report context. Empty Find clears highlighting/navigation. The exact-reference tier requires the entire parsed query to contain one atom equal to the complete permitted reference; a matching atom among other atoms does not qualify.

### REQ26-D22-C015 — Completeness, chunking and resource limits

Assess index coverage over the eligible structured **pre-text-filter** scope. An unindexed item cannot yet be known not to match the query. Excluded/private/index-forbidden sources are outside declared coverage; unreadied eligible sources are gaps. Emit a truthful incomplete state without revealing hidden source counts. A count/zero/completed ranking is authoritative only when the relevant corpus and exact query completed under current gates. Do not declare complete because every already-returned hit has an index row.

Use source-targeted reads and tenant-leading indexes rather than all-tenant hydration. Normalized literal substring retrieval may use escaped parameterized LIKE/position with pg_trgm candidate indexes, followed by exact verification. Short/punctuation-only patterns can have no useful trigrams and require broad scans. Apply permitted work/person/inbox scope, budget execution and return Refine search when needed. A timeout or truncated candidate list is not a successful zero. Do not discard single-character languages simply to fit a trigram optimization.

Do not concatenate an entire conversation into one tsvector. PostgreSQL17 text search has vector, lexeme and positional limits and language-dependent transformations; those cannot become undisclosed source truncation. If a large item is segmented for storage/index efficiency, candidate retrieval may use any qualifying segment to locate its parent, but must not require all query atoms in one segment. Final verification evaluates all atoms against that one complete eligible source item. Phrase candidates need sufficient overlap derived from the maximum **normalized** phrase length or an equivalent streaming candidate/verifier that cannot miss boundary matches; redaction/field boundaries remain hard. Never fetch/scan a file's contents for filename search.

The deployment profile fixes and tests normalized expansion, current source/segment size, page size, excerpt length/count, query/row/time limits, concurrent work and per-tenant fairness, cancellation, worker/backfill batches, query/handle/cache lifetimes and recovery/freshness deadlines. These values are explicit activation evidence, not speculative universal quotas. Source units over a supported processing boundary become an owner-repair/coverage condition; they are not silently omitted or clipped. UI query bounds are independently 256 scalars/1,024 bytes/16 atoms.

### REQ26-D22-C016 — Revisions, privacy, live pages and navigation

At source restriction/redaction/expiry admission, current serving gates invalidate all stale derived contributions before asynchronous physical deletion. A returned candidate's old body/revision cannot establish a hit even if the old index is still present. Metadata/detail/filename revisions and owner policy matter as much as message bodies. Retained exact IDs/withdrawal fences contain no forbidden content. Restore must apply current source constraints and disposed-generation fences before projecting or serving old records.

Search uses live data, not permanent result membership. A page cursor binds the authorized query/coverage/version/sort and stable keyset; current authority is always rechecked. Mid-query/page topology and source changes can invalidate a continuation or alter ordering. Do not silently substitute a new query or claim snapshot completeness; return the current valid page or a scoped Results changed/Refresh state as appropriate, preserving opened source and draft. Never keep long-lived sensitive result bodies to simulate a snapshot. Selected action IDs are explicit and current commands reauthorize them; changing search membership cannot retarget bulk work.

Match navigation carries original source ID/revision and current root/context qualification through a bounded private handle, not a raw excerpt in a URL. Reopen rechecks source identity and permission; if changed, show current qualified state and match refresh instead of resurrecting the excerpt. Filename navigation stops at metadata; explicit byte access uses the original attachment/version and current storage/hygiene gate. Find in conversation uses the same exact query and eligible source basis, traversing all declared searchable retained items with bounded paging, not the mounted DOM.

Queries, excerpts, normalized text and index material are sensitive derivatives with owner lifetime. Source-derived material cannot remain searchable/readable beyond source authority; physical retirement follows the actual bounded owner cleanup, lawful preservation and restore policy. Independently authored query text remains governed configuration under D20, while known source-derived query fragments retain their restrictions. Search logs/Recent copies cannot create a new retention purpose. D20 handles are authenticated references, not bearer grants. Caches and in-flight requests carry tenant/principal/acting scope plus query/source versions; revocation/tenant switch fences late responses. UI cannot retract a screenshot or previously observed text, but Asym stops new serving and clears stale controlled representations promptly under its owner contract.

### REQ26-D22-C017 — CRM, Email Studio and future AI

CRM search applies D9 original-source relevance/correspondence basis before D10 root union. A record linked to B does not inherit A's old searchable messages. D12 relations do not recursively enlarge the corpus, and a Staff context citation proves no access to its target. Exact references or participant strings create no Party, identity link, contact history, receipt or approval. Shared underlying Asym identity remains authoritative; no cross-system sync is introduced.

P17 Email Studio owns reusable wording and exact preparation; Support owns admitted conversation/draft/recipient/source facts; P6 owns actual tenant Resend delivery evidence. Only actual eligible admitted Support source text participates. Search/Find does not call Resend/provider search, prepare messages, copy a note into a reply or consume P6/P17 Recent. Index failure is local to search; an otherwise valid reply still follows its independent admission/delivery controls. A search hit is never permission for a financial/care/contact mutation.

Future AI/broader retrieval can consume a later-qualified version of the typed source contract: original identity, current eligible projection/revision, mode/coverage semantics and retrievable evidence. Actual AI context/egress/citation/retention/suggestion/connection requirements remain with Phase40 and shared Core owners; file content with Phase29-compatible mechanics and its semantic owner. No embeddings, provider keys, extraction, unused adapters, AI query grammar or disabled AI UI now. A future feature cannot reinterpret a saved keyword query or lift indexability exclusions merely to improve recall.

### REQ26-D22-C018 — Migration and proof

Inventory actual stores and source-type eligibility, index existence, legacy q semantics and current URL/caching behavior. Add compatible projection/version/withdrawal contracts; backfill only current eligible originals with original admission times. Legacy sources with uncertain admission or retention are not silently treated as safe. Fence old raw-message/body/index endpoints, fixture authority and raw-query serialization. Old searches require exact legacy compatibility or explicit reviewed upgrade, not a partial migration that reports false complete results.

Gate source kind and tenant activation on real coverage/privacy/query proof. Search stop controls preserve ordinary source work and current owner navigation while denying unsafe retrieval; old destructive/leaky code cannot be the rollback fallback. Recover through current-source roll-forward and rebuild. P01–P40 define source, grammar, permissions, failures, concurrency, migration, accessibility and production-shaped acceptance.

### REQ26-D22-C020 — Accepted source coverage and permanent boundaries

Current keyword search covers eligible Support details, admitted messages and internal notes, qualified D12 Staff context and permitted attachment filenames. Source kind and delivery state remain truthful: an admitted queued, failed or uncertain reply is not labelled Sent or Delivered. Search never substitutes a combined transcript or arbitrary CRM properties for original source identities and revisions.

Index eligibility is separate from read permission. Phase10 restricted-tier and P9 care/finance-provenance exclusions remain governing floors. There is no direct-scan bypass for data whose indexing is forbidden. Private drafts, unadmitted prepared candidates, raw MIME/headers/provider bodies, D19-held intake, Email Studio reusable sources and P6/P17 Recent copies are outside the corpus. ADR0031's prohibition on using Recent as search authority remains explicit.

Broader search and AI-assisted conversation search are recorded as the founder's future direction, outside current scope. No attachment extraction, OCR, semantic answers, embeddings, provider/model calls, speculative vector columns or disabled AI controls are authorized now. Later qualification reuses typed original source/revision, eligibility, coverage, mode and provenance through the appropriate Phase29/40/shared AI boundaries.

### REQ26-D22-C021 — Accepted matching, filters and complete user journey

One item-scoped literal fragment/quoted-phrase contract requires all atoms within an eligible original source item. It permits partial-word fragments, preserves punctuation and uses versioned Unicode NFC/full casefold/whitespace normalization. It adds no stemming, accent stripping, implicit Boolean language, wildcard, regex or fuzzy meaning. Straight and paired curly quotes, escaping, incomplete-input guidance and literal apostrophes follow the complete companion contract. Bounds remain 256 Unicode scalar values, 1,024 UTF-8 bytes and 16 atoms. A single-character query is valid; an actual resource limit calls for Refine search, never a false zero or falsely complete capped result.

Redacted or hidden gaps cannot create substring/phrase adjacency. Unquoted atoms may occupy separate permitted visible runs of the same source item; different fields or messages cannot jointly satisfy an item match. The explicit Person or email filter supplies permitted cross-field refinement without turning email into identity or disclosure authority.

The existing search field, Status/Assignee/Labels and qualified Filters remain the primary interface. Search in adds a compact source refinement with All, Details, Messages, Notes, Staff context and Attachment names. The initial 200ms debounce is IME-aware and cancellable, with Enter immediate; it is not a latency promise. Existing explicit user/saved sort survives. A new unconfigured text search uses the exact-reference-first, then original-source-recency Best match order with unknown time last and stable ties; no occurrence-frequency score. Transient search ordering does not overwrite saved queue ordering.

Clear search retains filters and makes Search in dormant when text is blank. Clear filters keeps text, resets Search in and ordinary refinements, preserves inbox/view identity as Modified and mandatory CRM/report context. Reset view remains distinct. Search all my accessible Support conversations explicitly broadens ordinary work scope while retaining query/Search in and all access boundaries; leaving a mandatory CRM/report context requires explicit Open in Support Hub with return context. An exact ID is not a scope bypass.

One current root result follows original-source authority and exact matching before D10 grouping, count and pagination. Safe excerpts identify their source kind and navigate to the current qualified original source/revision. Filename lookup never automatically fetches bytes. Find in conversation searches the complete eligible retained source population rather than mounted DOM and preserves CRM/report basis; an empty Find clears highlights/navigation. Loading, indexing/incomplete coverage, errors, Refine search, true no matches and changed results remain distinguishable.

### REQ26-D22-C022 — Accepted database, privacy, concurrency and recovery contract

One shared API/list/query owner uses a private rebuildable Asym Postgres projection, qualified candidate retrieval and exact verification. No external search engine or parallel legacy engine is introduced. pg_trgm remains subject to actual extension/index/plan qualification. Candidate or chunk boundaries cannot alter match truth. Pre-text eligible scope determines completeness; completeness is not inferred only from returned candidates.

Current tenant/source/field/context gates apply before hits, rank, count and snippets and again at navigation. D9 CRM association with one original source does not expose another through merge; D12 related conversations remain independent. Tenant-aware references, private grants, both RLS USING/WITH CHECK, immutable attribution, parameterized queries and service/definer/worker paths must enforce the same boundaries. No query/result action mutates Party identity, ownership, CRM records, giving or care data.

Source admission and a durable projection intent or discoverable gap commit atomically. Revision-ordered, idempotent jobs reread current sources without body copies in events. Index failure cannot prevent otherwise qualified authoritative source admission. Immediate serving restrictions at redaction, expiry or reclassification precede bounded physical cleanup; restore barriers prevent resurrection. No instantaneous-erasure claim is made.

Complete predicates precede count/page limits. Continuations bind the current query/scope and revisions; changed live results require truthful Refresh semantics rather than an invented snapshot. Highlighting escapes current source text and maps normalized offsets to original graphemes. Query handles are authenticated and bounded; raw queries do not enter URLs, referrers, telemetry or a new recent-search archive. Cache generations include tenant, principal, scope and relevant versions.

Saved coverage/parser/normalizer versions preserve supported meaning inside the same owner or require reviewed reconciliation. There is no silent broadening on upgrade. D21 component-first report cohorts remain exact through drilldown rather than substituting a root-createdAt filter. Finite source/derived retention, body-free diagnostics, durable lifecycle receipts and current permissions extend across caches, exports, backups and restores.

### REQ26-D22-C023 — Email Studio, delivery and acceptance evidence

The explicit Email Studio integration record documents the accepted seam: P17 owns reusable authoring, qualified presentation and exact preparation; Support owns source eligibility, search, current draft/recipients and admission; Phase6 owns actual delivery/evidence using the tenant's qualified Resend connection. Search itself does not prepare, publish or send, requires no new Email Studio template and never searches the library or Recent as a fallback. Later human replies retain their independently authorized P17 → Support → P6 path. D13's Support request received template and eligibility remain separate. Search cannot trigger a confirmation, follow, label, CRM interaction or business action.

Additive inventory/backfill, original timestamps and explicit unknown history, old-writer/URL/fixture fencing, stop controls, safe roll-forward and restore barriers remain required. All 40 proof groups remain required and unexecuted: documentary/source checks and the isolated existing-matcher experiment do not prove the new parser, SQL, RLS, capacity, browser, accessibility or operational implementation.

## D22 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D22-O01

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed forbidden hit/count/rank/snippet/filename, cross-tenant contribution or restored forbidden source.

**Owner:** Platform security/on-call and Support search owner.

**Response:** Immediately contain the affected serving path; preserve minimal evidence, purge/repair scope and require source-authorization regression proof before reactivation.

### OP26-D22-O02

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed false-complete/false-zero result, source-boundary match error, duplicate continuing result or silently changed saved-query meaning.

**Owner:** Support query owner.

**Response:** Withdraw misleading completeness, expose truthful unavailable state, repair predicate/projection/version mapping and verify exact boundary examples.

### OP26-D22-O03

**Signal and threshold:** Any eligible projection gap beyond its registered recovery/freshness deadline, or one stale revision successfully replacing current projection.

**Owner:** Source/index worker owner.

**Response:** Reconcile from current source, retry idempotently, block stale serving and identify missing durable scheduling; never replay old payload copies.

### OP26-D22-O04

**Signal and threshold:** Registered query/error/resource budget exceeded for two consecutive five-minute windows, or any tenant escaping its concurrency/resource ceiling.

**Owner:** Core operations plus query owner.

**Response:** Apply scoped backpressure/cancellation, provide Refine search or temporary unavailable state, inspect safe query class/plans and repair without adding result caps disguised as completeness.

### OP26-D22-O05

**Signal and threshold:** Any unresolved migration/source-eligibility/saved-meaning conflict at activation, or a reproducible staff inability to reach a valid displayed match.

**Owner:** Support product/configuration owner with query owner.

**Response:** Gate the affected scope, assign bounded repair through existing operations, preserve ordinary Support handling and verify exact source/navigation semantics. No raw-query collection campaign or mandatory new workflow.

### REQ26-D22-C024 — Operating and qualification sequence

These are required operational contracts, not automations created in this session. Exact deployment profile limits are activation gates, not invented measured service levels.

## D23 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D23-R01 — One managed model for all legitimate Support inboxes

Adopt inbox-managed signatures with responder personalization as the ordinary human-email reply model. B, universal team-only signatures, is the strongest simpler alternative: less identity disclosure and configuration, less personal continuity. C, personal signature libraries, offers individual variants but adds stewardship and inconsistent details without a demonstrated Asym requirement. A permits a deliberately configured team-only signature within the same managed model; it does not implement all three alternatives.

Use the same capability for Donor Care and any other authorized Support inbox. Inbox wording and approved public responder details express the actual team; do not create departments, staff roles, ministry workflows or donor-specific template variants merely as examples. This signature has no business-action, permission or identity-verification authority.

### REQ26-D23-R02 — Email Studio owns the reusable source; copy it into the draft

Qualify a narrow **Reply signature** purpose in Phase17's existing tenant-owned structured Saved Section authoring/publication capability. It is distinct from D18's Reply/Internal note saved wording; it is not a third mode in that picker. Support owns a compatible same-tenant inbox-consumer binding. There is no Support-owned raw-HTML signature store, personal signature library, new email Layout Role or system-message catalog key.

When a new external reply draft first needs its signature, resolve one eligible complete published signature variant and copy that exact structured revision into a managed draft slot, with source/revision/copy provenance. Do not store a runtime nested Saved Section expression or re-expand mutable source on Send. Ordinary signature edits never fan out into existing draft copies or history. P17 prepares the complete approved body using the existing compatible Service message Role Layout and Brand Kit; no per-inbox Role Layout is introduced. Reuse is one owner and copy semantics, not synchronization between two libraries. This explicitly qualifies the previously open D4/D18 signature seam while preserving ADR0030.

### REQ26-D23-R03 — Public responder identity has its own qualified meaning

Resolve personalization from the actual authenticated human admitting the reply and that person's current tenant membership, through the existing identity/profile owner's authorized public-presentation projection. Never use conversation assignee, template author, CRM record owner, supplied agent ID, email match or a user-editable claim as authority. Public responder name is an explicitly suitable display value; do not split first/last names, derive it from a login address, disclose legal name by default or infer a title from IAM privileges.

If the existing owner lacks a suitable public-name field/command, qualify that minimal tenant-membership presentation extension in the identity owner. Do not create a second staff directory or repurpose the current displayName endpoint that also changes full_name. Own-public-name edits require current identity-owner permission, clear external-use explanation, trusted attribution and a new revision; changing them does not change legal/auth/CRM identity. Optional public title is available only from an equally qualified owner field; inbox/team wording is sufficient otherwise. Private email, phone, photo, location and care/missionary records are not fallback inputs.

### REQ26-D23-R04 — Separate authoring, publication, inbox configuration and sending

Use existing Core capability and scope conventions for signature-source read/use, source author/edit, publish/review, inbox binding management and actual Support reply. A delegated inbox manager can select an eligible published source within their scope without becoming its publisher; a Studio publisher gains no inbox administration, conversation or CRM access merely by publishing. General reusable metadata and source previews obey their authorized audience; impact counts and linked inbox names reveal only permitted configuration context.

Keep ordinary qualified self-publication under P17 simple. Its existing protected-publication and tenant-stricter independent-review rules remain effective when actually applicable, including shared Brand Kit/layout changes used by protected messages. Do not invent an always-two-person signature review rule or bypass a protected floor by naming content a signature. Human reply composition is not a new publication event.

### REQ26-D23-R05 — Add, find and edit through one coherent management journey

Provide Support settings → Inboxes → the selected inbox → **Reply signature**, showing effective source, language, current published revision, a compact preview and clear **Change signature** and authorized **Edit in Email Studio** actions. New signature and Customize open the same focused P17 authoring capability with a preserved return destination; no disconnected second editor or copy/paste transfer.
