Email Studio exposes the same assets through its Signatures-purpose view with search, Active/Archived and meaningful name/usage metadata. Contextual access shows only eligible assets.

New starts from a restrained tenant-compatible starter or a deliberate copy of an eligible source. Duplicate creates a new source identity and unpublished draft with provenance, never a live alias. Give it a clear internal name, optional description and declared language. UI labels explain internal metadata versus recipient-visible text. Unsaved work, permissions, loading, no signatures, no matches, validation failure, save uncertainty and unavailable assets have distinct repairable states. No setup wizard or personal-signature onboarding is required for every responder.

### REQ26-D23-R06 — Saving a draft does not publish or apply it

P17 draft autosave uses optimistic concurrency and explicit Saving/Saved/Not saved/Conflict feedback. A save checkpoint, preview, commit, publication and inbox application are different effects with different receipts. A published source opens as a new editable candidate; its current publication stays in use until a valid new publication succeeds. Review the exact candidate, language/fields/assets, before/after and permitted consumer impact. Ordinary **Publish** or required **Submit for review** follows existing P17 rules; failure preserves the prior good publication.

An unpublished new source cannot be selected as an inbox's effective signature. A contextual **Publish and use for this inbox** convenience may sequence the existing commands, but must truthfully distinguish Published from Applied. If the second step fails, the source remains published and the prior inbox binding remains effective; reconcile the same apply intent. No cross-owner best-effort transaction may show both steps complete when only one succeeded.

### REQ26-D23-R07 — Deterministic inbox defaults and safe shared updates

Each inbox resolves exactly one effective complete signature variant for a supported locale, or one explicit permitted team-only/no-optional-signature posture. The logical binding identifies an exact eligible immutable signature publication and its approved locale-resolution generation; every draft copy records the exact selected variant revision. There is no personal-first/first-row/null-owner fallback ladder, row-order default or runtime deep merge. Reusing one source across several inboxes is deliberate. Publishing a new signature revision does not advance inbox bindings automatically or require a global inbox transaction. It may remain published and unassigned.

Change binding compares its expected revision and commits the new binding/resolution evidence and history atomically. The maintainer's reviewed Use for inboxes action may apply a published revision to an explicit bounded authorized set, validating all selected consumers and expected heads before an atomic set replacement; failure changes none of that selected set. Keep source publication separate from application and show current versus available newer version. A contextual Publish and use can complete the ordinary single-inbox journey in one deliberate action with R06's truthful two-stage result. Existing draft copies remain pinned when the binding changes; an explicit refresh copies from the now-selected revision. Qualified public-name changes are resolved under current actor/public-data checks before new preparation. Actual source/privacy/retirement fences can stop unsafe use. Do not manufacture a per-inbox shared-content fork merely to store selection. Changing a shared source does not change From/Reply-To, routing, assignment or CRM ownership.

### REQ26-D23-R08 — Professional visual freedom within the email presentation system

Default to clear, compact text: approved public responder name, team/organization identity and only useful approved contact information. Permit restrained emphasis, line breaks, links and an optional approved logo through the signature profile. Tenant Brand Kit supplies compatible email-safe typography, colors, spacing and contrast; app editing controls retain base-maia/Base UI and shared semantic tokens. Do not force Asym's web UI colors into tenant email branding.

Offer a clean text starter and a logo-with-text starter as authored examples within the same profile, not new Layout Roles. Essential identity stays real text. Do not include promotional banners, donation appeals, tracking pixels, animated imagery, social-icon strips, personal portraits, long disclaimers or decorative complexity by default. No mandatory role-by-inbox-by-language style matrix. Plain text must preserve useful identity and link meaning. No universal optimal pixel size, byte cap or deliverability claim is inferred from a vendor example; enforce qualified shared presentation/asset bounds and publish their concrete values before activation.

### REQ26-D23-R09 — Governed logo, links and asset disclosure

The initial signature purpose permits at most one logo occurrence. Select a qualified tenant-owned immutable asset with scan/readiness, content type, dimensions, size, alternative-text purpose and publication/use scope; uploading or replacing it uses the shared asset owner and creates a new version. A draft upload is not a published or publicly retrievable file. Remove staged unused assets through the owner's cleanup path. Never fetch arbitrary pasted image URLs, store base64/blob URLs as publication authority, hotlink private case files or render an employee avatar implicitly.

The complete message must deduplicate/omit optional repeated branding through its qualified presentation contract before review, never hide required identity. Hosted/CID representation is the existing P17/P6 asset contract's decision: provider CID support alone does not qualify it for Asym. Do not introduce a second image pipeline. Images blocked, omitted or unavailable must leave the signature understandable. Informational HTTPS, mailto and tel destinations require context-specific validation and escaping; visible labels cannot conceal a changed destination. Header injection, protected-action links, message-recipient variables and arbitrary record-path tokens are forbidden here. Links disclose no private context and never change the actual Reply-To.

### REQ26-D23-R10 — Language and team-only behavior are explicit

Store exact authored language variants under the same source and the existing P17 locale/fallback rules. A translation is independently authored/reviewed content with truthful freshness, not an automatic translation promise or a combinatorial signature library. Copy the variant matching the reviewed reply's resolved locale; do not infer language from a person's name or rewrite their public display name. Long, non-Latin, single-part and RTL/mixed-script names must remain intact.

An inbox may deliberately use team-only signature wording. Missing optional public-name data uses only an explicitly configured compatible team fallback, visibly reflected before approval. A missing required value blocks preparation with a targeted repair path; no fabricated sample/name/email substitution. Team-only signature means exactly that: From display, body, attachments and quoted history may still identify staff. Do not promise anonymity; any fuller privacy need must be checked through the existing complete-message and Sender/Reply Identity owners.

### REQ26-D23-R11 — One visible managed block in the normal reply composer

Show the resolved managed signature inline below the editable human body before Send, with a quiet labelled **Signature** details menu. Its display is not another focusable editor instance. Normal responders do not pick from a library on each reply or directly rewrite the managed source. **Refresh signature** deliberately replaces only the managed slot against the expected draft revision, preserves body/attachments/recipients and the draft's omission choice, and returns focus predictably. Restore reveals the retained pinned copy after current eligibility checks; it does not silently fetch a newer version. If that copy cannot be used, offer explicit Refresh/repair rather than substitution. An actual sending-inbox or resolved-locale change reselects/requalifies the signature copy for that new context and shows the difference before approval, preserving the body/audience/attachments and omission choice where permitted; routing or assignee changes alone are not that trigger. Any actor/audience/public-data change invalidating reviewed preparation is shown before new approval.

Because this is an optional human closing, allow **Hide for this reply** and **Restore signature** as deliberate local draft actions where the signature purpose permits omission. They never remove required organization/legal/footer content owned by P17, change the inbox default or persist as a hidden preference for later replies. No extra confirmation modal is needed for reversible hide/restore. Exactly one managed signature slot exists per draft; D18 insertions, refresh and retries cannot duplicate it. Do not regex-delete a manually typed closing, a quoted previous signature or historic content to guess intent. Internal Notes carry internal authorship and no external signature.

### REQ26-D23-R12 — One canonical document and exact preparation/delivery

P17's versioned Asym structured document with canonical Tiptap JSON is the authoritative content representation; HTML and real plain text are derived compiled artifacts. The signature copy and its origin, typed field descriptors and omission state participate in the reviewed complete draft/preparation. Signature-source authoring previews use stored synthetic fixtures. Real responder/recipient context is resolved only in the authorized live Support draft/preparation, never exported into the shared library preview.

Support owns current actual actor, visible audience, source access and atomic reply admission. P17 resolves only authorized public presentation facts and compiles the complete body with compatible immutable dependencies. Phase6 sends the sealed HTML/text/envelope through tenant-owned Resend under D4/ADR0029/0032. No mutable provider template, direct Support mailer, global fallback or rerender on retry. A routine publication/name change does not rewrite prepared or sent history; actual restrictive fences follow definitely-unsubmitted versus may-have-submitted recovery. Signature content is not delivery proof, a cryptographic signature or proof of representation.

### REQ26-D23-R13 — Tiptap everywhere it serves rich authoring, with bounded profiles

Use shared Tiptap 3 editing for human email replies, internal notes, D18 personal/shared reusable wording, signature authoring and any existing Support staff-brief/long-form field whose accepted owner contract supports rich text. For fields intentionally plain, a Tiptap plain-text profile is appropriate only if it improves an existing long-form editing workflow without changing its authoritative semantics. Do not add rich data merely because the editor can.

Use purpose-specific code-owned profiles for Reply, Internal note, saved wording and Reply signature over the same canonical schema. Only authorized nodes/marks/attributes/assets/variables are enabled for that purpose in both editor and server. Signature admits paragraphs/text/hard breaks, restrained emphasis, safe links, public responder tokens and the governed optional logo; not headings, lists, tables, code, blockquotes, mentions, receipt/action nodes or arbitrary layouts. Reply/note retain their separately qualified vocabulary rather than inherit every StarterKit feature. Search, subjects, labels, names, emails, dates, filters, statuses and reason selectors stay appropriate native/shared inputs. Read-only conversation history uses the safe static renderer rather than mounting an editor for every message. Unsupported content/rendering failure is an explicit current-authority-aware unavailable/repair state, never a successful empty message; static text derivation preserves block boundaries and D22's source/redaction semantics.

### REQ26-D23-R14 — Validate before parsing; never silently lose canonical meaning

Validate the complete original JSON against the versioned canonical purpose/schema, including unknown attributes, marks, node positions, allowed value types, depth/size/count budgets and protected/source metadata, before a Tiptap/ProseMirror parser can normalize it. Then perform editor-schema and server semantic/disclosure validation. Toolbar visibility is not a content or permission boundary. The installed-source experiment proves that hidden toolbar features remain schema-admissible and unknown attributes can disappear despite a strict parser option.

Handle contentError by stopping writable initialization/autosave/admission and preserving the original owner-retained bytes, with a useful read-only Needs migration or repair state. Merely enabling content checks does not authorize retrying stripped content. Known safe clipboard text/formatting conversion may normalize into the profile with a clear concise report of removed unsupported formatting; unsafe active content and external assets never execute/fetch. Unknown canonical saved structure must not be treated like harmless pasted styling. Migration is a reviewed new candidate with loss report, never silent in-place replacement.

### REQ26-D23-R15 — Variables, mentions and editor actions stay inert until authorized

Use indivisible typed picker nodes rather than executable brace strings or arbitrary property paths. For signatures, allow only the current purpose's public responder and approved team/organization descriptors; forbid donor/giving/care/missionary fields, protected actions, dynamic recipient lists, arbitrary expressions, free-form CSS/HTML and user-defined nodes. Do not recursively interpret resolved text. Literal braces in correspondence are ordinary text unless they are actual typed nodes.

Shared editor reuse does not enable @mentions, broadcasts, AI rewrites, collaboration or automation in a signature. Internal-note mentions follow the existing current-user and admission checks; a saved scaffold does not notify anyone. Switching Reply/Note preserves separate drafts and provenance. Pasted hidden/internal-only data cannot become externally disclosable by changing the toolbar or stripping its origin. Signature/public-name edits never update a CRM record or complete an underlying action.

### REQ26-D23-R16 — Accessible, responsive and durable authoring

Use Core's shared Base UI/maia controls, visible labels, semantic toolbar/button states, keyboard navigation, screen-reader naming, focus restoration and equivalent accessible outline/field editing of the same document. Placeholder text alone is not a label. Pasting, undo/redo, links, variables, logo selection/removal and publication have keyboard/touch paths; no hover-only repair or drag-only rearrangement. Announcements distinguish formatting toggles, save status and failures without reading every keystroke or countdown.

On mobile, the signature remains a compact inline part of the message and long-form editing uses available width. Test narrow/zoomed viewports, text expansion, RTL/IME, focus with the virtual keyboard and images blocked. Reuse D4/P17 tenant/principal-scoped draft recovery; preserve unsaved work across qualified navigation/retry, never publish or send from offline/queued editor intent automatically. Mark Not saved until server confirmation. Revoked access clears unauthorized material and stale responses cannot repopulate another tenant's editor.

### REQ26-D23-R17 — Database and RLS make ownership enforceable

Asym Postgres remains authoritative through the shared business API. Use tenant-aware keys/FKs for inbox, signature source/family/revision, publication, asset and membership endpoints; stable source identity is distinct from mutable name and real actor attribution. Require valid purpose/state/revision combinations and one effective binding per inbox, with exact locale resolution. No nullable owner-agent convention may toggle a shared object into personal ownership. Reject unknown ids, stale expected revisions and update-as-create behavior; do not silently upsert a lost published source.

Revoke unqualified direct table writes. Evaluate grants, RLS SELECT and effective USING/WITH CHECK for every mutation, views/security-invoker behavior, function execute grants, fixed definer search paths and service/worker checks. Omitted WITH CHECK can inherit USING in PostgreSQL; the required proof is actual old/new-row and column invariants, not syntax alone. Tenant, actual actor, authorship, publication, audit and membership facts come from trusted current server context. Updates cannot move rows across tenant/owner/source/purpose or invent publication. Narrow column mutation and owner commands enforce facts beyond row visibility. Asset/storage paths use the same source and tenant checks.

### REQ26-D23-R18 — Concurrency and idempotency attach to the business effect

Autosave, create/copy, publish, inbox apply, refresh/hide, archive/restore and public-name changes each use their owning revision/command boundary. Same durable intent and identical inputs reconcile its original result; changed input conflicts; a new deliberate action has a new identity. Old replay cannot restore an earlier default or overwrite a later draft. Server responses distinguish original outcome from current state. Out-of-order autosave replies cannot mark a newer draft Saved.

Publication and its head/control evidence are atomic; inbox rebinding and its revision/history are atomic. Serialize default switch against source publication/restriction/archive and current capability generation so a retired/cross-scope source cannot win a race. A preview is not a write lock; compare current heads at commit. Durable secondary work is idempotent and source-revision-aware; logs/events carry minimal identifiers, not full draft bodies. Correct actor history records service execution separately from initiating human authority.

### REQ26-D23-R19 — CRM continuity without a staff or customer shadow

Requester, message participant, authenticated responder, tenant membership, CRM Party, represented organization, coordinator and CRM owner remain distinct. Signatures personalize the responder, not the requester. Support opened from an authorized CRM context uses the same draft, signature source and sending path, preserving return context; the CRM association never expands source or signature permissions. Public-name maintenance stays in its identity owner and cannot update Party.full_name/contact values or create CRM people to satisfy a renderer.

Only normal admitted correspondence contributes to its existing permitted Support/CRM history projection. Saving, publishing, selecting, refreshing or hiding a signature is configuration/draft history, not a contact interaction or new sent message. CRM merges, contact changes or unlinking cannot reassign responder identity or rewrite old correspondence. Giving, receipts, refunds, recurring gifts and care workflows retain independent domain permissions and authoritative outcomes.

### REQ26-D23-R20 — Archive, restriction, departure and retention differ

Routine archive stops new selection/copying, preserves required history and does not revoke valid draft copies/preparations. An archive of a source still effectively bound to inboxes requires explicit reviewed replacement/return to a compatible team default or permitted no-optional-signature posture for those consumers; no dangling defaults or invisible fallback. A source maintainer lacking inbox-management scope cannot silently rebind those inboxes. If all affected consumers exceed the registered atomic-operation bound, authorized managers may deliberately rebind bounded subsets while the source remains active, then atomically archive against the complete remaining set/revision; never silently truncate the affected set. A safety restriction must remain available even when ordinary replacement or compilation fails: current-use fences stop unsafe use and route repair to the right owner.

Shared source custody is tenant-owned and survives creator departure. Member removal revokes the person's current use, not shared publications or sent messages by cascade. No email-based reassignment of custody. Source revisions, public-name revisions, copied draft/prepared/admitted text, assets, audit and command receipts keep their actual finite owner purposes. D16/D17 restrictions and restore barriers govern copied content and known derivatives; no forever signature history, stale public-name exposure, leaked draft export or silent resurrection. Already sent email cannot be recalled by editing a signature.

### REQ26-D23-R21 — Source-derived search and history remain truthful

D22 searches eligible admitted original message content, including whatever signature was actually admitted, under its current source/revision/retention rules. It does not search the reusable signature library, private drafts, provider Recent or today's resolved profile in place of past wording. Ordinary signature-source changes do not bump conversation activity, reply-target metrics, labels, follows or search timestamps. A template/public-name correction requiring source restriction uses the owning privacy workflow rather than silently rewriting a historical reply. Reports do not count signature insertion as a reply or support completion.

### REQ26-D23-R22 — Failure recovery belongs to the failing owner

Editor load/save failures preserve authorized draft work and show local repair. Signature publication failure keeps the previous valid publication; binding failure keeps the previous binding. Missing/restricted required facts or dependencies block the affected preparation with exact safe guidance, not every unrelated inbox. A configured compatible team/no-optional-signature posture may proceed only if the complete current approved message remains allowed; no secret fallback strips unsafe content after approval.

Email Studio maintenance or signature library search is not a Resend operation. Sending failure remains D4/P6 exact-effect recovery, with prepared/may-have-submitted states and no blind rekey/resend. Technical logs contain safe identities, revisions, cause classes and timing; durable author/publisher/configuration history is distinct from source communication history and security audit. Real owner repair attention uses existing P17/P6 presentation contracts, not a new signature-email template or notification campaign.

### REQ26-D23-R23 — Qualify the actual Tiptap dependency closure

Use stable Tiptap 3 as explicitly selected, through the shared UI boundary. Prefer its current composable React API where it improves shared toolbar/context composition; retain a sound useEditor wrapper when replacing it adds no benefit. Next.js editor initialization must keep immediatelyRender:false where required; mounted editor state and production server compilation remain separate.

Before activation, audit the exact consumer dependency closure, align the interdependent Tiptap release/peer cohort and qualify the current stable release with React Email, parser, extensions and Node runtime. No blind whole-repo upgrade, copied third-party UI kit, Radix primitive, second editor framework or mismatched duplicate editor runtime is authorized by this decision.

### REQ26-D23-R24 — Browser editing does not prove email rendering

Use the P17 server compiler and approved node mappings for deterministic HTML and real plain text. Tiptap static rendering and React Email export are useful implementation capabilities, not automatic substitutes for the canonical validator or proof of email-client compatibility. Never accept caller-provided bodyHtml/bodyText as independently authoritative signature sources. Do not pass untrusted JSON directly through a renderer and rely on its unknown-node fallback.

Qualify the pinned mappings in the actual production runtime without general DOM emulation or a new markup language. Prove complete-message output, synthetic and actual authorized-context parity, no duplicate wrapper/footer, email-safe layout/read order, stable links, HTML/text equivalence, images-blocked/dark/light/high-contrast/narrow/long-name/RTL cases and representative supported mail clients. Use real test deliveries only in the implementation test flow, through the tenant's qualified Resend path with safe synthetic fixtures and test attribution.

### REQ26-D23-R25 — Bound the work and keep ordinary composition fast

Before activation, register concrete numeric document bytes, nodes/depth, field lengths, variable/link counts, logo dimensions/bytes, complete-message totals, autosave/compile/query budgets and tested concurrency in the shared purpose/asset contracts. Enforce the strictest applicable bound before expensive parsing/rendering and prove zero, exact maximum and over-limit outcomes. The one-logo signature bound is a product choice, not a vendor limit. Do not claim unlimited signatures, payloads or editor instances, nor import folklore byte/font thresholds as universal safety.

Use complete authorized queries and pagination for library/consumer management, indexed tenant/source/revision/binding lookups, scoped caches and bounded impact evaluation. Signature-source publication is independent of a global inbox graph. Selected binding sets are bounded and atomic; existing P17 Brand Kit/Role Layout shared-dependency changes still keep their governing complete-graph validation. Load editor code for editing surfaces; read-only message lists use static rendering. Isolate editor subscriptions to necessary state, preserve focus/selection, and avoid recompiling the whole message or rereading every CRM record on each keystroke.

### REQ26-D23-R26 — Migrate deliberately and preserve a safe rollout path

Inventory every old signature row, bodyHtml/bodyText/agent-generated path, inbox setting, macro/import/fixture, editor profile and API writer. Do not auto-publish raw legacy HTML or silently import private staff data into a public signature. Convert eligible content into a new structured candidate with source provenance/loss report; incompatible sources stay access-controlled read-only Needs migration. Reconcile inbox defaults explicitly, including missing/departed owners and existing agent-owned selections. Preserve original history and required privacy fences, not destructive cascades.

Add owner schema/contracts before compatible readers; qualify conversion, P17 preparation and binding commands; fence old writers/direct sends; then activate per qualified scope. Stop controls can disable new signature/editor writes while preserving safe existing reads, drafts and already admitted effect reconciliation. Rollback cannot revive raw HTML authority, mixed unsupported schema, withdrawn assets or old broad policies. Restore requires current source restrictions before serving; use roll-forward when new schema/content cannot safely run on old code.

### REQ26-D23-R27 — Trace every requirement to proof without overstating readiness

Maintain D23-R01–R28 → UX/data/evidence → ADR/glossary → OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets → implementation and release evidence. P01–P44 below are required independent outcome proof, not tests mirroring the implementation. Documentation validation checks consistency, preservation, source pins and links only.

### REQ26-D23-R28 — Finish the bounded capability without importing adjacent products

No Tiptap Cloud, paid collaboration/comments/version-history service, AI generation/search/translation, CMS/editor migration outside the genuine shared seam, campaign signature system, generic workflow engine, digital-signature product or new CRM is required. Existing P17 revision/preview/publication, Core IAM/assets, shared UI and P6 delivery remain the owners. D13 automated acknowledgements retain their real Email Studio template; human signatures add no system-message catalog entry. No routine signature save/publish/apply sends mail or changes Support work. Further AI search remains the founder's separately recorded future direction.

### REQ26-D23-C001 — What a responder sees

The ordinary reply composer contains the editable answer and one compact managed signature immediately below it, before any deliberately included quoted history. Staff see its actual resolved wording before sending. Signature text is readable/selectable but not an independent editable region that a pasted reply, Select all or a formatting command can accidentally change. The complete outgoing document still includes this managed slot as canonical structured content; visual separation does not mean a hidden append at Send.

Illustrative content only; these examples establish no new inbox, role or ministry workflow:

The displayed name is the actual responder's qualified public wording. The second line describes the tenant's real inbox/team. It is not inferred from access rights, giving access, a CRM record or the conversation coordinator. An optional logo can sit above the same text using the qualified presentation; no essential meaning depends on loading it.

The quiet **Signature** menu offers Details, **Refresh signature**, **Hide for this reply** or **Restore signature** when appropriate. It is labelled and keyboard/touch accessible. No routine picker, permanent extra toggle row or mandatory preview dialog is added. Hide affects only this draft's optional closing; a small “Signature hidden · Restore” state explains it. The next reply starts with its configured signature. Required organization/legal content in the shared frame remains visible and cannot be removed through this control.

Refresh copies the current selected signature revision into only the managed slot. It preserves the answer, audience, attachments and this draft's Hide choice and participates in draft undo/revision handling before admission. Restore reveals the retained pinned copy after current eligibility checks; if unusable, it offers explicit Refresh/repair rather than silently substituting newer content. An actual sending-inbox or resolved-language change requalifies the copy for that new context and shows the change before approval, preserving the answer/audience/attachments and the omission choice where allowed. Routing or assignee changes alone do not trigger it. Manually typed closings and quoted older signatures are not deleted by guesswork. Inserting D18 wording never appends a second signature.

### REQ26-D23-C002 — A focused inbox settings page

At **Support settings → Inboxes → [Inbox] → Reply signature**, show:

- The selected publication's internal name, authored language and a readable synthetic example.
- A clear state: **In use**, **Newer version available**, **Needs attention**, or an explicit permitted team-only/no-optional-signature posture.
- **Change signature**, which selects an eligible published revision, previews its effect and saves the inbox binding through Support.
- **Edit in Email Studio** and **New signature** when the person has the separate authoring capability.
- A concise explanation: “Used for new email replies from this inbox. Existing drafts keep their selected version until refreshed.”

Do not expose tenant IDs, compiler hashes or provider jargon in the normal screen. Details/history can show source/revision and actual actor when helpful. A person who can configure this inbox but cannot publish may select an existing eligible source. A person who can publish but cannot configure the inbox can edit the source without implicitly changing that inbox. A person with neither receives a useful read-only preview instead of a dead-end editor.

An explicit selection persists an exact published revision, not a mutable “latest” alias. A newly published revision appears as available to authorized managers; it does not silently update inboxes. **Use for inboxes** supports a deliberate bounded selection with before/after and permitted affected names, current revisions and any blocker. The selected set changes atomically or not at all. Users outside the scope cannot infer hidden inbox names/counts.

### REQ26-D23-C003 — Create or edit in Email Studio

The contextual action opens a focused **Reply signature** source view inside the existing authoring surface and preserves **Back to [Inbox]**. Email Studio's Signatures-purpose list addresses the same source records. It has search, Active/Archived, internal names, language, published/draft status and current permitted use. It is not a second library copied from Support.

**New signature** starts with a text-first compatible starter. A logo-with-text starter is an example of the same allowed content, not another layout engine. **Customize** or **Duplicate** deliberately creates a new source draft with provenance; a shared-source edit creates a candidate under its existing identity. Neither operation changes current use.

The form contains internal **Name**, optional **Description**, authored **Language**, a short Tiptap editor and synthetic preview. These metadata controls remain ordinary inputs. The signature body toolbar offers only the qualified purpose's emphasis, links, typed public fields and governed logo control; undo/redo remain available. Typography, color/contrast, spacing and logo presentation use the compatible Email Studio Brand Kit controls. More professional appearance comes from readable composition and dependable output, not arbitrary HTML or CSS.

The public-field picker explains the actual value meaning: **Responder public name**, optional owner-qualified public title, and qualified team/organization values. It contains no donor/customer/CRM property browser, role inference, signature-source author, assignee, personal email, private phone, location, avatar or protected-action token. Current contact wording and links use approved team/organization details; D23 adds no per-person public email/phone descriptors or private-profile fallback.

A Logo control chooses or uploads through the existing governed asset picker. It shows scan/readiness, accepted types and the actual published size/dimension bounds. The author can replace/remove it and supply appropriate alternate-text intent without editing markup. Essential identity remains text; an optional repeated logo in the shared frame is handled by the approved complete-message presentation before review. Loading and failed uploads do not become broken image URLs in a publication.

### REQ26-D23-C004 — Save, publish and apply are distinct

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Action                               | Visible result                                                                                       | What stays unchanged                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Autosave / Save draft                | Saved checkpoint with current revision, or Not saved/Conflict with repair                            | Published source and inbox bindings.                                                  |
| Preview                              | Synthetic complete-message HTML/plain-text and supported scenario previews                           | No source publication, inbox update or message.                                       |
| Publish                              | Exact candidate becomes an eligible immutable source publication                                     | Existing bindings, copied drafts and history.                                         |
| Submit for review                    | Existing P17 review state when policy requires it                                                    | No implied publication or application.                                                |
| Use for this inbox / Use for inboxes | Exact selected eligible publication becomes the source for future draft copies in the reviewed scope | Already copied draft text and admitted preparation/history.                           |
| Publish and use for this inbox       | One deliberate UI action sequences publication and application                                       | If application fails, the source is Published but not Applied; prior binding remains. |
| Restore a prior version              | New draft from permitted historical source, with comparison and normal publication                   | Existing immutable history.                                                           |

The contextual publish-and-use button names the actual target inbox. A success state must report both stages accurately. The UI can reconcile an uncertain result without asking the person to republish or recreate the same signature. When another manager changes the inbox meanwhile, show the current binding and compare rather than overwriting it. No signature operation sends mail or generates a new CRM interaction.

A new publication may remain unassigned. Publishing signature content must not require authority over every inbox that once used it. By contrast, a change to an existing shared Brand Kit/Role Layout still follows its own P17 impact and protected-review rules. The focused signature editor cannot quietly broaden those permissions.

### REQ26-D23-C005 — Public name and privacy

“Public responder name” means the current tenant-membership presentation value approved under the identity owner's policy. Approved does not invent another review queue for every nickname. Staff who can maintain their own public presentation use the shared owner command from a contextual link with a clear explanation of external use. The change does not edit legal/auth/CRM names. Tenant-specific context remains clear if the same person belongs to more than one tenant.

Use the full supplied public string without first-name extraction or ASCII-only restrictions. A public title is optional and must have a qualified source; use the team line if there is none. Missing optional fields omit their complete line/separator. Missing name chooses only an expressly approved team fallback, with its actual result visible, or blocks with a focused repair message.

**Team only** is appropriate when the inbox intentionally speaks as a team. Do not label it Anonymous: headers, body, quoted content and attachments can still identify people. The complete preview must make that distinction visible when configuring the policy, and full-message privacy needs go through the existing identity/sender owners.

### REQ26-D23-C006 — Archive and safety correction

An unused source can be archived from new selection/copying. If a source is currently selected by inboxes, show **Replace and archive** to a person with the necessary source and affected-inbox rights. They review an eligible replacement or explicit permitted team/no-optional-signature posture for each affected consumer. The replacement and archive conditions must win one ordered atomic result; otherwise archive does not complete. This is a real dependency, not a broken editor asking for direct database repair.

A source editor without those inbox rights can see a scoped explanation that the source is in use and the necessary configuration handoff; hidden names/counts stay hidden. If the complete affected set exceeds the atomic action's registered bound, authorized managers can deliberately apply replacements to bounded subsets while the source stays active, then archive against the complete remainder; the UI never truncates the affected set or claims premature completion. No requirement to compile a broken body precedes an archive/configuration correction. A safety restriction is different: it can fence unsafe source use immediately even if replacement is unavailable or no manager is present. The owning repair path distinguishes safe existing pins, definitely-unsubmitted work and possibly-sent effects.

Restore makes a permitted source eligible again after current checks, but does not rebind old inboxes or restore removed content by accident. Creating staff departure, role loss or same-email reuse does not delete the team's signature or hand its custody to another person. Ordinary signature retirement never recalls sent mail or reconstructs redacted history.

### REQ26-D23-C007 — Tiptap across Support Hub

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Surface                                                    | Editing choice                                                                           | Required restraint                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Human email reply                                          | Shared Tiptap Reply profile with managed signature projected alongside the editable body | Canonical complete draft and actual audience approval; no arbitrary HTML export as authority.          |
| Internal note                                              | Shared Tiptap Internal note profile                                                      | Separate draft; no external signature or delivery, inert saved scaffold mentions.                      |
| D18 My/Shared reply wording                                | Same P17 structured Tiptap authoring with purpose-specific fields                        | Preserve existing personal/shared permissions; no signature duplication or automatic business actions. |
| Reply signature                                            | Narrow P17 Tiptap profile                                                                | Managed public-field vocabulary, one optional governed logo, no tables/layout scripting.               |
| Existing rich staff brief or long-form Support content     | Shared Tiptap with its actual owner profile                                              | D12 source/retention/visibility remains; do not invent a new rich-text fact to justify an editor.      |
| Subject/name/label/search/email/filters/date/status/reason | Appropriate ordinary shared/native input                                                 | No rich content or editor dependency for simple values.                                                |
| Admitted history, result snippets and static previews      | Safe source-aware static renderer                                                        | Avoid one editable engine per message; renderer is not a new write authority.                          |

The accessible equivalent outline edits the same canonical source; it is not a raw HTML or second authoritative plain-text mode. Content-error handling preserves the unsupported original and disables writable autosave until repair. The signature-purpose link contract may permit qualified mailto/tel without broadening an unrelated Post editor's HTTP/HTTPS-only policy.

### REQ26-D23-C008 — Required visual and usability proof

Preview typical, longest permitted public name, absent optional fields, team-only, long authored translations, RTL/mixed script, images blocked, narrow/zoomed viewport, dark/light/high contrast and real plain text. Browser preview is useful but does not promise pixel equivalence across email clients. A professional published signature is gated by the P17 complete-message rendering checks.

Keyboard, screen reader, touch and IME users must complete creating, saving, resolving a conflict, choosing a logo/field/link, reviewing, publishing, applying, refreshing, hiding/restoring and returning to the inbox. The normal reply path adds no obligatory steps. Local loss of connection preserves qualified draft recovery and shows Not saved; reconnection does not automatically send or publish. See P01–P44 for the full measurable outcome contract and independent UX evidence for factual comparisons and their limits.

### REQ26-D23-C010 — Ownership matrix

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact                                                      | Owner                                                                | Authoritative versus derived                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Authenticated human and active tenant membership          | Core identity/IAM                                                    | Trusted server identity; no email-match authorization.                                                                      |
| Public responder presentation                             | Existing shared identity/profile owner, minimally extended if needed | Tenant-membership-scoped public name/optional qualified title; distinct from legal/full name, login, IAM role or CRM Party. |
| Signature source and authored variants                    | P17 Saved Section authoring, purpose Reply signature                 | One canonical structured source with immutable revisions/publications.                                                      |
| Signature selection for an inbox                          | Support configuration through the shared business API                           | Exact published revision and qualified locale-resolution binding with expected revision.                                    |
| Compatible Brand Kit / Service message Role Layout        | P17 presentation owners                                              | Existing complete immutable dependencies, no new per-inbox Role Layout.                                                     |
| Managed signature copy                                    | Support draft, through qualified P17 copy/validation                 | Copy of exact published variant plus provenance; not a live source lookup.                                                  |
| Complete reviewed preparation                             | P17, with Support/identity/owner-authorized facts                    | Immutable complete document, compiled HTML/text, dependencies, source/actor/audience and hashes.                            |
| Actual mail envelope, tenant Resend and delivery evidence | P6 / existing provider adapter                                       | Sealed request and provider evidence; signature strings are not delivery proof.                                             |
| CRM identity, relationship, contact, giving/care work     | Actual existing business domains                                     | No authoritative support-side copies or signature-driven updates.                                                           |
| Library usage/impact, search and caches                   | Owner-qualified projections                                          | Rebuildable and current-access constrained; never write or retention authority.                                             |

P17's canonical Asym message includes Tiptap JSON but is broader than an unvalidated editor tree. Client-provided HTML/plain text, extra extensions and raw profile properties do not satisfy the canonical contract. Actual current code gaps are documented in the data review and Tiptap review.

### REQ26-D23-C011 — Why copy-in, not a new layout or live fragment

ADR0030 and P17 define Saved Sections as authoring copies. D23 adds a narrow qualified signature purpose rather than violating that invariant. The inbox consumes a published source revision; the draft receives a managed copy. P17 then compiles that complete document under the already-qualified common presentation.

The arrows do not imply CRM synchronization or a live lookup on delivery retry. Copy source identity, publication revision, selected locale, content hash and effective owner-control revision are provenance. Authorized public-value resolution is a separate preparation fact. Once a complete preparation is admitted, no signature-source/profile/default edit changes its bytes.

### REQ26-D23-C012 — Logical constraints and trusted mutations

Use the actual owning tables/types after inventory. The following invariants are mandatory regardless of physical names:

- Each reusable signature has one immutable tenant/source identity and one code-owned purpose. All locale variants and publications reference that tenant/source. It is shared tenant-custodied content, never personal because owner_agent_id happens to be null.
- Published source structure, publication/variant identities and compiled evidence are immutable. Mutable labels/descriptions cannot smuggle changed content into an existing revision. Editing/restoring creates a new candidate.
- Each inbox has one current versioned selection/posture. An exact compatible publication plus deterministic authored-locale policy resolves at most one full variant. Optional team fallback or no-optional-signature is explicit; unresolved required data is not an empty success.
- Same-tenant composite references bind inbox, source, publication, asset and member endpoints. Use actual endpoint data types consistently; reference strings are not actor identities. Index referencing lookup columns according to real plans rather than assuming FK creation indexes them.
- Creator, editor, reviewer, applier and responder remain distinct trusted actor facts. Caller supplies intended content and expected revisions, not trusted tenant, publisher, audit author or security-control status. Creation and update have different identity semantics; lost/missing update target does not become new content through upsert.
- Current capability/resource checks precede mutation and are rechecked at the atomic effect. An allowed row update cannot alter tenant, purpose, custody, canonical parent or published status arbitrarily. Derive these through the owning command and constrain permissible columns/state combinations.
- Published sources and already admitted communications do not depend on a departing agent row's cascading lifetime. Preserve minimized attribution and necessary source-control evidence under owner retention. Ordinary deletion cannot cascade through shared publication, history or independent CRM records.
- A draft has at most one managed signature occurrence, whose copied structure/provenance and explicit omission state participate in the draft revision. Public values and copied source stay distinct. A raw body match is not occurrence identity.

Review table/column grants, direct REST/collection writes, service clients, maintenance/import paths, exposed views/RPCs, storage paths and restored permissions. Evaluate SELECT plus effective UPDATE USING and WITH CHECK; PostgreSQL may derive a missing check from USING, so audit effective behavior. Prefer invoker behavior where applicable; genuinely needed definer functions have narrow execute grants, fixed safe search path, fully qualified relations and current actor/resource authorization. A service-role client bypassing RLS must enforce the same domain boundary; its trusted tenant context alone does not prove publication authority.

### REQ26-D23-C013 — Public responder values

The minimal extension, if existing fields cannot qualify, belongs to the existing shared identity owner and exact tenant membership. A public display string and optional public role/title are explicitly externally usable under owner policy. They neither establish role authority nor alter legal/auth/CRM names. The current generic profile displayName update also changes full_name, so it cannot be repurposed as this command without correcting its semantics at the owner boundary.

Self maintenance affects only one's authorized public presentation; tenant governance can constrain or maintain it through existing scoped capabilities. “Approved” means currently eligible under those rules, not a mandatory second reviewer. A readonly view or private employee field is not automatically eligible for email disclosure. Header and body contexts have distinct validation; signature body text must not inherit an overrestrictive ASCII/header-only name policy. Team-only/no-name policy remains an explicit valid configuration.

No email address proves the mapping among auth user, profile, membership, Support agent and CRM Party. Changed email, merged Party, shared church address, reassignment or newly invited same-address account cannot take over another responder's identity. If a valid actual actor cannot be established, D1's actor failure applies; the system cannot pretend a human reply came from System merely because team-only text would render.

### REQ26-D23-C014 — Source, binding and draft transitions

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Operation                                    | Required boundary / valid result                                                                                                                            | Forbidden result                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create / Duplicate source                    | New stable identity and unpublished candidate; duplicate has provenance                                                                                     | Existing signature mutated by accidental id reuse; auto-published legacy content.                                                                                   |
| Autosave candidate                           | Expected candidate revision, authorized structured content, new revision receipt                                                                            | Stale write wins; unsupported input stripped and saved; optimistic Saved before confirmation.                                                                       |
| Commit / Publish                             | Existing P17 immutable candidate, validation/review, expected publication head                                                                              | Caller sets Published; previous publication destroyed on failure.                                                                                                   |
| Select / apply publication                   | Exact eligible revision, expected inbox binding, current scoped authorizations; atomic replacement/history                                                  | Clear default then set; first-row fallback; private/personal/cross-tenant source bound.                                                                             |
| Apply to selected inboxes                    | Explicit bounded set with expected heads and same current source generation; all or none                                                                    | Hidden entire-tenant update or ambiguous partly applied selection.                                                                                                  |
| Publish and use                              | Distinct publication result then qualified apply result; durable retry reconciliation                                                                       | Unpublished source selected; Applied claimed after only publication; republish to retry apply.                                                                      |
| New draft copy                               | One exact selected variant copied into managed slot                                                                                                         | Mutable live Saved Section node or repeated append per render.                                                                                                      |
| Refresh / hide / restore optional block      | Current draft revision, omission preserved by refresh, retained pinned copy shown by Restore after current checks, visible result and undo before admission | Body/recipients/attachments overwritten; hidden signature silently revealed; unselected newer version substituted; mandatory footer removed; cross-mode disclosure. |
| Prepare / admit                              | Current actual responder/audience/source/identity eligibility; exact full content frozen                                                                    | Assignee as responder; stale revoked value; client HTML overriding canonical JSON.                                                                                  |
| Routine source publication or default change | Existing bindings/copies retain exact pins until deliberate apply/refresh                                                                                   | Silent update of existing drafts/history or re-render of approved send.                                                                                             |
| Routine archive                              | No new selection/copy; effective consumer references explicitly replaced or posture reviewed before atomic archive                                          | Dangling defaults; implicit team or no-signature fallback; archive blocked on parsing a broken body.                                                                |
| Safety restriction                           | Immediate current-use fence under actual owner and repair obligations                                                                                       | Waiting for all inbox managers, treating ordinary Archive as recall, rewriting possibly sent mail.                                                                  |
| Restore                                      | Current eligible new candidate/publication as required; no implicit rebinding                                                                               | Removing safety fence or resurrecting disposed data because a prior version existed.                                                                                |

Source publication is not globally coupled to all inboxes. A new signature can publish unassigned, and a manager can keep an old still-safe selected version. The normal UI offers the new version and deliberate application. Existing P17 Brand Kit/layout dependency graph validation remains independently required for those shared dependencies; a signature source is not used to bypass it.

Archive-in-use is exact: an explicit Replace and archive operation validates its entire current affected binding set and source revision, current source/manager rights and replacement/posture eligibility, then commits those replacements and the archive atomically. A concurrent new binding or permission change conflicts. Bound the set under the owner command contract. For an over-bound complete set, deliberately rebind authorized bounded subsets first while the source remains active, then archive against the complete current remainder; never silently truncate or claim an archive while it remains active. A source author without the necessary affected-inbox rights cannot perform this ordinary transition; they can use the existing configuration handoff. Safety restriction does not require that quorum and preserves current no-use fences even when repair is unavailable. This avoids both silent breakage and a new bespoke approval workflow.

### REQ26-D23-C015 — Editor and rendering contract

Tiptap uses a versioned code-owned profile aligned with the canonical server allow-list. The signature profile is narrower than general Reply/Note profiles. Validate original JSON keys, attrs, shapes, source ids, purpose and budgets before parser normalization, then schema and semantic/output rules. Supported pasted styling can be normalized with a loss notice; unknown saved semantic structure is held read-only for reviewed migration. Content-error callbacks stop writable fallback and autosave of altered content.

The source remains Tiptap JSON; browser HTML, HTML-only signature forms and independent bodyText edits are removed from authoritative writers. Use a shared restricted link/asset profile for signatures without globally expanding the Post editor's HTTP/HTTPS-only policy. P17 maps allowed nodes to email-compatible HTML and genuine plain text; static-renderer/React Email APIs are mechanisms, not policy. Compiling occurs against declared numeric budgets and actual supported Node/dependency versions. The installed 3.22.3/3.23.1 mixture must be reconciled and tested against the qualified stable cohort, not merely hidden behind a ^ range.

### REQ26-D23-C016 — Email Studio and Resend seam

Human replies remain outside the finite system-message catalog. **No new system-message template key is required for signatures.** The reusable published signature source is an Email Studio authoring asset, not a Resend provider template. D13's **Support request received** remains its own real template with eligibility/deduplication; it does not impersonate a responder or satisfy a human-reply target because a public-name token exists.

Signature management, preview, application, source search and per-draft refresh/hide perform no provider call. An actual human reply uses P17's ready exact preparation, Support's atomic current-source/actor/audience admission, then P6's sealed tenant Resend envelope and current delivery evidence. No direct client/backend Support sender, mutable template id/alias, provider-side re-render, global credentials or donor-contact synchronization is introduced. Resend CLI is operational tooling for an explicitly authorized later test/admin action; it is not an app runtime compiler or alternate send path.

The existing raw-body webhook verification and owner/connection/envelope mapping continue unchanged. Signature edits do not reset idempotency keys, restart acknowledgements, change replies, split group envelopes or repair delivery by resending. Possibly submitted work is reconciled with its original exact effect. Provider-rendered/client-downloaded images are not proof of message reading or identity.

### REQ26-D23-C017 — Retention and traceability

Do not keep raw public-name values in an eternal source history to explain a message whose content has expired. Source revisions, controlled publication artifacts, approved draft copies, prepared messages, original admitted content, minimal delivery/security audit and replay fences each follow their actual finite owner lifetime. D16 restrictions/D17 expiry/D22 indexing apply to the original source and known derivatives; a reusable-source reference cannot extend body retention. Search reuses eligible historical admitted text rather than looking up today's public profile or the signature library. Restore cannot serve before current source/permission/retention fences are applied.

Audit source and binding mutations with minimal actual actor, source/target revision, cause, command/result and safe timing. Communication history is created only through actual message admission. Public-name/profile and CRM history remain separate; signatures never update contact timestamps, giving outcomes, reply metrics or coordination. R01–R28/P01–P44 are the exact acceptance trace. No deployed database, RLS, renderer, email client or provider proof is claimed by these logical requirements.

### REQ26-D23-C019 — One authoring source, several purposeful surfaces

Email Studio/Phase17 owns the canonical structured signature source, authored variants, immutable revisions/publications, governed assets and preparation. D23 qualifies a narrow published Saved Section purpose, **Reply signature**, distinct from D18's Reply/Internal note saved wording. It is not a personal signature library, a new Service message layout variant per inbox, a system-message catalog key or a provider-hosted template.

Support owns the exact published signature selection for an inbox, current draft, managed signature copy, actual actor/visible audience checks and local reply admission. Existing shared identity owns the tenant-membership public responder name and optional qualified public title; approved team/organization content belongs to its actual owner. Responder name is not assignee, template author, legal/full name, login email or CRM owner. The generic profile update that also changes full_name is not a public-name shortcut.

The same signature source is reachable through Email Studio and the contextual inbox action. There is no HTML synchronization, copied configuration library, second staff directory or alternate CRM record. Capability to configure an inbox, edit/publish an asset, maintain public identity and send a reply remains separate. Real permissions—not navigation—decide which actions appear and execute.

### REQ26-D23-C020 — Save, publish, select and copy

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Operation                    | Owner and authoritative result                                                                   | What it does not do                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Add/Edit/Duplicate signature | P17 authoring candidate with canonical Tiptap JSON and provenance                                | Does not publish, change inbox selection or send.                                         |
| Autosave/Save draft          | P17 revision-checked draft checkpoint                                                            | Does not make unsaved content usable for others.                                          |
| Publish                      | P17 exact immutable eligible signature publication                                               | Does not silently advance inbox bindings or already copied drafts.                        |
| Use for inboxes              | Support atomic, bounded, current-authorized replacement of exact selected publication references | Does not modify the signature source, sender headers or CRM facts.                        |
| Publish and use              | One UI action with truthful distinct publication/application results and durable reconciliation  | Does not claim Applied when only Published succeeded.                                     |
| New reply/explicit Refresh   | Copy the exact selected eligible variant into one managed canonical draft slot                   | Does not create a live Saved Section expression or expand a mutable template at dispatch. |
| Hide/Restore                 | Deliberate omission/restoration of this draft's optional closing                                 | Cannot hide required organization/legal framing or change later drafts' defaults.         |

Ordinary publication and binding changes leave existing valid copies pinned. Refresh preserves the draft's omission choice. Restore uses its retained eligible copy, not an unselected newer publication. Actual sending-inbox/language changes requalify the copy visibly before approval; routing and assignee changes alone cannot impersonate a responder. Source restriction, permission loss and retired unsafe dependencies remain stronger current-use fences.

The existing compatible Service message Role Layout and Brand Kit are complete immutable P17 dependencies. Saved Sections are copy-in authoring accelerators, not a live fragment graph. Repeated insertion/refresh adds at most one managed signature and never guesses away manual or quoted historical text.

### REQ26-D23-C021 — Tiptap edits; P17 validates and compiles

Use shared Tiptap for suitable rich authoring: replies, internal notes, D18 wording, signatures and qualified existing long-form Support fields. Purpose-specific profiles constrain nodes, marks, attributes, variables and assets in both editor and server; a hidden toolbar button is not a schema restriction. Validate original canonical JSON before any parser can discard unknown meaning, preserve invalid retained source for read-only repair, and prevent a stripped autosave.

Signature authoring uses a compact public-value vocabulary and professional text with one optional governed logo. Simple subjects, names, labels, search and other ordinary values stay appropriate inputs. Conversation history uses safe static rendering, with errors distinguishable from empty content. No new Tiptap Cloud, AI, collaborative editing or paid editor service is accepted.

P17's server compiler owns deterministic complete-message HTML and real plain text. Synthetic shared-source previews and actual authorized-context preparation remain distinct. Browser HTML, independently editable bodyHtml/bodyText, arbitrary extra extensions or React Email export do not become authority. The observed mixed Tiptap dependency closure must be aligned and qualified before activation; no upgrade was performed by this ratification.

### REQ26-D23-C022 — Actual email continues through tenant Resend

Human Support replies remain outside the finite system-message catalog. **No new system-message template key is required for signatures.** The published signature is an Email Studio authoring asset. D13's **Support request received** retains its own actual template, intake eligibility and deduplication; signatures cannot make an automatic acknowledgement appear human or satisfy a human-reply target.

An actual reply obtains exact P17 ready preparation, passes Support's current-source/actor/audience admission, and is delivered by Phase6 through the tenant's qualified Resend connection. P6 freezes the envelope, sender/reply identity and prepared HTML/text; there is no mutable Resend template ID/alias, rendering at retry, direct Support mailer or shared Asym sender fallback. Resend CLI remains operational tooling for separately authorized test/admin work, not an app-level compiler or alternative delivery spine.

Internal notes remain non-deliverable. Adding, saving, publishing, applying, refreshing, hiding or searching signatures creates no mail, acknowledgement, CRM interaction, business completion or follower notification. Real source repair attention uses existing qualified owner presentation; it is not a new signature-email campaign.

### REQ26-D23-C023 — Lifecycle and proof

Routine archive requires explicit safe replacement/posture for active consumer bindings. A popular source can first be deliberately rebound in bounded subsets, then archived against the complete remainder; no hidden truncation. Safety restriction can fence use without waiting for replacement or a manager quorum. Shared sources survive ordinary creator departure. Restore cannot reinstate old permissions or disposed content.

Signature source, public-name data, draft copies, preparation, admitted messages, delivery evidence and minimal audit each retain their actual finite owner purpose. D16/D17/D22 source restrictions and restore barriers continue to apply. Today’s template/profile must not replace historical admitted wording or provide a Recent-copy search fallback. Editing a signature cannot recall sent mail.

### REQ26-D23-C024 — Accepted ownership and public identity

Email Studio/Phase17 owns the narrow published Reply signature Saved Section purpose, canonical structured content, authored variants, immutable publications, assets and preparation. Support owns the inbox's exact selected eligible publication and its current draft, managed copy and admission. Existing Service message Role Layout and Brand Kit remain the complete presentation owners. No per-inbox Role Layout, personal signature library, live Saved Section expression, raw-HTML authority, provider template mirror or new system-message key is introduced.

A new external draft or explicit Refresh copies the exact selected eligible signature variant into one canonical managed slot with source/revision/copy provenance. Its origin differs from the actual responder values later resolved for preparation. Source publication does not update inbox selections automatically; it may remain published and unassigned. Explicit current-authorized binding changes choose exact immutable publication/locale policy. Existing safe draft copies, prepared messages and admitted history retain their pins.

The actual authenticated responder and active tenant membership supply identity authority. Public responder name and an optional qualified public title come from the existing shared identity owner's explicitly external presentation facet; qualify the smallest extension there if current fields do not provide it. Approved means current owner-policy eligibility, not a newly invented reviewer for every nickname. Self/tenant maintenance obeys its scoped owner command and does not alter legal/auth/CRM full name or contacts. The existing displayName endpoint that also changes full_name is not a safe shortcut. Assignee, CRM owner, template author, email matching, login email, private phone/photo/location, invented names and sample values are not fallbacks. Team/organization contact wording is approved separately; D23 adds no per-person email/phone descriptors.

### REQ26-D23-C025 — Accepted professional design and complete journey

Provide one focused Reply signature settings experience for each inbox, with current selection, published revision/language, readable preview and clear Change/Edit in Email Studio/New actions based on actual rights. The same source is discoverable through Email Studio's Signatures-purpose view, using search, Active/Archived and permitted usage metadata. Contextual authoring preserves the return destination and does not grant authoring, publication, identity or inbox-management rights. New/Customize/Duplicate create appropriate private candidates and provenance rather than changing active content.

The professional default is compact real text: approved public responder name, actual team/organization and useful approved contact links. A text starter and logo-with-text starter use the same bounded purpose. At most one governed logo occurrence, approved assets/readiness/alt purpose, compatible email typography/spacing/color/contrast and complete-message validation support polished output without an HTML/CSS editor, layout builder, promotional panel or role-by-language matrix. Essential identity remains readable when images are blocked. App authoring follows Core base-maia; tenant email branding remains P17-owned.

Autosave/Save draft, Preview, Publish and Use for inboxes have distinct outcomes. P17's current ordinary self-publication remains simple; actual protected and tenant-stricter review floors stay intact. Publication commits an exact validated candidate and keeps prior-good content on failure. Applying a revision atomically compares and replaces a bounded explicitly selected authorized inbox set. Publish and use may sequence the two owner commands in one deliberate UI action, but a published source with failed application is not called Applied. Durable reconciliation never republishes merely to retry selection.

Staff see the resolved managed signature inline before Send without a normal picker or mandatory preview modal. It is part of canonical reviewed content, not a late HTML/text append. Refresh replaces only the managed slot and preserves body, audience, attachments and Hide choice. Restore reveals the retained pinned copy after current eligibility checks, not a silently substituted newer version. Actual sending-inbox or resolved-locale changes requalify the selected copy and display the difference before approval; routing/assignee changes alone do not trigger identity substitution. Actor/audience/public-value changes obey current review/preparation fences.

Hide for this reply is a deliberate reversible omission of only the optional closing, visible with Restore, limited to the draft and not a future personal default. It cannot remove required organization/legal footer content. D18 wording insertion and repeat actions cannot duplicate the managed slot. Manual or quoted prior signatures are not removed by regex guesswork. Team-only is an explicit compatible posture/fallback, not an anonymity promise: headers, body and history can still identify staff. Missing required facts block with targeted repair; missing optional values omit complete lines/separators rather than disclose private fallbacks.

### REQ26-D23-C026 — Accepted Tiptap and canonical rendering scope

Tiptap serves the shared rich authoring for external replies, internal notes, D18 reusable wording, signatures and suitable existing long-form Support content. Each uses its actual owner-purpose profile. Simple search, subjects, names, labels, emails, dates, statuses and other ordinary values remain suitable native/shared inputs; read-only history uses safe static rendering. The accessible outline edits the same canonical source rather than a second raw/plain authority.

Signature vocabulary is deliberately narrow: text/paragraphs/hard breaks, restrained emphasis, safe links, qualified public fields and the governed logo. General Reply/Note vocabulary remains independently qualified. Toolbar hiding, arbitrary extraExtensions, browser HTML and generic parser flags are not policy. Validate original JSON keys/attributes/structure/source metadata and finite bounds before potentially lossy Tiptap parsing, then apply schema, semantic and disclosure checks. Unsupported saved source stays read-only and repairable with authorized original retention; contentError cannot silently create an autosaved stripped replacement. Clipboard normalization reports removed unsupported formatting without running active input or fetching unqualified assets.

P17's versioned Asym structured document contains canonical Tiptap JSON and other governed message meaning. The server compiler produces deterministic complete-message HTML and real plain text with correct block/source boundaries. Static failure is explicit rather than empty success. Purpose-specific mailto/tel support does not broaden unrelated Post link policy. Tiptap/React Email rendering tools do not themselves prove server authority, output equivalence, email-client behavior or accessibility.

Stable Tiptap 3 is accepted as the technology direction. Observed installed core/react 3.22.3, mixed 3.23.1 lock entries, React Email editor 1.5.3 and npm stable core 3.31.3 are dated evidence, not an upgrade or permanently frozen production pin. Qualify and align the actual interdependent package/peer closure with the canonical parser/renderer/schema/Node runtime before activation. Preserve sound SSR immediatelyRender:false and shared context; prefer the composable API where beneficial without an unrelated rewrite. No Tiptap Cloud, paid collaboration/history service, AI generation/search/translation or second editor system is accepted.

### REQ26-D23-C027 — Accepted durable data, lifecycle and privacy invariants

Asym Postgres and the shared business API own authorized mutations. Tenant-aware endpoint constraints, immutable source/publication/copy identity, valid purpose/state combinations and one effective selection per inbox prevent shadow ownership.
