Actual actor/tenant/audit/publication facts are server-derived. Separate use, authoring, publication/review, inbox binding, public-name maintenance and reply admission capabilities; inspect direct grants, effective RLS USING/WITH CHECK, mutation columns, views/RPCs/definers/service workers and storage together. PostgreSQL's effective-check semantics, not an explicit-clause checkbox alone, determine correctness. Retire broad legacy and raw-HTML writers rather than place a safe-looking editor over them.

Autosave/create/copy/publish/apply/refresh/hide/archive/restore/public-name operations retain owner-specific durable command identity and expected revisions. Replays reconcile original outcomes and cannot resurrect an old default or overwrite newer work. Publication/head evidence and binding/history changes are atomic at their owners; secondary work is idempotent and source-aware. No transaction surrounds provider I/O, and no generic workflow engine is introduced to make these commands safe.

Routine Archive stops new source selection/copy and requires explicit compatible replacement/posture for currently bound inboxes, comparing the complete affected set and revisions atomically. If that set exceeds the registered command bound, authorized managers may deliberately rebind bounded subsets while the source remains active and archive against the complete remainder. Never truncate or report incomplete archival as success. An ordinary source editor without affected-inbox rights cannot silently rebind them. Safety restriction remains independently available without compiling the broken source or waiting for manager coverage. Restore rechecks current scope/schema/assets/privacy and never rebinds old inboxes automatically.

Shared source custody survives staff departure; same-email reuse transfers no identity or ownership. Signature/public-name/source/draft/prepared/admitted/audit/receipt lifetimes remain distinct finite owner purposes. D16/D17/D22 withdrawal and restore barriers apply to current and known derived copies. Today's signature or public profile never replaces historical admitted text or supplies a Recent-copy search fallback. Configuration/draft edits do not change CRM identity, contact history, giving/care outcomes, assignment, reply targets, labels, follows or conversation timestamps. Actual admitted correspondence alone contributes to its qualified history and metrics.

### REQ26-D23-C028 — Accepted Email Studio, delivery, rollout and proof

The explicit Email Studio integration record and independent seam review preserve the complete ownership and copy/preparation distinction. P17 authoring/preparation → Support current actor/audience/source admission → P6 exact tenant Resend envelope remains the sole human-reply path. No signature system-message template key, mutable provider rendering, global sender fallback or direct Support mailer is added. D13 Support request received remains its own real Email Studio template/eligibility. Internal notes remain non-deliverable. Resend CLI is operational tooling for separately authorized later test/admin work, not a runtime alternative.

Qualify actual public identity, P17 purpose/source/asset/profile/compiler contracts and concrete registered bounds; align the runtime closure; add strict owner validation/commands; build the focused copy-in/settings/composer journey; migrate legacy data into reviewed candidates or read-only repair; fence old writers; and prove the complete cross-owner release matrix before scoped activation. Existing safe pins and effect reconciliation survive outages/stop controls. Rollback/restore cannot revive raw HTML, broad permissions, incompatible schema or withdrawn content. O01–O05 monitor residual faults after these preventive gates, not instead of them.

One ordinary qualified responder replies with the approved personal name and team details without per-reply setup; team-only works when configured.

## D23 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D23-O01

**Signal and threshold:** One verified cross-scope/private-value disclosure or accepted forbidden identity mutation.

**Owner:** Core identity/security owner with Support owner.

**Response:** Fence affected read/preparation/mutation path, preserve minimal incident evidence, correct source and known derivatives, qualify before reopening.

### OP26-D23-O02

**Signal and threshold:** One canonical/preview/prepared-output mismatch or new preparation using a revoked signature/asset revision.

**Owner:** Email Studio/compiler owner.

**Response:** Stop affected new preparation/publication generation, preserve safe pins, investigate exact revisions and roll forward; never rerender a possibly sent effect.

### OP26-D23-O03

**Signal and threshold:** One eligible active inbox has an unintended missing/invalid effective binding, or one atomic default/receipt invariant fails.

**Owner:** Support configuration owner.

**Response:** Show Needs attention for affected inbox, reconcile current binding and original command; use only explicitly allowed compatible posture, no first-row fallback.

### OP26-D23-O04

**Signal and threshold:** First failed/ambiguous autosave or unsupported-canonical-content initialization.

**Owner:** Shared editor owner and source authoring owner.

**Response:** Immediately show Not saved/read-only repair as appropriate, preserve authorized original work, reconcile before claiming Saved; never persist stripped source.

### OP26-D23-O05

**Signal and threshold:** First operation exceeding its registered document/asset/compile/query budget, or first overdue source-cleanup obligation under its registered deadline.

**Owner:** Shared email/editor performance owner for budgets; records/source owner for cleanup.

**Response:** Enforce bounded work and protect draft, route typed repair with identifiers, investigate capacity or delayed cleanup; a deadline miss never relaxes serving restrictions.

### REQ26-D23-C029 — Operating and qualification sequence

These controls monitor residual faults after the required preventive gates. They are not substitutes for authorization, compatibility, retention or capacity qualification.

## D24 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D24-R01 — Accept C as one curated human-reply capability

Provide shared curated reply-and-work shortcuts for one current authorized Support conversation's external Reply draft. A shortcut supplies a suggested reply and permitted Support changes for deliberate review. Selecting, previewing, editing or saving it never sends or changes live work. No personal shortcut library, action-only execution mode, internal-note-and-work mode, bulk reply, new conversation/intake creator or automatic invocation is added. D18 My/Shared wording and normal individual controls remain available.

A, content-free Support action shortcuts, remains the strongest narrower alternative; B, existing controls plus saved wording, is the strongest no-build alternative. C is selected because it can make recurring reply-and-follow-through combinations coherent. This is founder product direction supported by documented help-desk patterns, not measured Asym demand, time savings or proof every tenant uses the same combination. A shortcut that adds no useful combination can remain ordinary D18 wording.

### REQ26-D24-R02 — Ministry fit without invented business authority

Serve the founder's target organizations that receive donor requests while supporting missionaries and mission projects. Let each tenant curate its actual wording, language and support practices. Illustrations such as asking for receipt details or explaining next steps on a giving request are examples, not seeded departments, observed tenant frequencies or permission to infer sensitive ministry facts.

Support can coordinate an owning-domain action and communicate about its verified outcome; it cannot make a shortcut perform or certify a refund, receipt correction, recurring-gift change, allocation, CRM contact update or member-care action. A requester's email match is not identity or representation proof. Unknown/unlinked requesters can use the D1 qualified no-Party reply path. Do not create a CRM person to fill a template or require a donor relationship to receive ordinary help.

### REQ26-D24-R03 — A fixed form preset, not a parallel workflow interpreter

Support owns a versioned preset for its existing human reply-admission form, referencing P17/D18 wording and a closed flat desired-state patch. It does not own an ordered action program. Reuse the shared code-owned command descriptors and domain semantics; if that narrow owner seam is missing, qualify it rather than add a second configurable vocabulary or synchronize registries later.

Phase34 retains the sole configurable trigger/condition/action vocabulary and workflow-run state. D24 introduces no trigger, event enrollment, branch, loop, wait, schedule, arbitrary HTTP/script/SQL, connector call, task engine or rule evaluator. It does not forward-gate on the whole Phase34 product. This explicitly reconciles the roadmap boundary: the only executor here is the existing D4 human-authorized reply admission extended for the fixed allowed fields. Future automation cannot invoke this human authority under a forged actor; any automatic message requires its own qualified producer contract.

### REQ26-D24-R04 — One exact shared wording dependency and immutable shortcut revision

Each shortcut has one tenant/stable identity, plain internal name, optional description/when-to-use guidance, authorized use scope, immutable active revision and editable candidate lineage. Its active revision references one exact eligible published **Shared D18 Reply** wording source/variant policy, plus the fixed Support patch. It contains no independently editable reply HTML/text or embedded workflow code. Personal My replies cannot be exposed through a shared shortcut; deliberate contribution first follows D18.

Activation requires suitable shared wording and at least one declared non-Keep Support directive. Runtime may find some directives already satisfied; report those as unchanged, not failure or fabricated activity. All directives becoming unnecessary does not justify hidden mutation: show that the final reply has no work changes. Removing the entire pending plan deliberately returns the draft to normal reply semantics while preserving actual text provenance. No invisible fallback to a different wording revision or source is allowed.

### REQ26-D24-R05 — Closed initial Support patch

The initial patch permits exactly these dimensions: one D3 final work choice (Keep current status/Open/Waiting for requester/Waiting on our side/Resolved); at most one D6 handling choice over current responsible team/person (Keep, explicit compatible team/person, Me, or Shared/unassigned); and unique, disjoint Add-label and Remove-label sets referencing the curated D21 catalog. Keep means no requested change, not a stale captured value. No action order, toggles, repeated writes to the same dimension or contradictory label sets exist.

Me resolves to the current actual responder. On already assigned work it is reviewed reassignment, not a claim operation allowed to steal a concurrent claim. Preserve the current team unless explicitly changed; validate the resulting team/person relationship. D6 manual eligibility applies even outside an automatic pool or above its advisory automatic limit. Do not run routing rules, reset receiving controls or waive D7/D8 human-control/review fences.

No new priority, snooze/reminder preset, inbox move, conversation merge, related-conversation creation, note/mention, delegated task, follower, recipient/subject/thread/sender/signature change, safety disposition, retention/redaction, CRM/giving/care action or external effect is permitted. D3 status changes retain their existing reminder consequences; the shortcut invents no independent reminder policy. The selected action list replaces the legacy macro enum as accepted scope.

### REQ26-D24-R06 — Use, curation, publication and action authority remain distinct

Use current Core capabilities and existing qualified inbox/team scope to separate shortcut use, shortcut maintenance/activation, P17 shared-wording authoring/publication and actual source mutations. A shortcut's audience is only a discoverability/use restriction; it grants no source, CRM, asset or assignment permission. Effective availability intersects shortcut scope, current conversation context, D18 source/asset audience and the actor's actual action authority.

A curator can maintain reusable metadata without general access to donor conversations. A source publisher does not become a Support administrator. Ordinary qualified Support configuration activation needs no new mandatory second-reviewer workflow; content publication retains P17's actual protected and tenant-stricter rules. Widening scope requires current authority and revalidation of all exposed variants/assets; do not silently widen P17 content audience or use an old audience snapshot as current access.

### REQ26-D24-R07 — Find and preview without executing

Expose a labelled **Reply shortcuts** entry within the existing composer insertion/action area, distinct from content-only **Saved replies**. Use a compact searchable picker with understandable names, concise use guidance and current scoped availability; a person may browse or preview without changing their draft. Avoid forced folder syntax, dozens of seeded definitions, a second global search page, automatic selection, popularity-driven changes or AI chrome.

Preview shows the selected wording variant, introduced files/fill-ins and concrete pending status/handling/label outcomes in the current authorized context. It distinguishes available, incompatible, missing required input and unavailable dependencies without exposing forbidden titles or records. A staff member sees what will be prepared before selecting **Use shortcut**. Keyboard selection inside the picker never sends; cancellation preserves the draft and focus.

### REQ26-D24-R08 — Stage a coherent private draft, with no live Support effect

Using a shortcut copies its exact qualified wording into the current canonical Tiptap Reply draft under D18 insertion rules and stages the patch in the same logical private-draft revision. Record shortcut/wording revision, insertion mode, actual source/asset provenance and relevant current context. No live label, assignment, status, note, message intent or provider effect occurs at this point. Saving/restoring the private draft preserves this meaning and never executes it.

The work patch is typed draft metadata, not executable Tiptap nodes or text that can be copied/pasted into another message. The source remains a normal editable human reply; typed variables/fill-ins and assets obey D18/D23. One draft can have at most one staged shortcut plan. Do not stack macros, deduce an action sequence from button order or silently merge conflicting presets.

### REQ26-D24-R09 — Keep pending changes visible beside the final action

Show a compact **With this reply** summary beside the composer action area. It names the actual pending status, handling and labels, distinguishing Keep, requested change, unchanged and blocked. Pending values do not masquerade as live conversation fields. Staff may edit or remove permitted pending directives through the same qualified controls without editing the shared shortcut; modifications remain local and recorded in final intent.

Preserve D4's explicit primary labels: Send reply, Send and open, Send and wait for requester, Send and wait on our side, or Send and resolve. Where labels/handling are also staged, visibly and programmatically associate the With this reply summary/count with that action so it cannot appear to send only. The phrase Send and apply describes the composite operation, not a replacement generic button that hides the status. Native header controls retain their separate immediate semantics; their changes trigger current revalidation rather than silently rewrite the pending plan.

### REQ26-D24-R10 — Change, detach, Undo and mode switching cannot leave a hidden plan

**Change shortcut** presents an explicit choice. Default **Keep current reply; replace pending changes** preserves the existing body, attachments, signature and real wording provenance; the new shortcut's suggested wording/files are not inserted. Record kept-current mode rather than falsely crediting the new source with that text. Optional **Replace reply with new wording** uses D18's explicit reviewed whole-body replacement and safe asset/Undo rules; no fragile attempt to find previously inserted paragraphs after editing.

**Remove shortcut, keep reply** detaches pending shortcut work only. It preserves current human wording and its source restrictions. Undo/Redo that crosses a shortcut staging/replacement boundary restores the prior draft and pending plan coherently, or conservatively disarms affected pending work with a clear explanation if exact restoration cannot be proved. Ordinary Undo of later typing does not needlessly discard a visible valid plan. No text-only Undo may leave a hidden Resolve/assignment action armed, and no Redo may rearm without current eligibility.

Reply and Internal note remain separate drafts. Switching to Note never carries shortcut actions or external audience into Add note. Returning restores only the permitted Reply draft/plan; it does not execute it. Conversation/tenant/account changes fence stale responses and drafts. Detaching a plan is not permission to send restricted copied wording.

### REQ26-D24-R11 — Honest wording, values, files and signatures

P17/D18 owns canonical structured wording, typed fields, one-use fill-ins, language, assets, publication and safe copy-in. D23 owns the managed signature behavior. A shortcut cannot override the selected signature, external identity, visible recipients or shared frame. HTML and real plain text are compiled from the final canonical document, not independent macro body fields or repeated brace-string substitution.

Required unresolved fill-ins or forbidden values block preparation; optional omission/fallback is the existing typed contract, not sample data or empty-string invention. Do not infer identity, language, donor status or protected disclosure from an email match. A common group reply must be valid for every admitted recipient and preserve D2's visible-group rules. Source updates do not silently repersonalize or overwrite the draft.

Introduced assets use exact qualified D18 occurrences and current readiness/disclosure. Repeated references do not duplicate existing attachments; cancellation/Undo removes only introduced appearances, never preexisting or later independent work. Internal task/care files and official receipts cannot become reusable assets merely by being attached to a shortcut. Protected outcome confirmations require their actual owner-qualified facts/purpose; this feature cannot prove arbitrary natural-language assertions true or perform the action they describe.

### REQ26-D24-R12 — One atomic reply-and-work admission

Extend the existing D4 server-authorized local admission to the fixed desired-state patch. First obtain durable ready P17 preparation for the exact reviewed body/audience/signature/assets/locale. Then one conditional Asym database transaction claims that preparation and commits the Support message intent, final D3 work/reminder effects, D6 handling, D21 label effects, trusted before/after history, shortcut-use receipt and durable dispatch/recovery intent. No request loop of separately committed mutations implements this capability.

Validate the complete resulting state and current owner preconditions in one unit of work. Failure, stale review or denied required component before admission commits none of these effects and preserves the private draft. Unchanged directives are explicit no-ops, not skipped unavailable actions. No stop-on-error option or compensating best-effort rollback of the current runner is the permanent fix. P17 preparation staged before admission has no dispatch authority until claimed; orphaned candidates follow owner cleanup. No transaction spans Resend I/O.

### REQ26-D24-R13 — Canonical work and handling truth outrank shortcut convenience

D3 defines the four work meanings. A courtesy update does not establish Waiting; an unsent draft does not contact a requester. Waiting on our side requires a real outstanding input already sought; a shortcut does not create the missing task/request. Open precedence, mixed waits, reminder consequences and current unread/review obligations stay intact. Resolve must pass D3/D5/D11 obligations, including required owner-result review; an independently linked process need not be terminal when Support can legitimately finish.

D6/D7/D8 assignment and handling controls remain authoritative. Shortcut use does not waive a required handling review or current access fence, select a CRM owner, take back absence coverage or force a new automatic assignment. D7 Keep is a runtime coverage decision, not a reusable shortcut instruction. D8 review-first blocks handling changes until the separate review, not otherwise-authorized reply/status/label work when no handling change is requested. D8 A can be settled by an explicit eligible individual manual assignment even when automatic release is paused or Shared lacks independent coverage. Do not impose automatic-pool limits on a valid manual assignment. A changed assignee is not the reply author. All affected original label contributors and their current source permissions follow D10/D21; root-only membership edits or hidden-source mutation are invalid. D5 No response remains its separate explicit ending review and evidence; it is not a hidden shortcut status preset.

### REQ26-D24-R14 — Review binds current context and resulting intent

Bind the reviewed shortcut revision, actual final document, typed patch, conversation/original-source topology, relevant work/handling/label/membership generations, actual actor, complete admitted audience and P17 preparation dependencies. A different conversation, late reply, merge/Undo, permission change, source restriction or target departure can make a formerly valid preview stale. Refresh current permitted context and require review of changed meaning; never auto-rebase Resolve or silently drop a failed directive.

Use current source/field checks before previews, target choices, counts, snippets and final admission. A result arriving after navigating from one donor to another cannot populate the new draft. Preserve unrelated typed work and distinguish the original command outcome from today's state. Routine metadata edits that do not affect the admitted meaning need not create artificial collisions; security/control and actual relevant revisions must.

### REQ26-D24-R15 — Durable retries and provider evidence stay separate

The durable business identity is the reviewed reply-admission intent, with an immutable semantic hash including its final patch and provenance. Same identity/same input reconciles the same result; changed input conflicts. A new deliberate reply is new intent even if wording is identical. Lost responses reconcile before another send is enabled. Request/provider transport keys are not permanent business identity.

After local admission, the work effects have happened and the reply is Queued, not Delivered. Resend failure, suppression, uncertainty or a later adverse event does not roll back or replay old labels/handling/status. D4/P6 reconciles the original sealed effect; D3 creates fresh causally appropriate review when needed under current handling. No new sender/account, rekey, mutable template, repeated whole-group send or blind resend. Counterpart domains' actual action status remains independent.

### REQ26-D24-R16 — Create and maintain through a focused Support form

Provide **Support settings → Reply shortcuts**, with Active, Drafts and Archived views plus a Needs attention filter. Each entry shows name, eligible scope, wording version/language, compact work summary and safe maintenance status. Use plain searchable metadata, restrained columns and current permissions; no graph canvas, nested folder grammar or mandatory tags. Tenant Support configuration maintainers are accountable; creator departure cannot orphan tenant custody or impose a new global role.

New/duplicate creates an unpublished configuration candidate with a clear name, optional when-to-use guidance, qualified use scope, a selected published Shared Reply and the fixed work fields. Incomplete but structurally safe drafts can be saved with actionable validation; they cannot activate. **Create/Edit wording in Email Studio** opens the same owning source with preserved return context. No second Tiptap body editor or raw HTML field appears in the shortcut form, and no Save conversation as shortcut harvests live donor/care material. Reusable wording contribution first follows D18 generalization and publication.

### REQ26-D24-R17 — Content publication and shortcut activation are distinct

P17 publishes the exact wording candidate under its own permissions/review. Support saves, reviews and activates an exact shortcut configuration revision only after source purpose/scope/variants/assets and target/schema compatibility are proven. **Review and activate** exposes wording, use scope and resulting work together, with before/after for edits. Activation is not sending, task completion or content publication, and no new universal second reviewer is required.

If one contextual action helps publish wording then activate the shortcut, preserve separate truthful results and durable reconciliation. Published wording with failed activation is not an Active shortcut; prior valid configuration stays active. Activation compares the expected active head and commits revision/control/history atomically. Selecting a new published wording revision is deliberate; no mutable latest reference or source save silently changes all shortcuts or existing staged drafts.

### REQ26-D24-R18 — Keep updates and dependency repair understandable

Ordinary edits create a candidate; activating a new revision affects future selections. Valid already staged copies/plans remain pinned unless deliberately changed, subject to current restrictions and command preconditions. Show **Newer wording available** separately from **Needs attention**; old still-eligible content is not broken merely because a new version exists. Review a wording/target/scope update before activation and preserve actual locale/fallback meaning without silently dropping a translation.

Ineligible label operations, departed targets, inaccessible wording, unavailable assets or incompatible schema produce precise maintenance reasons. Label eligibility is operation-specific: Add requires current active catalog eligibility; Remove may target exact currently authorized existing memberships of an ordinarily archived label. Archive alone does not invalidate that permitted Remove. Missing or restricted labels retain their current owner gates. Do not silently substitute an assignee, recreate a label, widen a source audience or resolve a broken reference by title/email. A current use can be blocked even if the health projection is stale; direct source gates remain authoritative. Repair uses existing owner navigation and exact references, not database surgery. No routine mass email or repeated banner on every conversation announces a library edit.

### REQ26-D24-R19 — Archive and safety restriction must work when the shortcut is broken

Ordinary **Archive** stops new selection and activation without requiring the broken wording, target or action values to resolve or compile. It preserves already staged otherwise valid revisions under their owner policy and is not an emergency revocation. **Restore** rechecks current eligibility and never silently restores old active dependencies or safety-restricted material. An older shortcut revision can become a new reviewed candidate; history is not edited in place.

Actual safety/authorization withdrawal fences current reads, staging and qualifying preparation/admission immediately, with the existing definitely-unsubmitted versus may-have-submitted rules. It does not recall sent email. Tenant source/configuration custody survives maintainer departure; same-email accounts inherit no access. Routine hard Delete is not a shortcut around retained dependencies, source evidence or cleanup. Finite records policy owns actual disposal and safe attribution minimization.

### REQ26-D24-R20 — Database, RLS and the complete mutation surface

Asym Postgres remains authoritative through the shared business API. Enforce same-tenant source/publication/variant, shortcut revision, scope, draft, conversation, team/member, label contributor and preparation/receipt relationships with actual endpoint types and suitable composite constraints. Active revisions are immutable; one current active head and at most one staged plan per draft hold. Typed patch structure, noncontradictory labels, valid state/nullability, revision monotonicity and idempotency uniqueness are enforced at the authoritative boundary and in constraints where appropriate.

Tenant, actual user/profile/member, author, reviewer/control status and audit attribution derive from trusted current server context. A caller can propose permitted fields and expected revisions, not move a row across tenant/purpose/custody, publish by setting a flag or forge a human execution identity. Creation and update differ; a missing update target is not recreated by upsert.

Review grants, direct collection/REST writers, effective SELECT/USING/WITH CHECK, additional permissive policies, views, RPC execute grants, fixed definer search paths, storage and service/worker code together. PostgreSQL can derive WITH CHECK from USING; prove actual old/new-row and column invariants rather than assuming the absence of syntax is a vulnerability. Privileged clients independently enforce the same capabilities. Fence all legacy macro, automation, import/fixture and client-history writers that bypass the compound owner boundary.

### REQ26-D24-R21 — Cross-surface CRM continuity and source minimization

Requester, admitted participant, authenticated responder, public responder name, tenant membership, CRM Party, represented organization, Support coordinator and CRM owner remain distinct. The same shortcut journey may be opened in an authorized CRM-context Support conversation, preserving return context and draft; that context neither changes its recipient audience nor exposes unrelated merged originals or restricted CRM/care/giving fields.

Read only owner-authorized context needed for the actual reply. CRM/giving/care changes and protected documents use their existing owner commands, validation, approvals and history; Support can navigate or coordinate through D11 but the shortcut does not include these actions. Resolving Support does not certify their completion. Only actual admitted correspondence contributes to its permitted Support/CRM history projection. Selecting, previewing, saving, activating or archiving a shortcut creates no Party, interaction or false last-contact timestamp.

### REQ26-D24-R22 — Retention, privacy and portability preserve actual provenance

Shortcut configuration/revisions, source wording/assets, private stage copies, prepared/admitted messages, command/use receipts, caches, maintenance feedback and audit have separate finite owner purposes. No shortcut receipt stores a second full reply body, resolved donor facts, raw search query or secret. D16/D17/D22 restrictions and restore barriers cover known derivatives. Template source is not a fallback for expired correspondence; Recent is never a search corpus. Detaching/removing a plan preserves actual copied-content restrictions and cannot declassify it.

Reuse qualified owner import/export where available, without adding a Support-specific format. Export only currently authorized configuration and eligible source references/content through their owner; omit real recipient fills, credentials, private drafts, permissions and activation authority. Imports create destination-owned inactive candidates with explicit source remapping and validation, never active cross-tenant recipes or automatically created labels/people. If the owner export/import seam is not activated, provide clear unavailable behavior rather than invent a new transfer system for D24.

### REQ26-D24-R23 — Useful maintenance reporting with exact meaning

Provide a small curator view of current health, last recorded use and usage in a selected period, using minimal durable admission receipts. **Shortcut-assisted reply** means one locally admitted human reply retaining one staged shortcut association and its actual final patch/provenance. Count once per admission intent, including explicitly unchanged directives; exclude picker views, selection, canceled/detached plans, preflight failures and provider retries. Kept-current wording mode remains distinct from inserted/replaced source, without claiming uninserted wording was used. Queued use is not delivery or successful resolution.

Scope before aggregation and drilldown. Period uses half-open admission timestamps in the visible reporting timezone; current permission changes govern accessible results. Merge/Undo groups display without duplicating original admission facts. Exact same-evaluation drilldown/export preserves that receipt cohort, not conversation creation date or today's status. Incomplete retained evidence is Unknown/partial, not zero/Never. No usage tags pollute D21, no per-agent leaderboard, invented time-saved metric, auto-retirement threshold or AI success score. Optional specific feedback uses existing owner repair attention and safe metadata, not a new case-body feedback archive.

### REQ26-D24-R24 — Accessible and fast in the actual staff journey

Preserve Core base-maia/Base UI and shared Tiptap purpose profiles. Clear labels distinguish Saved replies, Reply shortcuts, With this reply, current values and pending values. Support keyboard/touch/screen-reader use, semantic field summaries, focus return, IME, conditional errors and equivalent accessible editing. No hover-only disclosure, color-only state, drag-only action ordering, noisy countdown or automatic navigation to another conversation. Mobile preserves every declared effect and final approval; it cannot silently insert only text while discarding the plan.

Use tenant/principal/context-generation-scoped draft recovery and current source gates. Offline or uncertain save shows Not saved/Pending recovery; reconnection never sends or applies automatically. Register concrete source/document/asset/label-set/lookup/transaction/compile/query bounds and tested concurrency before activation. Validate before expensive work, use complete scoped queries and appropriate FK/lookup indexes, and prove exact boundaries and production-shaped skew. Reuse static reads and selective editor subscriptions; no second editor runtime or whole-CRM fetch per keystroke. Do not invent universal vendor quotas or latency guarantees.

### REQ26-D24-R25 — Future AI is an explicit direction, not current scope

Record future AI augmentation for discovery, context-appropriate draft assistance and maintenance candidates. Do not add an AI button, vector index, model/provider call, background transcript mining, Tiptap AI service, automatic translation, generated action language or service execution now. The useful foundation is already needed by the manual product: typed immutable sources/presets, exact staged intent, current eligibility, minimal outcome evidence and the same reviewed admission boundary.

Any later AI capability consumes ADR0099's purpose-routed tenant AI foundation and Phase40's product boundary, not a Support-only model router or copied CRM. ADR0035 Eve concerns GitHub-session engineering orchestration and is not authority for processing customer support data. The shared product foundation owns tenant provider connections and credential revisions, exact purpose/capability/model/region/data-use/budget bindings, classification- and authorization-gated minimum-data AI Egress Manifests, invocation evidence and non-authoritative suggestion versions. Restricted/care/security/high-risk contexts retain the governing remote-egress prohibition; no silent provider/model/purpose fallback is permitted. Retrieval/processing permission, tenant/source restrictions, provider retention and actual actor authority must be separately qualified. Read permission is not automatically permission to send data to a model. D22's indexing exclusions cannot be bypassed by calling a new index an AI assistant. Human acceptance still invokes the owning typed command; neither AI output nor its egress manifest confers write authority.

### REQ26-D24-R26 — Research the AI progression before enabling it

The recommended future research sequence is: evaluate useful candidate tasks and consent/data scope on qualified synthetic/redacted data; test suggesting only currently eligible active shortcut revisions; then evaluate explicitly requested wording adaptations and unpublished maintenance candidates if they outperform the manual baseline without weakening safety. These are research hypotheses, not accepted launch features or a commitment to a particular model.

Future output is untrusted data constrained to the same typed fields and authorized source references. Incoming messages, attachments, template text and tool results cannot instruct the system to widen access, run a command or publish. Suggestions must be reviewable/dismissible with no silent selection, and human final body/actions remain visible. No AI auto-send, activation, publication, assignment, CRM/giving mutation or training from live conversations is authorized here. Similarity/confidence or user feedback is not permission or proof of truth. No operational or governance review is waived by generated wording.

Before later activation, the owning phase must set falsifiable domain/safety/usability criteria, authorized datasets, source-citation/abstention behavior, prompt-injection/privacy tests, cost/latency limits, model/prompt/version trace, retention controls, rollout/kill switch and accountable incident response. Compare wrong-shortcut/incorrect-action/unsupported-claim rates and time to a correct reviewed reply against manual work; clicks or adoption alone are insufficient. Keep raw sensitive prompts/output out of generic logs and prevent cross-tenant learning/feedback authority. Human public responder identity cannot disguise a future autonomous actor.

### REQ26-D24-R27 — Failure visibility and accountable operations

Differentiate missing/ineligible source, incomplete fill-in, invalid resulting work, stale context, save/preparation failure, denied admission, admitted Queued reply and delivery uncertainty. Preserve permitted work and provide the exact next safe action. Shortcut health is a projection; it never overrides current authoritative eligibility. Plain reply and unrelated inbox work remain available when their actual dependencies are valid; do not fallback to stale cached HTML, a different wording source or a direct sender.

Audit curated source changes, activation/archive and actual admission separately from technical traces and security incidents. Use stable safe source/revision/command/cause identifiers and current responsible owner; do not log bodies or raw PII merely to debug a preset. Required source/dispatch/repair intent is durable and idempotent with the owning effect. P17/P6 existing local attention can represent qualified real repair, without a new shortcut-notification template or broad subscriber blast. Reading a notice is not repair.

### REQ26-D24-R28 — Migrate and roll out one permanent path

Inventory current macros, canned content references, priorities/snooze/note effects, client/server runners, mutable action arrays, broad writers and all entry surfaces. Convert only eligible generic wording through D18/P17 and only fixed permitted fields into inactive reviewed shortcut candidates. Unsupported or uncertain combinations remain read-only for explicit remediation; do not silently drop a step and activate a weaker operation. Preserve actual source IDs/provenance/history and explicit unknowns, not historical false outcomes.

Add schema/owner contracts and compatible readers first; qualify P17 preparation and shared in-transaction primitives; implement one staged draft/compound admission; fence legacy writers and automatic paths; migrate and validate; then activate qualified scopes. Mixed old/new deployments cannot expose the new composer over old sequential mutations. Stop controls prevent new staging/admission while preserving safe draft/history and admitted-envelope reconciliation. Rollback/restore cannot reenable raw HTML, broad permissions, old loop semantics or withdrawn source. Use reviewed roll-forward when new data cannot be safely understood by old code.

### REQ26-D24-R29 — Precise proof and traceability

Carry D24-R01–R30 into the glossary/ADR and these companion contracts, then only through implementation OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets and implementation/release evidence. P01–P50 below prove positive, negative, source, permission, concurrency, migration, accessibility and cross-owner outcomes.

### REQ26-D24-R30 — The resulting bounded product

The complete capability is one curated shared Reply preset, one exact eligible source, one visible staged plan and one human final admission, with understandable creation, activation, repair, update, archival and scoped maintenance evidence. Preserve D18 wording, D23 signatures/Tiptap, D3 work, D6 handling, D21 labels, P17 preparation and P6 Resend as their actual owners. No second CRM, workflow framework, public portal, ticket hierarchy, AI platform, message catalog or financial engine is introduced to make the shortcut feel seamless.

### REQ26-D24-C001 — Find the right combination where the reply is written

Place **Reply shortcuts** in the existing Reply composer's insertion/action area, beside or within the same labelled menu as **Saved replies**, with visibly different labels. Saved replies supplies wording; Reply shortcuts supplies wording and pending Support changes. No shortcut selector appears in the ordinary Internal note composer, no global second inbox is added and no automatic selection occurs on opening a conversation.

The initial compact picker has one search field, scoped matching names and concise descriptions. It searches authorized shortcut metadata, not conversation bodies or the CRM. Use current inbox/team eligibility to reduce the list. Do not require users to learn folders, punctuation-based categories, tags or a second filter builder. Reuse existing accessible list/picker patterns; Enter selects within the picker and can never submit a message. If the configured library outgrows the compact list, paginate/search the same bounded authorized catalog rather than truncate silently.

Each result shows a recognizable name, one-line use guidance and a concise work summary, such as **Ask for receipt details · Wait for requester**. An optional Preview opens the full proposed wording and current-context changes without touching the draft. **Use shortcut** stages the selected combination. Preview is available but is not a mandatory modal step for every repeat use because the full resulting draft and work remain visible before admission.

An unavailable source is not rendered from an old cached copy. Ordinary staff get a concise permitted reason and can use another shortcut or a normal reply. A maintainer with the appropriate source authority can follow **Review shortcut** to the actual repair. Forbidden names, hidden people or restricted files do not appear in reasons or counts. A genuinely empty catalog says **No reply shortcuts available for this inbox** and leaves Saved replies and ordinary replying clear; it does not ask every responder to create a shared recipe.

### REQ26-D24-C002 — Prepare, personalize and review

Using a shortcut creates one coherent private draft revision: actual D18 wording/asset copy plus one pending Support plan. The live conversation header, labels, assignment and status do not change. The existing Tiptap editor keeps the human reply editable. Managed signature, typed fields, one-use fill-ins, language and attachments retain D18/D23 semantics. The shortcut cannot add recipients, choose a signature, impersonate an assignee or make an official receipt.

Below the body and close to the final button, show **With this reply**. This is a compact summary, not a full second property sidebar:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Example pending line           | Meaning and available action                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Status: Waiting for requester  | Requested final work choice; use the qualified existing selector to change it locally.                         |
| Handling: Keep current         | No handling mutation. It does not freeze the current assignee.                                                 |
| Add label: Receipt question    | Explicit addition from the curated Support list. An existing membership is shown as Already applied/unchanged. |
| Remove label: Follow-up needed | Explicit removal, subject to all actual original-source permissions.                                           |

These are illustrative names; they are not seeded tenant classifications. Show only the dimensions relevant to the plan, with a concise Keep current explanation available. Staff can edit/remove permitted directives for this reply without changing the shared shortcut. A blocked directive has a specific inline error; it is not silently dropped. Editing a live header control still has its existing immediate meaning and causes the pending plan to revalidate. Avoid making pending values look as if they were already saved to the conversation.

Preserve D4's action wording: **Send reply**, **Send and open**, **Send and wait for requester**, **Send and wait on our side**, or **Send and resolve**. When additional handling or label changes are staged, the visible and programmatically associated With this reply summary makes the composite action clear. Do not replace the meaningful status label with an ambiguous generic Apply. Disabled controls expose the actionable reason; color or an icon alone is insufficient.

One draft has one plan. There is no action ordering or stacking. Adding labels and selecting a final status are a desired result, not sequential steps a responder has to arrange. An already-satisfied plan shows that nothing in live work needs changing; sending can still be a shortcut-assisted reply under the exact reporting definition. Removing the whole plan deliberately returns to normal reply behavior.

### REQ26-D24-C003 — Change your mind without losing work

**Change shortcut** offers the following explicit modes within the current draft:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Mode                                                  | Body and assets                                                                                                                                                       | Pending work                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Keep current reply; replace pending changes — default | Preserve actual current wording, assets, signature and original provenance. New suggested wording/files are not inserted.                                             | Replace the one pending plan with the new shortcut's allowed plan and revalidate. |
| Replace reply with new wording                        | Show/review the D18 whole-body replacement; preserve/remove asset occurrences under its existing rules. Do not guess which edited paragraph came from the old source. | Replace the plan in the same logical draft command.                               |
| Cancel                                                | Preserve current draft.                                                                                                                                               | Preserve current plan.                                                            |

This keeps an edited donor response safe while letting a responder change follow-through. The application records kept-current mode truthfully; it cannot credit the newly selected wording as inserted. The new shortcut and its dependencies still need to be eligible. **Remove shortcut, keep reply** removes the staged shortcut association and work only. It does not make restricted copied content safe to send.

Undo/Redo crosses body-and-plan changes as one app-owned draft-history operation. Ordinary Undo of a later sentence remains normal text editing. Undo of applying/replacing a shortcut restores both sides, or conservatively disarms the affected plan with a clear explanation if exact restoration is impossible. Redo cannot silently rearm a Resolve action or bypass current context checks. Copy/pasting body text never transfers executable work. Do not use a text-equality heuristic or every editor-update event to guess whether a plan survives.

Reply and Note keep separate drafts. Switching to Note cannot apply reply actions or carry external recipients; returning to Reply restores only the permitted prior draft. Navigating away/back preserves context through existing private draft recovery. A different tenant, account or conversation fences stale saves and async results. Visible **Not saved** or **Recovering draft** must never look like a sent reply; reconnection never sends automatically.

### REQ26-D24-C004 — Send and understand the result

1. The responder reviews real recipients, actual wording/files/signature and the compact pending work. Required fill-ins and current owner preconditions are resolved before admission.
2. The existing preparation path validates/compiles that exact reply. No live work changes yet. A recoverable failure preserves permitted draft content and says what needs correction.
3. One guarded local admission commits the message and all permitted Support changes together. A stale or denied required component commits none of them. The UI refreshes changed meaning for review rather than auto-rebasing or dropping a directive.
4. After admission, show the normal Queued reply plus actual new work values and a concise history entry. Queued is not delivered. A lost response reconciles the existing intent before allowing another send.
5. Provider failure/uncertainty follows D4/P6 recovery. It does not rerun old work or rewind today's assignment/status. A fresh causally appropriate review can open under D3 when needed.

Do not add a success dialog to every reply or send unnecessary requester notifications about internal shortcut usage. Actual admissible correspondence appears in existing Support and permitted CRM history. Selecting or maintaining a shortcut does not create a contact interaction.

### REQ26-D24-C005 — Three illustrative ministry journeys

**Donor asks which receipt is involved.** An eligible responder opens an existing request, verifies its audience and chooses a tenant-curated Ask for receipt details shortcut. They personalize the question, review any label and Waiting for requester, then send. No receipt lookup privilege is inferred and no receipt is generated or changed. A qualified unidentified requester can receive an ordinary reply without creating a CRM Party.

**Request needs an internal giving answer.** The responder first uses the actual owning-domain/D11 handoff to seek the required answer when appropriate. A shortcut may then prepare an honest progress reply and Waiting on our side. It cannot create the missing handoff or treat a label as proof it exists. If an actual result still needs Support review, Resolve is blocked. A merely linked ongoing process does not automatically prevent legitimate Support closure.

**A missionary/project question needs a different Support worker.** The responder chooses approved general wording and an eligible manual handling target, reviews that person's resulting Support role and sends. Neither assignment nor the shortcut grants access to missionary location, member-care facts, project finances or CRM ownership. If handling requires separate review, preserve the draft and resolve that review or remove the handling directive; other authorized work need not be blanket-blocked.

These are designed examples grounded in Conrad's target population, not claims about measured tenant workflows or frequencies. Each tenant curates its actual language and procedures.

### REQ26-D24-C006 — Create and maintain the library

Use **Support settings → Reply shortcuts**, consistent with current product settings navigation and access. The maintenance list has Active, Drafts and Archived views and a Needs attention filter. Prioritize name, scope, current wording version/language and compact work summary. Current health is more actionable than a large dashboard. Last recorded use/period use can be a restrained maintenance detail, not a staff leaderboard.

**Create shortcut** opens a focused form:

1. Name, optional when-to-use guidance and eligible use scope.
2. A selected published Shared Reply card showing its actual purpose, approved variant/language policy and source version.
3. The small set of final Support choices: work status, handling and curated label additions/removals. Keep current is explicit. Unsupported task/CRM/email/automation actions are not available.
4. A safe representative preview, unresolved-input/dependency checks and **Save draft** or **Review and activate**.

Do not place a second Tiptap body editor in this form. **Create wording in Email Studio** or **Edit wording in Email Studio** opens the same owning source editor with return context. Email Studio uses the ratified Tiptap purpose profile; it owns wording, typed fields, assets and publication. A maintainer without source publication rights can save the shortcut candidate and see the precise next permitted step. They are not given extra rights just to complete a wizard.

Reusable content begins with D18's deliberate generalization/contribution process. Do not harvest a live donor/care message into a shared shortcut with one click. Source-derived private facts and attachments must not become library content through copying or an AI draft later.

Incomplete but structurally safe configuration can be saved. Show **Draft — select published wording**, **Draft — choose a work change** or the real missing requirement, not a generic error toast. Duplicate creates a new unpublished candidate referencing qualified shared wording; it never makes an active copy or clones donor facts. Tenant configuration custody survives creator departure through current capabilities, without appointing a new global shortcut role.

### REQ26-D24-C007 — Publish wording, then activate the exact combination

Content publication and Support activation are separate operations and permissions. **Review and activate** shows the exact wording revision, use scope and final work choices; editing an active shortcut shows changes from its current revision. It creates a new immutable configuration version and conditionally moves the active head. Conflicting editor changes require reconciliation, not last-write-wins.

If a contextual helper guides Publish wording and return, report both results accurately. A published wording revision may exist while shortcut activation fails. Say **Wording published; shortcut still a draft** and preserve the candidate for correction. Do not say nothing was saved or repeat publication blindly. P17 publication keeps its real protected/tenant-stricter rules; ordinary Support configuration activation does not invent a mandatory second reviewer.

An active shortcut's new edit remains a candidate until activation. Staff continue using the current qualified active revision. A routine source update shows **New wording available** to the maintainer; it does not silently update active shortcuts or edited drafts. A current source withdrawal, broken target or incompatible schema shows **Needs attention** and blocks new use that is no longer eligible. Old but still valid wording is not automatically a safety defect.

Repair offers the precise action: choose an eligible target, review the newer source, narrow the audience, fix a required variant or archive. It does not silently choose a replacement person, create a missing label or downgrade the purpose. Label health depends on the operation: adding an archived label is blocked, but removing an exact authorized existing application of an ordinarily archived label remains useful and permitted. Actual restriction/missing-source gates still apply. Recheck just before activation, even if a cached health indicator was green.

### REQ26-D24-C008 — Retire or restrict even when something is broken

**Archive** must remain usable when a target was deleted or source is unavailable. It stops new selection and preserves minimal identity/history. It cannot demand a successfully executable shortcut first. A failed dependency should never force a maintainer to configure a fake team to pause use.

Routine archive and safety withdrawal are different. Routine archive does not erase admitted history or automatically invalidate every already staged copy; exact staged revisions still undergo current authorization and source eligibility. An authoritative restriction can block affected existing drafts/preparations under D16/D17/P17. The UI explains whether the reusable shortcut was archived or actual content was withdrawn, without exposing restricted details.

Restoration creates/reviews a current candidate rather than blindly resurrecting obsolete targets. Irreversible owner retention/deletion may preserve a minimal tombstone as required; a shortcut cannot recreate purged content from its source reference or a restore backup. No new indefinite full-body archive is added.

### REQ26-D24-C009 — Learn what needs maintenance

Show exact admission-based last recorded use and period use, scoped to the maintainer's current authorized evidence. A shortcut-assisted reply is one admitted reply retaining its staged association; views, selections, canceled/detached plans and retries do not count. A kept-current reply is distinguishable from wording inserted/replaced by that source. Queued usage does not claim delivery, a correct outcome or saved time.

The period's timezone and half-open boundaries are visible. Drilldown/export uses the same receipt cohort; an old conversation replied to today belongs to today's admission cohort. Merging display groups does not count the same reply twice. Retention gaps show Unknown/partial; they are not Never used. No synthetic use labels contaminate the curated Support taxonomy. Feedback can flag a specific outdated source through existing qualified maintenance attention, with minimal safe metadata rather than captured conversation bodies.

### REQ26-D24-C010 — Accessibility, mobile and recovery acceptance

Use the existing Core base-maia/Base UI vocabulary, type scale and spacing. Desktop picker/preview and a narrow-screen sheet can differ in layout while retaining every effect and disclosure. Staff can complete the same reviewed operation by keyboard, touch and screen reader; there is no mobile text-only shortcut that silently discards work.

Prove focus placement/return, labelled search and controls, accessible pending-versus-current summaries, polite save/error announcements, IME and international text handling, touch targets, zoom/reflow and plain-language errors. Avoid nested popover traps, hover-only meaning, color-only health and an error that scrolls typed text out of view. Escape closes a picker without erasing work; keyboard shortcuts do not conflict with platform/assistive behavior. Real supported assistive-technology/mobile tests remain required.

Load authorized metadata first; fetch/compile content only where needed. Reuse shared Tiptap controls and static readers. Do not hydrate a whole library, repeatedly fetch CRM context per keystroke or add a second editor runtime. Register and test actual bounds for scoped lookup, source/document size, patch size, draft history, compilation and admission before activation; no vendor quota is adopted as an Asym performance claim.

### REQ26-D24-C011 — AI later, through the same human journey

There is no AI control or model call in this feature now. The useful future first hypothesis is suggesting an existing currently eligible curated shortcut, with a visible reason and ordinary preview/dismissal. It must outperform the manual path on correct completed replies, not merely clicks. Explicitly requested wording changes and unpublished maintenance candidates are later separate research questions.

Any later implementation consumes ADR0099/Phase40's shared purpose-routed tenant AI foundation, permission/classification/egress restrictions and non-authoritative suggestion evidence. It cannot use an engineering Eve workflow as a customer-data authority. A suggestion never publishes, activates or sends, and copying text from it cannot arm a hidden plan. The manual picker and owner-controlled admission remain understandable and usable without AI.

All source comparisons and independent corrections are recorded in the evidence register. All 50 release proof groups in the main review remain required and unexecuted.

### REQ26-D24-C016 — State and transaction model

Preview and staging are read/private-draft operations. No label, status, handling, live note or send intent exists solely because Use shortcut was clicked. The app-owned draft command/history boundary synchronizes body changes and plan changes; the Tiptap document does not serialize executable plans. Undo/Redo and mode/context switching follow R08–R10, not text-equality inference.

Before admission, validate the exact full recipient set, authorized sources/fields/assets, signature/public identity, actual human role, shortcut/configuration relevance and all current resulting Support preconditions. Recheck relevant generations for work, assignment, membership, source restrictions and merged-original topology. A routine irrelevant name edit should not invalidate an otherwise unchanged operation; changes to actual authorized meaning must.

One conditional database unit then claims exact ready preparation and records **all** local effects: message intent; status/reminder; handling; label membership across affected original contributors; before/after business history; shortcut use receipt; and durable dispatch/recovery intent. If any required component fails before this commits, none commits. No “continue after error”, unavailable-step skip, stop-on-error flag or compensating saga of local REST calls is acceptable. The future implementation must provide shared in-transaction primitives rather than nest existing independently committing public endpoints.

The four D3 work states preserve their semantics. A courtesy update alone cannot establish Waiting. Waiting on our side requires actual requested input; the shortcut does not create an owner task. No response remains D5's separate end-follow-up review/evidence. Resolve is gated by genuine unfinished Support obligations/required D11 result review, not every linked process. Review-first handling blocks the handling change until its separate review; it need not block otherwise-authorized reply/status/label work if handling is kept. An explicit eligible individual manual assignment can settle D8 A even if automatic release is paused or Shared lacks independent coverage.

After admission, a lost HTTP response reconciles the same durable intent/hash. Changed input with that identity conflicts. New deliberate reply means new intent even when text matches. Provider keys are transport aids, not the durable identity. Queued is truthful local outcome; delivery is separate evidence. A later failure does not reverse or reapply old work. Existing D3/D4/P6 causal recovery can raise current review without hijacking a later worker's state. No transaction includes network send, and no recovery silently changes sender/recipients/body/source or resends a whole group.

### REQ26-D24-C018 — Database, authorization and persistence proof

Use tenant-aware primary/foreign/unique keys for shortcuts, versions, source references, target references, draft plans and receipts as required by actual owner representation. Do not accept cross-tenant same-ID references or source IDs without purpose/audience validation. Required fields/non-nullability, finite lengths/patch dimensions, disjoint label sets, valid lifecycle combinations, active-head integrity and semantic-hash uniqueness need enforceable constraints plus one authoritative mutation boundary. Use suitable indexes for tenant/source/target/FK lookup and actual scoped list/report access. There is no money field or new financial precision model here; giving money remains owned elsewhere.

Trusted current server context derives tenant, human actor/member/profile, author, approver/control status and audit attribution. Client input contains proposed allowed values and expected revisions only. Creation cannot be smuggled through an update upsert; deletion cannot recreate a missing object. An allowed update cannot move a permitted row to another tenant/purpose/custody, swap a published source illegally or turn a private candidate into active work.

Review direct API/collection writers, table/column grants, RLS SELECT/USING/WITH CHECK, all permissive policies, view behavior, RPC execute grants, definer ownership/fixed search path, storage and privileged workers together. PostgreSQL can derive WITH CHECK from USING; inspect actual effective behavior rather than declaring missing explicit syntax a finding. Row policy alone does not protect trusted columns or prevent service-role bypass. Authoritative commands must apply equal boundaries in service/worker paths and recheck all actual current original contributors, not only the visible merged root.

Retain separate minimum records for configuration audit, actual human command history, security incidents and technical traces. No before/after document body copies or PII-bearing template variables go into general logs. Private draft/source/admitted-message/asset retention remain their respective D16/D17/P17 purposes. Restore barriers prevent old code or backups re-exposing withdrawn derivatives. Qualified owner import/export creates remapped inactive destination candidates; no Support transfer dialect, identity creation or activation rights are introduced.

Same-evaluation drilldown/export uses the same authorized receipt cohort. Missing retained evidence produces Unknown/partial, not zero/Never. No new operational labels, cached body archive or agent ranking is required.

## D24 — Independently verifiable acceptance criteria

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Current untrusted email/model-shaped payloads cannot become commands, recipients, publication or execution authority. Actual future-model evaluations occur only under later qualified governance before AI activation.

Stories: US26-D24-05. Requirements: REQ26-D24-R24, REQ26-D24-R25, REQ26-D24-R26, REQ26-D24-R27, REQ26-D24-R28, REQ26-D24-R29, REQ26-D24-R30.

### AC26-D24-P49

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Source/curation/admission/provider/security history and technical traces remain distinct; minimal safe IDs explain outcome without raw message/query content.

Stories: US26-D24-04. Requirements: REQ26-D24-R20, REQ26-D24-R22, REQ26-D24-R23.

### AC26-D24-P50

**Given** the applicable permitted and forbidden actors, source states and boundary fixtures stated in this criterion, **when** the specified action/event is exercised through the confirmed acceptance seam, **then** the following observable outcome must hold:

Full D24 trace survives later specification/tickets/releases; no hidden workflow/CRM/editor/AI platform or unsafe rollback path is introduced.

Stories: US26-D24-05. Requirements: REQ26-D24-R24, REQ26-D24-R25, REQ26-D24-R26, REQ26-D24-R27, REQ26-D24-R28, REQ26-D24-R29, REQ26-D24-R30.

## D24 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D24-O01

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed cross-scope disclosure or accepted unauthorized actor/action/source mutation.

**Owner:** Core security/identity and Support owner.

**Response:** Fence affected reads/admission, retain minimal incident evidence, correct source/derivatives and qualify before reopening.

### OP26-D24-O02

**Signal and threshold:** One admitted reply/patch mismatch, partial local compound effect or duplicate business-effect receipt.

**Owner:** Support admission/data owner.

**Response:** Stop affected shortcut admission, reconcile exact intent from durable evidence, preserve P6 effects and repair; no blind rollback/resend.

### OP26-D24-O03

**Signal and threshold:** First authoritative dependency failure affecting new use, or first stale health projection that still advertises an unusable shortcut.

**Owner:** Support shortcut maintainer, with P17/source owner.

**Response:** Mark scoped Needs attention, block invalid current use, route exact repair or allow Archive without compiling the failure.

### OP26-D24-O04

**Signal and threshold:** First ambiguous/failed draft save or inconsistent Undo/staged-plan restoration.

**Owner:** Shared editor and Support draft owner.

**Response:** Preserve permitted text, visibly disarm uncertain work, reconcile before showing Saved/ready; never send on reconnect.

### OP26-D24-O05

**Signal and threshold:** First breach of registered query/compile/transaction budget, cleanup deadline or same-evaluation usage/drilldown parity.

**Owner:** Relevant performance/records/report owner.

**Response:** Bound execution, keep current serving restrictions, flag incomplete reporting and repair the exact projection/dependency; do not invent zero or relax authorization.

### REQ26-D24-C030 — Operating and qualification sequence

These monitor residual faults after mandatory preventive gates; none turns a known correctness requirement into monitor-only work.

## D25 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D25-R01 — Equal plain-language paths, one receiving product

Present the two initial address choices with equal prominence and no preselection, then show only the selected guide. A known suitable existing address and a fresh dedicated address are both legitimate starting points. Preserve progress when switching or returning. This selects onboarding behavior over the already-scoped forwarding and BYO receiving capabilities; it adds no Gmail/Microsoft mailbox sync, history import, telephony, public help center, AI or multi-provider mail platform.

A, existing-address-first, is strongest when an appropriate address is already known. B, dedicated-address-first, is strongest for a known fresh program or separate intake. C avoids presuming tenant prevalence and asks one understandable factual choice. This is product judgment, not measured conversion advantage or evidence that every ministry has the same workflow.

### REQ26-D25-R02 — Keep the address, inbox, team and public identity distinct

An inbox is the authorized Support work destination; its name and handling team are not email addresses or CRM owners. The public incoming address, exact receiving route, outgoing From, Reply-To destination and managed signature are separate facts. Show a recipient-facing preview with each actual value before activation. Keeping `donorcare@harbor.example` as a public contact address does not promise it can be the From address under P17's approved transactional domain. No login/assignee/private profile fallback invents identity.

The founder's mission/donor-care context is the target population. Named examples illustrate possible use, not proven tenant frequencies. A personal employee mailbox or mixed confidential ministry mailbox is not presumed appropriate for shared Support intake. Select the intended Support scope and owning privacy boundary before forwarding; restricted care remains with its actual owner.

### REQ26-D25-R03 — A focused, resumable setup surface

Enter from Support inbox settings or the empty-inbox state with tenant/inbox context intact. The common journey is address choice, address and route, qualified connection checks, verification, then review and activation. Show concise progress and one next actionable issue, reusing existing integration/domain settings through contextual navigation. Save safe incomplete configuration as Draft; no raw state flag can make it Ready or Active. Simple names, addresses and DNS instructions are ordinary inputs; Tiptap is reserved for the already-qualified content surfaces.

Saving, Leaving setup or returning from provider settings does not activate, send, delete captured input or erase completed valid proof. Back preserves shared fields and branch-specific candidate information. An unknown save outcome reconciles the same command before showing Saved. Secrets and challenges never enter persistent browser form state. Do not reset typed fields whenever an unrelated query refresh arrives.

### REQ26-D25-R04 — Split responsibilities without transferring authority

Use current Core capabilities to distinguish Support configuration, current source/inbox access, tenant delivery/credential/domain administration, P17 reply-destination acceptance, and D19 review/coverage. Provider/DNS changes require the tenant's actual outside administrative authority. Configuration access does not reveal donor messages; permission to read Support mail does not reveal credentials or confer domain administration.

Provide copyable nonsecret instructions and an authenticated return location for another qualified administrator. Sharing instructions grants no role or challenge completion right and sends no email itself. Provider/P17 secrets use the existing protected owner handoff; no emailed key, transferable verification token or new approval-routing system. Current permissions and step-up requirements are rechecked at each consequential command and after an administrator departs.

### REQ26-D25-R05 — Extend the shared Resend owner explicitly for receiving

Retain the tenant's single P6/P17 Resend account/team ownership and connection aggregate. Preserve the domain-restricted Sending-access credential for outbound. Receiving API hydration cannot use that key: current Resend documents only `sending_access` and `full_access`; OAuth also requires `full_access` for non-send routes. Add one purpose-separated inbound credential facet under the same managed encrypted revision/custody controls. Do not widen or replace the outgoing key or create a global fallback.

The receiving credential currently has provider-level Full access. State that honestly to the authorized connection administrator; it is not a provider-enforced read-only credential. Confine its use to the qualified server ingestion/repair adapter's closed read operations and exact registered connection resources; never expose a generic proxy, outbound sending, domain/key/webhook mutation or credential to ordinary Support. Same-account proof uses current exact provider objects/canary evidence linked to the shared connection, not labels, key hints or caller metadata. A pending unproved credential may perform only those bounded account-proof reads, never ordinary incoming body/attachment retrieval or exposure. Prove positive and wrong-account behavior before activation. OAuth adds no narrower privilege today and is not introduced here. This is an explicit P26 receiving-purpose extension to the outbound-only credential contract, with residual credential-compromise risk and mandatory owner controls.

### REQ26-D25-R06 — Authenticate provider scope before trusting message data

Use the existing opaque per-connection signed ingress to select exactly one registered tenant/account/environment/secret revision before parsing or resolving a destination. Verify the raw body, validate the exact event schema and record scoped provider evidence. Never select a tenant from message metadata/tags, sender, To/Cc/Bcc, default From domain or a claimed tenant ID. Signed transport authenticates a provider event, not the truth or authority of every email header.

The same connection endpoint can dispatch registered `email.received` events to the P26 owner and outbound evidence to P6. P17's outbound reducer still makes no outbound transition for inbound events. Preserve required subscription union and business-specific dedupe/readiness when changing registrations; do not demand a webhook per inbox or another provider plan merely to separate owners. Provider receiving domain catch-all behavior does not authorize catch-all Support routing. Unproven/contradictory recipient or tenant evidence enters the already-owned restricted recovery path, never an arbitrary inbox.

### REQ26-D25-R07 — Exact address identity and controlled route ownership

Parse one mailbox with the shared versioned canonicalization/IDNA policy. Preserve valid local-part semantics; do not collapse Gmail dots/plus variants, lowercase all local parts, equate aliases or infer organizational identity from an email suffix. Bound input and reject header injection, multiple-address/group syntax and provider-unsupported forms with an actionable error. International names remain supported; international address capabilities require actual transport qualification rather than a blanket ASCII rule or false promise.

Each public-address binding resolves to one authorized inbox for its qualified receiving context. Multiple explicitly verified addresses may lead to one inbox, but one new setup does not silently capture a domain or remap an existing active address. Existing matching bindings show a safe conflict/authorized navigation; no unique-key exception redirects another route. Cross-tenant/other-environment conflicts reveal no owner details. Dedicated local-part availability in a catch-all domain means available in the owner registry, not that an external mailbox object was provisioned.

### REQ26-D25-R08 — Establish safe custody before external mail can arrive

Register a server-owned candidate receiving context and working durable capture/recovery before exposing forwarding/DNS instructions that can start delivery. Candidate capture is qualification-only, not an Active ordinary inbox. Store known-owner early input under the existing finite source-owned custody and classification rules. Unknown ownership uses separately authorized platform recovery; candidate tenants cannot inspect it.

Separate exact expected verification traffic from real early messages.
