Neither creates normal conversations, CRM Parties/interactions, D13 acknowledgements, reply targets, assignments, labels or following updates merely because it arrives during setup. Show authorized safe counts and the consequence of continuing/canceling. Do not leave real early mail indefinitely in an invisible setup queue or reset its received-at, retention or utility when activation occurs. An external change can begin delivery before Asym knows it; absence of a click is not proof no mail arrived.

### REQ26-D25-R09 — Existing-address path preserves continuity with truthful limits

Ask for the public address the tenant intends to keep. Confirm appropriate mailbox control/monitoring through the existing P17 external destination process where applicable before forwarding obscures that independent access proof. Create the tenant-bound candidate target, give provider-specific redirection/forwarding guidance and preserve original mailbox custody. Qualify the actual method's recipient/header/thread behavior; manual forward, mailbox rule, alias, shared mailbox, distribution group and multihop forwarding are not presumed equivalent or universally prohibited.

Handle the email provider's own destination-confirmation message in the restricted setup view, only for the exact initiated candidate and currently authorized operator. Never auto-click arbitrary incoming links, classify by a display name/domain alone or turn this confirmation into a Support ticket. The provider administrator may still need to return to the provider to enable/save forwarding after confirming. Then independently test new mail and the ordinary reply path. Upstream spam rules/forwarding prohibitions may block mail before Asym custody; show that limit and the scoped repair or alternative path. Do not recommend weakening organization-wide protections or claim historical/two-way synchronization.

### REQ26-D25-R10 — Dedicated-address path isolates receiving without replacing ordinary mail

Ask for a new address on a suitable tenant-owned receiving domain/subdomain in the same qualified Resend account. Prefer a dedicated subdomain where an existing domain already serves everyday mail. Reuse existing qualified domain facts but prove receiving-specific records/current ownership separately; a sending-domain check alone is insufficient. Never add competing root MX records or replace existing root mail routing as a setup shortcut. Show provider-returned exact record values in copyable fields with current status and meaningful recheck, not hard-coded regions/hosts/priorities.

Register only the intended exact public-address binding. Catch-all reception does not create arbitrary inboxes, addresses or CRM identities. Additional receiving domains do not replace P17's chosen transactional sending domain, Default Sender or default human reply destination. Provider-managed receiving addresses are technical targets where qualified, not automatically approved tenant-public addresses or shared platform senders. The new address is not an IMAP/POP mailbox, personal mailbox license or email-hosting product.

### REQ26-D25-R11 — Separate the proof dimensions and their limits

Track at least current connection/account scope, receiving-domain/route, public-destination control, external new-message arrival, ordinary reply return, outbound preparation/delivery compatibility and accountable monitoring/review coverage as independent evidence. Render a concise summary with the failing dimension and one owner action. A started test is Checking; a provider 2xx is not automatically verified; mail-server acceptance is not inbox placement; a successful test proves its exact path/revision at that time, not every future filter or continuous monitoring.

Bind evidence to candidate generation and actual source/connection/address revisions. Late, duplicate, wrong-address, previous-generation or unauthenticated proof cannot complete current setup. Material change invalidates only affected proof; ordinary internal-label edits do not cause ritual retesting. Recheck at relevant configuration change, security incident, concrete drift or owner-defined proof expiry. No invented deliverability score, global Connected truth, endless polling or periodic live canary without an actual purpose.

### REQ26-D25-R12 — Resolve the P17 managed-reply-destination gap

P17's existing external-mailbox challenge is not proof for a new Asym-managed mailbox merely because Asym received its own code. Add a typed **managed Support route** proof method to the existing Human reply destination owner, alongside its external-access method. P26 produces evidence bound to exact tenant/account/environment/domain/public-address/inbox route/candidate generation, actual qualified new-mail and reply return, and current access/monitoring custody. The stepped-up P17 reply manager accepts that method for the exact destination revision; no new reply purpose, template key, general alias engine or P17 ingestion owner is introduced.

External mailbox challenges retain same-initiating-human/current-capability/step-up/single-use controls; their codes remain excluded from ordinary Support/history/Recent/logs. Do not auto-complete them from incoming traffic or transfer a challenge to an IT helper. A managed route may be transport-qualified while ordinary intake remains inactive, breaking circular activation without opening public Support work. Changing the selected inbox binding does not silently repoint tenant-wide Default human replies or other purposes; any such adoption uses the owning explicit reviewed operation and its current impact checks.

### REQ26-D25-R13 — Qualification traffic is bounded owner work, not a general sender

Reuse P17/P6's fixed inert qualification producer with the exact candidate credential/sender/destination and an approved real control mailbox/sink. It may operate in its narrowly allowed Testing state before production Ready; ordinary replies, acknowledgements and catalog messages remain blocked. No shared platform bootstrap key, arbitrary-recipient test mailer, caller-authored headers/body or donor merge fields are introduced.

A controlled external new message and a reply to the exact prepared canary exercise the route. An authorized person may perform the external-mailbox steps; do not invent an automatic platform relay to avoid them. Synthetic proof identifiers bind purpose/generation without granting access, and known verification traffic stays outside ordinary Support/CRM metrics. The integration/P17 owner defines fixed noneditable proof content and safe expected sender/link handling; Email Studio does not provide a free-form template for it. Provider failure after possible submission reconciles the same occurrence, never a blind Send again.

### REQ26-D25-R14 — Bounded verification and anti-abuse controls

Reuse current owner challenge controls: trusted actor/tenant/candidate/purpose/address binding, finite expiry, one live challenge per relevant revision, safe keyed verifier, replay protection, attempt cap, resend cooldown and per-actor/tenant/address/global burst control. Register and test exact limits under the owner before release rather than adopt vendor example numbers as universal policy. GET may display the authenticated operation; only a current authorized mutation completes it. No URL click by a mail scanner activates an inbox.

Verification can establish one thing—external access, provider routing or controlled return—without establishing the others. Do not reduce proof to a matching subject/code or trust arbitrary Authentication-Results/Received headers. Sanitize authorized setup mail, suppress remote tracking/active content, expose only the needed confirmation action, and retain no secret code in audit. A verification message mixed with real sensitive material is not automatically safe to display; unknown traffic follows ordinary source classification/review.

### REQ26-D25-R15 — Activate one reviewed current configuration atomically

Review exact public address, actual From/Reply-To/signature, inbox scope and existing qualified coverage/acknowledgement choices. Activation is a server-owned conditional transition over current proof and configuration generations. Atomically install the authorized active binding, activation/actor history and durable reconciliation/release intent in the Asym write boundary. If a required proof, role, uniqueness or target constraint fails, leave the prior good configuration intact and show the exact issue. Provider/DNS I/O is not inside that database transaction.

Do not activate through a raw route save, completed wizard checkbox, DNS lookup, provider success response or `23505` update fallback. D6 receiving/assignment controls, D13 confirmation eligibility and D19 review coverage remain separate accepted meanings, exposed in context rather than silently enabled. Activation neither claims all previous mail has been processed nor treats the user clicking Finish as a provider action.

### REQ26-D25-R16 — Account for early arrivals without rebasing history

Activation schedules complete, bounded reconciliation of retained eligible early input under current source and D19 rules. Only ordinary eligible traffic enters its proper inbox; verification, restricted, expired or still-unresolved inputs keep their distinct disposition. Show progress and safe counts, with errors/unknowns instead of fabricated zero or Completed. Preserve original provider/Asym receipt times, retention, D13's existing utility window and D14 original obligation age/meaning. No backlog replay restarts an acknowledgement clock or silently sends stale confirmations.

Use scoped database predicates before pagination and deterministic continuation, not the first 50 rows followed by in-memory filtering. Resolve each input only with its durable authoritative admission/disposition and necessary continuation intent; queued dispatch is not completion. Duplicate events, worker restart and same address matches cannot create duplicate conversations or effects. Preserve attachment/body incomplete-versus-empty distinctions and existing intake acceptance responsibility.

### REQ26-D25-R17 — Switch paths and cancel without pretending to undo outside changes

Switching choice creates/revises the candidate and invalidates affected pending proof while preserving reusable permitted fields. It does not repoint an Active route, delete received mail or automatically turn off provider forwarding/MX. Show any outside change still requiring the tenant's action. Cancel stops new candidate work and performs finite safe cleanup; residual arrivals remain recoverable under their actual owner and expiry. Do not deallocate/reassign a receiving target while delayed mail could be misattributed to a different owner.

The primary action is Save and leave or Cancel setup as appropriate; explain impact only when external delivery/captured input exists. No multi-dialog ceremony for a harmless path change before outside effects. Pending commands reconcile before a second tab can overwrite the candidate; stale success never restores an older path.

### REQ26-D25-R18 — Replace and add addresses deliberately

Address change is a new candidate binding/proof, not an in-place identity rewrite. Keep the prior working route until the replacement passes qualification and the authorized manager reviews impact. Atomically cut new work to the exact ready binding, retaining original conversation and immutable prepared-message lineage. Existing messages/replies may still arrive through the old address; provide an explicit bounded transition/alias retention or owner-approved retirement plan based on actual dependencies, not an arbitrary fixed grace period or an unending hidden alias.

Each additional address has its own control/readiness binding. Never move someone else's active route by catching a uniqueness error, overwrite original creator attribution, adopt a domain default from one alias, or infer domain-wide authority from one mailbox challenge. A new address can be linked to the same inbox without moving CRM contacts or rewriting sender history. Returned mail to a retired route stays owner-recoverable where accepted; no silent assignment to a different tenant or newly reusing employee address.

### REQ26-D25-R19 — Pause, repair and retirement have distinct effects

Pausing ordinary intake/admission for one inbox does not stop SMTP reception at an external provider, disable every tenant email, erase captured mail or close Support work. Display those distinctions; preserve source capture/recovery as required and fence unsafe new effects. Incoming routing failure, outbound failure, revoked read credential and ordinary D6 receiving availability are distinct conditions. Authorized reading/draft work that remains safe is not blanket-disabled by a provider badge.

Retirement reviews active public addresses, original return routes, bindings, unsubmitted/prepared/indeterminate sends, unresolved custody and outside changes. Stop new use, maintain necessary bounded reconciliation and record exact cleanup/tenant-provider instructions. Shared tenant connection disconnect is a separate impact-reviewed owning operation; one inbox's Delete must not call it. Restore/reconnect requalifies current authority and never resurrects purged content, retired owner mappings or disabled old writers.

### REQ26-D25-R20 — Credential and provider changes preserve old effect identity

Receiving-key/webhook rotation uses pending proof, conditional new-use cutover, bounded old-event overlap and existing managed secret destruction/restore barriers. Suspected compromise fences affected authority immediately and requires provider revocation/replacement; do not retain compromised credentials for convenience. Exact old incoming events and already prepared outbound work retain their account/connection lineage during authorized reconciliation; no cross-account rekey/resend.

Capture provider-created/rotated secrets once through existing protected custody and redact them from any later provider response. Current direct API/CLI documentation describes signing secrets in webhook reads; treat those reads as secret-bearing, and never expose them as ordinary setup status. A stale search excerpt initially suggested otherwise and has been superseded by the pinned direct source. Do not make safe custody depend on later provider reread availability. An ambiguous provider mutation reconciles its exact known object/operation before any create/rotate retry. Manual provider administration remains truthful outside work; a UI progress flag is not a provider receipt.

A qualified exact-object read may recover an interrupted creation/rotation when current owner authority, intended object and actual revision are proven; capture recovered material in the same protected custody. This is not a generic secret-discovery endpoint or permission to adopt an unrelated current secret. Unknown object/revision remains incomplete without blind recreation or repeated rotation.

Receiving repair must not gratuitously depend on a new outgoing production send when current exact registered provider-object proof suffices. Conversely, usable intake alone does not grant ordinary outgoing readiness. Domain/team/region ownership changes are explicit replacement and requalification with impact, not ordinary settings edits. Never delete or replace a shared provider domain/webhook to repair one inbox without complete owner dependency proof and authority.

### REQ26-D25-R21 — CRM and cross-surface continuity remain source-owned

Requester, message participant, authenticated administrator/responder, CRM Party, represented organization, inbox worker and CRM owner stay distinct. A verified support address proves no requester identity, membership or giving/care authority. Setup, proof messages, route health and activation create no fake Party, donor interaction, gift action, target credit or staff productivity event. Actual admitted correspondence later uses the existing deduplicated history projection and current CRM permissions.

Reuse actual owner navigation for context, source linking and authorized business action; no duplicate CRM snapshot/store or external CRM synchronization. Address/domain verification cannot expose missionary/care facts or expand inbox content scope. CRM record merge/unlink/deletion and employee email reuse do not reassign receiving-route ownership; current source identities and lineage remain authoritative.

### REQ26-D25-R22 — Constrain the authoritative data and transitions

Use tenant/account/environment-aware identities and composite relationships for candidate/active address bindings, provider connection/secret revisions, proof attempts, inbox destinations, source custody/review, command receipts and audit. Enforce one current active mapping for the exact qualified receiving destination and one active candidate head/expected generation per edited binding; independent candidates may coexist only without conflicting claims. Preserve immutable original attribution and append current change actors separately.

Typed valid state/proof/purpose combinations, required references, disjoint candidate versus active authority, unique event/command identities and safe delete behavior prevent cross-tenant reparenting or orphaned accepted input. Configuration can be mutable only through its versioned owner; proofs and source/effect history are append-only with explicit supersession/correction. No money field or duplicated financial precision model is introduced. Actual limits/indexes/migrations follow the shared owners and registered bounds, not guessed physical schema names.

### REQ26-D25-R23 — Verify effective authorization, not only RLS syntax

Derive tenant, current actor/member, account/route ownership and audit fields from trusted server context. Current capability and exact source/destination rights apply to reads, target lookup, verification, activation, replay, cleanup and workers. Caller metadata cannot publish a route, change tenant, forge a checker, transform a permitted row into forbidden scope or recreate a missing update target by upsert.

Inspect grants, RLS SELECT/USING/effective WITH CHECK, updateable columns, permissive policy combinations, views, RPC execute grants/definer search paths, storage and privileged service code together. PostgreSQL may derive WITH CHECK from USING; absence of explicit syntax alone is not a flaw. The current inbound-route table already revokes browser grants—do not misreport it as publicly writable. Its privileged commands and relationships still need the new current-authority/atomicity proof. Fence every legacy route/default/fixture/import writer that bypasses this owner.

### REQ26-D25-R24 — Truthful failure and durable recovery

Represent Not started, Checking, current proved fact, Needs action, provider unavailable and unknown outcome according to the relevant owner; do not conflate them with configuration Draft/Active/Retired. A failed query is not zero pending mail, a verification POST is not completion, and a local acknowledgement requires durable recoverable custody. Unknown tenant evidence is not permission to try candidate tenants. Lost commands reconcile exact durable identity plus semantic hash; changed input conflicts and real new intent gets new identity.

Every authoritative write that requires later resumption/audit/repair has durable continuation with the owning effect. At-least-once jobs/events cannot duplicate input admission or overwrite later configuration. A staff-approved correction records its actual scope and cause; no direct database repair or rerouting all historical mail as the ordinary recovery path. Provider facts remain provider facts and outgoing uncertainty never authorizes a new envelope.

### REQ26-D25-R25 — Finite custody, minimization and restore safety

Candidate settings, verification content, early ordinary input, hydrated raw/header/body/files, provider URLs, command evidence and admitted messages have distinct finite owner purposes. Reuse D16/D17 and P17 preparation/challenge policies; do not create an indefinite setup archive, retain proof codes in logs, or use raw bodies as permanent audit. Provider retention and temporary URL expiry are separate constraints, not Asym guarantees of recoverability forever.

Original received-at and expiry survive pause/activation/cancel/retry. Known source withdrawal affects authorized derivatives before physical cleanup; no source fallback through Recent or a provider fetch reconstructs expired content. Secrets/verification codes never appear in exports, shared instructions, browser storage or ordinary Support. Backup restore applies route retirement, scope changes and destruction barriers before decrypt/read/worker activation. External mailbox/provider copies remain separately owned and cannot be claimed deleted by Asym Cancel or redaction.

### REQ26-D25-R26 — Complete accessible, restrained UI

Preserve Core base-maia/Base UI and shared responsive patterns. Two equal initial choices, labelled inputs, exact copyable DNS/forwarding instructions, current progress, clear verification messages and one next repair action should be enough. No hover-only meaning, color-only health, hidden activation, automatic focus jump, perpetual spinner or dense protocol checklist in the default view. Technical details are progressively disclosed when they help the responsible administrator act.

Support keyboard, touch, screen reader, zoom/reflow, IME/international names and low-bandwidth interrupted setup. Copy reports success or a manual-selection fallback; submitting twice does not duplicate work. “I need my email administrator” preserves progress and safe instructions, not an entitlement or approval proxy. Save conflicts preserve the newer server record and local permitted input for reconciliation. Validate with actual administrator/IT split and both mobile/desktop paths before release; attractive screenshots alone do not prove usability.

### REQ26-D25-R27 — Observable operations without surveillance or noise

Show concise owner-scoped health: what is known, last relevant proof, impact, safe pending counts and next action. Keep provider acceptance, input custody, qualification and normal Support work histories distinct. Technical traces use safe scope/revision/event/command identifiers; durable business history records actual operator intent/outcome. No body/credential/code logs, deliverability score, tracking pixel or fabricated “no mail lost” metric.

O01–O06 below identify signals, thresholds, owners and responses after mandatory prevention. Detection of upstream mail never delivered to Asym is inherently limited; report explicit known failure or evidence gap, not a false diagnosis. Existing P6/P17/D19 grouped repair/attention handles real owner action without a new alert framework or notification for every DNS poll.

### REQ26-D25-R28 — Email Studio has a precise seam

P17 owns content/publication, safe compiler/presentation, Sender/Reply identities and their proof acceptance; Support owns receiving/inbox configuration and ordinary admission; P6 owns tenant credentials/transport/evidence through the shared connection. D18 saved replies, D23 signatures/Tiptap and D24 shortcuts remain their accepted qualified sources. Setup can select/preview eligible existing content and navigate to its owner without duplicating it or acquiring publishing rights.

No new tenant-editable system-message key, per-inbox template runtime, arbitrary verification body, provider-template mirror or direct Support mailer is added. Existing fixed qualification messages stay outside catalog truth, with narrow proof authority and no donor/CRM effects. D13 automatic request confirmation is a separate real template and cannot confirm setup or run on a provider challenge. The explicit managed-route proof and inbound credential/ingress extensions amend only the necessary P17/P6 seams; original records remain historical and intact until implementation propagation.

### REQ26-D25-R29 — Qualify real provider capability before activation

Pin exact SDK/API/error/schema fixtures for receiving metadata/body/raw/header/attachments, actual recipient/authentication provenance, same-account proof, webhook replay/dedupe, declared permissions, retention/URL deadlines and shared rate/quota behavior. Current `received_for` is documented as header-derived and is not automatically SMTP-envelope attestation; SDK declarations are not transport proof. Prove actual trusted source routing with spoofed/contradictory To/Cc/Bcc/Received/auth headers, forward methods and ordinary new/reply mail before claiming automatic routing is safe.

Validate the actual received-email identity and bounded response schema instead of treating HTTP 200 or an empty object as successful hydration. Preserve ordered duplicate headers in qualified raw acquisition when provenance requires them; a flattened header dictionary is insufficient. Request the qualified safe HTML representation and inspect the actual returned format; missing/incompatible raw or excessive inlining is explicit incomplete evidence, not empty content. Attachment pagination must retain and consume continuation through the complete source set before claiming completion. Refresh temporary URLs only through current exact owner authorization, enforce approved hosts/redirect/size/type limits and no arbitrary server fetch, and preserve legitimate attachment-only inputs.

If an exact method cannot satisfy mandatory source/tenant/return-path requirements, it remains unavailable with a clear reason; do not compensate with guessed headers, permissive fallbacks or a fake verified badge. Existing Resend-first mandatory qualification remains; other-provider contingency research occurs only on an actual mandatory-capability failure, not as a hidden second launch provider. P01–P50 are required release evidence, not claims this proposal is already proven in production.

### REQ26-D25-R30 — Roll out one qualified path without destructive cutover

Inventory current global-secret webhook, payload/domain tenant inference, mutable routes, default routing, legacy sender settings, all API/collection/import/worker writers and existing live-like data. Add compatible constrained owner contracts/readers and candidate/proof/custody primitives first. Classify/backfill only evidenced facts; legacy routes are not automatically verified. Keep unclear mappings in accountable repair while preserving accepted mail and current lineage.

Qualify shared receiving credential/ingress and P17 managed-destination proof, then build both complete guides and guarded activation, then migrate/fence every bypass before scoped activation. New UI cannot sit over the old unique-conflict redirect or partial resume loop. Mixed-version/restore/rollback cannot reenable global keys, caller tenant selectors, false readiness or retired routes. Roll forward when old code cannot safely read new evidence. No commit, formal OpenSpec/PRD, issue graph or runtime migration is performed during this review.

### REQ26-D25-R31 — Bound work without losing completeness

Reuse tenant-fair P6/shared execution budgets for sending and receiving under the same provider account/quota. Register finite metadata/document/attachment/proof-attempt/lookup/capture/reconciliation/query limits, pool/transaction budgets and capacity alarms before release, with explicit exact-boundary tests. Avoid one provider webhook per inbox, full mailbox hydration in setup, per-keystroke provider calls and unbounded source downloads.

Use database filtering before pagination, durable deterministic cursors and current eligibility on each resumed batch. Prioritize recovering accepted input within actual material deadlines through the existing scheduler without a second generic queue/workflow platform. A partial scan or exhausted budget reports incomplete progress, never zero or complete. Cache proof/health by actual tenant/actor/context generation where relevant; cached convenience never grants access or activation.

### REQ26-D25-R32 — Trace and finish the bounded decision

Record C with D25-R01–R32, all category findings, complete UX/data/evidence, the accepted glossary definitions, P01–P50 and O01–O06. The new owner proof/credential/ingress seams are explicit amendments for implementation governing-artifact propagation; no competitor overrides Core silently. No AI, mailbox-sync, CRM or generic onboarding platform is needed.

### REQ26-D25-C001 — The first screen

From Support's empty state or **Settings → Inboxes → Add inbox**, open an ordinary full-page setup surface, not a modal inside another modal. Preserve the current tenant and an existing draft/candidate where applicable. The first screen says **Set up your Support email** and offers two equal accessible choices:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Choice                              | Description shown to the administrator                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Use an existing Support address** | Keep the address people already use. We'll guide you through connecting incoming mail. |
| **Create a new Support address**    | Set up a dedicated address for this team's Support requests.                           |

Neither is preselected, labelled Recommended or placed behind Advanced. The administrator chooses the known situation; provider-specific instructions come afterward. Continue is explicit and a keyboard selection never activates or sends. Changing the selection before outside work is simple and preserves shared entered information. A short “Which should I use?” explanation covers existing suitable address versus new/separate intake without a technical questionnaire.

The visible progress groups are **Address → Connection → Verify → Review** after this choice. Keep completed checks when still valid, show only the current path and one next action. The labels describe the user's work, not a new workflow runtime. A candidate may be saved incomplete; **Saved draft**, **Not saved**, **Checking** and **Active** are different states.

### REQ26-D25-C002 — Existing-address journey

**1. Name the inbox and enter the public address.** For example, Maya at illustrative Harbor Mission enters Donor Care and `donorcare@harbor.example`. The internal inbox name is clearly separate from the address. Do not infer a donor-care team, CRM organization, security classification or access from either field. If the mailbox mixes private employee/care mail, explain that shared Support intake should cover the intended requests only and offer the new-address route. Do not silently forward everything in a personal mailbox.

Validate one mailbox using shared address rules. A typo, multiple addresses, unsupported international form or existing active binding produces a precise field error. If the current user can manage an existing matching inbox, offer that authorized destination rather than creating a duplicate. A conflict outside their scope reveals no tenant/person details. Do not guess aliases, strip plus tags or merge different addresses by name.

**2. Reuse the tenant's shared email connection.** Show what is already qualified and what needs the email administrator. Sending and receiving readiness remain distinct. If no receiving capability is configured, the user reaches the existing integration surface with their candidate preserved. Explain the additional receiving credential to its authorized owner: Resend currently requires Full access to read incoming mail. Asym uses a separate key for receiving and confines its use to receiving/proof operations. Do not mislabel it read-only or reuse the Sending-access key. The everyday responder never sees secrets.

**3. Establish address control and prepare the incoming target.** Preserve P17's external-mailbox access proof before forwarding where applicable, with the same initiating authorized stepped-up actor and protected code. Register candidate capture/recovery before displaying a target that can receive mail. Provider destination confirmation, mailbox access and route verification are separate tasks. A newly managed route uses the separately qualified managed-destination proof, not an Asym challenge surfaced through its own intake.

**4. Give the relevant forwarding instructions.** Ask which mail service or administrative method applies only when the instructions depend on it. Offer clear steps for the qualified Google/Microsoft/other-provider method, an exact copyable target, and **Copy setup instructions**. This preserves the public address; it does not connect an IMAP mailbox or import history. Show **I need my email administrator** as a save-and-handoff path, without emailing secrets or granting a helper inbox/CRM access.

Use wording such as **Complete these steps in your email provider, then return here**. Copy feedback confirms actual clipboard success; if denied, allow selecting the full value. An external policy block leads to its scoped owner instructions or the dedicated-address alternative. Do not tell a tenant to disable all outbound forwarding safeguards. Qualify redirect, mailbox rules, shared mailboxes and groups individually; do not claim every forwarding method preserves the same message source.

**5. Handle provider confirmation where it occurs.** Some providers send a confirmation to the new target before they permit forwarding. Show only the exact expected provider confirmation in the authorized setup step, sanitized and inert until the operator deliberately follows the qualified action. It is not a normal Support conversation, requester message or P17 external-access challenge. A spoofed sender/title, token copied into unrelated mail or browser scanner visit cannot complete proof. If a provider still requires Enable forwarding/Save afterward, keep that step explicit. Seeing its confirmation is not proof forwarding is enabled.

**6. Verify incoming new mail and ordinary replies.** The fixed qualification operation names its actual controlled target and expected outcome before sending. An approved real control mailbox supplies a new incoming message and a reply to the exact canary where required. Status refresh sends nothing. Show Checking until the expected current-generation evidence arrives, and distinguish **Message reached this inbox's receiving route**, **Reply returned correctly**, **Sending qualified** and **Action needed**. A success only proves that observed path at that time; it is not a guarantee about upstream spam filters, mailbox access forever or future delivery.

Unexpected real mail may arrive while this happens. Say, for example, **Mail is arriving while setup is incomplete. It is being held for authorized review.** Show a current safe count or Unknown/loading state and permitted navigation, never bodies to a DNS-only helper. Do not acknowledge, assign or start ordinary targets for setup input. Original source custody and expiry apply from actual receipt.

**7. Review the real recipient-facing identity.** Display:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Preview line           | Meaning                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| People write to        | The public incoming Support address.                                                                    |
| Replies come from      | The actual P17-approved display name and From mailbox, which may use the tenant's transactional domain. |
| Their reply returns to | The exact qualified Reply-To destination.                                                               |
| Signature              | The current eligible D23 managed signature presentation.                                                |

This makes a preserved public address compatible with a different approved outgoing domain without misleading the user. Changes to source wording/signature open the existing Email Studio owner with a return path. No editing From/Reply-To strings inside a rich-text body, no new per-inbox template or implicit tenant-wide Default human replies change.

**8. Review who handles the inbox and activate.** Present the existing D6 receiving/handling and D19 intake-review coverage, plus the accepted D13 acknowledgement setting, using their qualified controls. Setup does not invent new roles or silently enable these settings. **Activate inbox** summarizes the actual binding and pending intake consequence. The server rechecks current proof, scope and candidate generation. A conflict preserves the prior good state and explains what must be reviewed; no successful-looking toast hides a failed binding.

**9. Finish with a clear staff transition.** Show the active public address, current verified path and link to the inbox. State that new Support replies are handled in Asym; forwarding does not capture replies written independently in the old mail service. Preserve that service's copy under its own policies rather than promising deletion or synchronization. Retained eligible early mail is reconciled visibly through current intake rules with original timestamps; qualification messages remain excluded. Do not say all prior mail was imported or all received mail is processed merely because activation succeeded.

### REQ26-D25-C003 — Dedicated-address journey

**1. Name the inbox and choose the new address.** For a new Harbor Mission program, an illustrative choice is `care@support.harbor.example`. Explain that this is a dedicated Support destination, not a new personal webmail mailbox or license. The approved local part/domain must be available in the actual tenant receiving registry; provider catch-all reception does not mean every address is active in Asym. Other tenants' registrations are never revealed.

**2. Select or prepare an appropriate receiving domain.** Reuse a qualified tenant-owned receiving domain when available. When ordinary root-domain email already exists, guide a dedicated subdomain. Show the intended domain and the ordinary-mail impact before external changes. Do not replace/add competing root MX records, rewrite website DNS or switch the tenant's transactional sending domain. A sending-verified domain still needs receiving-specific proof.

**3. Reuse the same connection and protected receiving setup.** The shared tenant Resend account, separate receiving credential and authenticated ingress are configured through their existing owner. No new webhook per inbox or second credentials page appears. Setup can identify missing provider plan/capacity facts without pushing an unnecessary upgrade or claiming a different key creates more quota.

**4. Register candidate custody, then show the DNS work.** Only after candidate capture/recovery is ready, display the exact provider-supplied receiving records in Name/Type/Value/Priority fields. Copy preserves bytes; narrow screens wrap or offer an accessible scroll region. **Copy setup instructions** lets the email/domain administrator act outside Asym. Do not build a generic DNS editor or ask them to upload credentials/screenshots as proof. **Check records** inspects current evidence; checking is not activation and should not repeatedly send mail.

An existing conflicting domain or a claim/region/account move has its own owner impact/replacement path. Do not make a destructive provider transfer part of ordinary Add inbox. If DNS propagation or provider proof is pending, preserve progress and show the actual next step, without claiming a universal completion time.

**5. Prove the managed route.** A new managed address has no separate external mailbox in which the owner can safely complete P17's old mailbox-access challenge. Use the typed managed Support proof: qualified domain/account/address binding, controlled new-mail and reply-return evidence, and current authorized monitoring acceptance. Qualification capture can operate before ordinary inbox activation. Only the fixed test producer may use candidate sender/Reply-To state; no donor reply or acknowledgement is enabled as a shortcut around the cycle.

**6. Review identity and operating choices.** Use the same People write to / Replies come from / Their reply returns to / Signature preview and D6/D13/D19 owner settings as the existing-address path. DNS verification does not publish content or change the organization's Default Sender/Default human reply destination. Required rights remain separate even though navigation is coherent.

**7. Activate and make the public address usable.** The same guarded activation installs the current ready binding and durable intake reconciliation. After success, offer Copy address and Open inbox. Publishing it on a website, changing a giving receipt's Reply-To or updating another source still uses that owner's authorized operation; setup does not silently edit CRM, CMS, Email Studio or previous messages. Any early real input remains accounted for under its original source lifetime.

### REQ26-D25-C004 — Complete maintenance behavior

One **Email settings** view reachable from the inbox shows the active address, receiving method, exact From/Reply destination, concise current proof/impact and relevant next action. A pending replacement appears as a candidate beside the working configuration; it does not replace the current values on Save.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Situation                         | Complete behavior                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Save and leave                    | Preserve permitted candidate/proof progress; show Saved only after reconciliation. Never retain secret fields or resend on return.                                                            |
| Switch path                       | Preserve reusable entered fields; invalidate incompatible proof; explain outside forwarding/DNS cleanup if already changed. Existing Active route remains unchanged.                          |
| Cancel setup after mail arrives   | Stop candidate operations, preserve finite custody and give exact external cleanup tasks. Cancel does not undo DNS/forwarding or delete accepted mail.                                        |
| Two administrators edit           | Conditional revision conflict; show authorized current change and preserve local permitted input for review. No last-write-wins route replacement.                                            |
| Change address                    | Create/prove a replacement, review impact and cut over atomically; retain required old-return-route handling with a finite owner plan.                                                        |
| Add another address               | Qualify that exact binding and its use; no automatic wildcard/domain default or new source permissions.                                                                                       |
| Retire an address/inbox           | Review active bindings, early/held input, old replies and pinned send/reconciliation dependencies; stop new use with clear outside cleanup. No automatic closure or retirement autoresponder. |
| Incoming path fails               | Show current known failure and its receiving owner action. Distinguish failure to observe a test from proven routing failure. Preserve accepted source and safe draft/read work.              |
| Sending fails but receiving works | Show that distinction; incoming mail remains accountable, while actual outgoing sends follow P6 gating/recovery.                                                                              |
| Pause an inbox                    | Explain what ordinary processing is paused and that external SMTP/forwarding can continue. Do not disconnect all tenant Resend or erase work.                                                 |
| Rotate or revoke a credential     | Owner-managed protected operation, current proof and bounded event overlap; compromise treats the actual Full-access scope honestly. No keys in support messages.                             |
| Provider/domain migration         | New qualified connection/route generation with owner impact review; old effects reconcile in their original account. No silent transfer/replay.                                               |
| Reconnect/restore                 | Recheck current authority and only affected proof, preserve history/received-at/expiry and never resurrect an old route or purged content.                                                    |

Where the exact source/body cannot be recovered within actual provider availability, state that limitation and retain appropriate body-free evidence. Do not ask requesters to resend as the standard recovery mechanism or imply Asym captured upstream messages that never reached its custody.

### REQ26-D25-C005 — Accessibility and validation

Use Core's exact base-maia/Base UI components, semantic tokens, typography and responsive layout. The initial cards act as an accessible single-choice group, with names and descriptions available to screen readers. Labels explain public address versus internal target. Focus returns correctly after external settings/navigation; long addresses/DNS values remain distinguishable under zoom. Error summaries link to affected fields, valid input remains, and async results are announced politely once rather than every polling tick. A persistent blocker cannot exist only in a toast.

No hover-only help, color-only readiness, automatic advancing on test arrival, clipboard-only access, arbitrary protocol syntax in the first screen, AI setup assistant or complex animation is needed. Keyboard, touch and desktop/mobile administrators receive the same declared operation. Safe low-bandwidth recovery does not weaken verification or silently activate when connectivity returns.

P01–P50 require actual both-path/new-and-existing-tenant/operator-split/negative-case/AT/provider tests before activation. P17's existing staff-proof discipline should be reused where applicable, not replaced by a polished mockup or an invented universal success rate.

### REQ26-D25-C007 — Source-of-truth map

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact                                                                                     | Authoritative owner                                                        | Consumer and invariant                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tenant/account/environment identity and current actor/capabilities                       | Core identity/authorization and shared connection owner                    | A message header, domain suffix or caller-supplied tenant never selects authority.                                           |
| Resend tenant account, outbound Sending-access credential, provider submissions/evidence | P6/P17 shared `tenant_email_settings` aggregate and protected revisions    | Existing outgoing rules unchanged; receiving does not create another outbound key path.                                      |
| Receiving credential and receiving capability proof                                      | Additional purpose-separated facet under that same shared connection owner | Current provider Full-access key is confined to closed server receiving/proof reads; no false read-only claim.               |
| Signed provider ingress                                                                  | Shared opaque per-connection ingress                                       | Verify raw bytes first; registered receiving events go to P26, outbound evidence to P6; preserve subscription union.         |
| Candidate/active public address to inbox binding and operational activation              | P26 Support configuration owner                                            | Current exact tenant/account/environment/source-scoped binding; activation is not provider acceptance or mailbox identity.   |
| Public-destination access/managed-return proof acceptance and Reply-To revision          | Existing P17 Human reply destination owner                                 | External challenge or explicitly added managed Support proof, never mutual substitution by self-received code.               |
| Receiving source, hydration, setup verification custody and held ordinary input          | Existing intake/source/recovery owners with narrow candidate purpose       | One accepted source, durable disposition and finite lifetime; no normal Support/CRM side effects before qualified admission. |
| Default Sender, real From/Reply-To, signature, reusable wording and preparation          | P17 with D4/D18/D23/D24 purpose contracts                                  | Setup reads/selects qualified owner references; no raw body/header override or implicit global-default change.               |
| CRM Party/relationships, giving, missionary/care records                                 | Their actual Core domains                                                  | No setup/verification-created Party/history/action; read and later mutations require own authority.                          |
| DNS/mailbox forwarding and external copies                                               | Tenant mail administrator/provider, with captured bounded proof in Core    | An Asym state change cannot claim to undo external DNS, synchronize outside replies or delete outside copies.                |
| Health/progress/counts                                                                   | Current authorized projection of those facts                               | Replaceable and scoped; never activation, access or completeness authority.                                                  |

### REQ26-D25-C008 — Three necessary governing amendments

**Receiving credential purpose.** ADR0029/P6 and P17's connection description must distinguish the outgoing-only instantiable key rule from the new P26 receiving purpose. Resend currently exposes only Full access for non-send reads; OAuth does not narrow that. The permanent current-provider design uses a separate inbound key, same exact tenant account, existing managed envelope encryption and current revision/rotation/revocation/purge controls. No Full-access key is accepted as the outgoing credential. Full access still creates a whole-account compromise blast radius at Resend; a local read allowlist reduces app exposure but cannot revoke provider privileges. Security review must test isolation and whole-account incident response.

The read adapter accepts only closed owner operations for exact allowed received-email/raw/attachment retrieval, bounded recovery listing and required registered account/domain/webhook/canary proof. No client-chosen URL, method or arbitrary provider resource ID. Account proof can use exact immutable current provider object evidence already bound to the connection, plus the existing controlled canary where needed; a repair does not always need a new ordinary outbound send. A pending unproved key is restricted to bounded account-proof reads; it cannot retrieve or expose ordinary incoming bodies/files before account mapping succeeds. Positive/wrong-account behavior must be qualified in the actual pinned API. A label, hint or DNS record alone does not prove the key's account.

**Shared ingress.** P17's described event ingress is extended to deliver registered incoming event kinds to P26 after exact shared authentication. Its outbound reducer retains the rule that incoming events create no outgoing lifecycle transition. One endpoint can serve the connection's required event union; this avoids a new endpoint per inbox, provider-plan coupling and duplicate secrets. Independent business owners retain incoming receipt idempotency and outgoing attempt evidence. The shared connection's observed health can affect both facets without collapsing them into one readiness flag.

**Managed Support destination proof.** Extend the existing P17 Human reply destination's exclusive proof shape with a managed Support route variant. P26 produces current tenant/account/environment/domain/public-address/inbox-binding/generation and controlled new-mail/return-path evidence. The same qualified stepped-up reply manager accepts the exact destination revision and accountable monitoring responsibility. P17 owns acceptance and pinned reply identity, not capture/threading/intake health. External-mailbox access challenges still require the same initiating authorized human and their code remains excluded from Support. Merely seeing Asym's own challenge in an inbound queue cannot satisfy that proof.

These amendments introduce no new configurable reply purpose, catalog template, OAuth platform, credential store or CRM owner. They must be traced into the existing system ADR/OpenSpec/P17/P6 artifacts only in a implementation specification stage; the exploratory ADR records the required changes now without silently editing governing history.

### REQ26-D25-C009 — Break the setup/readiness cycle deliberately

A candidate endpoint can be **registered and capture-capable** while its inbox is **not active for ordinary work**. Narrow setup custody exists before the user changes external forwarding or receiving DNS. The fixed P17/P6 qualification producer can use exact candidate sender/Reply-To/credential state only for its controlled inert proof operation and an approved real sink/control mailbox. This is the existing testing capability extended for managed return-path proof, not an arbitrary sender or production override.

An external person/control mailbox may supply the required new message and reply to the canary. Do not create a new automated platform outbound account to make the loop convenient. Freeze exact proof mode, target, candidate generation, content and expected evidence before I/O. A status poll sends nothing. A timeout after possible submission reconciles the same sealed intent and may remain unknown; it cannot send a replacement just because the screen was reopened.

Keep separate:

1. P17 external-mailbox access challenge — current initiating stepped-up human; nontransferable completion; codes excluded from Support.
2. External provider forwarding confirmation — inspectable only through the exact authorized bounded setup task, inert until deliberate qualified action, no generic trusted-sender bypass.
3. Controlled route/canary evidence — verifies the exact candidate path and expected actual source, not ownership of a human identity.
4. Real early mail — finite current source custody/classification with no setup-token shortcut into normal work.

### REQ26-D25-C010 — Data dimensions and impossible states

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Concept                      | Required fields/constraints in the actual owner model                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Candidate setup              | Tenant/account/environment, intended inbox, selected path, public address/receiving target references, safe incomplete fields, expected candidate generation, actual creator/change actors. No direct Active flag or secret body field.                               |
| Current address binding      | Exact receiving authority/public destination and one authorized current inbox, active revision/generation, proof references, lifecycle and predecessor/successor lineage. No uniqueness-error redirect.                                                               |
| Proof attempt/observation    | Exact tenant/principal/purpose/candidate/connection/domain/address generations, issuance/expiry, expected source/evidence shape, outcome and safe immutable evidence reference. Terminal fact corrected by explicit supersession, not rewritten.                      |
| Receiving secret revision    | Purpose-separated protected material under shared managed cryptography, exact scope/account/environment/revision binding and current use/retirement/purge/revocation/restore facts. No raw client export.                                                             |
| Accepted incoming source     | Provider/account/environment receipt identity, original timestamps, current candidate/active-routing basis, classification, hydration state, finite expiry and exactly one recoverable disposition/continuation. No duplicate row solely for webhook secret rotation. |
| Setup traffic classification | Actual constrained expected attempt association, never just subject/from-string matching. No general code/body log or automatic normal Support admission.                                                                                                             |
| Mutation receipt             | Trusted current actor, immutable semantic input identity/hash, expected and actual revisions, authoritative outcome and required durable continuation/audit. Changed input cannot replay under same identity.                                                         |

Use composite tenant/account/environment-aware foreign keys and unique constraints rather than globally existing IDs. One physical receiving authority cannot be claimed by two tenants/environments through separate local records; provider-account isolation and the shared authority registry must agree. A tenant can bind multiple separately qualified public addresses to one inbox. Exact address/domain-default overlaps require the current owning routing contract; setup does not silently create a domain default or capture unrelated addresses. Current source conflicts must resolve explicitly instead of precedence winning by array order.

Keep creation attribution immutable; append actual current change actor rather than overwrite `created_by`. Separate create/update/replace so a missing update target cannot be recreated by upsert. Configure safe delete behavior: no cascade removes accepted source, required proof/history or old sealed effect evidence. No new money representation exists. Enforce nullability/state/purpose consistency and finite input dimensions in database constraints and the single typed mutation boundary, not UI convention.

### REQ26-D25-C011 — Conditional transitions and atomic effects

Lifecycle is not a giant state that encodes every provider condition. Candidate/configuration lifecycle, evidence readiness, actual inbox activation, credential health and source custody remain separate. The visible status is derived from their current meaning. Two administrators use expected revisions; a concurrent proof invalidation, route claim or permission loss defeats stale activation. Save or provider 2xx alone never installs an ordinary active binding.

One local guarded transaction validates final resulting authority, claims the current proof/candidate generation and commits active binding, change history and durable reconciliation/secondary-effect intent. Provider/DNS mutation is outside that transaction and retains its own exact operation identity/uncertainty. Intake admission/release similarly resolves each source only with its correct durable continuation/effect, not by marking a batch resolved before dispatch. No compensation loop over independent writes is the permanent design.

Svix delivery IDs, provider inbound message IDs, RFC Message-IDs, candidate generations and business command identities are distinct. Deduplicate raw-event delivery under verified endpoint/account scope and accepted source under stable provider-account/receipt scope so secret overlap/replay cannot duplicate mail. Preserve multiple pieces of evidence when one raw source reaches an intended multiple-recipient situation without inventing arbitrary recipient-union authority. Thread tokens correlate only within current trusted scope and never override contradictory destination evidence.

### REQ26-D25-C012 — Safe capture and complete acquisition

Tenant scope comes from the registered signed connection, never payload tags or recipient-domain matching. Within scope, qualify actual provider/trusted-hop recipient provenance before automatic routing. Current Resend `received_for` is documented as derived from Received `for` clauses; it is not inherently an SMTP-envelope attestation. Ordered duplicate-preserving raw headers may be required to distinguish provider-added evidence from caller content. A JSON header dictionary cannot prove ordering or multiplicity. Neither SPF/DKIM pass nor a signed webhook proves requester identity or benign content.

Parse/validate the pinned API response: matching provider ID, expected field types/size, actual HTML format and complete attachment pagination. The current successful `{}` response behavior must fail as incomplete; absence of text/HTML can still be legitimate attachment-only input. Do not inline uncontrolled base64 assets or fetch arbitrary URLs. Hydrate raw/attachment signed URLs only from qualified current owner responses under approved hosts/redirect/size/type limits, with current expiry and safe retry/refresh. Provider copies/availability and Asym source retention are distinct.

List/filter pending sources in the database before pagination, with deterministic cursor progress and current eligibility per batch. A failed query, missing page or unknown hydration is incomplete, not zero or completed. Activation/reconnect preserves original received-at, source expiry and D13/D14 timing; verification does not generate targets or reset a backlog's usefulness. Never make a requester resubmit the standard solution to an intake outage.

### REQ26-D25-C013 — Current authorization and least exposure

Support configuration can view safe status without raw incoming bodies; an IT helper can apply public DNS/forwarding instructions without donor/CRM access. Reading a confirmation is a constrained source/purpose operation, not general access to a setup mailbox. P17 acceptance keeps its real step-up and actor restrictions. Active tenant membership and current resource capabilities are rechecked in every server/worker path; cached UI state or prior setup invitation cannot authorize later effects.

Inspect table/column grants, all effective RLS USING/WITH CHECK/SELECT rules, permissive policies, service paths, RPC grants/definer search paths, views and storage. The current inbound route tables revoke browser grants and are service-owned; that is a useful base, not proof their commands are safe. PostgreSQL derives WITH CHECK from USING where applicable; missing explicit syntax alone is not a finding. Allowed updates cannot change tenant, purpose, owner, proof actor or destination beyond the reviewed operation. All old global-key/inferred-tenant/route-upsert/import/fixture entry points must be fenced.

### REQ26-D25-C014 — Maintenance and old-route continuity

Path switch/cancel may invalidate a candidate without undoing outside changes. Captured mail retains current finite custody; canceled targets cannot be reassigned across owners while late mail may arrive. Address replacement creates a new qualified binding, preserves the old working path until reviewed cutover, and retains required old reply routes with an explicit finite dependency-aware transition plan. A blanket fixed grace period cannot prove all old prepared messages/conversations have ended; an unbounded hidden alias is equally wrong.

Inbox pause, incoming failure, outgoing failure and tenant connection disconnect are distinct. One inbox's pause/retirement must not delete a shared provider domain/webhook or disable unrelated tenant receipts/security mail. Complete impact review governs shared deletion/disconnect. Credential compromise applies to actual provider Full-access blast radius; local read isolation does not make its theft harmless. Rotation/reconnect uses current exact account proof and bounded overlap, preserves old source/effect identity and never relabels old receipts into a new tenant/account.

Capture signing secrets at creation/rotation under owner custody rather than making custody depend on later provider availability. Current direct API/CLI documentation describes webhook reads as including the signing secret; scrub those fields before any ordinary status response, log or evidence projection. Earlier contradictory search text was stale and is not current authority. Ambiguous external changes reconcile before retry; retired/purged authority cannot reappear through database restore or old code.

Qualified exact-object reads may recover interrupted creation/rotation under current owner authority with proven intended object/revision and protected recapture. They are not a general secret browser or permission to adopt a different operation's key. If exact correlation is unavailable, preserve incomplete state and prior safe operation instead of blind create/rotate retry.

### REQ26-D25-C015 — Email Studio, CRM, retention and operational proof

Email Studio owns existing content, signature/profile/Reply destination acceptance and preparation. It does not own DNS, receiving, forwarding, credential administration or held-message routing. Setup references qualified content, previews actual public identity and returns to the same source editor where appropriate. Fixed qualification traffic has no tenant-editable template key; D13 Support request received remains a distinct true system message and never acknowledges setup challenges. No new Role Layout, raw HTML authority, Tiptap DNS form or direct provider sender is introduced.

CRM context consumes only actual authorized admitted correspondence and source links. No setup contact, fake donor, mailbox-derived Party authority, financial action or care-state update. Distinct requesters/participants/responders/administrators/represented organizations keep their identity model. Source restriction/redaction/expiry applies to known derivatives before serving; setup/Recent/provider fetch cannot reconstruct purged content. Verification secret retention is shorter and more restricted than reusable configuration evidence; every source keeps its actual finite owning purpose.

P6 shared rate/quota/reputation and provider plan constraints remain tenant-account facts across sending and receiving keys. Register bounded operations and complete resumable processing; do not poll/hydrate whole mailboxes on each setup page load. Observe known evidence, current impact and one owner repair action with safe identifiers. O01–O06 in the main review define concrete triggers and responses, not a new observability platform.

### REQ26-D25-C017 — One product journey across distinct owners

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Fact or action                                                                                            | Authoritative owner                                 | Support Hub's role                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tenant Resend account, encrypted credential revisions, provider registration and delivery evidence        | Shared P6/P17 connection owner                      | Consume exact qualified references and purpose-scoped capabilities.                                                                                     |
| Receiving candidate, qualified address-to-inbox binding, activation, safe early intake and reconciliation | P26 receiving/configuration owner                   | Present the two equal setup guides and manage Support handling through current authorized commands.                                                     |
| Actual From, Reply-To acceptance and sender defaults                                                      | P17 identity/destination owners                     | Show actual values; select qualified references; never equate public incoming address with From or silently replace tenant defaults.                    |
| Canonical reusable wording, signature sources, approved versions, presentation and immutable preparation  | Email Studio/P17, including D4/D18/D23/D24          | Show contextual previews and eligible selectors. Support's Tiptap reply draft is the current human-authored instance, not a second shared source store. |
| Human reply/work admission                                                                                | Support with the qualified P17 preparation contract | Commit the exact authorized reply and permitted work effects once, then hand off durable sending intent.                                                |
| Transport and externally observed outcomes                                                                | P6 tenant Resend adapter                            | Display authoritative delivery/recovery state; never infer success from setup or draft save.                                                            |
| CRM identities, relationships, giving and care records                                                    | Their respective Core domains                       | Permission-aware contextual navigation and separately authorized actions; setup verification creates no Party or business interaction.                  |

Setup lives in Support inbox settings, with contextual return from shared integrations and Email Studio. It is not a second credential console or template catalog. Plain fields handle addresses, DNS records and setup instructions; Tiptap serves the accepted reply, note, wording and signature content surfaces. No secret or verification code enters reusable content, private reply drafts, browser persistence, search or ordinary Support history.

### REQ26-D25-C018 — 1. Receiving-purpose credentials under the same connection

P17's existing outgoing Sending-access key remains purpose-limited and domain restricted. D25 adds a separate inbound credential facet to the same tenant connection, with the same protected custody, revision, rotation, revocation and destruction controls. This is an explicit amendment to an outgoing-only key description, not evidence that that description already covered receiving.

Current Resend API-key and OAuth documentation offer Full access for the required non-send reads. The receiving key therefore has provider-level **Full access**. Asym's closed server read allowlist limits its own use; it does not turn that key into a provider-enforced read-only credential. Same-account proof must use exact current registered objects/canary evidence, not labels, hints or incoming metadata. An unproved candidate can perform only bounded account-proof reads before ordinary body or attachment retrieval. No generic HTTP proxy, Support-visible secret, outbound adapter use, fallback account or new OAuth product is authorized. The residual whole-account compromise risk remains explicit and must be qualified through the owner's actual security/incident proof. Resend API-key permissions, OAuth scopes.

### REQ26-D25-C019 — 2. Shared authenticated ingress with owner dispatch

The registered opaque connection endpoint establishes tenant/account/environment and authenticates exact raw bytes before destination parsing. It dispatches registered receiving events to P26 and outbound evidence to P6. Receiving events do not acquire outbound-reducer semantics. Registration changes preserve the required subscription union and stable business deduplication across secret rotation; a webhook per inbox is unnecessary.

Message headers remain untrusted facts inside an authenticated provider event. In particular, header-derived `received_for` does not establish independent SMTP-envelope authority. Exact destination/source qualification is a release gate, with restricted recovery for insufficient or contradictory evidence. Neither Email Studio wording nor CRM matching determines routing authority. Resend received-email representation.

### REQ26-D25-C020 — 3. Managed Support destination proof within P17

P17 retains ownership of Human reply destination acceptance. D25 adds a typed managed Support route proof variant: exact tenant/account/environment/domain/public address/inbox binding/configuration generation, qualified new-mail and reply-return behavior, accountable monitoring and current authority. P26 produces the evidence; the current authorized, stepped-up P17 manager accepts and pins it. Existing external-mailbox challenges retain their same-initiating-actor rule and protected code handling. Receiving Asym's own challenge cannot self-verify an external mailbox.

Candidate capture and a fixed, inert qualification canary through the existing P17/P6 controlled real-sink path can work in Testing before ordinary inbox activation. This breaks the otherwise circular demand to activate before testing the return path. It does not allow arbitrary test messages, a tenant-editable verification template, a platform sending fallback or ordinary customer mail. A real external controlled mailbox can originate and answer the qualification exchange. Exact provider/account and current-authority proof remains mandatory.

Accepting one inbox destination is not a hidden update of the global Human replies default. Any owner-level default change remains a separate explicit operation with visible impact.

### REQ26-D25-C021 — Complete use and maintenance sequence

1. Staff chooses an existing public address or a new dedicated address with equal prominence and no preselection. Draft save preserves progress without activation.
2. Shared connection owners qualify current receiving credentials and registered ingress. Support establishes safe candidate custody before external forwarding/DNS instructions can cause arrivals.
3. The email administrator performs the applicable outside change; protected provider confirmation and P17 destination proof remain distinct. A completed DNS check alone is insufficient.
4. Testing qualifies new intake and reply return through current exact bindings. Real early messages remain separate from verification traffic with original receipt time, finite custody and no acknowledgement/CRM/work effects before admission.
5. Review shows public incoming address, actual From, Reply-To, managed signature, handling and current readiness separately. Conditional activation records binding, audit and durable continuation together.
6. Real admitted correspondence uses ordinary Support/Tiptap, D18 wording, D23 signatures and D24 shortcuts. P17 prepares; Support admits; P6 dispatches and reconciles. Setup is not a new message-preparation or delivery path.
7. Change, repair, pause, rotation, retirement and restoration preserve exact admitted identities and finite old-return dependencies. Changing a source or signature never rewrites prepared/sent correspondence. Canceling setup does not claim to reverse external forwarding or DNS, discard accepted input, or delete outside copies.

### REQ26-D25-C022 — Secret recovery and evidence correction

The immutable official CLI README at commit 0155104, line 502 confirms that current webhook GET output is secret-bearing. Earlier contrary search-excerpt interpretation was corrected before this ratification and must not be restored. Capture creation/rotation responses under protected custody; scrub read responses too. A qualified exact-object GET may recover an interrupted owner operation with current authority and correct object/revision proof. This is not a general secret browser, nor a promise of indefinite provider recovery.

### REQ26-D25-C023 — Accepted experience and authority

The initial Use an existing Support address and Create a new Support address choices have equal prominence with no preselection. Both use the already-scoped qualified forwarding/dedicated receiving product. Safe incomplete drafts, contextual IT handoff and return, exact current proof, readable status, actual recipient-facing identity preview and conditional activation are accepted. Keeping a public incoming address does not promise that it can be the outgoing From. No mailbox synchronization/history import, alternate CRM, telephony, help-center, AI or generic mail-management platform is introduced.

Candidate custody must work before outside forwarding/DNS can cause arrivals. P17 external-mailbox challenges, provider forwarding confirmations, controlled qualification mail and real early messages have distinct authority and finite custody. Verification never becomes ordinary Support/CRM/acknowledgement/target traffic. Activation reconciles actual eligible early mail with original receipt/retention/utility/obligation meaning. Cancel does not undo outside changes or discard accepted input.

Exact tenant/account/environment comes from the registered authenticated connection before message parsing, not sender/recipient domains or metadata. Header-derived received_for is not independent SMTP-envelope proof. Qualified exact-source address bindings, trusted actors, immutable creator evidence, current generation/capabilities, old/new-row authorization and all writer fences govern one atomic local activation/history/continuation boundary. Provider/DNS effects remain separately evidenced. Partial pages, failed queries and unknown results cannot become complete/zero/verified.

Replacement qualifies before changing a prior good route; old reply lineage and pinned effect dependencies have finite controlled transition. Inbox pause, receiving availability, outside SMTP reception and tenant connection shutdown are distinct. Repair/rotation/retirement/restore preserve current authority, exact old effect identity, finite custody and purge barriers. CRM/giving/care actions stay with their actual owners; setup creates no fake Party or business history.

### REQ26-D25-C024 — All three Email Studio and shared-owner amendments are accepted

The explicit integration record and independent seam review document the complete accepted boundary.

1. Add a separate receiving-purpose credential facet under the same P6/P17 tenant Resend connection and protected revision/custody controls. Preserve the outgoing domain-restricted Sending-access key. The current receiving key has provider Full access, honestly disclosed; a closed server read allowlist is not provider-enforced read-only permission. Unproved keys perform only bounded account-proof reads before ordinary hydration; same-account/wrong-account qualification and whole-account incident response remain mandatory.
