No OAuth product or global fallback is added.
2. Extend the shared opaque signed ingress to dispatch registered receiving events to P26 after exact raw-body authentication and scope selection. Preserve outgoing reducer authority and required subscription union, distinct business dedupe and rotation semantics. No endpoint per inbox or metadata-selected tenant.
3. Add managed Support route proof to the existing P17 Human reply destination owner. P26 supplies exact current source/binding/generation/return-path/monitoring evidence; the current stepped-up P17 manager accepts/pins it. Existing external-mailbox challenges cannot self-complete from Asym's own received code. Candidate-only capture and fixed inert P17/P6 canary qualification with an approved real control mailbox/sink work before ordinary activation, without an arbitrary mailer or platform sending fallback. New inbox binding does not silently replace a global default.

Email Studio keeps canonical wording, signatures, approved versions, presentation, identity acceptance and preparation. Support keeps inbox intake/work and human admission; P6 keeps transport/provider outcomes. D18/D23/D24 remain intact. No new editable verification template key, source-body store, per-inbox Role Layout, provider-template mirror or direct sending path is created. Simple setup inputs are not rich-text documents; Tiptap remains the accepted content editor where appropriate.

The original source correction is ratified too: immutable Resend CLI README0155104 physical line502 confirms webhook GET is secret-bearing. Protected creation/rotation capture and scrubbed reads are required; qualified exact-object read recovery is allowed under current object/revision/owner proof. Do not restore the earlier stale-excerpt contradiction or promise indefinite provider recovery.

### REQ26-D25-C025 — Accepted sequence and evidence limits

The three owner amendments are now settled decisions, to be propagated explicitly at the implementation governing/specification stage. Establish shared credential/ingress/proof/custody boundaries and guarded primitives, then both setup/maintenance guides and the fixed qualification producer, then exact activation/reconciliation and legacy fences, then applicable P01–P50 actual release proof. O01–O06 monitors residual faults after prevention.

## D25 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D25-O01

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed wrong-tenant/account/environment disclosure, routing effect or forged proof accepted.

**Owner:** Core security/identity and P6 ingress owner.

**Response:** Fence affected scope, retain minimal incident evidence, repair authoritative mapping/derivatives and requalify before reopening.

### OP26-D25-O02

**Signal and threshold:** One known accepted input without durable disposition/continuation, one missed eligible resume item or one DB error shown as zero/complete.

**Owner:** P26 intake/recovery owner.

**Response:** Stop false completion, preserve custody, repair complete scoped reconciliation and account for every affected original.

### OP26-D25-O03

**Signal and threshold:** First authoritative credential/domain/webhook/route proof failure or stale proof used for activation.

**Owner:** Tenant delivery administrator with P6/P17 owner.

**Response:** Block affected new effects, show exact impact/repair, preserve safe intake/history and requalify only affected evidence.

### OP26-D25-O04

**Signal and threshold:** One double activation/conflict overwrite/creator rewrite or lost-acknowledgement duplicate effect.

**Owner:** Support configuration/API data owner.

**Response:** Fence faulty writer, reconcile exact current command/generation, restore correct mapping with audited correction rather than replay.

### OP26-D25-O05

**Signal and threshold:** First breach of registered resource/rate/cleanup/material deadline or incomplete backlog represented as finished.

**Owner:** P6 operations and P26 records/recovery owner.

**Response:** Apply owner backpressure, report incomplete state, recover before actual expiry where possible and record irrecoverable limits without fabricating data.

### OP26-D25-O06

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed setup action that unintentionally changes outside mail routing, broadens unrelated scope, loses user work or makes verification inaccessible.

**Owner:** Support UX owner and responsible tenant mail administrator.

**Response:** Stop affected guide/action, preserve current work/custody, correct the flow and repeat the affected staff/AT/permission journey before release.

### REQ26-D25-C026 — Operating and qualification sequence

These controls monitor residual faults after prevention; they do not defer known correctness gaps.

## D26 — Binding requirements

### REQ26-D26-R01 — Bounded new origin, one canonical work record

Allow deliberate staff recording of a received phone/in-person request needing continuing Support handling. Extend the staff-created/no-native-mail model explicitly; D12's required incoming-email trigger does not already authorize this origin. Reuse the same canonical conversation identity, D3 work states and owning commands. No second ticket, generic call log, automatic all-calls intake, telephony, audio recording, transcription, SMS/chat, device-offline synchronization or AI is added. Updates to existing work use that work; ordinary relationship cultivation, general tasks and restricted care retain their owners.

### REQ26-D26-R02 — Every applicable CRM record has complete Support access

Apply D9 discovery to all accepted origins and work states. For each requested Party, select active explicit relevance OR independently qualified actual correspondence, apply current joint visibility, then deduplicate by tenant/current D10 conversation root before counting or paging. Both reasons may justify one row. No mandatory Party, primary link, household/organization/beneficiary fan-out or inferred linkage from a phone/name/email match. Unlinked work remains valid and serviceable in Support with a clear No linked CRM record state; it becomes discoverable on a Party after a qualified association, not before. “Every” means every applicable authorized record through the complete view, not every tenant record on every Party.

### REQ26-D26-R03 — Distinguish the people and authoritative facts

The staff recorder, person who reported the request, requester, represented person/organization, observed contact endpoint, CRM Party, assigned worker and CRM owner remain separate meanings. A reported name or callback number is unverified Support context, not a new authoritative contact or proof of identity/representation. Resolve the actual actor through trusted Auth/profile/tenant membership/Support identity; do not derive authorship from an email match, current assignee or caller-supplied author field. CRM contact corrections and consequential giving/care actions use the owning domain's current permissions, validation and approvals.

### REQ26-D26-R04 — Support-first entry without a forced CRM detour

Use **Record a request** in the normal Support entry area, distinct from Send email and D12 Create related conversation. Preserve tenant and any currently suitable inbox context. A focused form captures the request, Phone/In person source, responsible inbox and optional known context. Show existing relevant work when it is already discoverable within current authority; do not force an exhaustive CRM search or disclose inaccessible matches. Related records are optional peers. No fake email, placeholder Party or automatic Create contact shortcut is needed to unlock Save.

### REQ26-D26-R05 — CRM-first entry is the same command with reviewed context

The CRM Overview/Communications Support section offers **Record a request** only where both creation and current Party-reference permissions allow it. Open the same form with the current Party visibly staged as a removable Related record and the originating return context preserved. From an actual encounter record, also stage its exact permitted reference; never copy the whole activity body or secretly broaden relevance. Admit the request and all reviewed links together. If a link/source becomes invalid, reject preserving permitted input or offer an explicit revised Create without that link; no silent partial success that leaves the request missing from the originating CRM record. No caller URL parameter is authority.

### REQ26-D26-R06 — Small form, truthful saving and private drafts

Use the D23-qualified Tiptap staff-context profile for a concise brief, with ordinary inputs for short title/source/inbox and shared D9 selectors for context. Allow authorized existing-source reuse without requiring the person to retype it; any new brief states the Support need, not a second authoritative encounter transcript. Optional occurrence details stay collapsed until needed. The primary action is **Record request**, with **No email will be sent to the requester** nearby. Cancel before admission has no work effect. Finite actor/tenant-scoped draft custody uses existing Support draft primitives; no raw browser-local permanent archive, ambient submit shortcut or automatic admission on blur. Unknown save outcomes reconcile the same operation before Saved is shown. Changes of tenant, permission or entry context cannot silently retarget an unsaved draft.

### REQ26-D26-R07 — Open work with deliberate, qualified handling

Creation starts D3 Open: the request needs attention now. Use an explicitly chosen/currently qualified inbox; Shared handling is the default for a new standalone request, with an ordinary visible choice of eligible team/person/Assign to me. Do not silently assign the recorder, follow on their behalf, inherit another conversation's handler or run D6 automatic first-email routing. Optional follow-up reminders are deliberate D3 choices, not copied from a CRM task or source call. Respect D7/D8 eligibility and review controls. Invalid staged handling produces an actionable correction rather than a silent fallback. Existing owner tasks are referenced or bound through D11 when needed, not duplicated automatically. Existing qualified staff assignment/attention notifications retain D12/P6's actual source, recipient, preference and delivery rules; no new requester notice or all-team blast is introduced, and optional staff-email failure cannot block manual work admission.

### REQ26-D26-R08 — Manual handling and email readiness are independent

Manual admission needs the inbox's current work acceptance, classification, accountable handling and actor authorization. It does not require a public email address, qualified MX route, receiving credential or P17 sender. The same inbox can accept qualified manual work while its email path is not ready; no third email-setup branch or new provider product is implied. Archived/retired work scope cannot receive new work; an email-only pause does not itself prohibit an otherwise authorized manual action. Conversely manual admission cannot activate receiving, bypass D19 email review or authorize outgoing mail. D25 email configuration and actual P17/P6 readiness remain independently visible and enforced.

An authorized inbox manager can establish a named Support work inbox with its required access/coverage before or without configuring email. If no eligible inbox exists, Record a request offers contextual inbox setup or a safe administrator handoff while preserving its permitted draft. **Configure email** is a separate action using D25's same two equal paths. This explicitly extends D25's email-first Add inbox assumption; it adds no third receiving method. Qualify current mail-shaped inbox schema/DTOs so manual-ready work requires no dummy inbound/From/Reply-To address, and an undifferentiated active flag cannot confer mail readiness.

### REQ26-D26-R09 — Truthful staff source and absent native correspondence

Admit one typed staff-recorded source/brief with stable origin identity and protected provenance. Show **Recorded by [staff] · Phone/In person** as staff context, never a caller-message bubble, claimed transcript or fabricated provider receipt. Native first/last incoming/external message times and direction remain absent, native message counts zero, until real correspondence exists. The request title is staff-authored content, not an email subject until an actual outgoing subject is reviewed. Qualify schema, DTOs, validators, lists, search, exports, reports, automation guards and legacy readers together; no `now()` or literal `"null"` fallback manufactures a message/contact. Origin stays stable after later email occurs.

### REQ26-D26-R10 — Recorded time and reported occurrence are different clocks

Trusted admission records who saved and when, in UTC with original precision, and cannot be backdated by the caller. Optional when-received information is separately marked staff-reported, with its supplied precision and timezone meaning. A date-only or unknown time must not become invented midnight or verified provider time; future encounter claims are rejected/corrected rather than creating a scheduled intake. Editing reported details is an attributable correction, never a rewrite of recording time, service target, audit occurrence or financial evidence. Display localized dates and relevant zones; record ordering and retention use their stated trusted clocks.

### REQ26-D26-R11 — One source fact, references rather than duplicate encounter bodies

Support owns the request brief/work; an independently recorded CRM/relationship encounter stays with its actual owner. Reference that exact source under a closed typed owner contract and joint source permissions. Do not turn the current legacy `donor_activities` table, a generic timeline row, `contact_ref` JSON or a polymorphic free-form ID into a new shared interaction authority. Support-first capture may later be exposed through qualified Support projections; it is not mirrored into a second editable CRM call note. A minimized Support brief can describe the distinct unresolved need while referencing the source, but cannot copy restricted source material or create a retention escape. No generic encounter platform or Phase28-wide dependency is required for this narrow capability.

### REQ26-D26-R12 — CRM placement and a complete, quiet list

Preserve D9's separate Support conversations section; the existing financial “support” summary is not this feature. Overview retains up to three currently accessible unfinished conversations and a visible View conversations link, including when the preview is empty. Communications → Support conversations is a complete permission-filtered paginated view, default Unfinished with an obvious All option for resolved/history. Include manual and email origins without requiring a P6 event. Show permitted title, work status, handling, current inbox and provenance; no stored transcript excerpts are required. Denied/hidden rows contribute no count or locked-card hint. Loading, empty, unavailable and content-expired are distinct authorized states.

### REQ26-D26-R13 — Narrow zero-message ordering amendment

For a conversation with real external correspondence, retain D9's latest actual external-message occurrence and stable canonical-ID tie-break. For staff-created work with no native external correspondence, use its original trusted recorded/created time as the explicit fallback, label it **Recorded**, and show **No email yet** where helpful. Never call that Last message. This narrowly extends D9 for manual and existing D12 staff-origin work; it is not generic last-activity ordering. Notes, link changes, labels, assignment, read time and provider callbacks do not move the row as new correspondence. Reported call time cannot game recency. If historical creation evidence is unknown, preserve an explicitly unknown sortable class, not `now`.

### REQ26-D26-R14 — View and work inline through the same Support detail

A CRM row opens the same canonical Support detail within the shared record/navigation shell when space permits; narrow screens and direct/refresh links have an ordinary full-page route. Provide Open in Support Hub and contextual return without losing permitted list filters/scroll/selection or the user's separate private draft. Avoid stacked modal editors. Reuse the actual Support thread/source cards, qualified attachments, notes, collision protection, assignment, work controls and reply composer; no reduced copied transcript or second CRM reply/resolve endpoint. Current read-only/action permissions are known before edit, rechecked at command admission, and explained without exposing protected targets. CRM and Support failure/loading boundaries remain independent.

### REQ26-D26-R15 — Joint permissions precede all content and discovery

Enforce current tenant, Party reference/read, Support conversation/source and field/classification policy before rows, counts, previews, snippets, attachments, search, export, prefetch, streams or mutations. An inbox assignment, relevance association or conversation participant never grants CRM, giving, missionary or care access. Apply the same policy to both entry points, deep links, cached responses and privileged workers; never use a connector administrator's viewing lens. Current capabilities govern edits, not a broad staff role or stale JWT alone. On access loss, remove forbidden content/drafts from the visible context through existing policy while retaining only safe recovery/navigation; no revealing “one hidden request” badge.

### REQ26-D26-R16 — Actual CRM history remains actual history

Manual recording, context links and inline viewing create no requester-correspondence/P6 email event, ordinary copied CRM Activity marker, note or last-contact update. Independently qualified staff attention retains its actual producer, recipient, template, P6 event and optional-email dedupe contract; it is not a conversation message from the requester. D9's Support summary supplies discovery independently of actual Communication history. Real later correspondence uses P6's existing source/member evidence and one read-composed CRM timeline with dedupe and qualified attribution. Existing independent encounter history remains visible only through its owner. Record Support creation/correction/link outcomes in the qualified Support business/audit history; no duplicate authoritative timeline store or bidirectional Support↔CRM synchronization.

### REQ26-D26-R17 — Later email is a deliberate first-thread operation

Reuse D12's explicit Start email thread semantics with a new manual-origin recipient path: there is no incoming trigger from which to infer recipients. Staff deliberately selects a qualified endpoint under current contactability and disclosure rules; optional authorized CRM lookup is convenience, not identity proof or automatic Related-Parties expansion. Preserve D2 reviewed audience, real new lineage, actual From/Reply-To and D23 signature. The internal brief and source attachments are not automatically copied into a public draft. P17 prepares, Support admits and P6 dispatches/reconciles one exact effect. Missing email leaves manual work usable; missing mail readiness yields a clear repair path without losing the request. Uncertain send never becomes a blind new send.

### REQ26-D26-R18 — Work promises and email targets retain their meanings

Manual creation, reported phone occurrence, a note or a claimed callback does not create/fulfill a D14 email reply target. D3 reminders and actual work promises govern manual follow-up. Preserve D14's existing nuance: a genuinely accepted human Start email thread in a staff-origin original establishes Next for later eligible incoming correspondence. A draft, queued effect or private note establishes no confirmed boundary. Unknown first-send acceptance retains D14-R07/R10's candidate First/Next interpretations and earliest applicable possible deadline, labelled Reply timing needs confirmation; it must not force First or score a success/breach. Definite rejection removes only invalid candidates. Native email receipt and target-age rules continue unchanged when actual mail arrives. Resolve and callback notation do not prove receipt correction, refund, recurring-gift change, contact update, delivery or requester satisfaction.

### REQ26-D26-R19 — Later incoming mail and duplicate work are deliberate

Replies on a real qualified outbound lineage join under existing source routing. A separately arriving new email with no proved lineage must not auto-attach to a manual request based on name, number, subject, recent proximity or current CRM email. Show currently authorized relevant work to support explicit D10 merge or D12 related-work judgment; do not manufacture original-mail provenance. One call may reveal multiple independent needs and two workers may record distinct requests, so content similarity is not an authoritative uniqueness key. Deduplicate retries by durable operation identity, not people or text.

### REQ26-D26-R20 — Correct, cancel and preserve responsibility

Before admission, Cancel discards the draft through its finite custody policy. After admission, edits are current authorized corrections with immutable original actor/time and versioned source availability; an ordinary “Undo save” cannot delete real work. All D12 unused-tracking guards remain: no subsequent independent activity, native/admitted/possibly submitted mail, external/owner effects, active merge participation, additional dependent continuation/referral or protected draft being discarded. Only when those guards pass, extend created-in-error cancellation for a standalone source with the additional requirement that no genuine obligation remains, or the exact remaining work has a durably accepted authorized current home. A legitimately used/completed request cannot be reclassified as created in error merely because nothing remains owed. There is no original email conversation to invent or silently rehome into. Use a distinct non-success ending and protected retirement control with audit; do not inflate solved metrics, destroy source evidence or cancel an independent encounter/task. Otherwise use truthful current work/context correction and retain actionable obligations. Merge/Undo, reopening and later input retain D3/D10 semantics and never revive expired content.

### REQ26-D26-R21 — Links, merges and independent source lifecycle

Use D9's current conditional add/remove/correction/Undo and Party merge/repoint provenance. Linking/unlinking changes relevance only, not recipients or source retention. Removing the sole relevance basis removes the CRM row; independent qualified correspondence keeps one row with its truthful reason. Party merges dedupe discoverability without merging Support work; unmerge uses actual provenance, not today's email. Source deletion/archival/revocation gives a safe unavailable reference, not copied fallback text or a cascade that erases request/work/audit. Keep a qualified owner repair path when an erroneous link becomes unreadable.

### REQ26-D26-R22 — Finite content retention includes the new brief once

Explicitly extend D17's human-content eligibility to the first admitted staff-recorded request brief, using trusted admission as its content occurrence. The brief/title and equivalent JSON/text/HTML/search/draft/attachment derivatives remain Support-owned content with D16 restrictions and D17 finite purpose. Ordinary edits, CRM linking, projection refreshes and backdated occurrence correction do not reset the retention anchor; actual later eligible new notes/replies/input follow D17. Expiry/redaction removes ineligible representations from both surfaces and recovery paths without erasing independently owned CRM/financial evidence. Metadata and history remain only within their own minimal finite purpose; a view or permanent CRM note is not a backup archive.

### REQ26-D26-R23 — Reuse existing search and saved-view semantics

D22 already permits an eligible Staff context brief with zero messages. Add this admitted origin to that existing kind and its current source/visibility/expiry rules, not to a new CRM/phone/AI index. Simple D20 filters and counts use the same complete source-qualified query; no browser filtering of loaded rows. Existing saved predicates retain their defined meaning and version. No broad last-activity filter, source reinterpretation or silent global-search expansion is implied. Ordinary search excludes private drafts, restricted source payloads and expired content; a permitted retained request row is not permission to resurrect its old brief.

### REQ26-D26-R24 — One guarded local admission and durable retry

One Support-owned transaction admits the original work identity, brief/source provenance, current handling/reminder choices, exact reviewed D9 links/source references, audit, durable receipt and required identifier-only invalidation/outbox intent. Recheck current authority, canonical targets and relevant revisions at that boundary. A rejected source/link/handling state writes no silent subset. Keep network/provider I/O outside. Use a tenant-scoped durable operation identity and semantic hash covering the reviewed effects; identical retries reconcile the original outcome and latest state separately, changed meaning conflicts. After cancellation/merge/correction, replay cannot resurrect the old request. Current permission also governs receipt reads. Two tabs cannot independently admit one shared draft occurrence twice.

### REQ26-D26-R25 — Supabase schema and constraints encode the actual invariants

Use non-null tenant/original request/source IDs, same-tenant composite foreign keys, immutable creation fields, consistent origin/provenance shape, and constraints distinguishing absent correspondence from true message facts. D9 relevance retains at most one active resolved-Party association per original/current mapping under its merge contract; source citations do not become a second identity spine. Required brief/source history cannot disappear through cascade delete. Preserve existing canonical identifier types and values, including Support TEXT IDs; use native UUID only where that owning identity is UUID. Do not rekey Support to implement this origin. Use UTC instants/appropriate date types, bounded validated Tiptap JSON plus derived text, explicit nullability and enums/checks consistent with the accepted model. Cross-row authorization, current-root, source-use and work-acceptance invariants use the single guarded owner boundary rather than mutable cross-table CHECK expressions. No new money field, float, receipt ledger or giving precision change is introduced.

### REQ26-D26-R26 — Grants, RLS, columns and privileged paths agree

Preserve Core's tenant ENABLE/FORCE posture, least-privilege role/table/column/function grants and single current authorization policy. Protect source, provenance, operation, link and audit tables from raw browser read/write; compound conversation creation and protected state changes are server-command-only. Inventory/fence generic direct INSERT/UPDATE and old service writers, not only the new route. Evaluate effective RLS old-row USING and resulting-row WITH CHECK, SELECT/RETURNING behavior, multiple policies, views, RPCs, storage and definer/service-role/NHI paths. Supabase default-grant changes do not revoke old explicit grants. Invoker views obey the invoking role's privileges; they are not enough when the role itself bypasses RLS. Harden required definer code with exact execute grants, safe search_path and the same actor/resource gate. No caller-controlled tenant/author/approval/role may transform an allowed row into a forbidden state.

### REQ26-D26-R27 — Complete, bounded queries and current caches

CRM list membership comes from indexed tenant/Party/relevance/source joins, current visibility and D10 canonical dedupe before keyset paging/counts. Qualify beyond the current configured Data API max_rows=1000, Support cap2000 and CRM activity cap50; those source numbers are limitations to test, not accepted product limits. Index actual reverse predicates and cursor ordering, bound payload/links/assets/transactions through registered owner limits and measure plans with skewed tenant sizes. Reuse current read-model/collection conventions; no N+1 transcript hydration or unbounded all-tenant prefetch. Tenant/actor/Party/access generation/filter/cursor scope fences caches and late responses. After create, the returned authorized identity and targeted canonical read reconcile CRM discovery; projection delay never reports a false failed save or encourages duplicate creation.

### REQ26-D26-R28 — Failure, history and operational recovery are first-class

Distinguish validation rejection, permission change, save pending/unknown, admitted work, projection unavailable, mail-not-ready and actual send failure. Durable admission/audit/continuation prevent committed work without a recoverable discovery path. Optional CRM section failure isolates that section, not the whole CRM record; Support remains authoritative. Business history records recorder/origin/current corrections/actual actions; security audit covers access and denied privileged attempts; technical logs use safe IDs/revisions/error classes without brief/contact payloads. Reconciliation and repair use owner commands, not direct database edits or repeated imports. O01–O06 below provide named signals, thresholds, owners and responses after prevention.

### REQ26-D26-R29 — Rollout preserves old evidence and stops unsafe writers

First qualify the shared source/authorization/command/query contracts, then additive origin/nullable-mail/read changes and both UI entries, then inactive legacy conversion and writer fences, then actual release proof. Do not relabel email-only history, infer manual sources from notes/phone fields, or backfill fictitious message timestamps/Party links. Mixed-version deployment must prevent old readers from inventing mail and old CRUD from bypassing new constraints. A kill switch stops new manual admissions while existing requests, CRM discovery and admitted effects remain safely readable/recoverable. Roll forward or use compatible readers after new-origin data exists; reverting to an email-only model is not a safe rollback.

### REQ26-D26-R30 — Coherent UI and independently testable traceability

Use Core base-maia, Base UI, semantic tokens and shared components; one responsive detail/form, labelled fields, keyboard/focus restoration, clear errors/status, no hover-only actions or required drag. Preserve long/international names, accessible reflow, locale/timezone meaning and input under low-bandwidth retry. Validate complete Support-first/CRM-first/CRM-view-only/correction and later-email tasks with representative staff and assistive technology; no claim of perfect UX or compliance comes from a wireframe. Carry D26, the exact shared-owner amendments, four glossary terms, P01–P50 and operational controls into the implementation ADR/OpenSpec/design/tasks/tickets/tests/release chain. “Ticket” introduces no new aggregate. AI augmentation/search remains future research under existing governance, with no model egress or action authority here.

### REQ26-D26-C001 — One form and one detail

The normal staff concepts are **Record a request**, **Support conversations**, **Related records**, **Internal note**, and **Start email thread**. The interface never asks the worker to choose an entity type called case versus ticket versus conversation. One shared form records a received need; one shared Support detail is used from either surface. “Phone” and “In person” identify how the request was received, not calling or recording software.

Illustrative example: a donor says their receipt appears incorrect. Staff records the need for investigation. A finance-authorized person later performs any correction through the receipt domain. This example is not evidence that every tenant uses this workflow or that a call proves the person's identity.

### REQ26-D26-C002 — Path 1 — begin in Support Hub

1. **Launch.** Use Record a request from Support. The current tenant remains visible. A specific current inbox may be prefilled if still qualified; an all-inbox view does not pick an arbitrary inbox. The same navigation shell supports a focused form; small screens use a full-page presentation.

If no eligible inbox exists, offer contextual inbox setup to an authorized manager or a safe administrator handoff, preserving the permitted request draft. A manager can create a named Support work inbox and its required access/coverage without an email address. Configure email remains a separate action using D25's two equal setup paths; no dummy address or third receiving method is introduced.

2. **Describe the need.** Enter a short request title and a concise staff-authored brief using the bounded Tiptap staff-context profile. Choose Phone or In person. Help text explains that this records an account of a request, not a recording or message from the requester. Retain input when validation or context refresh occurs.
3. **Use what is already known.** Add optional observed requester/callback information and permitted Related records. One name field supports international names; email is optional. A current CRM match is a selectable contextual record, not verified identity. If the exact existing encounter/request is already known and readable, reference or open it without re-entering its content. Do not require a universal CRM search or automatically choose a similar match.
4. **Keep timing light.** Recording time is automatic. Add when received only if needed; preserve exact, date-only or unknown meaning visibly. Do not ask the worker to invent a time just to submit. Show the relevant timezone when an exact time is entered; invalid future occurrence is corrected in place.
5. **Review responsibility.** The responsible inbox is explicit. Shared is the new standalone default, with normal eligible assignment/Assign to me and optional follow-up reminder. A teammate's absence or lost access is handled by existing controls. A missing valid assignment is not silently replaced by the creator. Existing source tasks do not become duplicate tasks.
6. **Record.** The primary button says Record request. Adjacent help says No email will be sent to the requester. This creates Open work and the reviewed brief/context/handling together. Separately qualified staff assignment/attention keeps its existing notification policy. An inline error names the field or changed prerequisite, preserving permitted data. A pending or unknown response shows Checking whether this was recorded and reconciles the same occurrence before another create is offered.
7. **Continue normally.** Open the canonical detail. The source card reads Recorded by [staff] · Phone/In person, with separate recording/reported time. No email yet is honest; there is no fake sender, delivered badge or first-reply timer. Notes, handling and work controls use the existing Support model.
8. **Use CRM or email deliberately.** Related records open the shared qualified CRM shell with a return path. Start email thread is a separate public-authoring action with deliberate audience selection and actual mail readiness. A missing address leaves the Support work usable; it does not generate a placeholder or a request to the donor to resubmit.

### REQ26-D26-C003 — Path 2 — begin on a CRM record

1. **Find current Support context.** On the Party Overview, the separate Support conversations preview shows up to three accessible unfinished requests and View conversations. This is not the financial support/giving summary. In Communications → Support conversations, Unfinished/All exposes the complete eligible set with ordinary simple filters.
2. **Choose existing or new work.** Open the current matching request if this is an update. Otherwise use Record a request. Only currently authorized actions appear; lack of permission must not be discovered after substantial editing.
3. **Carry reviewed context.** The same form opens with the current Party visibly staged under Related records. Its name/type/disambiguation is permission-aware. It can be removed. If launched from an actual interaction, show that source as a separate reviewed reference; do not equate it with a Party link or automatically copy its notes/files.
4. **Capture the same minimal information.** Source, brief and qualified handling use the Support-first form. Do not re-enter known permitted information. Do not silently select the Party's present email as recipient, assume the Party made the request, or make the Party's CRM owner the Support assignee.
5. **Save together.** Record request admits work and the exact reviewed context links atomically. If access/source/Party merge state changes, explain that the context needs review and preserve allowed input. Create without that link is an explicit revised choice where legitimate; a success must never quietly omit the link promised by the CRM entry.
6. **Stay in CRM while seeing the real request.** Show the same canonical Support detail in the shared shell/side presentation when it fits. The new linked request is discoverable in the current full CRM view. A brief projection delay has a truthful pending/retry state and the actual returned identity; no duplicate save is needed.
7. **Return without losing place.** Close/back returns to the same permitted Party/view/filter/scroll. Open in Support Hub uses the same ID and preserves a safe return location. Refresh/deep-link/new-tab has a full-page fallback. Drafts remain separate, actor/tenant scoped and subject to current rights; switching surfaces is not a new draft author or send.

### REQ26-D26-C004 — Every email-origin request is viewable through CRM too

The full CRM Support view includes each currently permitted request justified by an explicit relevance link or qualified correspondence, regardless of manual/email origin. Both bases produce one row, with concise truthful reasons. All includes resolved history; the preview's three-row limit and Unfinished default do not define the full population.

Opening an email-origin row uses the normal source/thread cards, qualified attachments, notes and actual delivery indicators inside the same Support detail. It does not use a reduced CRM transcript with missing attachments or a parallel composer. Read-only users see the actual authorized read experience and only their permitted actions. Changes made from CRM go through the same collision/current-authority checks and produce the same durable outcome as Support Hub.

CRM Communication history remains independently based on actual source-owned communication. Merely linking or recording a request adds no email event or last-contact update. This gives full request visibility without teaching staff that every related CRM record actually participated in the conversation.

Link, label, assignment, internal note and provider callback updates do not cause unexplained row jumps. No automatic global activity sort is added. Filter state and count meaning are consistent across preview, full list and navigation; count never includes inaccessible inboxes.

### REQ26-D26-C006 — Correction and maintenance

- **Wrong Related record:** Remove context link or correct through D9's owner command. If correspondence independently justifies the row it remains with that reason; explain the actual result rather than promising that all history vanished.
- **Wrong source claim/time:** Record an attributable correction. Original recorder/server time remains; a reported date change does not backdate response credit or extend retention.
- **Duplicate work:** Use actual D10 merge/Undo or D12 related-work judgment. Do not deduplicate all requests with the same person or title.
- **Created in error:** Retain all D12 unused-tracking exclusions before checking settled responsibility/current work home. Subsequent independent activity, admitted/possibly submitted mail, owner/external effects, merge/dependent continuation/referral or protected draft loss prevent unused cancellation. A legitimately used request is not “created in error” merely because it is completed. A standalone request has no original email conversation to silently receive abandoned work.
- **Source or Party access revoked:** Requalify both directions and remove unavailable content. A permitted work brief cannot become a copied fallback for restricted source data.
- **Staff departure/coverage:** Work stays in its tenant/inbox; actor history remains distinct from assignment. Use existing D7/D8 handling rather than copying staff profile data into the brief.
- **Record merge/archive:** Use canonical Party/source references and current owner eligibility. A Party merge does not merge Support conversations or grant access.
- **Retention/redaction:** The initial published brief enters D17 once; ordinary edits/context changes do not renew it. Both surfaces and all derivatives honor D16/D17. Independent financial/CRM records retain their own lifecycle.

### REQ26-D26-C007 — Visual and accessibility contract

Use Core's exact base-maia/Base UI foundation and shared semantic tokens. A calm hierarchy separates request description, optional context and responsibility. Keep primary work prominent; secondary context/source details disclose progressively. Avoid a dense new call-center form, a channel switch inside the send composer, multiple save buttons with overlapping meaning or nested modal stacks.

Use visible programmatic labels, helpful inline errors and non-disruptive save announcements. Keyboard focus follows launch, validation, save and contextual return predictably. Do not rely on color, hover, icons alone, dragging, pointer precision or automatic form submission. Reflow at narrow widths and zoom, long names and localized labels must remain workable. Preserve permitted input through slow connection/retry; do not claim disconnected-device operation or store private drafts indefinitely. Existing qualified asset controls handle attachments; no new recording/transcription surface is included.

The intended standard is WCAG 2.2 AA with actual shared-component and staff-task qualification, not a conformance claim from this document. W3C's redundant-entry and notification guidance supports avoiding repeated input and explaining outcomes; it does not replace user testing. Redundant entry, Form notifications.

### REQ26-D26-C008 — Email Studio's exact role

Recording a brief uses an appropriate shared Tiptap editor without creating an Email Studio message source or a provider send. Saved staff-context structure, if offered through already-qualified reusable content, remains content-only; D24 external reply-and-work shortcuts do not execute on intake.

A later public reply uses D18 eligible wording, D23 actual inbox/responder signature, explicit D2/D12 audience and first-thread intent, P17 immutable preparation, D4 Support admission and P6 tenant Resend dispatch. Related Parties and the internal brief are not automatic recipients or merge values. No new template key, Role Layout, provider-template mirror or alternate mailer is needed. The data contract supplies the ownership and failure boundaries behind this journey.

All applicable P01–P50 remain required and unexecuted. The complete two-entry/CRM-view/correction/later-email journeys must pass representative staff, keyboard, assistive-technology, mobile, slow-network and current-permission tests before this is described as implemented or fully usable.

### REQ26-D26-C010 — The same record from both surfaces

Support-first and CRM-first entry use one shared form and one Support-owned admission command. CRM can visibly stage an authorized Related record and an exact existing encounter reference; the reviewed request, links and local effects admit together. Every applicable manual/email request and resolved history participates in D9's complete current-authorized CRM Support view. Its row opens the same full qualified Support detail inline or through the full-page fallback, with preserved navigation/drafts. No CRM-local composer, source-body mirror, second ticket or independent send/resolve endpoint.

CRM owns Parties and relationships. Support owns work, its brief and relevance associations. An independently recorded encounter stays with its actual owner. Shared display does not transfer editing or disclosure authority, grant access to either domain, or manufacture a Communication event/last-contact update.

### REQ26-D26-C012 — Saving is not contacting the requester

The exact form help is **No email will be sent to the requester**. This is deliberately narrower than a promise that no staff notification can ever occur. A separately qualified assignment/attention event retains its existing P6 local/optional-email contract. It does not become native requester correspondence or create an email reply target. There is no new requester acknowledgement, staff blast, producer, message-template key, Role Layout or provider-template mirror.

The initial brief uses the accepted staff-context Tiptap profile and Support custody. Where already-qualified reusable staff wording is used, D18's content-only purpose/source controls still apply; reading or inserting wording cannot assign work, publish content or send mail. D24's curated external reply-and-work shortcuts do not execute on manual intake. There is no automatic conversion of the brief, notes, CRM data or original encounter into reusable Email Studio content.

### REQ26-D26-C013 — Manual work setup and later email setup

A qualified manager can create a named work inbox with access/coverage without fake inbound, From or Reply-To values. If none is available, Record a request offers a contextual setup or safe administrator handoff while retaining the permitted draft. This is the explicit accepted extension to D25's email-first Add inbox assumption.

Configure email subsequently uses **Use an existing Support address** or **Create a new Support address** with equal prominence. D25's same connection, receiving-purpose credentials, authenticated ingress, candidate custody, managed-destination proof and conditional email activation remain intact. A work-ready flag does not mean an email route, sender, credential or external destination has been verified. This adds no third receiving method or provider platform.

### REQ26-D26-C014 — First email from a manual request

Start email thread requires a deliberate qualified recipient selection because there is no received-email trigger. Authorized CRM contact lookup may help, but a Related Party, its current preferred email, assignee or observed callback number is not an instruction to address someone. The source brief and private files stay internal unless a distinct currently authorized public composition incorporates permissible information through its proper rules.

The author reviews audience, actual From/Reply-To, wording, signature and any current handling action. P17 prepares one immutable qualified message; Support admits it; P6 dispatches/reconciles that effect. Draft, queued, accepted, delivered and read remain different states. Possibly submitted mail must not be rekeyed or replayed to achieve apparent success.

D14 remains exact: manual save creates no incoming-email target. A genuinely accepted Start email can establish Next for later eligible incoming correspondence at the qualified send-intent boundary. Unknown acceptance retains candidate First/Next interpretations and the earliest applicable possible deadline, labeled Reply timing needs confirmation. Definite rejection discards only invalid candidates. No retrospective phone-note timestamp manufactures response credit.

### REQ26-D26-C015 — Lifetimes and correction

The first admitted manual brief joins D17's human-content activity set once at trusted recording/admission time. Reported encounter time is separate. Ordinary edits, CRM links, list refreshes and provider callbacks do not renew retention. D22 reuses the eligible Staff context brief source kind; this does not expand into CRM/global/AI search. All actual source restrictions and derivatives remain bounded by D16/D17, with no copied CRM Note archive.

All D12 unused-tracking exclusions remain before the additional standalone created-in-error no-obligation/current-home test. Legitimately used work cannot be relabeled just because it is complete. Existing canonical Support TEXT IDs remain stable; no rekeying is needed for this origin. Source, Party and work correction retain their actual owner evidence and present-day authorization.

### REQ26-D26-C017 — Minimal logical shape

Retain the canonical Support original and current D10 handling model. Add a typed staff-recorded origin/brief, not a second ticket or generic encounter table family. Origin describes how Support work began; later email does not change that origin. A manual request has no incoming-email trigger. D12-related work retains its real trigger/reference; email-origin work retains its actual provider/source identity.

The manual brief has its own stable Support source identity, schema version, current content revision/restriction state, trusted author and admission occurrence. It is a staff account of the request. Optional reported occurrence information retains exact/date-only/unknown precision and zone meaning independently. Observed names/callback endpoints are minimal classified Support content, not authoritative CRM updates. Do not manufacture an anonymous CRM person or use text copied from a source as evidence of identity.

If an actual encounter already exists, reference its exact owner ID with same-tenant and current source-use validation. A separately minimized Support brief can describe the unresolved need, but it is not an editable twin of the encounter. A source unavailable later stays unavailable; the system cannot retrieve an old copied body to fill the gap. No speculative event bus, generic relationship catalog or arbitrary polymorphic target JSON is required.

Native external message counts/time/direction remain correctly absent/zero until real messages are admitted. The current `support_conversations` email/address/non-null-time assumptions and collection/mapper contracts must be changed together before admitting the origin. The actual-source probe proves current mapper incompatibility only: hard-coded email, literal null strings and changing read-time message timestamps on synthetic zero-mail input, with a valid email control.

Do not rekey existing Support identities to implement this origin or freeze a generic union schema. Invalid cross-row current-root/authority/obligation states require the guarded owner transaction; a CHECK constraint cannot safely query mutable external owner state. No monetary amount column or change to financial precision is needed.

### REQ26-D26-C019 — Admission, retry and correction

1. Authenticate inside the server handler/command; resolve trusted current actor and tenant. Parse only allowed intent fields. The route stays a thin application boundary over the canonical shared business API.
2. Resolve the durable operation and payload meaning. A matching committed occurrence returns its original safe receipt and separately current state. A changed meaning conflicts. Current permissions govern disclosure of both.
3. Recheck current inbox work acceptance, classification, handling/coverage and optional source/Party reference permissions under a consistent guarded state. Actor ID, reported caller ID and assignee are not interchangeable.
4. Atomically commit the new original request/brief/Open work, reviewed Shared or explicit eligible handling, any explicit reminder, complete reviewed links/references, attribution/history, receipt and required identifier-only invalidation/reconciliation intent.
5. Return the actual authorized identity. A CRM-first caller can open that same detail and reconcile its full list from canonical state. Projection delay is not failed admission. Durable continuation recovers secondary effects without replaying create.

A Party/source permission change rejects the compound create and preserves permitted draft content. An explicit revised create omitting that link is a new reviewed semantic operation after the first outcome is known, not automatic fallback. Concurrent requests with genuinely distinct identities remain possible; one name/date/brief is not a unique business key. Similarity can aid authorized staff judgment only.

Corrections do not rewrite original actor/time or convert the brief into an incoming email. Created-in-error cancellation first retains all D12 unused-tracking exclusions: subsequent independent activity, native/admitted/possibly submitted mail, owner/external effects, active merge or dependent continuation/referral and protected draft loss make it ineligible. Only then does the standalone additional no-obligation/accepted-current-home test apply. It cannot retire legitimately used/completed work simply because nothing remains owed. It is a non-success ending with protected retirement/evidence, not delete-and-recreate. Source and destination current controls prevent stale cancel/merge/replay from abandoning or resurrecting work.

### REQ26-D26-C020 — Complete CRM query and inline access

For the requested canonical Party, candidate membership is the union of active explicit D9 relevance and qualified actual correspondence. Apply joint Party/Support/source/field visibility, resolve current D10 handling, deduplicate by tenant/canonical conversation and then page/count. Use covering indexes for actual source/relevance and cursor predicates; avoid loading a general Support list and filtering it in the browser.

Manual zero-mail work is eligible through explicit relevance. Ended work is in All; Unfinished is a default filter, not a data deletion policy. The Overview preview remains capped at three and links to the complete view. Current financial `support` totals remain separate. When both discovery bases exist, show one row with both truthful reasons. Removing a relevance link cannot erase independent correspondence; source attribution correction is its own owner path.

Default ordering retains actual latest external-message occurrence for records with mail. Staff-origin records with no mail use original trusted recorded/created time, labeled Recorded; stable canonical ID resolves ties. Reported call time and mutable `updated_at` are not this sort. Unknown legacy evidence gets an explicit unknown class. The new fallback is a deliberate D9 amendment, not a generic last-activity model.

The CRM view opens the same canonical Support detail/read/action contracts, inline where the shared shell permits and full-page otherwise. It keeps all currently qualified content/attachments/actions and read-only limits. Both entry routes bind the same ID and policy; a drawer or client cache is never a permission boundary. Safe return locations are local/validated and tenant/Party scoped; user-controlled navigation state cannot become an open redirect or data-access instruction.

Use scoped cache/query/realtime keys and current access generations; permission/source/link change requalifies both directions. No unrestricted hidden count, transcript prefetch or integration-admin lens. An authorized Support projection outage is isolated and retryable; a denied target reveals no existence. CRM uptime must not depend on a successful Support query for unrelated data.

### REQ26-D26-C021 — Supabase authorization posture

The configured local PostgreSQL major version is17. Hosted version, grants and actual deployment policy require release verification; local config is not live-state proof. Core migrations already enable tenant RLS and explicitly include UPDATE WITH CHECK for the old Support tables, while authenticated CRUD spans19 core Support tables. Later inbound-route revocation does not by itself revoke the core conversation/message/audit grants. The defect is insufficient current resource/field/immutable/compound-command protection if reused, not simply missing RLS syntax.

Require least-privilege explicit grants for every new/protected table, column, view and function. The exposed-schema RLS floor is defense in depth; `service_role` and applicable owners can bypass it, so the same current actor/resource policy must be enforced by every privileged command/read. Deny raw browser control/provenance/audit/association access and fence direct conversation/source writers. Do not grant broad raw tables merely to make a new CRM pane work.

For any authorized browser-safe projection, prove its effective underlying and invoking privileges. `security_invoker` is available in PostgreSQL15+; it does not narrow a service role that already bypasses RLS. A required SECURITY DEFINER function must have hardened search_path, exact execution grants and current actor/resource checks; the keyword is not authorization. Review SELECT/RETURNING behavior and all applicable permissive/restrictive policies, USING and resulting-row checks, including whether updates can change protected tenant/source/author/control state. Storage access follows source and byte-owner policy, not just a visible CRM link.

**Verified correction to skill shorthand:** PostgreSQL17 reuses USING as WITH CHECK for UPDATE/ALL when WITH CHECK is omitted. Omission alone does not prove reassignment is allowed. Explicit clauses improve clarity, but effective predicates, protected columns and grants determine safety. Similarly a definer function's effective privilege depends on its owner and grants. PostgreSQL17 CREATE POLICY, Supabase RLS.

Supabase's current default-grant rollout concerns new tables; old explicit grants remain. Therefore deployment must declare intended grants/revocations and test actual Data API access rather than relying on project creation date or a dashboard badge. No global grant workaround or assumed automatic lockdown. Supabase Data API change.

### REQ26-D26-C022 — Email Studio, targets, retention and search

Manual admission has no requester email preparation or transport call. Existing qualified staff assignment/attention uses D12/P6's separate actual producer and recipient policy, without making staff-email availability a work-admission gate. An authorized manager can establish a named work inbox and required access/coverage with no dummy inbound/From/Reply-To fields; the current mail-shaped inbox schema/DTO must be qualified too. Work acceptance is not D25 email activation or a generic isActive shortcut. Configure email remains D25's two equal paths, separately reachable from the same inbox.

A later first email uses the explicit manual-origin recipient branch, actual P17 identity/wording/signature/preparation, D4 admission and P6 dispatch. Existing D14 accepted Start email → subsequent Next semantics remain; unknown acceptance retains candidate First/Next and the earliest applicable possible deadline rather than forcing First. No email target/fulfillment occurs from the brief itself.

Initial published manual brief joins D17's human-content activity set once at trusted admission. Ordinary edits/context changes/late logs do not renew it. Title/brief/derived content stays finite Support material, separate from independent CRM/financial retention. D22 already has eligible Staff context brief search; this origin uses that kind. No external activity corpus or AI index is added.

### REQ26-D26-C023 — Migration and proof

Inventory old schema/defaults/DTOs/caches/list/report/source writers first. Add compatible readers and conditional constraints before enabling creation. Evidence-only legacy conversion must not infer phone origins or Party links. Fence both generic browser and service writers before exposing protected new data through CRM. A kill switch pauses only new manual admissions; existing requests and admitted effect reconciliation remain safe. Old email-only code is not a valid rollback after new data exists.

P01–P50 require actual database constraints, multi-role Data API/RPC/storage tests, joint current-policy tests, concurrent/partial-failure admission, complete queries beyond known caps, migration/backfill/restore, both UX journeys and later real email proof. All remain required and unexecuted by this specification. SQL text review and the source probe cannot certify hosted RLS or release readiness.

### REQ26-D26-C025 — Accepted bounded work and complete CRM experience

One canonical Support record and one shared form/command serve Support-first and CRM-first entry. Record an actual phone/in-person request that needs continuing Support work, with a concise visibly staff-authored brief, protected recorder/time, optional reported occurrence and reviewed context. No fabricated email, compulsory Party, second ticket, call log, telephony, recording, transcription, generic activity platform, device-offline capability or AI is introduced. Ordinary relationship tasks, finance and restricted care retain their owners.

New standalone work starts Open with Shared handling unless the worker deliberately selects another currently eligible handler; reminders are explicit and no email-intake routing is replayed. A manager can establish a named work inbox and qualified access/coverage before configuring email. No eligible inbox has a draft-preserving contextual setup or safe administrator handoff. Configure email remains D25's two equally presented paths; manual work readiness does not confer receiving/sending readiness or require dummy address fields. This is the accepted narrow extension to D25's email-first setup assumption.

CRM-first creation visibly stages removable current Party context and exact existing-source references. Request, brief, handling, reviewed links, history, receipt and durable continuation commit together, or reject without a silent subset. Unknown outcomes reconcile the same occurrence; changed meaning conflicts. Existing encounter bodies remain with their owners rather than being cloned into a second editable log. Support's source remains a minimized account of the unresolved need.

Every current authorized manual/email origin and resolved history participates in D9's complete justified CRM Support view. Joint visibility precedes dedupe/count/page; explicit relevance and independently qualified correspondence remain distinct bases. Unlinked work stays valid in Support. Overview's up-to-three Unfinished preview is only a preview; Communications → Support conversations provides the complete Unfinished/All view. The same canonical detail works inline where practical and full-page otherwise, preserving filters/scroll/return and permitted private drafts. There is no copied transcript, reduced CRM editor, hidden count, transitive household/company membership, administrator viewing lens or second write endpoint.

### REQ26-D26-C026 — Accepted chronology, ownership and Email Studio seam

Zero native mail has zero native count and absent mail/contact facts, not now or literal null strings. The explicit D9 ordering amendment uses original trusted Recorded time for staff-created work without external messages; actual-message occurrence remains authoritative once correspondence exists. Reported encounter date/time/precision is distinct and cannot backdate server evidence, targets or retention. Notes/link/assignment/provider updates do not create fake recency. Preserve current Support TEXT identifiers; no rekey migration is required.

The explicit Email Studio integration and independent seam review document the accepted boundary. Tiptap's staff-context profile does not transfer brief ownership. Manual save sends **no email to the requester**, creates no fictional requester-correspondence event and executes no D24 shortcut. Independently qualified staff assignment/attention retains its actual D12/P6 source, recipient, preference, template and dedupe contract; optional staff-email failure cannot block manual work.

Start email thread has a deliberate manual-origin audience branch with no invented incoming trigger or automatic Related-Parties recipients. Email Studio/P17 keeps qualified wording, signature, actual From/Reply-To, typed fields and immutable preparation; Support admits the exact reviewed effect and P6 dispatches/reconciles tenant mail. No internal brief or file is automatically made public. There is no new template key, Role Layout, provider-template mirror, credential or direct mailer.

D14 remains precise: manual capture creates no email reply target; genuinely accepted Start email can establish Next for later input. Unknown acceptance retains candidate First/Next interpretations and the earliest applicable possible deadline, not forced First or scored success/breach. D17 explicitly includes the first published brief once at trusted admission; ordinary edits/context changes do not renew retention. D22 reuses eligible Staff context brief search without global/CRM/AI corpus expansion. D16/D17 restrictions apply across both surfaces and all derivatives, preserving independently owned required evidence.

### REQ26-D26-C027 — Accepted correction, data safety and release sequence

All D12 unused-tracking exclusions remain before the additional standalone created-in-error no-obligation/accepted-current-home test. Used or completed legitimate work cannot be retired merely because nothing remains owed, and no original email conversation is invented for rehoming. D9 link correction and Party merge provenance, D10 merge/Undo, D3 current obligations and original source ownership remain intact.

Current tenant/actor/resource/source authority, stable typed identifiers, same-tenant constraints, protected creator/provenance/control fields and one compound command govern every writer. Effective grants/RLS old/new-row semantics, SELECT/RETURNING, views/RPC/definer/service/storage paths and direct legacy writers require the same boundary. The PostgreSQL USING fallback correction is accepted; missing WITH CHECK syntax alone is not a vulnerability claim. Complete indexed queries replace cap-limited loaded-row filtering. Source and authority facts remain current while optional CRM projections recover.

Later authorized implementation proceeds from source/authorization/transaction foundations to complete CRM queries/shared detail, both forms and later-email use, compatible migration and all-writer fences, then actual P01–P50 proof. A kill switch stops new manual admissions while existing source/work/discovery/recovery remains safe. O01–O06 monitors residual faults only after preventive gates. No old broad reader or email-only mapper is a safe rollback over new-origin data.

## D26 — Required operational controls

### OP26-D26-O01

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed wrong-tenant or unauthorized CRM/Support source disclosure, including count/attachment/prefetch.

**Owner:** Core security/authorization and Support read owner.

**Response:** Fence affected read/action scope, preserve minimal evidence, repair policy/derivatives and requalify before reopening.

### OP26-D26-O02

**Signal and threshold:** One admitted eligible request absent from its complete authorized CRM query, or a projection failure reported as zero.

**Owner:** Support–CRM projection owner.

**Response:** Preserve canonical work; show unavailable/reconcile; repair exact source/link/query path and verify full affected cohort.

### OP26-D26-O03

**Signal and threshold:** One duplicate admission for the same durable occurrence or one partial work/link/audit commit.

**Owner:** Support command/data owner.

**Response:** Stop faulty writer, reconcile exact identities/current obligations and repair through audited owner commands before re-enabling.

### OP26-D26-O04

**Signal and threshold:** One requester email/fictional mail event/auto-Party/duplicate task/optional follow/reply-target event caused solely by manual save, or one fabricated native-message time.

**Owner:** Support product/command owner with P6/P17 owner where affected.

**Response:** Disable the incorrect effect/reader, preserve actual work and external truth, correct projections and rerun no-effect proof; retain independently qualified staff attention.

### OP26-D26-O05

**Signal and threshold:** First breach of a registered query/resource/retention/purge deadline, or one expired derivative still retrievable.

**Owner:** Support records/operations owner with CRM read owner.

**Response:** Block invalid disclosure, report actual incomplete state, apply bounded recovery/backpressure and requalify the violated contract.

### OP26-D26-O06

**Signal and threshold:** One confirmed user journey that loses saved/draft work, sends unexpectedly, or blocks the required keyboard/AT task.

**Owner:** Support UX owner and shared UI owner.

**Response:** Stop affected flow, preserve work/custody, correct interaction and repeat the failed staff/accessibility task before release.

### REQ26-D26-C028 — Operating and qualification sequence

Monitor residual faults after safeguards and release gates, not instead of correcting known defects.

## Exact interaction-source cardinality clarification

### REQ26-D26-CARD01 — One interaction may give rise to separate legitimate work

When an independently authorized original interaction already exists, Support references its stable owner identity and revision rather than cloning its body, participants or attachments. A Support brief describes the bounded work request and is not a second authoritative encounter transcript. When Support first captures the need, its request/source is authoritative for that bounded need; do not dual-write a CRM encounter or Notes body solely for timeline appearance.

Multiple legitimate independent requests may arise from one interaction. Neither interaction ID alone nor a person/date/summary combination is a universal uniqueness key. Deduplicate the same requested admission effect by its durable command identity while permitting genuinely distinct needs. AC26-D26-P12 and AC26-D26-P25 must prove both the no-shadow-record case and two independent issues from one real interaction. This is the adopted O26-02 clarification of the final source/command contract, not new scope.
